  • Payday among the bills, on the phone: Finances' Coming up shows each paycheck of the next two weeks on its day among the bills, and says how much of what's due comes before the next one ($2,104.49 of it before Alex's paycheck on Nov 6).
  • Cash flow and Where it goes open their detail: on the Finances Dashboard, the arrow on either card opens Recurring, where the typical month is laid out payment by payment. A kind on Where it goes opens Recurring on its own payments (Cards, or Home among the bills).
  • Reports you can click: on Finances › Reports, Where it went has Show all for every payee past the five largest, and a category, a payee, or a month on its charts opens Transactions showing just those transactions (this month's or last month's when that's the stretch picked); each category says its share of the spending first, and Transactions' category filter takes a group too (Food finds Groceries and Eating out).
  • What the payments come to: Finances › Recurring › Payments says what those shown add up to a month and a year (18 payments: about $5,948.10 a month, $71,377 a year), following Bills, Cards, Spending or Saving when you pick one; and Largest first lists them by what each costs a month; one that isn't monthly says what that is (Every Saturday · $866.67 a month).
  • A budget's daily allowance: pick a budget for its transactions this month; under what a budget has left, Finances says how much a day keeps it on budget to the end of the month or pay period ($225.08 a day for 2 days), and the budgets' bars now line up.
  • Amounts in Finances' boxes, to the cent: Update balances and the forms start a box with an amount's cents in two places (2512.40, not 2512.4).
  • Next paychecks, month by month: Finances › Pay lists the coming paychecks under each month, with how many it has and what they bring in all, so a month with a third paycheck (or one moved in from the next month by a holiday) stands out.
  • No half-empty rows on Finances: in a window of usual width, What you own and What you owe sit side by side, Reports' By tag and the Dashboard's Net worth take the whole row, and in a wide window the calendar's day and month cards stack beside it.
  • An app's page on the iPhone says less: its logo, its state, the round Open, Restart, Stop and Logs buttons, its week, what it's for in a line, its last backup and its address, as in the mockup. Everything else (updates, details, settings, the backup in full, what CrowdSec stopped) is one tap away, under More About the app.
  • Folded groups on the iPhone's Status show their apps' logos: a row of logos, as a Home Screen folder, with the names under them, in place of the plain line of names. Only an app that isn't simply running wears a badge.
  • Watch Start, Stop and Restart happen on the iPhone: on an app's page, the button you tapped turns into a spinner and the state reads "Restarting…" in blue, then changes to the new state with a tap you can feel when Status has it (a buzz if it failed). Tapping an app on Status now grows its page out of the row.
  • The iPhone app at the largest text sizes: Status's card and tiles, Finances' paycheck line and Spending's ring stack instead of squeezing; the ring's number, Wallet cards and the small account cards keep their words inside them, as Wallet's do.
  • Settings on the iPhone, tidied like iPhone Settings: each setting shows only its name and value, switches flip in place, and a setting opens its own page with what it does; the long notes under each section are gone.
  • The iPhone app takes https addresses only: the one exception, plain http to the homelab on the same Mac, was for the Mac version of the app, which is gone.
  • Tidy Up says what's going on: Audiobooks that are already one file each say so (All 177 audiobooks are one file each) instead of 0. Movies and TV say when Tdarr isn't answering (paused on battery, or stopped) rather than looking stuck, and Recently done no longer fills with collect stopped every few minutes. A step that stops says why, in the engine's own words, instead of The log says why.
  • The iPhone app, smoother: Finances shows the shapes of its cards while it reads instead of a spinner; an app's page opens with its logo big, round Open, Start or Stop, Restart and Logs buttons, and its week as seven coloured bars; the lock screen shows the new white icon with one Unlock button; and at the largest text sizes Finances' tiles stack instead of cutting off.
  • Investments on the iPhone, redone: what they're worth with the gain all time and this month, a line over the past month, 3 months or year you can run a finger along, how the money is split across your holdings, and each holding with its ticker in colour and its gain.
  • A new icon for the iPhone app: a violet server rack on a white tile, the other way round from before, like Proton Mail's. The mark on the pairing and lock screens matches.
  • The native Mac version of the Homelab app is gone: on the Mac, Homelab Wizard (the desktop app) is the way in. The iPhone and iPad app is unchanged.
  • Finances on the iPhone, as cards: checking as a Wallet card with what it is after the next paycheck, net worth with a line you can run a finger along (past month, 3 months or year), what's left to spend and the next bill side by side, the latest transactions, the bills coming up, and the rest of Finances one tap away. The red health line no longer sits atop every tab: what needs a look is on Status and its badge.
  • Unplugging no longer cuts Tdarr off mid-video: on battery, the other busy apps still pause at once, but Tdarr finishes the video it's on (starting no new one), then pauses too, so it leaves no half-made copy behind. Plugged in again, it picks up where it was.
  • Tdarr no longer fills the media drive: a video Tdarr was stopped part-way through (on battery, or by an update) left a copy as large as the video in its cache, and they added up (81 GB on one drive). Tidy Up now clears those leftovers by itself whenever Tdarr isn't converting anything, and says how much space came back. Your videos are never touched.
  • A transaction's note on the iPhone: the bank's own wording, kept from an import, isn't shown as its note (a memo you wrote before it still is), as on the computer.
  • Budgets on the iPhone: the page opens with what's left to spend this month, a bar of what's spent, and about how much a day that leaves.
  • More imported bills find their planned payment: a company pays the bill it's for even when the names differ (FPL pays your Electric bill, Mazda your car payment), a bill that changes each time (electric, water) still links when it's well off its planned amount, and last month's bills link too when you only added the payment to your plan this month.
  • Import a file's buttons stay in sight: Bring in and Cancel sit at the foot of the sheet however long the list, the list no longer scrolls inside the sheet, and the sheet doesn't bounce at its ends.
  • Backups on the iPhone, at a glance: a ring of how many copies are fresh, when the last backup ran and where it went, with Back Up Now and Test a Restore right under it.
  • Investments from the iPhone: Finances › Investments has Read Now, to read Ghostfolio again, and Add a Holding, to record a buy or a sale from your phone, as on the computer.
  • Settings on the iPhone, as the iPhone's own: your homelab at the top, then switches for nightly updates and the widget, and each section of the homelab's settings with its own coloured icon.
  • Transactions on the iPhone, like Wallet: the account's card on top with your other accounts to switch between, each transaction with its company's logo, and new ones marked with a violet dot until you've reviewed them. Tap one for its own page: a big logo and amount, what bill it paid, its category and note, and the other times at that place.
  • Finances on the iPhone, tidied: it opens with checking now and after payday, your net worth with its line, then a list like Settings: Transactions, Budgets, Bills, Investments, Accounts, Goals and Loans, each one tap away.
  • Status on the iPhone, at a glance: it opens with a ring of how many apps are running and the one that needs a look, with its Start and Logs right there, then tiles for backups, savings, nightly updates and health checks. The tab bar at the bottom shrinks as you scroll.
  • Ghostfolio, Wallos, and Firefly III that run elsewhere: an app you started in Docker yourself (Status says Runs elsewhere) now counts as running for Finances: Investments reads Ghostfolio once a day as Finances opens, and Update balances and Recurring offer From Ghostfolio, From Firefly III, and From Wallos, as they do for apps the homelab runs.
  • Payee logos on the iPhone: each transaction in the iPhone app's Finances shows its payee's logo, the same as on the computer: Netflix, your bank or your grocer in its own colours, or its initials when it has none.
  • Add a holding is always there: the Investments card shows Add a holding and Read now wherever you can change Finances (the computer, and a phone allowed to change it), not only when Status reports Ghostfolio running. If Ghostfolio doesn't answer, the card says so.
  • Cleaner transactions: imported bills read as the company (FPL, American Express, Apple Card, Fidelity, Apple Cash), and a car loan as its make (Mazda); the bank's long wording is no longer shown in the list (it stays in the transaction's note). A payment to your American Express or Apple Card is a transfer to that card. A bill whose name says nothing is linked to the planned payment of the same amount to the cent, within a few days. Renaming a payee (HOA) renames its other transactions too, and next month's import comes in by that name. New logos for FPL and Royal Caribbean, and American Express's and Goldman Sachs's own marks; a logo you picked yourself now fits inside its circle.
  • Clearer names on imported transactions: a bank file's direct debits and deposits come in without the bank's codes (Mazda Financial, not Mazda Financial Web …Web Id); Zelle says who (Zelle from Jane Doe), a card payment which card (Payment to Chase card ••1234), and Comcast is Xfinity. Importing the same file again gives the ones already in their clearer names, keeping their categories, and never adds one you renamed a second time.
  • Categories filled in on import: a transaction brought in from a bank's file takes what it's plainly for: the category you gave its payee last, its planned bill's (Xfinity paying Internet is Internet), a known company's (Costco is Groceries, Shell is Gas, Netflix is Streaming and music), or a payroll deposit's (Paycheck). Paying off your own card, or money moved from your own savings account, comes in as a transfer between them, not spending. Anything unclear is left for you, and the preview says each before it comes in. Importing a file again fills in those brought in before with none.
  • Is Ghostfolio's token right? Investments' Read now says Signed in to Ghostfolio even before anything is in it, with what to add there next, or says why it couldn't sign in. Settings › Ghostfolio security token now says what uses it, and to press Read now to check it. An account set up in Ghostfolio with nothing in it yet no longer reads as $0 here: its balance stays as you typed it.
  • Finances at night: in dark mode, Finances has a near-black background with its cards a step lighter and thin lines, easier on the eyes and quicker to read at a glance. A system set to more contrast keeps its own colours.
  • Is Ghostfolio's token right? Investments' Read now says Signed in to Ghostfolio even before anything is in it, with what to add there next, or says why it couldn't sign in. Settings › Ghostfolio security token now says what uses it, and to press Read now to check it. An account set up in Ghostfolio with nothing in it yet no longer reads as $0 here: its balance stays as you typed it.
  • Your accounts in the sidebar: under each group (Cash, Credit cards, Investments…) the sidebar lists its accounts, each with its round logo and balance; a group's arrow folds them away, and it stays folded. Every logo and category icon on Finances is round now too.
  • Each category in its own colour: on Finances, a category's icon is drawn in one colour on every row, budget, report bar, the money flow and the donut (Food is the same green everywhere, Utilities the same orange), so you can tell them apart at a glance, in light and dark.
  • Tidy Up, redesigned: Overview starts with the one thing to do next, larger, beside a ring of what's on the drive. Under it, a tile for each library in its own colour says what it holds, how far along it is, and what it waits on; a tile opens its tab, which now starts with that library (Music's with its clean-up step by step).
  • Transfers between your accounts, joined: money out of one of your accounts and the same into another within three days are offered on Transactions as one transfer (Join, or Not one transfer), so they count as neither spending nor income. Bringing in either bank's file again skips its half.
  • Transactions link to the bills they pay: Transactions lists those already in that look like a planned payment (looks like Electric, planned $140), each with Link or Not it, and Link all; a linked one says pays Electric. A transaction you type picks its planned payment by itself, saying so, until you pick another.
  • A bill paid early isn't taken out twice: importing a bank's file links each row that plainly pays a planned payment (its name or logo, about its amount, near its day), so the forecast doesn't take that bill out again on its day. The preview says Looks like Electric, planned $140, and you can change or remove it before bringing them in.
  • A bill due the day you typed in your balances comes out: Finances used to take it as already paid, so the forecast came out too high by that bill. It now comes out on its day; if your balance already had it, mark it Already in under Taken as done.
  • Something stopped? Each screen says what to do: a stopped app's page says, under its name, why it isn't running and what helps (Start, quit the program on its port, plug in its drive, or read its log). A phone that can only look says to start it from the computer instead of showing nothing. The watchdog alerts when an app stops by itself, and Status's Watchdog line names a stopped app it doesn't check instead of only All 47 checks passed.
  • A stopped app says when it stopped, and why: an app that stopped by itself read just Stopped, the same as one shut down cleanly. Its row, its page, the phone, and homelab status now say Stopped at 3:12 AM: it ran out of memory (or it quit with an error, another program is using its port 9925, Docker couldn't start it) with a red dot, Needs a look and the menu bar count it, and one Docker gave no reason for says when. On the phone, a folded group's app names no longer push Status sideways.
  • Setup's steps are read in full: each step's description was cut to one line with "…" (in a smaller window, every one), and so was why a step didn't work, with what to press next. Both are read in full now; the chevron stays only on a step with more to know.
  • An app's week says when it was down, and why: its page said Missed checks on Tuesday, with nothing on what a check is or how long. It now says Last down Tue at 3:10 AM for 45 minutes: HTTP 502 · 2 outages (or Down since … while it is), from the watchdog's own record of each outage. A stopped app's page no longer says checks start once Setup turns it on while they are on: it says the watchdog doesn't check it while it's stopped.
  • Status in a household's words: Choose stacks is now Choose apps (the sidebar, the menu, the shortcuts, and the CLI's hints); All baseline apps are up is The homelab's own apps are all up; the savings tile is Instead of subscriptions, $3,292 a year; and what CrowdSec caught reads Probing for a known security hole, from Netherlands · Example Hosting B.V., with its scenario and address on hover. On the phone, an app's log wraps its lines instead of cutting them off.
  • A stale backup says why: a copy marked Stale on Backups had only its age. It now says why from its app's state (It's stopped, so the nightly copy skips it. Start it, and tonight's copy catches up, or that Back up now tries again), on the computer and the phone. On the phone each copy takes two lines, with how many are kept, instead of three. Settings says Take the homelab off this Mac (and this PC), not this mac.
  • Lyrics are always on Tidy Up: once a lyrics check found nothing to tidy or add, every lyrics option disappeared, from Overview and from Music. Music now always has a Lyrics row with what the last check found and Check again, and before the first check Overview offers it too (See how many songs have lyrics), not only the Music tab.
  • Tidy Up starts with two things, not nine: on a new Mac with the media drive unplugged, Needs your OK listed the drive, each library on it, and each missing tool, nine rows. Now the drive is one row (Plug in the Media drive: Music, Movies, TV, Books and Audiobooks are on it, with Choose folder… for media kept elsewhere), and the tools are one (Install Python 3, ffmpeg and Calibre's tools), asking only for what a library that's here needs: with the drive away, just Python. A library's own tab names the tools it needs.
  • Tidy Up says when a job picks up where one stopped: a job that takes over from one cut off part-way (a restart, the app quitting) said so only in Terminal. The Tidy Up screen now says so too.
  • A books review, once applied: Overview no longer says the same books could look tidier, and Books says the review was applied, with Undo, instead of offering to apply it again.
  • When songs go missing in the music swap: a check that finds songs missing now says how many and whose (3 songs didn't make it into the new library: Radiohead (2 fewer), Björk (all of it)), with Put the old library back… and Check again, instead of asking for the same check again as if it had never run.
  • Tidy Up says what to do first: Overview has one main button, on the first thing to do and never on a step that throws things away; Music's tab shows its space beside its genres; a film with Tdarr reads Tdarr is shrinking 4 films, not what Tdarr has finished. On a phone the tabs sit in two even rows, and VoiceOver reads a job's steps and its end instead of every file it touches.
  • Tidy Up's numbers agree: sizes are counted as the Finder counts a drive, so the space won back at the top is the figure Recently done shows (it said 384 GB beside 412 GB freed), and the first line counts what Needs your OK lists. A books review that can't be read says why, with Try again, instead of saying every book looks tidy; Look… on the Books tab now shows the review; and when Tidy Up can't read its record, its card has Try again.
  • Tidy Up while another job runs: when the agent is collecting Tdarr's work, or a job runs from Terminal, Tidy Up shows it with its step and bar, and every button waits for it instead of failing with another Tidy Up job is moving files; once it's done, the buttons come back by themselves. A job that stopped part-way says what it was in words and carries on properly: a swap asks again and finishes (never This step needs your OK), and a books apply opens the review, so the books you left alone stay alone. Stop says Stopping… until the job reaches a safe point, and a job that fails says it didn't finish, with Try again.
  • A copy before anything risky: an app's databases are now dumped just before it starts again on changed settings, as they already were before an update: when it gets a domain or tailnet address, when it starts signing in with Pocket ID, and when Fix it applies settings changed by hand. The dump sits beside the nightly ones, and if it fails, the change isn't made.
  • Add to Home Screen, done right: the phone companion added to an iPhone's Home Screen has the app's icon, no longer a picture of the page, and Android's shapes no longer cut it. Opened from there, its splash on Android is the app's own background, and the bar above it follows light or dark mode.
  • Status read aloud: with VoiceOver or Narrator on, Status reads out each app's change as it happens, not only a job's result: Vikunja: Restarting…, then Vikunja: Running, and apps that go down together in one line. Nothing is read for Status while another screen is shown.
  • Shapes as well as colours: an app (or backup, or anything else) that is stopped or needs a look has a triangle beside it and one that is down a cross, where a running one has a circle, so a state reads without telling green from red, on a small screen, and in Windows' contrast themes.
  • An unplugged drive is waited for on Linux too: with the media drive out when the machine started, Docker made an empty music, films, or photos folder where the drive goes and started the app on it, so it showed an empty library and the drive's place was taken. Those apps now wait for the drive and start within a minute of it being plugged in, as on a Mac and Windows; installing makes their folders on the drive instead.
  • After sleep: when the computer wakes, every app is checked at once, not up to 15 minutes later: an app that went down while it slept is noticed (and restarted, or alerted about) straight away.
  • A drive comes back: apps waiting for an unplugged drive start within a minute of it being plugged in again, not at the watchdog's next check up to 15 minutes later.
  • Starting and stopping an app, without the log: Start, Stop, and Restart no longer open a dimmed panel of Docker's output (image downloads and all) to read and close. The app's row and its page say what is happening, Downloading the app… while it comes down first, and the row turns to Running or Stopped; Stop still offers Undo. If it fails, the row says why, with Details for what Docker said. Updates keep their panel, with what's new.
  • Lyrics for more songs, and why the rest have none: a song LRCLIB lists under another album, another length, or a title like Paranoid Android - 2009 Remaster is now found by a search when its exact record isn't there, and a song with no album tag is looked up at all (it was skipped as an error). When it's done, the card says what came of every song: added, already time-synced, instrumental, not on LRCLIB yet, or no title tag. Songs LRCLIB has nothing for are asked about again a month later, so running it again is quick, and Add lyrics on Overview counts only the songs still worth asking about.
  • Tidy Up, redone: Overview is one list of what needs your OK across every library, each line with what it wins back and its one button, so nothing is three clicks away; a ring of your music's genres; the media drive, what each library takes, and what is free; and what was done lately, with Undo on the music swap and the books' changes. Films, shows, and books have genre rings too, from Jellyfin or the films' .nfo files, and from Calibre's tags; a dropdown picks whose. A film or episode in the library twice is found by the scan and offered on Overview; Remove extras… keeps the copy with the best picture and puts the others in the Trash, after asking. TV says which episodes are missing from a season, by show. Films and shows Jellyfin has no poster for are named, and Fetch posters asks it to look again. Whatever Tidy Up puts in the Trash, its line in Recently done can put back with Undo. Each library has its own tab with what could be tidier, its space, and its history. New downloads and lyrics now live on Overview and Music.
  • Tidy Up, smoother: each library's name on Overview opens its tab; a library whose drive is unplugged says so on its tab and runs nothing until it is back; every card's heading lines up; New downloads shows its six steps in two even rows; and the words read right (Nothing went missing in green, 1 download … before it's filed, English only for the languages kept, H.264 written one way, Ready to review for the books).
  • Finances on the phone, what is coming up first: on a paired phone, Finances opens with Coming up: every bill of the next two weeks with its day and how soon (today's and tomorrow's in amber), a bill charged to a card marked with its card, and what leaves checking in all. Under it, the goals, each with what it needs a paycheck and See all; Calendar opens the whole month.
  • Finances, card charges on the calendar: a bill you charge to a card moves no checking money, so the calendar left it out. It now shows on its day, marked with its card and the day that card is next paid ("on Chase Freedom, due Nov 21"), apart from what checking holds.
  • Finances, a sidebar balance opens its own group: Cash, Investments, or another group's balance in the sidebar opens Net worth on that group alone: its total, each of its accounts month by month as a band of its own, and only its accounts listed. Show everything goes back to the whole page.
  • Finances, the calendar a year ahead: past the three months it reads checking for, the calendar goes on to a year from today with each payday and payment on its day, so a yearly renewal shows in its month. Those days show what is planned, without a balance.
  • Status, tighter: the short cards (Protection, What the apps keep, what is using power) stack in one column beside Recent alerts instead of one sitting alone beside a long list; an alert with a long list shows its first 3 lines and Show N more; and each app's size takes one line, its name, bar, and size side by side.
  • Keep using the app while a long job runs: Update all apps now, an app's update, Fix it, and the other commands in a window of their own have Hide while they run; they carry on, with a small bar at the foot of the sidebar that brings them back and says when they're done.
  • Jobs wait their turn instead of failing: pressing Back up now, a Setup step, Install, or an app's Start, Stop, or Restart while another job runs no longer says "another install or setup step is running". It waits its turn, says what it's waiting for where you pressed it, and starts by itself as soon as the one before ends. The other apps' buttons stay usable meanwhile.
  • Phones and the nightly jobs wait their turn too: a Restart from a phone, the nightly backup and update, and the app's own jobs now queue behind each other rather than running at once or being refused, each saying what it is waiting for; and the watchdog leaves the apps alone while an update or backup is working on them.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• The line atop Settings shows whole: with an app stopped (or away from home, or an update waiting), Settings' heading bar no longer slides over the line above it, so Mealie: Stopped and its Open Status show in full and can be clicked, at any width.
  • Settings in a narrow window with big text: a person's row in People keeps their name in words, its buttons wrapping under it rather than running past the edge, and This Mac's values (the container runtime, the folder, the version) wrap between words rather than a letter a line.
  • The tray icon is yours alone: on a computer with other accounts, another account can no longer quit your Homelab icon in the menu bar or tray, or keep it from starting.
  • A page sent to your phone is checked twice: Send to my phone's page goes on only if that phone may still open it as it arrives, so one made a wall screen, given to a household member or with Finances taken away a moment after the send gets nothing.
  • Release notes are plain text: homelab updates notes takes out control characters from what a project's releases say, so a release can't rewrite your terminal or set its title, and keeps a release's link only when it is on GitHub.
  • A household member's own Finances are backed up: the money a member keeps on their own phone is now copied each night with the household's records, so the encrypted off-site backup has it too. Before, it was in no backup.
  • Card prices stay with TCGdex: Update prices no longer follows a redirect to another site, so a card's name is only ever sent to TCGdex, and its pictures only come from TCGdex.
  • Your synced Files are backed up: the folders Syncthing keeps in step between your devices now have a nightly encrypted backup of their own (Homelab Files), so a file deleted by mistake on one device can come back. Before, they were in no backup. A homelab set up earlier gets the new job by itself the next night.
  • The books cleanup can't get stuck on a bad file: reading a cover or writing a book's details now has a time limit, so one damaged download can't hold up Tidy Up.
  • Frigate's and Firefly III's secrets stay off the process list: Frigate's broker password and Firefly III's nightly-jobs token no longer appear, even for a moment, in the list of running programs other accounts on the computer can see.
  • Lyrics go in as plain text: Add lyrics now takes out stray control characters from what the lyrics site sends, and leaves out lyrics far longer than any song's.
  • A stuck download can't hold up Tidy Up: filing new music gives beets an hour per step; a download that would keep it busy for good is stopped and said.
  • Tidy Up's notes survive two jobs at once: a film scan and Collect saving at the same moment can no longer leave Tidy Up's note of what Tdarr is shrinking half-written and forgotten.
  • A zip that won't fit isn't unpacked: Tidy Up's Inbox first checks how much a downloaded zip unpacks to, and leaves it alone, saying why, if it would leave the drive with less than 1 GB free.
  • Moving the homelab leaves Tidy Up's lists behind: a move file no longer carries what Tidy Up put in the old computer's Trash, filed there today, or found waiting in its Downloads; on the new computer they named files that aren't there.
  • Tidy Up reads only so much of an answer: a reply from the lyrics site, MusicBrainz, or an app at home that never ends no longer takes Tidy Up's memory; past a sensible size the job says so and goes on.
  • Needs a look names only downloads: It's a film…, It's an episode… and picking an album act only on something in a Downloads folder Tidy Up watches, so a changed list can't have them move a video or songs from anywhere else into your library.
  • Tidy Up's keys stay with their own app: when Jellyfin, Tdarr, Plex, Audiobookshelf or Navidrome (or whatever answers at its address) sends Tidy Up on to another address, the app's key no longer goes along.
  • A download replaces only its own album: when new music replaces an album already in your library, Tidy Up now takes out of beets only the album with exactly those names, not every album whose names contain them, and a download's odd tags can't make it take out all of them.
  • The Inbox's Undo moves only what it filed: Undo under What I did today takes back only files in a library, and puts them only into a Downloads folder Tidy Up watches, so a changed record of what was filed can't have it move any other file, or put one anywhere else.
  • Undo in Tidy Up puts back only into its own folders: a thing goes back only into a library, a Downloads folder Tidy Up watches, or its reports folder, so a changed list of what went to the Trash can't have Undo put a file anywhere else in your account. Anything else stays in the Trash, and Undo says so.
  • A ticker stays a ticker: adding an investment, following a ticker in the Watchlist, and looking up a price now refuse a ticker or source of . or .., which could reach another of Ghostfolio's admin addresses, and a followed ticker's name is kept short.
  • A picture for an account can't be too large to show: Finances keeps a picture of your own only when it is at most 1,024 pixels on a side (the screen makes each 96), so one can't be small in the file but too large for a phone to open.
  • A git checkout updates only to checked releases: homelab upgrade moves the homelab folder only to a release whose files the project's own release workflow is shown to have built, from the very commit the release's tag points at, as the app's own update is checked. Changes on main newer than the latest release come with the next one.
  • Passwords, sign-in and bans wait a few days for new releases: the nightly update installs a new Vaultwarden, Pocket ID or CrowdSec only once it has been out 3 days, so a release pulled for a fault in its first days never arrives. homelab update <app> still takes it at once.
  • Back goes back to the tab you were on: in Finances and Tidy Up, Back (⌘[, the mouse's back button, a two-finger swipe) now steps back through the tabs you opened, Recurring to Spending to the Dashboard, before it leaves for the screen you came from. It went straight to Status.
  • Your own logos on the iPhone and iPad: a picture you set for an account, a payment or a payee on the computer (one you picked, or the real logo got from its website) now shows in the Homelab app too, where it showed a letter or an icon.
  • A username is a username: homelab person add --username takes small letters, digits and . - _ only, so a person's own folder is always theirs.
  • A phone changes only everyday settings: a phone allowed to make changes can change the computer's clock, quiet hours, alerts, update times and Tidy Up's choices, but no longer an app's folders, image, version or sign-in, which change on the computer.
  • The Mac app's updates are checked as Windows' and Linux's are: before the app on a Mac takes an update, it checks the download was built by this project's own release workflow, as on the other systems.
  • Tailscale's sign-in opens only a web page: the link Tailscale gives for signing in is opened only when it is an https address, never a file or a program.
  • Kopia's page can't be used by another website: Kopia now checks each request comes from its own page, so a site you visit while signed in to Kopia can't send it commands such as deleting snapshots. The homelab signs in to it the same way.
  • Kopia's password stays out of the process list: Kopia's server now reads its password from its settings instead of its command line, which any account on a Linux computer could see.
  • Get the real logo asks only real websites: Finances' logo lookup now also refuses the addresses the homelab's own networks use, and other ranges that are never a company's website, even when a site sends it there.
  • A device at home can't pick the address Home Assistant sees: Home Assistant now trusts only the proxy and Tailscale to say who a visitor is, so each password guess at its own port counts against the guesser. The homelab updates the starter configuration.yaml for you before Home Assistant next starts; anything you added there yourself stays. Home Assistant now finds Frigate, but no other app, by name inside Docker: for another app, use its https address.
  • Finances: category names no longer break mid-word ("Utilitie / s") on Where it goes and Spent this month when the window is a medium width: a narrow card puts its ring above the names.
  • Setup says what can wait: with every step done but one that can wait, the count reads 18 of 18 done · 1 can wait, not just 18 of 18 done under Finish setting up.
  • An impossible amount can't empty your transactions: a bank file (or a phone) with an amount of a trillion or more is now refused with a plain message. Before, one such number could save an empty list over every transaction.
  • Tidy Up says which day a job started: a job that started before midnight (the agent's overnight Collect, say) now says Started yesterday at 3:04 AM, not just Started at 3:04 AM, which read as this morning; and a job that stopped part-way says when it started too.
  • Typing in a form as it opens stays where you typed: a click into a field (Category, say) the moment a form opened could have its first letters land at the end of the first field (Paid to), because the form put the cursor there a moment later. Now it leaves the cursor alone once it's in one of the form's fields.
  • A card's file can't slip into checking unnoticed: an American Express file imported with the sheet left on checking came in as money in: every charge a deposit, no categories guessed (Shopping and Gaming are for money out), and a bill matched to money you're owed. The sheet now says so whenever most rows would come in as money in: on a card (or an American Express account not set up as a card) with Read them as charges, and on another account with Bring it into your American Express card (or your only card), in one tap. Before Bring in, a line says how many rows go out and come in, and how much.
  • Cleaner American Express names, again: a shop whose town runs into its store number in a file Amex spaced into columns (PET SUPERMARKET #100SUNRISE FL) is the shop alone, Amex's AMAZON MARKEPLACE is Amazon, and ANTHROPIC CLAUDE (cut short, with San Francisco run into it) is Claude.
  • Tidy Up keeps following a job it didn't start: one failed look at a job the agent or a Terminal was running made Tidy Up stop following it, so its card and the waiting buttons stayed until something else redrew the screen. It now looks again a few seconds later.
  • Books' Recently done says when you looked them over: after Look over your books, Recently done on Books stayed empty. It now says Books looked over, with how many it read and how many could look tidier (or nothing to change).
  • Tidy Up carries on the job that stopped, not another: a Tidy lyrics that stopped part-way came back as Adding lyrics and its Carry on asked LRCLIB about every song, and a Set up Tdarr or Check Downloads carried on as a preview that changed nothing, so its stopped part-way card never went away. A job now keeps how it was run, and Carry on runs it that way. One that stopped before this update, where that can't be told, says to start it again from Music.
  • A mortgage split with someone else falls as its papers say: with only your half of the payment in the plan, Net worth's paycheck-by-paycheck table had the mortgage falling by that half a month, while the Loans card used the papers' whole payment. A loan read from its papers now owes, after each payment day, what the papers say, on both. Checking still pays only your half.
  • Nextcloud and Firefly III see who you really are: they used to believe any device at home that claimed, in a header, to be someone else, once Settings let the apps listen on the home network. Now they believe only the proxy and Tailscale, from a small network of their own.
  • Paperless waits for its first account before going on the internet: a fresh Paperless lets whoever signs up first become its admin, so with a domain a stranger could have claimed it before you made your account. It now stays home only until its account exists, as Immich, Navidrome and the other public apps already did.
  • Dozzle and beets stay on this computer: the two apps without a sign-in of their own no longer follow Settings › Apps listen on to the home network.
  • Tdarr's setup in plain words: when Tdarr isn't installed, setting it up for Tidy Up's libraries now says to install it from Choose apps › Tdarr, as the app calls that screen, instead of the old Choose stacks (Media automation).
  • What you own and owe in a small window: at the largest text sizes, an account's change since the start (↓ $5.60k) squeezed its name to a word a line (Toyot / a / Finan / cial). In a narrow list the change now steps aside, as the Since card above sums it up.
  • Tidy Up's Which film? and Which show?: typing in two boxes quickly could wipe what was in the first, leaving File it greyed out. Each box now keeps what the others hold.
  • Tidy Up's questions start empty at once: opening Which film? or Which show? cleared its boxes a moment after it appeared, so anything typed in that moment (on a busy computer, a word or two) was wiped and File it stayed greyed out. Each question now starts empty as it's drawn.
  • Shares in parts of one: a holding added with 11.038 shares went into Ghostfolio as 11,038, read as a thousands mark, so a share showed as worth $0.60. Shares now take as many decimals as you type, and the form says what each comes to (11.038 shares at $602.77 each) before it goes. A holding Ghostfolio has no prices for yet no longer shows You paid $0.00 and what you paid as its worth: what you paid is read from its buys and sales, its worth is today's price Ghostfolio looks up (its details say so), and Ghostfolio is asked to gather the symbol's prices, also as soon as a holding is added.
  • An American Express file comes in the right way round: Amex lists charges as plus amounts, so a card's file imported into Finances showed every charge as money in. A card's file whose rows are mostly plus amounts is now read as charges (its minus amounts as payments to it), says so, and Charges are plus amounts in this file turns it off or on.
  • Finances on a phone: budgets keep their bars wide beside the day's allowance, and a twelve-month chart labels every other month (this one always) so the names don't run together.
  • A category's trend in its own colour: Reports' month by month for a category draws its bars in that category's colour, as everywhere else, not the red of all spending.
  • Cards and Spending told apart: on the Dashboard's Where it goes and the money flow, Cards had Spending's purple and Loans the Car's yellow; each now has a colour of its own.
  • A new plan reads right: with nothing owed, Net worth says Nothing owed rather than You owe $0.00 in orange; A typical month with no paychecks yet says so, without dangling dots; with no cushion set, the calendar's key isn't drawn as one; and the checking chart's key lists only the marks it has.
  • Finances' small words: Transactions' This month now says Kept over what the month kept, not just how many transactions it was, and Loans' Pay more no longer says about $0.00 a month before an amount is typed.
  • On Windows, a note being saved no longer reads as missing: for an instant while one part of the app replaced a note (such as when the last backup ran), Windows could say the file wasn't there, which reads as no backup yet. A read now waits while a save of that note is under way.
  • On Windows, a backup no longer starts by mistake: the agent's note of the last backup could read as missing for an instant while another part of the app saved it, which made a backup start at once. It now waits that instant and reads it again.
  • Transactions on the iPhone: the page opens on checking, not on an account with no transactions; homes, cars and collectibles are left out of the account cards, and each small card shows its logo, balance and whole name. "No Transactions" now sits under the heading instead of over it, with Show All Accounts.
  • A Chase checking account's CSV now comes in with each payee from its Description, not as CREDIT or DEBIT. Importing the same file again gives rows already brought in as CREDIT or DEBIT their payees, keeping any category you gave them, rather than adding them twice. A bank's file whose payee column only says which way the money went has its names read from another column, and the import says so when no payee is a name.
  • No surprise backup after a power cut: the background agent's note of when it last backed up was rewritten in place, so one cut off half-written read as no backup yet, and a backup started at once. It is now replaced whole, as are the job logs it trims, and on Windows a read at the very moment it's saved waits for it rather than reading as no note.
  • Your logs are yours alone: the jobs' logs and crash notes in scripts/logs could be read by another account on the same computer. The folder is now this account's only, an older one included, and new logs are too.
  • The weekly summary and Finances' reminders come once: the note that one went out was rewritten in place and its errors dropped, so a note cut off or not saved sent the message again the next night without a word. It is now replaced whole, and one that can't be saved says so in the nightly log.
  • Your own apps, added at once, are all kept: two of your own apps added at the same moment (from the app and from Terminal) could each write over the other, and one was lost. Each add now waits for the one before it, on a port of its own.
  • Settings the apps read are never caught half-written: the Homepage dashboard's list of apps, each app's sign-in settings, and the note that says which version of the homelab folder you have were rewritten in place, so one read at that moment (by Homepage, by an app starting, or by the next upgrade) could find half a file. Each is now replaced whole.
  • Tidy Up signs in to a new Tdarr by itself: Tdarr 3 takes no sign-up, so on a new Tdarr Tidy Up couldn't make its account and every Shrink stopped at Tdarr asks for a sign-in. The homelab now gives Tdarr a key of its own when it's installed (and gives one to a Tdarr installed before, restarting it once), and Tidy Up signs in with it.
  • Backup alerts read as sentences: Duplicati's warnings and errors showed in Recent alerts as a wall of encoded text (message=Duplicati%20Backup%20report…), running under its tag. They now say which backup and how it ended (The backup of Homelab AppData finished with warnings), with what went wrong, at most three lines. Long alerts wrap.
  • Tidy lyrics works, and in minutes: setting apart two languages on one line waited on LRCLIB for every song first, and a song LRCLIB didn't answer for (slow, blocked, or busy) was skipped and kept them. With thousands of songs that took hours, waited for power, and left most of them as they were. Tidy lyrics now sets every song right on this computer, asking LRCLIB nothing, on battery too, and Overview offers it beside Add lyrics. Adding lyrics sets each song right first too.
  • Shrink really hands films to Tdarr: Tidy Up said Tdarr has 4 videos in its queue, but Tdarr 3 read none of them, so its page showed nothing and the films waited forever. They're now handed the way Tdarr takes them, and Tidy Up says only what Tdarr has recorded. Films stuck from before are handed again within minutes, on their own.
  • Saves on Windows wait for a reader instead of failing: on Windows a settings file or record can't be replaced while another part of the homelab is reading it, and a save gave up after a fifth of a second. It now keeps trying, in the gaps, for up to two seconds.
  • Small notes the app reads are never caught half-written: when the last restore test passed, the home address from domain setup, and the last time Docker had to be asked the slow way were rewritten in place, so the app reading one at that moment could see nothing there and ask for a restore test again. Each is now replaced whole.
  • Rebuilding from a backup never leaves half a settings file: homelab rebuild rewrote .env in place, so the agent or the app reading it at that moment could find it empty and run without its settings. It's replaced whole now, as every other save of it is.
  • A hung app is restarted once, not twice: when two of the watchdog's checks ran at once (the regular one and the one after the computer wakes), one could lose the other's note of an app it had just restarted, and that app could be restarted again within the 6 hours it waits. Each check now adds to the note instead of writing over it.
  • A job cut off by a restart no longer holds up the others for 12 hours: each change (an update, a backup, a phone's Restart) waits its turn behind the jobs ahead of it. A job that a restart stopped left its place, and once another program had its process ID, everything waited behind it for 12 hours. Now it's cleared as soon as it's looked at, as Tidy Up's own lock is.
  • A phone you remove stays removed: when the phones' server noted a phone's visit at the moment you removed that phone, or took away Can make changes or Finances, on the computer, it could save the phone back as it was, and its link worked again. Every change to the phones' list now waits for the one before it.
  • Going back after an upgrade works even if the last one was cut off: the copy of your folder kept before each upgrade was rewritten in place, so an upgrade stopped part-way (a power cut, the app quitting) could leave going back with half a copy. It is now replaced whole, as are the app's list of releases, the storage reading, and Tidy Up's note of the ffmpeg it fetched.
  • Apps come back after a quit cut short: Quit notes every app it stops before it stops them, so they all start again later. A quit cut off while writing that note could leave it unreadable, and then nothing started them. The note is now replaced whole.
  • Tidy Up's music scripts run from Terminal recover from a Python upgrade too: music_tidy.py run by hand makes beets' setup again when the Python it was made with is gone, instead of stopping with No such file or directory. Your music library and its database stay as they are.
  • Finances saved from the computer and a phone at once are never lost: a save from each at the same moment could both go through, the second over the first, without the changed on another device message. One now waits for the other and is told. Tidy Up's record no longer fails to save when two of its jobs end together.
  • Tidy Up's notes read as text in a terminal: homelab media printed each of an engine's notes as a line of JSON ({"type": "info", "text": "Fixes planned"}); they read as the rest of its output again, and status --json still prints its object as it is.
  • Music jobs work again after a Python upgrade: when the Python that Tidy Up's beets setup (~/.music-cleanup/venv) was made with goes, through a Homebrew upgrade for example, every music scan, build, and lyrics run, and the inbox filing songs, failed with couldn't create …venv. Each run now removes a venv whose Python doesn't start, says so, and beets is installed again on that run, in about a minute.
  • Backups failing in the morning: when Backups couldn't be read, Status's overnight line asked for it again at once, over and over, keeping the computer busy and the page stuck. It now asks at most once a minute.
  • Tidy Up starts again after a job was cut off: a job stopped part way (the computer restarted or slept during the nightly sweep, or the app quit) could leave its lock behind under a number the computer later gave another program. Tidy Up then took the job for still running: the downloads, the nightly sweep, and the automatic jobs never ran, every job you started said another was moving files, and backups waited. A lock like that is now seen as left behind, and the next job takes over.
  • Tidy Up offers to set apart lyrics in two languages again: songs whose lyrics run a translation after a caret on each line (¡NUEVAYoL!^NEW YORK!) are put right by adding lyrics, but once every song had lyrics, Overview offered nothing, so they stayed as they were. Checking lyrics now counts them, Overview offers Tidy lyrics for them, and a check from before this asks to be run again.
  • Tidy Up's logs and crash notes no longer pile up: each Tidy Up job, its checks included, left a log that was never cleared, its background log grew without end, and the list of what went to the Trash kept every line forever. Job logs now go after 30 days, the background log is cut at 5 MB, what Undo can no longer reach leaves the Trash list, and crash notes go after 90 days.
  • Two jobs no longer save over each other's notes: the nightly update, the watchdog, and a rollback each keep a note of what every app ran before its update, and one could save over what another had just noted (a rollback, or when an app came up well); a Setup step ticked in the app as Setup opened elsewhere could come undone. Each now keeps the other's change, and these records, with the household's and the restart counts, are written whole, only for this account.
  • The watchdog's, the battery saver's, and the savings records are never half written: Status and the once-a-minute check could read one while it was being written and take it for empty, and two watchdog runs at once could save over each other. Each is now written whole, one writer at a time, and only this account can read it.
  • Pinning an app is never lost: pinning one app from the app and another from a phone at about the same time could keep only one pin. The pinned apps now live in a record of their own that each change updates in turn, and they move there by themselves after the upgrade, still in the order you pinned them.
  • Turning an app's alerts off is never lost: Tell me if it stops, switched from the app and a phone at about the same time, could keep only one of the two, since both rewrote the same line of the settings file. The list now lives in a record of its own that each change updates in turn, and it moves there by itself after the upgrade, with every app you had turned off still off.
  • Downloads wait out a busy registry: when GitHub's or LinuxServer's image registry asked to space out downloads, installing several apps at once gave up after under a minute with the image registry is spacing out downloads, and a rebuild from the backups stopped at its first step. Downloads now wait and try again for a few minutes, and the rebuild downloads Duplicati before it starts it.
  • A genre count that finds nothing says why: counting your films' or shows' genres with nothing to read them from said 0 films in 0 genres, from nowhere yet, and the Genres card went back to its first question as if nothing had run. It now says why (Jellyfin's API key isn't set, with where to make one, and no .nfo files beside them), and the card says what it counted, with Count again and Add Jellyfin's API key, which opens Settings at that key on Jellyfin's page. Couldn't tell Jellyfin and Couldn't tell Navidrome say where their login goes too.
  • An update installed by hand counts: after an update didn't go in place and you installed a newer release by hand, the app still said the update didn't install, and Try again stopped with no update is ready. A build as new as the one it was updating to, or newer, now counts as updated, and Try again with nothing newer simply closes the line.
  • Tidy Up signs in to Tdarr: Tdarr now asks for an account, and Set up Tdarr stopped with answered 401. Tidy Up makes Tdarr's first account itself when it has none (its password kept in Settings › Tidy Up), or signs in with the one you made, from Settings › Tidy Up (Tdarr user and password); without one, it says where the login goes. And Tdarr now actually shrinks what it's handed: a new Tdarr's node has no worker, so everything sat in its queue. Set up Tdarr, Shrink, and Collect give a node with none one worker (on the graphics card when there is one), which you can raise on Tdarr's page. When Tdarr isn't running, Collect and Shrink say so (start it from Status) instead of Something unexpected went wrong: … Connection refused.
  • Tidy Up says why a job stopped: when a scan couldn't start (ffmpeg not installed, say), it said only exit status 1, with the reason hidden under Show details. It now says the reason itself, the line is red in the details, and the fix names only your system's way to install ffmpeg (brew install ffmpeg on a Mac).
  • Tidy Up on Windows pauses the apps first: with Docker Desktop, Navidrome and Calibre-Web kept running while your music or books moved, because Docker names M:\music another way. They're paused now, as on a Mac. And music is tidied with beets on this machine, since beets' container can't open Windows folders.
  • Tidy Up finds Calibre and ffmpeg on a Steam Deck: Calibre from Discover (a Flatpak) or installed in your home folder, and ffmpeg from Homebrew or Nix, said Not installed. They're found now, and the books are tidied with them.
  • Tidy Up never replaces on a guess: a download whose library copy couldn't be read replaced it unchecked, and another cut of a film (an extended one) was put in the Trash as a duplicate. Both are now left where they are for you to look at, and a second version kept on purpose (Heat (1995) - Director's Cut) is never counted as a duplicate. The nightly sweep keeps a film's Subs folder and its subtitles in other capitals, and a Firefox download still being written beside its empty placeholder waits.
  • Tidy Up's names work on every drive: a film or show already in the library with its accent written the Mac way (Amélie copied from a Mac) got a second folder beside it on Linux and Windows; a long Chinese or Japanese title could be too long for a Mac's or Linux's drive, which count bytes; a title like CON.Air couldn't be made on Windows; and renaming heat to Heat on a Mac's or Windows' drive stopped with already exists. Names are now written one way, cut to fit in bytes, and kept clear of Windows' device names.
  • Tidy Up finds a library set through a link: with a library's folder written as a link (a Media folder pointing at the drive) or a Windows short name, Jellyfin and Tdarr were told about the wrong path and a film Tdarr had shrunk could not be collected. Paths are now compared as they really are.
  • Tidy Up never deletes outright on a USB stick or network drive (Windows): those drives keep no Recycle Bin, so what Tidy Up threw away there was gone for good. It now goes to a hidden .tidy-trash folder on the same drive, a folder a day, to restore from or empty yourself.
  • Tidy Up's cards have room again: each library's card, the books' card, and a running job's card had their words and buttons pressed against the card's edge, and the row of numbers on Overview, Movies, TV, and Lyrics touched the cards under it. They now sit inside the card with the same margin as Status's, with a gap under the numbers.
  • A finished install can be closed: on Choose stacks, the bar, each app's row, the details, and Ready to open stayed beside the plan until the next install. Close under Ready to open now puts them away.
  • An app update that did not go in place, on a Mac or Linux: when the app was still open a minute after the update asked it to quit, the new build was put in place under it anyway, so opening it only brought the old one back, and the app said the update did not install without saying why. Now it asks the app to stop, as on Windows, and puts the update in place; one that still will not stop is left as it was, and the line says so. That line is red, as a failure, with Try again and Download it (the newest release), not only words saying to.
  • The update line on Settings is whole again: Settings' header, which blurs what scrolls under it, also covered the lower half of Homelab Wizard … is ready and its buttons on a Mac (and in the Windows and Linux app). It now sits below the line.
  • An app you stop stays stopped, even at the same moment as another: stopping an app from a phone while the computer was starting another again at its time could be forgotten, and the watchdog then started the app you had just stopped. The list of apps stopped on purpose is now changed one at a time, and never read half-written.
  • Undo in Tidy Up puts back only what is in the Trash: a homelab moved in from someone else's file could have Undo put one of its files anywhere in your account, among the programs that start when you sign in included. Now Undo takes things only out of the Trash, where Tidy Up put them.
  • Time-synced lyrics for every song that has them: some songs (NUEVAYoL, for one) showed one still block of words with a translation after a caret on each line (¡NUEVAYoL!^NEW YORK!) instead of lyrics that scroll. LRCLIB's record for the album had plain lyrics only, and Tidy Up took them without looking for the time-synced ones another record has; it now looks. A translation after each line's caret now gets a line of its own under the original, at the same moment, so both languages show as the song plays, and a song with a .lrc or .txt file beside it gets its lyrics there, since Navidrome reads that file before the song's own. Songs it gave up on are asked about again on the next run.
  • Tdarr gets every film: Shrink handed Tdarr only the films the last scan had found, so a film Radarr filed since then was never shrunk. It reads the new ones first now. A film Tdarr has no record of a while after it was handed (Tdarr was restarting, say) is handed again, and after three tries it's named rather than waiting forever; a new download that was waiting for Tdarr is filed as it is then, so it doesn't stay hidden. A films library Tdarr's container can't open is named, with the folder it can, instead of being handed to Tdarr for nothing, and Shrink says when Tdarr's Tidy Up library is gone (run Set up Tdarr again).
  • Finances, smaller things: on Transactions, a filter whose last transaction you deleted or changed showed Every category (or account, tag, month) while the list stayed empty; it now lets go. A form's Save that couldn't go through said why, rather than Cancel again to drop it when you had pressed Cancel first. The heading's update them with Edit now names the button: Update balances.
  • A phone never sees an app's own password in its log: qBittorrent writes its temporary admin password to its log, and any paired phone, even one that only looks, could read it there, as could the alert about an app that keeps restarting. Passwords, keys, and tokens an app prints are now taken out of what a phone, an alert, or a report gets; the app on the computer still shows the whole log.
  • An app goes on the internet only once it has its first account: with a domain, installing Immich, Audiobookshelf, Komga, Navidrome, or Calibre-Web put it on the internet at once, where the first person to open it would have made its admin account (or signed in to Calibre-Web as admin/admin123). Each now stays at home until it has one; the domain plan says so, and Set up the domain puts it online after.
  • Hide amounts covers the alerts too: with amounts hidden, the nightly Finances reminders and the weekly summary still showed them on the phone's lock screen (Due tomorrow: Mortgage $1,845.00). They now say $••• there too.
  • The Beszel agent stays on the version you chose: it can control Docker, and it updated itself every night from its newest image, as the socket proxy once did. It is now pinned (BESZEL_AGENT_VERSION) and updated by hand after reading its notes.
  • A removed phone stops getting Status at once: a phone removed in Settings › Phones could no longer ask for anything, but one that had Status open kept receiving each change for as long as it stayed connected. It is now cut off within seconds.
  • A Mac update comes only from whoever signed your app: the app checked that an update downloaded whole, but not who made it. On a Mac, an update signed by anyone but the team that signed the app you have is now refused, and the app says so.
  • Apps can no longer read each other's passwords through Docker: the read-only view of Docker that Dozzle, Homarr, and Homepage use also answered any app asking for another app's settings, passwords included. Only those three reach it now.
  • A wall screen stays a wall screen: a screen paired in kiosk mode can no longer be given changes or Finances (beyond the money card) later in Settings › Phones, since anyone walking past could use them.
  • A phone on your Wi-Fi can't pretend it used the secure link: pairing through your domain's link now checks with the proxy itself whether the phone really came over https, so someone who catches a pairing code on the Wi-Fi gets a phone that only looks. Run Set up the domain once more to turn it on; the doctor reminds you.
  • Tidy Up installs exactly the music tools it was tested with: the one-time setup for music on this computer took the newest beets and its helpers from the internet, unchecked. It now installs the versions pinned for your Python, each checked against a fingerprint, and needs Python 3.10 or newer (3.10 to 3.14); a setup made before is brought to them once.
  • Tidy lyrics runs: Overview's and Music's Tidy lyrics stopped at once with Tidy Up doesn't run a job with "--tidy"; it now sets the songs' lyrics right.

Apps you stop stay stopped, money hides at a keypress, and a right-click on any app. Stop an app for good or for a while and nothing starts it behind your back; ⌘⇧H hides every amount, on your phones too, and a wall screen can show the next payday and bills; a right-click on an app on Status offers everything its page does. From this version each release is the next number (0.17.0, 0.17.1, … 0.17.10, then 0.18.0).

docs.title: New
docs.text:
• Right-click an app on Status: its row's own menu opens where you click, with Open, Open on a phone, Copy address, Start or Restart, Stop (it asks twice), Stop for a while, Logs, Back up now, and Tell me if it stops, without opening its page. Shift+F10 or the menu key opens it from the keyboard, and a right-click on a group's heading opens that group's menu.
  • The money card on a wall screen: pick Money card only beside a paired screen in Settings › Phones, and its Status shows the next payday and who is paid, what checking holds once its bills are paid, and the next 3 bills, with their logos. The screen is sent only those few things, never your plan, and no amount at all while Finances hides them. A screen still pairs without Finances, as before.
  • Finances, hide amounts: ⌘⇧H (Ctrl+Shift+H on Windows and Linux), View › Hide Amounts, or the eye on Finances and beside the sidebar's Accounts writes every amount as $•••, the sidebar's balances and the charts included, for a screenshot or a screen others can see. It is kept with your finances, so your phones hide them too, and it stays until you show them again. The forms you type in and the exports keep the numbers.
  • Stopped means stopped, and Stop for a while: an app you stop from its group's menu or its page stays stopped: Start the N stopped, the watchdog, the battery saver, and apps waiting for a drive all leave it, and its row says Stopped by you with Start beside it. Stop for a while (on its page, or a group's menu for the whole group) stops it for an hour, until 9 PM tonight, or until 8 AM tomorrow, its row says until when, and it starts again by itself within a minute of then. Starting the homelab (at login too) and Fix it leave such an app stopped, with the apps that need it, and Stop on an app's page now asks for a second click, as a group's does. The record is kept in the homelab's data folder, so it survives a restart and is backed up.
  • Take the homelab off this machine, from the app: Settings › This machine has it, with what else goes ticked: the apps' data, the homelab folder, the backups on this machine, Homelab Wizard itself, and everything else in the container runtime. Review what goes… shows the homelab's own plan, and nothing happens until uninstall (or delete everything) is typed. homelab uninstall has the same as --folder, --backups, --app, and --everything-else, on a Mac, Windows, and Linux. A backup folder in a cloud drive always stays, as deleting it would delete it on every machine signed in to the drive, and with the data gone the machine signs out of the tailnet, so it leaves Tailscale's admin console instead of keeping the homelab's name.
  • Finances, a money calendar: a Calendar view lays out each month: who is paid on which day in their colour, each bill and card payment with its logo, bank holidays, paydays moved before a weekend or holiday, and checking at the end of each day, marked when it falls under your cushion. Pick a day to see what moves and what checking holds after; the arrow keys move day by day. On a phone it is a list of the days something happens, week by week.
  • Finances, subscriptions together: Recurring › Subscriptions shows what they cost a month and a year, what renews in the next week and month, how many are paid yearly against monthly, and each one, dearest first, with its cost both ways and whether it is due today, tomorrow, in a few days, or was just paid. Each has a type (streaming, software, cloud and homelab, gaming, news, fitness, food, phone), suggested from its logo or name and yours to change, and the year's cost is split by type.
  • Finances, cards paid off with each paycheck: tick "I pay it off in full with each paycheck" on a card and type about how much goes on it between paychecks. Each payday into checking, whoever is paid, pays its whole balance, counted in checking after the bills and in what each paycheck leaves, and a typical month counts the card's spending once. A payment can also come "With each paycheck, whoever is paid".
  • Finances, your own logo: on any account or payment, "Use your own image" takes a picture file and shows it for that brand everywhere it appears (or for that name, with no brand). It is made small on your device and kept in the finances file, and Remove your image takes it out. Nothing is fetched from the internet.
  • The apps open at home with a VPN on: with a Cloudflare token, Set up the domain also points every app's name at this machine's address at home in Cloudflare's DNS (one record, *.your-domain, not proxied). Phones and computers at home then find the apps whatever DNS they use, Proton VPN's or the router's, without changing each device's DNS; the VPN app needs Allow LAN connections on. The tunnel's public apps keep their own records, and outside your home the address leads nowhere. When the router gives this machine a new address, the watchdog moves the name, and AdGuard's, within 15 minutes.
  • Jellyfin and Navidrome accounts for each person, and Reset password: with a Jellyfin API key and a Navidrome administrator's login in Settings (each with a Test), Add a person also makes their Jellyfin and Navidrome accounts, so Infuse, the TV apps and music apps such as Arpeggi sign in. One password for both is on their welcome page, with what to type in Infuse and a music app, and the homelab keeps it nowhere else. Reset password (Settings › People, or homelab person password <name>) gives them a new one on a fresh welcome page, with no PIN file or Terminal, and Remove turns those accounts off too. The welcome page no longer says there is no password to remember when there is.
  • beets, for a tidy music library: beets joins Navidrome and Feishin in the Music pick in Choose stacks (or ./homelab install beets). It matches music you add by hand against MusicBrainz, fixes the tags, adds covers and genres, and files each album as Artist/Album (Year) in the music folder, where Navidrome finds it at its next scan. Its library page is on this computer only, and its note shows how to import.
  • Finances, transactions: a Transactions view keeps what actually happened: money out, money in, or moved between your own accounts, each with its payee and logo, day, account, category, the planned payment it pays, and a note, newest first by day, with this month's money in and out. Kept in its own file beside the plan and backed up with it; on your phones too, view only where they may only look.
  • Finances, budgets: set how much a category may take a month or each paycheck, rolling over what is left if you like; Transactions shows each this month with what is left or how far over, a mark where an even pace would be by today, and a group's budget counting its own categories.
  • Finances, reports: a Reports view reads your transactions over this month, last month, three months, this year, or all: money in and out, spending by category with each group's own under it (refunds taken off), where the money went by payee, and money in against out month by month, each chart with its numbers for a screen reader.
  • Finances, import a bank's file: bring a CSV or an OFX/QFX statement from your bank's website into Transactions: it is read on your device, its columns guessed (and yours to change), US and European dates and amounts read, those already in skipped, and each payee given the category it had last. No bank connection, nothing sent anywhere.
  • Finances, recurring found: Recurring lists what your transactions show you pay on a rhythm (weekly, every two weeks, monthly, quarterly, or yearly) that isn't in the plan yet, as in "Hulu, $17.99 monthly since Jun 3", and adds one to the plan with a click.
  • Finances, tags: a transaction's tags show on its row; Transactions can show only one tag's, and Reports has a By tag card and a tag pick that narrows every report to it (what the road trip cost, say).
  • Finances, export: Reports' Export CSV saves the stretch's transactions (a tag's, when one is picked) for a spreadsheet, where you choose on the computer, shared or downloaded on a phone. A split is a row per part, and the file is readable only by you.
  • Finances, a category's trend: Reports draws a category's last twelve months, bar by bar, and says how this month so far compares with the same days a year before.
  • Finances, receipts: a transaction keeps its receipt: a photo (on a phone, straight from the camera), made smaller on the device, or a PDF, shown in its form and marked Receipt in the list. Receipts stay on the homelab beside the transactions and go into the nightly backup with them; one removed goes a day later. On a phone allowed only to look, a transaction with a receipt opens it under its row.
  • Finances, accounts in other currencies: an account can be kept in its own currency (a euro account, a UK pension), at a rate you type in; its balance and transactions stay in that currency, and Finances adds them up in yours. Nothing looks a rate up. Update balances asks for each in its own currency, Net worth shows both figures, and Pay › Paydays and money keeps the rates.
  • Finances, goals: Net worth has Goals: an emergency fund, a trip, a car, each with how much, by when, and a share of the accounts that count toward it (it never moves money). Each says what is left, what it needs a month and a paycheck to be there in time, and, from how the accounts grew lately, when it gets there at that pace, in amber when that is late. When together they need more a month than the plan puts by, Goals says by how much; What if tries another amount a paycheck, or another day, without changing anything.
  • Finances, loans: Net worth reads each loan to zero: what goes to it a month, the month it is paid off, and the interest still to pay at its rate, with the loan you pick charted to zero; in amber when the payment does not keep up with the interest or nothing goes to it, and listed apart once paid off. A card carrying a balance (a rate, and a payment into it) is read with them, and Pay more shows what an extra amount a paycheck does: to the loan you pick, and to all of them paid down the highest rate first or the smallest balance first.
  • Finances, money flow: Recurring draws a typical month as it flows: each person's pay in, and out to each kind of bill, what is saved, and what is left over (or what comes out of the accounts when a month takes more than comes in), with every amount listed under it.
  • Finances, a car's worth over time: give a car what it cost, when, and how well it holds its value, and Finances reads what it is worth today (most of the drop in its first year, less each year after, never below a tenth of its price) for net worth; a value you type in counts instead, and falls from that day.
  • Finances, financial independence: Net worth estimates what would be enough to live on (a year's spending over the share drawn a year, 4% to start), what the investment and retirement accounts hold toward it, and the month it gets there at what you put by and growth after rising prices (5% to start), with two points either way. It says it is an estimate, not advice, and both assumptions are yours to change.
  • Finances, what your homelab does now: Recurring lists the payments an app running on the homelab does the job of ("Jellyfin is running: Netflix still costs $185.88 a year"); Cancelled it takes one out of the plan and keeps it, and what those cancelled because of the homelab come to a year shows under them.
  • Finances, set aside for bills that come less often: Pay lists the bills that come every three months or once a year, what each costs a year and needs from each paycheck to be there when it comes, and their total, with a button that adds a payment into savings for it with each paycheck (or brings it up to date when the bills change).
  • Finances, reminders: the homelab's ntfy tells you about a bill or card due tomorrow, three days before a paycheck that will leave checking under your cushion, a week before a yearly payment renews, and each week the balances go without an update; each can be turned off in Pay › Paydays and money. The weekly summary ends with Finances too: what the next paycheck leaves, the biggest bills before it, and net worth with its change since last week.
  • Finances, a calendar feed: Pay › Paydays and money makes a link your phone's calendar can subscribe to, with the paydays and bills ahead (and their amounts, if you like). It works over Tailscale or the homelab's own domain, never the home Wi-Fi; a new link, or Turn it off, stops the old one at once.
  • Finances, payees as you'd write them: a bank's wording ("NETFLIX.COM", "AMZN MKTP US*2K4", "SQ *BLUE BOTTLE", "POS DEBIT SHELL OIL 57444 SAN JOSE CA") comes in from a bank's file as Netflix, Amazon, Blue Bottle, and Shell, with their logos and the category each had last; the bank's own wording is kept in the note. Transactions already kept as the bank wrote them show their logos too.
  • Finances, a payee's logo: Change logo on a transaction picks one (or None) for its payee: every transaction to it shows it, and the next one, typed or brought in from a bank's file, takes it too.
  • Finances, a mark for every payee: a payee with no brand's logo and no category's icon gets a mark of its own, its initials on a colour its name picks (Blue Bottle is the same BB every time), in Transactions, Reports, and a bank file's preview, where a plain letter was.
  • Finances, 39 more logos: everyday chains show theirs, from a bank's wording too: Google, IKEA, Taco Bell, Burger King, H&M, Uniqlo, Lidl, Booking.com, Hotels.com, Shopify, and Waze as their marks, and Trader Joe's, Whole Foods, Chick-fil-A, Dunkin', Subway, Wendy's, Publix, Aldi, 7-Eleven, Domino's, Pizza Hut, Safeway, Panera, Dollar General, Gap, Old Navy, Nordstrom, Sephora, Petco, PetSmart, GameStop, Barnes & Noble, Wayfair, Dollar Tree, JetBlue, Tesco, Zara, and KFC as initials on their own colours.
  • Finances, balances from Firefly III: Update balances has From Firefly III: on a click it reads the asset accounts' balances from Firefly III on this machine (with the importer's token), fills each matching account's box so the difference shows, and says which it could not match. Nothing changes until you Save.
  • Finances, subscriptions from Wallos: while Wallos runs, Recurring has From Wallos: on a click it reads Wallos's subscriptions on this machine (with its API key, WALLOS_API_KEY) and lists those not in the plan yet, each with its logo, rhythm, next day, and type, to add one by one or all at once. Ones already in the plan, turned off, or on a rhythm Finances doesn't keep are named, not added, and Wallos isn't changed.
  • Finances, balances from Ghostfolio: while Ghostfolio runs, Update balances has From Ghostfolio: on a click it signs in on this machine with your security token (GHOSTFOLIO_SECURITY_TOKEN), reads what each account is worth, and fills the boxes of the accounts with the same name and currency, for you to check and save. From Firefly III now shows only while Firefly III runs, and neither shows on a phone.

docs.title: Improved
docs.text:
