and, in a job of its own (REALDOCKER_REBUILD=1), a wiped homelab rebuilt from Duplicati's backups alone. .github/workflows/nightly.yml runs it every night and on pull requests that change the catalog; each new app joins its apps table internal/compose Reads compose files, ports, volumes, and x-homelab metadata internal/catalog Apps across every compose file, categories, bundles, validation internal/selector, detect, ports, install Choosing apps, finding running containers, free ports, install plans internal/docker, dockerapi, envfile The engine (Docker's API over its socket, or the named pipe on Windows, with the docker CLI behind it; commands run in containers) and .env internal/npm, domain, crowdsec Nginx Proxy Manager API, AdGuard, Cloudflare, tunnel ingress, the proxy's CrowdSec bouncer internal/backup, health, notify, schedule Jobs: dumps and archives, the backup overview, checks, ntfy, launchd, systemd, and Task Scheduler internal/duplicati Duplicati's API: jobs' last runs, creating, running, and repairing jobs, default options, restores internal/finance The Finances screen's plan in data/finance.json, read forward paycheck by paycheck internal/digest, savings, updates The weekly summary, what the apps replace (and its history), pausing and holding the nightly updates internal/diskspace Free space on each disk the homelab writes to (statfs, or GetDiskFreeSpaceEx on Windows) internal/diskhealth Each drive's own health report (SMART) through smartctl internal/procattr Windows: commands started without a console of their own open no window internal/upgrade The homelab folder against GitHub: changes waiting, fast-forward pulls, the app's build against the folder internal/setup, settings, api, host The first-time checklist and Settings tests, .env as a form, status for the app, per-OS profiles internal/wiring, homepage, adopt, custom Connecting apps through their APIs, Homepage's list of apps, moving old containers in, your own apps internal/docs Generated blocks in the notes, version and link checks internal/ui Terminal output and prompts The rest of internal/ Maintainer Guide › Code layout lists every package app/ The desktop app (its own module): app.go binds the engine to the frontend in web/dist (shared with homelab serve, as is internal/core); tray/ and cmd/homelab-tray are the menu bar item; per-platform files (menu_darwin.go, backdrop_windows.go, autostart_*.go, menuentry_linux.go) hold each OS's window, menus, and login items; packaging/ builds the Linux packages and the AppImage; preview/ runs the frontend in Chromium with a fake backend tools/media/ Tidy Up's engines (Python), with their tests in tools/media/tests and the music jobs' pinned versions in tools/media/requirements apple-client/ The native iPhone and iPad app (SwiftUI), a client of the phone companion mobile/finance, cmd/financewasm Finances' projection built for a phone (WebAssembly and an iOS framework)

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• make help lists the targets. make check passes before every commit: gofmt, go vet, bash -n, tests, and homelab validate.
  • make coverage passes: every package at or above its floor in coverage-floors.txt. Raise a package's floor when its tests raise its coverage; lower one only with the reason in the pull request.
  • make compose-config passes when a compose file changes (needs the docker compose CLI).
  • A new catalog app gets a row in test/realdocker's apps table (its page, and data put in and read back through its API where it has one), so the nightly run shows it starts and answers. Locally: go test -tags realdocker -v ./test/realdocker with Docker running (REALDOCKER_APPS=ntfy,vaultwarden for a few, REALDOCKER_KEEP=1 to leave them running).
  • A change to the desktop app passes make app-check (formatting, vet, and Windows builds of the app module for x64 and ARM64) and make frontend-check. The frontend is TypeScript in web/src; make frontend (or npm run build) compiles it with esbuild into web/dist/app.js, which is committed so the Go builds need no Node, and make frontend-check fails while it is out of date. Every screen is drawn by Preact components (.tsx, typed against web/types), one folder per screen or part (web/src/status, backups, choose, setup, settings, finances, page for an app's page, updates, job, sheets): a component file exports a mount…(element, props) function, and the screen's module in web/src/screens reads the data, runs the commands, and mounts the components with what they need; app.ts only chooses the screen and starts the app, and make frontend-check fails if it reaches 400 lines or anything calls document.createElement. Keep what someone types or toggles in the component (a typed setting, a click-again confirmation), and what a command changes as a prop (busy), never as an edit of the DOM Preact drew. Preact renders beside what it did not draw, so a mount point starts empty in index.html (or the component clears it first). It also type-checks web/src (npm ci fetches TypeScript and esbuild) against the Go side's types: web/types/backend.d.ts is generated from the methods the app binds and the events it sends, and after changing them, cd app && go test -run TestBindings -update . rewrites it (CI fails while it is out of date). It also fails on a Mac word ("menu bar", "Finder", "this Mac", OrbStack, ⌘) in a string outside a Mac branch (app/preview/words.mjs, like the Go side's TestNoMacOnlyWordsElsewhere). Its look follows each platform (html.os-mac, os-windows, os-linux in style.css); the preview stands in for one with platform in its mock. With Playwright and Chromium (npm ci, then npx playwright install chromium if no Chromium for Playwright 1.63 is installed): make app-smoke clicks through the buttons that run commands (Test a restore, Create the backup jobs, Get the update, Copy, …) against the fake backend in light and dark, then checks every screen as each system (Mac, Windows, GNOME, KDE, SteamOS), with and without more contrast, through axe (no serious or critical WCAG 2.1 AA finding), for a broken layout, and, as any system but the Mac, for a Mac word on the screen; CI runs it on every pull request and keeps the screenshots of a failure. SMOKE_ONLY=Setup runs the checks whose name has it, SMOKE_SHARD=2/3 runs every third one from the second (CI runs three at once in each theme's job, which together are every check), SMOKE_DEBUG=1 prints what axe measured. Text in the accent colour uses --link, and a filled button --primary and --primary-text: shades of the accent that read at 4.5:1 (a system blue is too light for small text on white). Colours are tokens only: a rule in style.css uses var(--…), and only a custom property in :root (or a theme's or platform's block) holds a colour itself (--shade-08 and --glow-08 are black and white at 8%); make frontend-check fails on a colour written in a rule, or in web/src outside the few files where a colour is data (app/preview/lint.mjs lists them with why). The shared blocks are in web/src/parts: Card and CardHead (a card and its heading row), Rows and Row (a list with a dot, a title, a line under it, what goes at the end, and when), Segmented (one choice of a few), Empty (what a list says with nothing in it), and Sheet (a panel over the screen for one task, as the command and log sheets are: the focus goes into it and back after, and Escape closes it through its own Close or Cancel); a screen uses them rather than writing their markup, and make frontend-check fails on a card heading, a card, a list of rows, a segmented control, an empty state, or a sheet written outside web/src/parts. make screenshots refreshes the pictures and fails if an element the page hid is displayed.
  • Anything that changes state previews first and acts only with --apply or a yes in a terminal.
  • Never print, log, or pass secrets on a command line. Read them from .env when needed.
  • A feature added or changed on any device changes its row in docs/Parity.md, the map of what each device can do; a new phone call is named there (TestParityNamesEveryPhoneCall fails until it is).
  • New behaviour gets a test. Network APIs are tested against httptest fakes; Docker against the fake CLI in cmd/homelab/main_test.go.
  • A change someone running the homelab would notice gets a line in CHANGELOG.md under Unreleased, in New, Improved, or Fixed. These are patch notes, read in the app before an update and on the release page: one line in plain words about what changed for you ("Opening a category on Status is instant"), not how. The pull request holds the detail.

docs.title: Releases
docs.text:
1. Move the Unreleased entries under a new version heading in CHANGELOG.md, with a bold one-line summary of the version under it, and add its compare link at the bottom.
  2. Set the version in VERSION and in the version: front matter of every note (./homelab validate checks they match).
  3. make check, commit, and tag v<version>.

docs.title: Security policy
docs.text: Homelab Wizard runs a household's passwords, photos, documents, and money on a computer at home, so a security hole matters. Thank you for taking the time to report one.

docs.title: Reporting a problem
docs.text:
Please don't open a public issue. Report it privately instead: on this repository's Security tab, choose Report a vulnerability. If you don't see that button, open an issue that says only that you have a security report to share (no details), and you'll be given a private way to send it.

A useful report says what can reach what: who the attacker is (someone on the internet, a phone that was paired, someone on the home Wi-Fi), what they send, and what they get. Steps or a test that shows it help most.

docs.title: What is supported
docs.text: The newest release only. The app updates itself, and the homelab files move forward with it (Update now, or ./homelab upgrade), so a fix reaches every install through the normal update.

docs.title: What has been looked at
docs.text: docs/Security.md has the security posture: what is reachable from where by default (nothing from the internet unless you choose it), how secrets and backups are kept, and every finding from the reviews of the app's own code, each with its fix and the test that shows it. CI runs govulncheck, gosec, and npm audit on every change.

docs.title: Homelab: native iPhone and iPad client
docs.text: A SwiftUI client for the Homelab Wizard phone companion (homelab serve, port 8099). This folder holds only source files; the scripts below make the Xcode project for you.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
You need a Mac with full Xcode (opened once, with your Apple ID added under Xcode › Settings › Apple Accounts; a free one is enough) and this repository cloned. Replace com.yourname with your own reverse-domain prefix and keep using the same one.

On the Mac itself, Homelab Wizard (the desktop app) is the way in: the native Mac version of this app was removed in November 2026.

The iPhone app. Plug the iPhone in, unlock it, tap Trust, and turn on Settings › Privacy & Security › Developer Mode once. Check the phone's address, then build, install, and pair (scan the QR code it shows from the app). With a free Apple ID, run it again within 7 days to keep the app working:

./apple-client/scripts/phone-address.sh

./apple-client/scripts/run-on-iphone.sh com.yourname

Paired devices: list them, or remove ones that were never used:

./apple-client/scripts/phones.sh tidy

The widget (optional): "All well" or how many apps need a look, on the iPhone's Home Screen. Build with it by putting HOMELAB_WIDGET=1 in front of the run script, then turn it on in the app under Settings › This Device. It needs an App Group, which a free Apple ID may not be able to sign; if the build stops there, run the script again without it.

Each script says what's wrong and what to do when something isn't ready. The rest of this README is the detail.

apple-client/
├── Shared/
│   ├── App/            HomelabClientApp.swift: @main, the Homelab menu (⌘R, ⌘L); AppCommands.swift: the App menu (⌥⌘S start, ⌥⌘R restart, ⌥⌘. stop, ⌥⌘L logs)
│   ├── Models/         Wire types (Status, AppStatus, EngineChange, …), AppAction, PairingCode, ServerEndpoint, DeviceCredential
│   ├── ViewModels/     AppCoordinator (lock state machine), PairingViewModel, DashboardViewModel, AppActionsViewModel
│   ├── Views/          AppCoordinatorView, PairingView, LockScreenView, DashboardView, AppDetailView, Theme (colours, pills, the app mark), Design (cards, logo circles, round buttons, wallet cards, the ring), Components/
│   ├── Resources/      PayeeLogos.json: the payee logos and their matching rules, made from the computer's by scripts/make-payee-logos.mjs
│   ├── Assets.xcassets AccentColor, so the system's own controls are violet too
│   ├── Services/       APIClient, LiveEventManager, SSEParser, APIError, JSONCoding
│   └── Security/       KeychainManager, BiometricAuthManager, SecureLog
├── Tests/              Swift Testing unit tests: parsing, validation, lossless edits, and the lock state machine (with fake keychain and authentication)
└── scripts/            make-xcode-project.sh (the Xcode project, iPhone and iPad), run-on-iphone.sh, phone-address.sh (checks the phone's https address), phones.sh (list or remove paired devices), test-scripts.sh (runs them all against stand-ins for Xcode, the iPhone and the homelab; CI runs it)

docs.title: Where it fits
docs.text:
Three ways into the same homelab, in two roles:

  • Homelab Wizard, the desktop app on the Mac that runs the homelab, is where it's managed: setup, Choose apps, installing apps, settings, Tidy Up, and pairing phones.
  • This app is a remote control for keeping an eye on it from an iPhone or iPad: status, alerts, backups, Finances, and quick changes behind Face ID or Touch ID. It does no setup, on purpose.
  • The phone web page (homelab serve, built from web/) is the same remote control in a browser. It stays a web page: it works on any phone (Android, a partner's, a visitor's) with no install and no Apple account. With a free Apple ID this app can't be shared, and lapses after 7 days.

As main adds phone-facing features to the companion, they're mirrored here (the main #… notes below).

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
It's laid out as Homelab Wizard is on the computer: the same screens, in the same order and with the same names (Status, Backups, Finances, Setup, Settings), in a sidebar on the iPad with Homelab Wizard's name atop it, and as tabs on iPhone. ⌘2 to ⌘6 pick them, the same numbers as the computer's. Choose apps and Tidy Up are on the computer only, since a phone can't reach them yet.

iPhone iPad Pairing The code, the pasted pairing link, or a scan of the computer's QR code. Optionally as a wall screen (look-only for good). The code or the pasted link Away from home (ADR-0023) With the computer set up for it (Setup › Reach Finances away from home) and paired at home afterwards: a read that can't reach home (Status, an app's page, Finances to look at) goes through the Cloudflare tunnel instead, sealed end to end with a key agreed at pairing (TunnelSeal, tested against the computer's own vectors), with the household's service token for Cloudflare Access. Home is tried first, for 4 seconds; after the tunnel answered, it goes first for 5 minutes, or until the phone's network changes (Wi-Fi to cellular, home again, a VPN on or off: NetworkKind, never the Wi-Fi's name), when home is tried first again. Changes, Settings, and live updates wait until home. Away mode: when neither home nor the tunnel answers (Cloudflare down, say) and nothing was read, Status lists just the apps on the internet (the catalog's public ones with an https address), as last read and kept in the Keychain beside the pairing (this phone only, behind the app's Face ID), each with whether its own address answers and Open; everything else comes back by itself when the computer answers. The same Locking Face ID / Touch ID / passcode at launch, and on return once the app has been away longer than Lock After (Settings › This iPhone: Right Away, or after 1, 5 or 15 minutes; 5 unless changed). Back sooner, it opens as it was left. Locking the screen locks it, a change still asks for Face ID after leaving, and a member's private Finances still lock as the app leaves; an opaque cover in the app switcher The same; the Mac locks as it leaves the screen Status On iPhone it opens with a card: a ring of the apps running out of all of them, and the one that needs a look with its Start (or Restart) and Logs, or "All well" and the night's line; then four tiles: Backups (opens the Backups tab), Saved, Updates and Checks. The floating glass tab bar shrinks as you scroll (iOS 26 and later). Then the live list, searchable by name, grouped as the computer's Status: Needs a look first, then the pinned apps, then each category (Media, Photos, …) and Other. A group where all is fine starts folded, its apps' names on one line; what you open or fold is remembered (names only), and is the computer's, the same on every device: on a device allowed changes, folding a group here folds it on the computer and the other phones (a look-only device keeps its own; StatusFolds, SetStatusFolds, no Face ID, since it only changes what shows open). Each row has its icon, "N% up" and a dot for what changed since you looked; on iPhone those apps are also listed together at the top, and Mark as Seen clears the dots. An app the watchdog stopped because Docker kept restarting it (main #427) reads "Stopped: it restarted 5 times in an hour", in red, and counts as needing a look. One the battery saver paused reads "Paused on battery", and one waiting for its drive "Waiting for the Media drive", both in orange. Start the stopped leaves out all of these, as the computer's Start them does. Needs a look counts as the computer's does: unwell, not answering, missing, or stopped when nobody stopped it on purpose. Rows use the computer's words for each state. The overnight line in the morning. Each state has its own shape as well as colour: a circle when up, a triangle to look at, a cross when down (main #449). With VoiceOver, what changes is said as it changes, in the row's words ("Vikunja and Immich: Restarting", main #451). Atop every other screen, one line says "All well", or the one thing that needs you (main #470). A stopped app nobody stopped says when, and why when Docker knows ("Stopped at 3:12 AM: it ran out of memory"); a crash is a cross (main #474). The same, in a three-column split view whose sidebar keeps its place, (no menu bar item or Dock count on the Mac yet: docs/Parity.md) An app's page What's wrong, its actions, its week (uptime and outages), about it (catalog, and another app here that does much the same job, main #438), its backup (the last nightly run, its copy, the restore test, and Back up now), its updates (when it was last updated, and whether its updates are held), where it can be reached from (home, tailnet, or the internet through the Cloudflare Tunnel), details, why it last started, addresses, logs (filter, errors and warnings in colour, Problems Only, copy with ⇧⌘C), and its settings (nightly updates, alerts, pin, and on a public app Reach it away from home, where the computer takes it, main #559; a home-only app says At home only) Under Nightly updates, Only on Sundays (or the days set on the computer, "Only on Saturdays and Sundays"), main #457.. Its log can Follow: read again every 4 seconds while open, at the newest line, until switched off, closed, locked, or a read fails The same, with an App menu (⌥⌘S/R/./L) What was done On an app's More About page, Recently Done: the newest few things done to it (Restarted Immich, 2 hours ago, by the watchdog), read from the computer's record (internal/history, the look-only History, every line redacted there); Everything That Was Done lists the last 90 days for every app, searchable by app, phone or word. Shown only where the computer answers History. The same, on More About in the app's page beside the list Links into the app (homelab://) homelab://status, homelab://app/<id>, homelab://app/<id>?do=restart, start, stop or logs, homelab://backups, homelab://finances and homelab://finances/<page> (transactions, budgets, bills, accounts, investments, goals, recurring, spending, inbox, cashflow, review), and homelab://tidy/inbox (Status for now: Tidy Up's Inbox is the computer's). The app unlocks as always first. A link never changes anything by itself: anyone can send one, so an action link opens the app's page with the action waiting for one confirming tap, and only on a device allowed changes (then Face ID, as the button). A link names an app by its exact id; anything unknown or malformed opens Status (DeepLink). The same: a link opens its screen in the sidebar, or the app's page beside the list, with an action waiting for its tap Send to my phone / Open on the Computer A page the computer sends this phone (its row menu's Send to my phone ›, ⌘K) shows at the bottom as From the Computer: Radarr with Open; on an app's More About page, Open on the Computer puts the computer's window on that app's page (a phone allowed to change things, no Face ID: it changes no data) The same, the banner over the split view Changes (allowed devices, re-authenticated) Start, Stop (confirmed, Undo), Restart, Stop for a while, Roll back, for one app or a whole list; a long press on a row opens its menu, as the phone page's does since main #447. A stopped app's row has Start on it, as a running app has Open on the computer's; on a device that only looks, the row and the app's page say Start it from the computer instead. A change waits its turn behind the computer's other jobs (main #425). The same, plus keyboard shortcuts and a right-click menu Status, below the apps The money card, watchdog, protection (with what CrowdSec stopped today, also on the proxy's and CrowdSec's own pages, main #430), alerts, savings (with what the apps have saved so far, month by month, main #437). When the watchdog has alerted that memory is nearly full, its card names the three biggest apps, with Stop (main #458); a failing check whose alerts are snoozed says until when (main #469), and Snooze… on it (for an hour, a day, or Alert again now) snoozes it from the phone, behind Face ID, where this device may make changes; under Recent Alerts, Every Alert lists what the computer kept of the last 90 days (AlertLog, past ntfy's 12 hours), each with when it cleared or who snoozed it until when, where the computer answers it, and Snooze… on one whose watchdog check still fails The same, below the app list, as on the computer Backups It opens with a card: a ring of the copies that are fresh, when the last backup ran and where to, and Back Up Now and Test a Restore; under it three tiles, the restore test, the password export and the second copy (Kopia, or the settings file), each a word or two in its colour (the owner's redesign, Nov 12). Then the copies that need a look (out of date, or shrank), those waiting for a drive or not copied yet, and the fresh ones folded to a row of logos until tapped; Duplicati's jobs, the restore tests, where they go and the password export are one tap down, under More. Each copy is beside the night before's, with a warning when one shrank to less than half (main #435). Backups in the sidebar Setup and Settings Settings is laid out as the system's own, the everyday ones first (the owner's redesign, Nov 12): the homelab on top (what this device may do, with This Device behind it: how it paired, its ID, Unpair); The Homelab: nightly updates, quiet hours, restarting an app that stops answering, undoing an update that breaks one, and alerts on the computer's screen, each in plain words; This iPhone: the lock, the widget, and Alerts From (the ntfy app, or this app: while it's open it shows the computer's new kept alerts as its own notifications, at most five at once and never the old ones, on this device only; where the computer keeps alerts); Everything Else: all the homelab's settings a section a row with its icon, Get help (a report) and About. Setup: what the machine runs, and Look for problems → Fix these. Settings: the homelab's settings (.env) as the computer's Settings shows them, by section, searchable, each by its name for people with its key, help and a switch where it's on or off, the everyday ones first; a device allowed changes changes the everyday ones (with Face ID), while a password or token shows only as set, and secrets and the settings the phone connects through are changed on the computer (needs the computer's Homelab Wizard with main #491); nightly updates on or off, a diagnostics report to share, this device (when it paired, and a warning if it paired without encryption), Unpair. What this device may do is read again every 5 minutes and after a failed change, so a phone whose changes were given for a while only (main #455) loses its buttons when they end; one removed on the computer is unpaired within seconds (main #456) Computer in the sidebar Finances (by level) Its home, as Settings is laid out: first what's left once the next paycheck is in and its bills are paid (Left until Nov 19, after the bills, and Under your $500 cushion on Thu, Nov 5 when checking dips under it before then), opening Bills; then checking now and after the next paycheck (before its bills), net worth with its line over three months and this month's change, then Transactions, Budgets, Bills, Investments, Accounts, Goals and Loans, each one tap away on a page of its own. On Investments, where Finances may be changed, Read Now reads Ghostfolio again and Add a Holding records a buy or a sale there (in an account, or a new one), with Face ID first, from a ticker or name Ghostfolio looks up. Transactions as Wallet shows a card's: checking's card on top, your other accounts as small cards to switch to (each with its logo and balance; not homes, cars or collectibles), then what happened with each payee's logo; one new since you looked has a violet dot until it's reviewed (this phone remembers only an HMAC of each seen transaction's id, under its own key). A transaction's page: its logo big, the amount, the day, what it paid, the account, its category, note (without the bank's own wording, as the computer leaves it out), tags and receipt, Edit, and the other times at that payee. Checking now and after the next paycheck, each opening how it adds up row by row, the computer's own steps (main #482). The plan, budgets, goals, loans, Taken as done, and transactions; money from someone outside the household says who from (main #483). Investments, as Ghostfolio last read them on the computer (main #489): the total, what went in, the gain and this month's change, a row a holding, each opening its worth at each read. Editing: balances, the cushion, budgets, goal targets, what a payment costs, waiting marks, transactions, and receipt photos. Finances in the sidebar; ⌥⌘N adds a transaction, ⇧⌘H hides amounts on every device Finances offline When the Homelab doesn't answer (no signal, or away from home without the tunnel), Finances shows the last Finances read on this phone, with As of when on top, to look at only: every change waits until the Homelab answers, and then the newest are read by themselves (every 30 seconds while it's open, or on a pull). Kept only on a phone at the view or edit level, sealed with AES-GCM under a key only this phone holds (its Keychain, this device only, while unlocked), with complete file protection and out of backups (OfflineFinances); gone when Finances is taken from the phone or it's unpaired. A lost phone keeps the last Finances it read until it's erased; Remove on the computer stops anything new The same Private Finances (a household member's own phone) Once she makes her Finances private (Make Them Private… under them: her 16-word recovery code shown once and two of its words typed back, then a passphrase of 12 characters or more; or on the phone's page), the Homelab keeps them locked and can't open them, whoever runs it; the app opens them on her phone: Open with Face ID once she opened them here before (her key kept in this device's Keychain behind Face ID only, never synced or backed up: PrivateFinancesKey), else her passphrase or the 16 words of her recovery code. They're read forward on the phone with the computer's own Finances code (HomelabFinance.xcframework, made by make phone-finance-framework, which make-xcode-project.sh runs when Go is on the Mac), shown by the same screens, and saved locked again; another of her devices saving first is said plainly. Lock (or leaving Finances, 5 minutes untouched, the app in the background) drops them from memory; what the household shares shows either way. Turn Privacy Off… (once she confirms) keeps them plain on the Homelab again, receipts included. Offline: her phone keeps her Finances as last read, still locked (never her key, never plain: PrivateOffline, complete file protection, out of backups), so Face ID, her passphrase or her code opens them with no connection; changes made then wait there, locked, N changes wait for the Homelab, and go by themselves once it answers (tried every 30 seconds); if another of her devices saved meanwhile, that's said plainly and the latest is shown. A receipt, and turning privacy off, wait until home. Her reminders: the computer can't read hers, so each time she opens them the app works out the next two weeks' with the computer's own code (mobile/finance.Reminders: a bill due tomorrow, a paycheck under the cushion, a yearly renewal, stale balances; each kind the plan quiets left out, amounts hidden with Hide amounts) and plans them as its own notifications, today's at once and each later day's at 9 AM (PrivateReminders); turning privacy off or unpairing takes them away (PrivateFinances, PrivateSeal) The same The Collection (Finances) The household's cards (Finances › Collection on the computer): what they're worth and the gain on what was paid, each card with its picture (read from the computer), its page with its price over time; Update Prices (a phone allowed to change Finances, after Face ID) has the computer read TCGplayer's prices from TCGdex. Add a Card and Edit (the same phone, after Face ID): name, set, number, condition or grade, how many, what one cost and when, what one is worth now and Keep This Price, and a photo of their own (Take a Photo with the camera, or Choose a Photo), shrunk to 800 pixels and sent without its location; Remove Card The same

docs.title: The look
docs.text: A plain iPhone app, as the owner chose: the system's large titles, tab bar, lists and back buttons, SF Pro, light and dark following the phone, with a violet accent. Shared/Views/Theme.swift holds the colours, with no other product's name, logo or artwork; Shared/Views/Design.swift the pieces every screen is built from: - Colours: a violet accent (also the asset catalog's AccentColor, set as the global accent by make-xcode-project.sh), a warm grey canvas behind white cards (blue-black behind dark ones), ink and a quieter ink for text, and calm status colours (success, warning, caution, danger, info). Every colour has a light and a dark value, and as text each keeps at least 4.5:1 contrast on its card. - Pieces (Design.swift): a card (.card(), radius 20, a soft two-layer shadow), a round logo circle (LogoCircle: 48 pt in lists, 58 pt in a grid, 96 pt on a transaction), a round action button (RoundActionButton: Open, Restart, Stop, Logs), a gradient wallet card and its stack (WalletCard, WalletStack), a ring of running out of total (ProgressRing), and a state pill with a dot (DotPill). Buttons give a light tap you can feel, and numbers roll from one value to the next. - Payee logos: a payee's brand mark in a circle on the brand's colour, its initials on a colour its name picks when it has no brand, else the icon of its category in the category's colour. The brands are the computer's own (web/src/finances/logos.ts: simple-icons, CC0, about 335), and so are the rules that read a bank's wording ("SQ BLUE BOTTLE", "AMZN MKTP US2K4") and match it to one. node apple-client/scripts/make-payee-logos.mjs (after npm ci in the repo's root) writes them to Shared/Resources/PayeeLogos.json, with the category colours from web/dist/style.css, and writes what the computer's functions answer for a few thousand payees to Tests/Resources/PayeeVectors.json; the tests check the app's Swift port answers the same, and CI checks both files are current. Nothing is fetched: which bank you use stays on the phone. - Shapes: states and counts in tinted pills, an app without an icon yet on a soft tile of its state's colour, and rounded bordered buttons. - App logos: every app the homelab knows has its logo in the app itself, on the same rounded tile (Shared/Assets.xcassets/AppLogos, one 180 px PNG each), so the lists look alike on every device and nothing is fetched for them. They're from dashboard-icons (Apache 2.0; see licenses/), credited under Settings › About. An app without one shows the icon the computer kept from the app itself, and failing that its state on a tile. After apps are added to the catalog, python3 scripts/fetch-app-logos.py (Pillow and PyYAML) fetches the new ones; a name the logo set spells differently goes in its ALIASES. - The app mark and icon: a violet server rack on a white tile (turned inside out in November 2026, as Proton Mail's icon is), on the pairing and lock screens, at launch, and on the app-switcher cover. The app icon is the same, with one mint "running" light. scripts/make-app-icon.py (Pillow) draws it from shapes into Shared/Assets.xcassets/AppIcon.appiconset: one 1024 px iPhone and iPad icon edge to edge with its iOS 18 dark and tinted variants.

docs.title: Check it first, without an Xcode project
docs.text:
On a Mac with full Xcode 16 or later installed and selected. The Command Line Tools alone aren't enough: SwiftUI's @State and @Entry are macros whose plugin ships only with Xcode, so a build with the tools fails on every @State with "plugin for module 'SwiftUIMacros' not found". Select Xcode once (sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer, then xcode-select -p shows a path inside Xcode.app), or prefix a single build with DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer.

cd apple-client && swift build && swift test

To also compile the iOS-only parts (the QR scanner, haptics, keyboard types), build the same package for iOS:

cd apple-client && xcodebuild -scheme HomelabClient -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' build

Package.swift builds everything in Shared/ except the @main entry point, in Swift 6 language mode, and runs Tests/.

The same checks run on every change on GitHub's Mac runner (.github/workflows/apple-client.yml): swift build and swift test, the package for iOS, the iPhone app from the generated project (unsigned), the screenshots in the simulator, and scripts/test-scripts.sh. The package is built and tested for macOS too, where swift test runs, though there's no Mac app. A compiler warning fails the job, since in Swift 6 most are data races waiting to become errors.

docs.title: Make the Xcode project
docs.text:
The quickest way (iPhone app): apple-client/scripts/run-on-iphone.sh com.yourname, with the iPhone plugged in, unlocked, trusting this Mac, and Developer Mode on (Settings › Privacy & Security › Developer Mode). It checks the phone's address first (phone-address.sh, below), makes the project, builds and signs for that phone (-allowProvisioningDeviceRegistration adds it to a free Personal Team), installs and opens it with devicectl, and shows a pairing QR code to scan in the app. With a free Apple ID the app works for 7 days; run it again to renew. The first time, the phone has to trust the Apple ID: Settings › General › VPN & Device Management.

The quick way (Xcode): apple-client/scripts/make-xcode-project.sh com.yourname makes it with XcodeGen (installed with Homebrew if missing), with every setting below, in ~/Developer/HomelabClient-xcode, outside the repository, pointing at this checkout's Shared/. Then pick an iPhone and press ⌘R in Xcode. By hand:

  1. In Xcode 16 or later (its SDKs make View main-actor isolated, which these sources rely on): File › New › Project › iOS › App. Name it HomelabClient. Choose SwiftUI and Swift, with no Core Data and no SwiftData.
  2. Delete the template's ContentView.swift and HomelabClientApp.swift.
  3. Drag apple-client/Shared into the project. Choose Create groups and add it to the app target. Drag apple-client/Tests into the unit test target.
  4. In Build settings for the app target:
  5. iOS Deployment Target 17.0. @Observable, ContentUnavailableView and sensoryFeedback need these.
  6. Swift Language Version Swift 6.
  7. On Xcode 26, set Default Actor Isolation = nonisolated. The new-project default is MainActor, but these sources mark @MainActor explicitly where needed. Under a MainActor default, the model and parser types would be main-actor-bound, and the background stream reader couldn't use them.
  8. In Info (Info.plist keys):
  9. NSFaceIDUsageDescription: "Face ID unlocks Homelab, which controls your servers." The Face ID prompt fails without it.
  10. NSCameraUsageDescription (iOS): "The camera scans the pairing QR code your computer shows, and takes a photo of a card for your Collection when you ask." Scanning to pair needs it, and Add a Card's Take a Photo. The first tap on Scan (or Take a Photo) asks for the camera; if it's refused, the app says how to allow it and the address and code can still be typed, and Add a Card offers Choose a Photo only.
  11. NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription: "Homelab talks to your homelab on the home network." iOS asks before an app reaches a home-network address such as the one homelab.<your domain> resolves to; this is the reason the prompt shows. Allow it, or the connection fails.
  12. ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption = NO. The app's only encryption is the system's HTTPS and Keychain, which is exempt, so App Store Connect stops asking at each upload.
  13. In Signing & Capabilities:
  14. Choose a development team.
  15. Make sure Shared/App/PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy is in the app target. It's the privacy manifest the App Store asks for. It states no tracking and no data collected, and the one required-reason API the app uses: UserDefaults, for its own settings (CA92.1). The Swift package leaves it out, as a library has no use for it.

docs.title: The day you sign
docs.text:
The app is built for a free Apple ID today (the owner's call, Nov 9, 2026): no push notifications, the widget only where its App Group signs, and a re-install with the cable every 7 days. Everything that needs the paid Apple Developer Program is built, tested, and kept compiling behind one switch. The day you join:

  1. Join the Apple Developer Program, with the same Apple ID, and note the team ID (10 characters, developer.apple.com › Membership).
  2. Make the project signed: HOMELAB_SIGNED=1 apple-client/scripts/make-xcode-project.sh com.yourname TEAMID. It turns on the widget and its App Group (as HOMELAB_WIDGET=1 does), push notifications (aps-environment), and the code under #if HOMELAB_SIGNED. Without it, the project is the same as before. scripts/test-scripts.sh checks all three ways, and CI builds the signed app on every change, so it keeps compiling.
  3. An APNs key for the computer: developer.apple.com › Certificates, IDs & Profiles › Keys › +, Apple Push Notifications service, download the .p8 once, and put it in the homelab's Settings (the alerts then go to the app as well as ntfy). Built when push lands.
  4. TestFlight for the partner's phone: Xcode › Product › Archive › Distribute App › TestFlight, then invite them in App Store Connect; their phone installs from the TestFlight app and stops needing the cable.
  5. Export compliance: the app's sealing for away from home (TunnelSeal: Curve25519 and AES-GCM from CryptoKit) is encryption beyond HTTPS, so before the first TestFlight upload set ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption as App Store Connect's questions lead (standard algorithms from the system, for the app's own data, usually count as exempt) rather than the NO the project says today.
  6. Notarise the Mac app too while signed: docs/Releasing.md.

Keep this list current as features that need signing land.

docs.title: Pair an iPhone over the home network (no Tailscale)
docs.text:
Tailscale is never needed. The phone needs an https address, and the homelab's domain gives it one at home: https://homelab.<your domain>, served by Nginx Proxy Manager with the domain's certificate. The Wi-Fi's DNS (AdGuard, or the router's custom DNS) sends that name to the homelab. The companion answers it only from the home network: anything that comes through the Cloudflare tunnel gets a 403, so it is never on the internet. Since the proxy says it reached it over https (X-Forwarded-Proto), the companion counts it as encrypted, and the phone may make changes and see Finances.

apple-client/scripts/phone-address.sh checks the whole way from the Mac, without changing anything: the domain in .env, that the name resolves to a home address, that the certificate is trusted (the iPhone refuses one that isn't, and so does this app), and that the companion answers behind the proxy (401, "not paired", without a token). Each failure says what to look at.

A VPN on the phone (Proton VPN, say) usually brings its own DNS, so homelab.<your domain> can't be found while it's on at home. The app then says the address couldn't be found. Let the VPN use the home network (its LAN or custom-DNS setting), or turn it off at home. Away from home, the phone reaches the companion through the Cloudflare tunnel instead, once the computer is set up for it (Away from home, above), with the VPN on or off.

Plain http://<this Mac>:8099 from the phone stays refused: the token would cross the Wi-Fi in readable form.

docs.title: Paired devices
docs.text: apple-client/scripts/phones.sh lists the phones and Macs paired with the homelab on this Mac. phones.sh tidy removes the ones never used (a pairing that failed half way, for example while the Keychain refused the token), after asking. phones.sh remove <id> removes one by its ID, never by name: two devices can share a name, and homelab phone remove <name> would take the first. The run scripts make no new code when the device is already paired and in use, so rebuilding doesn't leave duplicates.

docs.title: The server contract (read from the Go sources)
docs.text:
The companion on 8099 (internal/companion/server.go) doesn't serve the engine's /v1/* routes to devices. It wraps them:

Need Request Notes Pair POST /api/pair {code, name, kiosk} Answers {token, device}. The code is 8 characters, works once, for 10 minutes. 10 wrong codes lead to a 429. Who am I GET /api/me {id, name, canChange, finances} Status (/v1/status) POST /api/call/Status [] {result: Status, log}. LastStatus answers at once with the last reading. Cards (/v1/cards) POST /api/call/StatusBoard [n, ["watchdog","savings","protection","alerts"]] ndjson: {"result":Status}, then {"event":"status:card","data":Card} for each card Live (/v1/events) GET /api/events SSE: data: <engine.Change>, plus a : still here heartbeat every 30 s Back up now, Test a restore, Fix POST /api/call/Homelab ["backup"\|"restore-test"\|"fix", "", apply] Changes. Fix runs first without apply (a plan), then with it App settings POST /api/call/SetAppSetting [id, "updates"\|"alerts"\|"pinned", bool] A change: hold or release updates, watchdog alerts on or off, pin to the top Computer Host, SetUpdatesPaused [bool] (a change), Report (secrets removed by the computer; up to 3 min) Start / Stop / Restart / Roll back POST /api/call/AppAction [id, "start"\|"stop"\|"restart"\|"rollback"]; Stop for a while is StopUntil [id, RFC 3339] Needs canChange and https. One change from a phone at a time. {result: null, log}, or 500 {error, log}

All requests after pairing send Authorization: Bearer <token>. The token is 32 random bytes, base64url-encoded. The server keeps only its SHA-256 hash. The client receives the token itself, once.

docs.title: Security model
docs.text: Threat Mitigation Where Token sniffed on Wi-Fi https only, with no exceptions: ServerEndpoint rejects any http:// address (the Mac app's plain http to the companion on the same Mac went with it, and an endpoint it stored reads as corrupt and is deleted). There are no ATS exceptions. The server also makes plain-HTTP pairings from the network look-only. ServerEndpoint, APIClient Token sent to the wrong host The token is stored together with its origin. Every request and response URL is checked against that origin. Redirects are refused, because Foundation would copy the Authorization header onto them. A stored origin goes through the same address rules again when it's read back, and only /api/ paths are ever built on it. DeviceCredential, ServerEndpoint, APIClient.check, RedirectRefusal Token extracted from the device or backups Keychain with kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly, kSecAttrSynchronizable=false, and the data-protection keychain on macOS. The accessibility attribute is checked again on every read, and a mismatched item is deleted. KeychainManager Stale pairing after a reinstall Keychain items survive app deletion on iOS, so the first launch after an install deletes them. AppCoordinator.purgeKeychainIfFreshInstall Someone else picks up the unlocked device Face ID / Touch ID / passcode (.deviceOwnerAuthentication) at launch, and on return from the background once the app has been away longer than Lock After (iPhone and iPad: 5 minutes unless changed, or Right Away; measured by the monotonic clock, so changing the time can't stretch it; the Mac on every return). Locking the screen locks the app while it still runs (protectedDataWillBecomeUnavailable, a few seconds' background time after leaving); a change asks again after any leaving. A new LAContext each time, with no reuse window. With no passcode set, the app refuses to open. BiometricAuthManager, AppCoordinator App switcher snapshot An opaque shield covers the app whenever the scene isn't active (iOS). PrivacyShieldView Data left in memory while locked Locking stops the SSE stream and clears every reading. Late answers that arrive after the lock are dropped. LiveEventManager.clear Secrets in logs os.Logger only. Tokens and codes are never interpolated. Hosts and server text are .private. Error log lines use payload-free logName. The secret types print as <redacted> even through print or dump. SecureLog, APIError.logName Hostile or broken stream The SSE and ndjson parsers are bounded (4 MB per event, 8 MB per answer). The token's shape is validated, and server messages are cleaned before display. SSEParser, APIError.sanitize A planted pairing QR code A scan only fills in the address and code, through the same https-only parser as typing. Nothing pairs until the person taps Pair, with the host in front of them. A wrong server could only issue its own token; it never sees this device's real one. QRScannerView, PairingViewModel.scanned Path injection via method names /api/call/<Method> accepts only ASCII alphanumerics. APIClient.callRequest A change made from an unattended, unlocked device Start, Stop and Restart ask for Face ID / Touch ID / passcode again unless the owner authenticated in the last 2 minutes. The window is measured on the monotonic clock, so changing the device time can't stretch it. AppCoordinator.authorizeChange Accidental or repeated changes Stop is confirmed and offers Undo for 10 s (30 s with VoiceOver or Switch Control on, and announced), one app or a group. A group runs one app at a time, stops at the first failure, and authenticates once. One change at a time. Changes are never retried, and a timeout says the change may still be running. Buttons show only when the computer says canChange. App ids must look like catalog ids before they're sent. AppActionsViewModel, AppAction, APIClient.perform Card data, logs and alerts in memory Cards, logs and command output belong to the dashboard, so locking drops them. A late answer after a lock is dropped, not stored. Log lines are shown verbatim (never parsed as Markdown) and marked privacySensitive. What the app copies (an address, log lines) stays on this device: on iOS it's local-only, so not on Universal Clipboard, and expires in ten minutes; on the Mac, copied log lines are marked concealed for clipboard-history apps. One card that fails to decode only costs that card. CardsViewModel, LogsViewModel, StatusCard, Clipboard Finances save losing data, or undoing another device's Edits change only the fields they mean to (FinancePlanEdit) in the plan as the raw JSON sent. Its rev goes back, so the computer refuses a stale save, and the phone then reads the latest. The edit level, authentication, a sane amount, and never retried. FinancePlanEdit, FinancesViewModel.setBalance A receipt photo giving away where it was taken Re-encoded from its pixels alone (ReceiptCodec.preparePhoto): no EXIF, GPS or camera details, at most 2000 px and 2 MB. Receipt names must be the computer's hash form before they're sent or shown. ReceiptCodec What's kept on the device between launches Only the sidebar's choice and which Status groups are open (scene storage, group names only), the widget's one line where it's turned on (below), the overnight line's hidden day, and "changed since you looked" as HMAC-SHA256 values under a random Keychain key (this device only). No app names, times, or readings are kept readable. ChangeMemory, KeychainManager.deviceKey The widget showing the homelab without Face ID Built only with HOMELAB_WIDGET=1, and off on each device until turned on (with Face ID or Touch ID) under Settings › This Device. It shows only "All well" or a count, and when it was read: never app names. The unlocked app writes that one line to the App Group on each Status read; the widget has no token and reads nothing from the network. It's hidden while the device is locked (privacySensitive), only the Home Screen size is offered (no Lock Screen widget), and turning it off or unpairing deletes the line. WidgetSummaryStore, Widget/HomelabWidget.swift A phone changing what it shouldn't in .env Settings travel only over the https link and never to a wall screen; a secret's value is never sent (and dropped if it were). A device allowed changes may save only everyday settings, after Face ID or Touch ID: the computer refuses every secret and the settings a phone connects through (the companion, bind addresses, domain and proxy key, proxy ports, AdGuard's DNS address, Tailscale), and saves nothing if it refuses one. Keys are checked for their shape before they're sent, and values are never logged. ComputerViewModel.saveForm, APIClient.saveSettings, main #491 Fix applied by accident Fix always runs as a plan first. fix --apply runs only from that plan's Fix These button, after authentication. HomelabTasksViewModel, TaskOutputView Diagnostics report leaking secrets The computer removes secrets before sending. The phone shows the whole report before the share sheet, keeps it only while that sheet is open, and never logs it. ComputerViewModel, ReportView A logo carrying more than a picture The bundled logos are re-encoded from their pixels alone when fetched (no metadata), and the app names them only by catalog-shaped ids. Apps with one never ask the computer for their icon. scripts/fetch-app-logos.py, BundledLogo Command output kept or shown Docker's output is kept only for a failure's Details: the last 400 lines, cleaned, in memory, dropped on lock. It's never logged. APIError.sanitizeLog

docs.title: Not built yet
docs.text:
• Update. The phone method list (phoneMethods in cmd/homelab/serve.go) has no ReleaseNotes and no way to learn that an update exists. The computer offers Update only behind its release notes, so the phone doesn't offer a blind update. This needs a backend method first.
  • Finances editing beyond balances, budgets, goal targets, payment amounts and transactions: a payment's schedule and accounts, adding or removing payments, accounts, goal shares, transfers and split transactions. What's built:
  • turning the plan's Hide amounts on or off for every device (as ⌘⇧H on the computer);
  • typing in an account's balance or the cushion (the least checking should hold), changing a budget's amount, a goal's target or what a planned payment costs (not a card payoff, whose amount means the card's other spending), and marking a paycheck or payment as not in the balances yet (Taken as done) (SaveFinances, edit level). This edits the plan as the raw JSON the computer sent and sends it back whole, with its rev. Nothing the phone doesn't show is lost, and the computer refuses the save if another device saved first;
  • the money card (FinancesWall) in Overview, for any Finances level;
  • the plan (Finances) for view and edit: accounts today, net worth, and each pay period with its payments;
  • budgets, goals and loans from the same view;
  • transactions (FinancesLedger), newest first by month, searchable;
  • adding a transaction (SaveFinancesLedger, edit level): money in or out of one account, with payee, category, day and note. It's appended to the raw ledger and sent back with its rev. The computer gives it its id and checks it;
  • changing or deleting a transaction (by its id; transfers and splits stay on the computer). Everything else it holds, such as tags, bank id and receipt, is kept;
  • receipts: a kept one opens from its transaction (FinancesReceipt; pictures through a capped thumbnail, PDFs in PDFKit), and a photo can be attached to a new one (SaveFinancesReceipt). It's shrunk and re-encoded as JPEG with no metadata, so no location leaves the device. Amounts stay hidden until tapped and hide again on lock. None show while the plan's Hide amounts is on.
  • Investments: reading them now and adding a buy or a sale. The holdings Ghostfolio last gave are in the plan already (each account's holdings, the plan's holdingsRead), so the Investments card draws from Finances today (FinanceInvestments). The computer can now also be asked, from a device with Finances' edit level and over the https link only:
  • FinancesReadInvestments, no arguments: reads Ghostfolio now and keeps what each account holds on the plan's account of the same name. It answers {view, unmatched, accounts, holdings}: view is the plan read forward, as Finances answers; unmatched the names of Ghostfolio's accounts nothing here matched; accounts and holdings how many Ghostfolio has, matched or not (0 and 0 still means the token worked and Ghostfolio is empty). A wrong or missing GHOSTFOLIO_SECURITY_TOKEN, or Ghostfolio not running, is an error in words, never with the token.
  • FinancesFindSymbol, ["<what was typed>"]: up to 8 matches, each {symbol, name, currency, dataSource}. Nothing typed finds nothing. Only the typed ticker or name leaves the homelab, when Ghostfolio looks it up.
  • FinancesAddInvestment, [{account, symbol, dataSource, currency, shares, total, date, sold}]: puts a buy (or, sold: true, a sale) into Ghostfolio, then reads again and answers as FinancesReadInvestments does. account is the plan account's id (investment or retirement); or send newName instead to make a new investment account, in Ghostfolio and the plan by one name. symbol, dataSource and currency are a match from FinancesFindSymbol; shares more than 0; total what was paid (or got) for them all, without a minus; date YYYY-MM-DD, not in the future. What's wrong is said before Ghostfolio is asked. The computer's card does the same (main: internal/ghostfolio, shared by the app and homelab serve). On the phone these still need a view: an Add form and a Read now button, both behind Face ID or Touch ID as other Finances saves are.
  • "Downloading the app…" while an image is pulled. AppAction answers only at the end, so the phone can't see the pull happening.
  • Revoking from the device. The companion has no self-unpair endpoint, so Unpair deletes the token locally and tells the person to run homelab phone remove <id> (or scripts/phones.sh remove <id>).
  • The last Status while the computer can't be reached (the phone page does this since main #453). It's left out on purpose: it would keep readings on the device, and this app keeps none, nor anything once locked.
  • When this device's changes end (homelab phone until, main #455). /api/me doesn't say, so the app can't show it before it happens.
  • Optional: certificate pinning. It's left out on purpose, because Tailscale and Let's Encrypt certificates rotate every 90 days.
  • A look-only home Wi-Fi mode over plain http. It's left out on purpose: the token would cross the Wi-Fi in readable form (the computer makes such a device look-only for good). It's a decision to make before building it.
  • App Intents (Shortcuts) and Live Activities. They need targets in the Xcode project, and a choice about what may run or show without unlocking. (The widget is built: see Start here.)
  • The iPhone app run against a real homelab serve. The iPhone app builds on the Mac runner; it hasn't been installed on a phone yet (run-on-iphone.sh).

docs.title: Before changing anything
docs.text:
Read the Maintainer Guide first. The critical facts:

  • Nginx Proxy Manager is a locally built image with the CrowdSec bouncer. Never update it by pulling jc21/nginx-proxy-manager; use ./homelab update nginx-proxy-manager.
  • Duplicati jobs use container paths (/source/..., /staging/...), never paths on the computer.
  • Everything joins the homelab Docker network. The proxy and the tunnel reach apps by service name (immich-server:2283), not through host.docker.internal.
  • The budget tracker's folder is stacks/budget-tracker (not money).
  • Run Compose through the CLI: ./homelab compose <app> <args> picks the right project, folder, and .env.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
One computer runs everything: containers in its container runtime (OrbStack on a Mac, Docker Engine on Linux, Docker Desktop on Windows; Host), plus two native apps (Jellyfin, and the phone companion that homelab serve runs). The drawings below use the Mac. Apps are split into Compose projects that share one Docker network.

Every new homelab starts in Home mode (HOMELAB_DOMAIN empty): Tailscale gives each app an https address on the tailnet, and nothing needs a domain, Cloudflare, or the proxy. With a domain, all traffic, from the LAN or from the internet, enters through Nginx Proxy Manager, where CrowdSec blocks known attackers. The topology below is that domain setup.

docs.title: Topology
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  subgraph Internet
    visitor([Phone on mobile data])
    edge[Cloudflare edge<br/>TLS and managed rules]
  end
  subgraph Home["Home network · 192.168.1.0/24"]
    device([Phone or laptop on Wi-Fi])
    subgraph Mac["Mac · 192.168.1.10"]
      jellyfin[Jellyfin<br/>native app :8096]
      subgraph Orb["OrbStack · network: homelab"]
        adguard[AdGuard Home<br/>DNS :53]
        npm[Nginx Proxy Manager<br/>:80 and :443<br/>with the CrowdSec bouncer]
        crowdsec[CrowdSec]
        cloudflared[cloudflared]
        apps[Apps<br/>one project per category, and the stacks]
      end
    end
  end
  device -- "DNS: where is photos.example.com?" --> adguard
  adguard -. "192.168.1.10" .-> device
  device -- "then HTTPS" --> npm
  visitor --> edge
  cloudflared == "tunnel, opened from inside" ==> edge
  edge --> cloudflared
  cloudflared -- "http" --> npm
  npm --> apps
  npm --> jellyfin
  crowdsec -. "reads logs, sends bans" .- npm

Nothing listens on the router: the tunnel is opened from the Mac outwards, and every request, from home or from the internet, passes the same proxy and the same CrowdSec check before it reaches an app.

docs.title: Traffic paths
docs.text:
Home mode: device in the tailnet → https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:<port> → Tailscale Serve in the tailscale container → app by service name. With TAILNET_ADMIN_APPS=false, the admin apps are left out and open on this machine only.

LAN: device → AdGuard Home (*.example.com → 192.168.1.10) → Nginx Proxy Manager (TLS, CrowdSec check) → app by service name on the homelab network.

Internet: visitor → Cloudflare edge (TLS, managed rules) → Cloudflare Tunnel → http://nginx-proxy-manager:80 → CrowdSec check, using the visitor's address from CF-Connecting-IP → app.

Native apps: Nginx Proxy Manager → host.docker.internal:8096 → Jellyfin on the Mac.

Only apps marked public: true get a public hostname in the tunnel. Every other hostname exists only in AdGuard, so it never resolves outside the home network.

Single-container apps are grouped by category, one project each (compose.yaml holds the categories, presets, and native apps). Multi-container apps get their own project so they can be stopped, updated, or restored without touching the rest. Inside a stack, databases stay on the stack's private network; only the web-facing service joins homelab.

docs.title: One engine, three ways in
docs.text:
flowchart TB
  app[Desktop app<br/>Choose apps, Status, Backups, Finances, Setup, Settings]
  tray[Menu bar item<br/>health, savings, Back up now, Update apps now]
  phone[Phone companion<br/>homelab serve: Status, Backups, and Finances on a paired phone]
  cli[homelab CLI<br/>Terminal]
  jobs[Background agent<br/>launchd · systemd · the Run key]
  engine[Engine · internal/*<br/>catalog, install plans, domain, backups, checks, wiring]
  files[(compose files with x-homelab metadata,<br/>.env, data/*.json, docs/Savings.md)]
  compose[docker compose<br/>one project per stack]
  apis["APIs<br/>Nginx Proxy Manager, AdGuard Home, Cloudflare,<br/>ntfy, Duplicati, Pocket ID, the *arr apps"]
  app --> engine
  phone --> engine
  phone -- "actions" --> cli
  app -- "actions" --> cli
  tray --> engine
  jobs --> cli
  cli --> engine
  engine -. reads .-> files
  engine --> compose
  engine --> apis

The desktop app and the phone companion read through the engine directly (catalog, status, plans, installs) and run the CLI for actions, so a button and a Terminal command always do the same thing. The engine reads the containers, their events, what they use, and the runtime's info from the runtime's own API over its socket (internal/dockerapi; Docker Desktop's named pipe on Windows), one request on a kept connection, with the docker CLI answering whenever the API fails (DOCKER_API=off keeps the CLI; homelab doctor says which is in use); starting and updating apps is still docker compose. It also follows the container runtime (internal/engine, from those events): a container that starts, stops, or changes health reaches the app's Status and the menu bar item at once, gathered into one change per burst, instead of at the next poll. The agent serves it on a socket only your account can open ($XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/homelab-wizard/engine.sock on Linux, the cache folder elsewhere): GET /v1/hello, /v1/status (?now without waiting for the apps' pages; requests that arrive together share one reading of the runtime), /v1/status/last (the last reading and when it was taken, which a window that opens draws at once, marked with its age, while it reads a fresh one), /v1/events (each change, as Server-Sent Events, carrying the Status read after it, so a window draws it without asking), and /v1/cards (the cards beside Status, read once for every window and phone, each sent as it is read; internal/board), so the app, the menu bar item, and the phone companion follow one engine (homelab serve passes the changes on to paired phones at /api/events); without the agent, each follows the runtime itself and looks for the agent again each minute. The phone answers only on the home network and the tailnet, and only to phones paired with a one-time code. The compose files are the single source: the CLI, the app, the generated docs, and the savings figures all read their x-homelab blocks. Scripts read the CLI's --json output, one {"schema": 1, "type": ..., "data": ...} object per line; internal/api/testdata/contract.json holds the fields a test keeps stable (Commands).

The frontend is TypeScript (web/src): each screen's module (web/src/screens) reads its data through the engine into a store (store.ts), runs the commands, and mounts Preact components per screen and card (web/src/status, backups, choose, setup, settings, finances, page, updates, job, sheets, and the shared blocks in parts), which draw and keep what is typed; app.ts only chooses the screen, answers the keyboard, and starts the app. esbuild compiles it into web/dist/app.js, committed so the Go builds need no Node; the types it is checked against are generated from the methods the app binds (web/types/backend.d.ts). The desktop app and the phone companion load the same files.

docs.title: Watching and healing
docs.text:
Each layer catches what the one before it cannot:

What goes wrong Noticed by Put right by A container stops or crashes Docker's events, at once Docker's restart policy A container runs but its page does not answer, or its health check fails Status asks each app's address as it loads (internal/api); the watchdog every 15 minutes The watchdog restarts it after two failed checks in a row, once in 6 hours at most (AUTO_HEAL); Fix it restarts, then recreates An update leaves an app unwell (unhealthy, restarting, or not answering) The watchdog, 20 minutes to 6 hours after the update Rolled back to the image it ran before, its updates held (AUTO_ROLLBACK) .env or a compose file changed, but the container still runs the old settings Compose's configuration hash on each container against what Compose would make now (api.Changed) Fix it (or up) recreates it Backups, indexing, or downloads crowd out the apps in use CPU weights: background containers get a quarter of the default share while the CPU is busy

Before an update, the app reads the GitHub releases of the project each image comes from (internal/releases: from releases: in x-homelab, the image's source label, or a ghcr.io name), newer than the version it runs, cached for 6 hours. Explain this sends an app's last lines, with passwords and tokens taken out, to the Ollama on this machine (internal/explain); nothing goes to a service outside the house.

The desktop app updates itself (internal/selfupdate, app/updates.go): it looks every 15 minutes and when its window comes forward, downloads a newer build ahead, and Update now (the line at the top of the window) moves the homelab files forward (homelab upgrade), then downloads the newest app build, the repository's Latest release (each build of main is one, v0.9.4-beta and on; the newest vX.Y.0 with UPDATE_CHANNEL=stable), checks its SHA-256 checksum, and replaces the running app: on a Mac the .app bundle, on Windows the files put in place by Windows' own PowerShell (as an administrator only when the app is in Program Files), on Linux the AppImage by a rename or the package through pkexec. Each attempt's steps go in update.log in the user's cache folder, and a build that did not go in place says why when the app opens again.

docs.title: A night in the homelab
docs.text:
When What Notes Every 15 minutes Watchdog Checks the container runtime, the proxy, the tunnel, every app's health and page, the database dumps' age, Duplicati's jobs, and the public names; alerts on the second failure in a row, restarts an app that hangs (once in 6 hours), and pings the outside heartbeat 01:00 Duplicati: Photos Immich's library, encrypted, into Proton Drive 03:30 homelab backup Dumps every database (consistent SQLite copies too), archives listed volumes, copies .env and the homelab's own records in data/ (the household, phones, Finances), and notes each app's image digest; so every database has a dump from just before the updates. It also measures photos per person and each app folder (data/storage.json), asks GitHub once a day for homelab updates, and on Sundays sends the weekly summary 04:00 The agent's nightly updates For each app with a newer image: stops it, dumps its databases and copies its data, then starts the new image and writes the version it now runs to .env (<APP>_DIGEST, which a start, a move, and a rebuild bring back); reports to ntfy. The watchdog then keeps each app's previous image for a week and rolls back an app that stays unwell or stops answering 05:00 Duplicati: Databases, Secrets The fresh dumps and .env, encrypted, into Proton Drive 05:30 Duplicati: AppData, Stack Data Every app's settings folders Weekly Duplicati: Infrastructure, Jellyfin, Calibre The stacks folder and the larger libraries

Details: Automation and Backups.

docs.title: Baseline and slot-in apps
docs.text:
• Baseline: everything without a profile. ./homelab up starts it, and the startup job runs it after every login.
  • Optional: services with profiles: [optional] are defined and documented but stay off until ./homelab install <app>.
  • New services: add a block to the category's file in compose/ (or a folder under stacks/ for an app with its own database) with an x-homelab block. The CLI then installs, proxies, publishes, documents, and monitors it like the rest. See Contributing.

docs.title: Security boundaries
docs.text:
Layer Control No open router ports Cloudflare Tunnel and Tailscale connect outward Tailnet (Home mode) Only devices signed in to your tailnet reach the apps; TAILNET_ADMIN_APPS=false keeps the admin apps on this machine only Edge Cloudflare's free managed ruleset Ingress (LAN and tunnel) Nginx Proxy Manager with the CrowdSec bouncer Detection CrowdSec reads every proxy log and pulls the community blocklist App ports Bound to 127.0.0.1 on the Mac; other devices go through the proxy Accounts 40-character passwords in Vaultwarden, 2FA where offered Secrets .env (mode 0600) and Vaultwarden What the app asks outside GitHub, for homelab and app updates and apps' release notes (project names only); the Ollama for Explain this is on this machine

See Security for details and Decisions for why.

docs.title: Known architectural limits
docs.text: Limit Effect Single host If the Mac is off or asleep, everything is down. homelab move out and move in carry it to a new machine, and homelab rebuild brings it back from the backups when the machine is lost. The awake job keeps it from sleeping while plugged in (KEEP_AWAKE). FileVault After a restart nothing runs until someone logs in (OrbStack and the jobs run in the login session). A router that cannot push DNS Each device's DNS is set to 192.168.1.10 by hand, or Tailscale's DNS setting points every Tailscale device at AdGuard (@adblock). No VLANs Everything shares the home LAN.

docs.title: Automation
docs.text: Everything that runs on its own, and how to check it is alive. Setup › Scheduled jobs (Install the jobs) sets them up; you do not need to run any of them by hand.

docs.title: Scheduled jobs
docs.text:
./homelab schedule install installs one background job, com.homelab.agent (homelab agent), so the system's login items list one homelab entry. On a Mac it is a LaunchAgent in ~/Library/LaunchAgents, run as you in your login session, which is where OrbStack's engine lives; on Linux, a systemd user unit; on Windows, the homelab-agent value in your user's Run key, started through homelab-run.exe so no window opens. The agent starts the menu bar item too when it is set to start at login. Each part below runs as its own process, so one failing leaves the rest running, and writes scripts/logs/<part>.log. A log that reaches 5 MB is split before the next run: its older half replaces <part>.1.log and the newer half stays, so the watchdog's, written every 15 minutes, stays under 8 MB for as long as the homelab runs. homelab report reads the two as one. Installing removes the five separate jobs older versions installed.

Part When Runs Purpose startup At login homelab up --apply --wait-media 15m Starts anything in the baseline that is not running; waits up to 15 minutes for the media drive first backup Daily 03:30, or as soon as the machine is awake after a missed night homelab backup --apply Dumps every database, archives listed volumes, notes each app's image by its digest, copies .env and the homelab's own records (data/*.json, data/people, data/sso, data/finance-receipts, data/finance-cards, data/members: the household, phones, Finances with its receipts and card pictures, and each member's own Finances) into recovery-staging, keeps the newest 7 of each; alerts duplicati-alerts on failure. Also measures the app folders and each person's photos (Status › What the apps keep), records the day's savings, sends the monthly restore-test and vault-export reminders and Finances' reminders (a bill due tomorrow, a paycheck under the cushion, a yearly renewal, stale balances; each can be turned off in Finances), asks GitHub for homelab updates (for the menu bar), and on Sundays sends the weekly summary (Monitoring) watchdog Every 15 minutes homelab watchdog --quiet Checks the runtime, every app, the database copies, the off-site jobs, the CrowdSec bouncer, free disk space, the apps' memory, and with a domain every public hostname (Monitoring); alerts tunnel-watchdog when something breaks or recovers, and keeps 7 days of counts for the % up this week badges. Keeps each updated app's previous image for a week, and rolls back an update that stays unwell backup-check Sundays from 07:00, or as soon as the machine is awake after homelab backup-check --quiet Duplicati's own Verify of each job that has run: a sample of its files at the destination downloaded and compared with the hashes it recorded. What it found is kept in data/backup-check.json; a damaged file makes the watchdog count that job as failing (and alert) and Backups say so beside it, until a check passes again. It runs beside the other parts, so the watchdog never waits for it awake Always (from login) homelab awake Keeps the machine from sleeping while it is plugged in, so the apps stay reachable; the screen still turns off. On a Mac this is caffeinate -s, which a laptop on battery ignores. KEEP_AWAKE=false (Settings, or unticking Keep this Mac/PC/computer awake while plugged in in the menu bar item's or tray icon's menu) lets it sleep as set; the job follows the setting within a minute, either way. homelab doctor warns when the machine would sleep with nothing keeping it up (it reads the sleep setting on a Mac, in GNOME, and on Windows). Whatever KEEP_AWAKE says, it also starts the apps the battery saver paused within a minute of the machine being plugged in (BATTERY_SAVER) serve Always (from login) homelab serve The phone companion on port 8099, home network and tailnet only (Phone companion); PHONE_COMPANION=false turns it off

Check the agent with ./homelab schedule status (installed, last exit code). Each part's own log tells you what it did.

docs.title: Nightly updates (the background agent)
docs.text: Property Value Who The background agent, as homelab update --all --nightly; no container holds Docker's socket for it (Watchtower did this until 0.14) Schedule Daily at 4:00 AM (WATCHTOWER_SCHEDULE, named for Watchtower), after the 03:30 backup; not while homelab updates pause holds them (UPDATES_PAUSED) Scope Every app with a newer image, except those updated by hand (below) and held ones Cleanup The watchdog keeps each app's previous image as homelab-rollback/<app>:previous for a week (homelab rollback <app> goes back to it), then removes it; other old images go at once Before Each app with a newer image is stopped, its databases dumped and its folders and named volumes copied (recovery-staging/before-update, up to UPDATE_COPY_LIMIT a folder), then started on the new image: the same as homelab update <app>. The version it now runs goes into .env (<APP>_DIGEST), so a start, a move, or a rebuild brings that version back rather than a newer one After An app updated 20 minutes to 6 hours ago that is unhealthy, restarting over and over, or whose page does not answer on two checks in a row is rolled back by the watchdog, its updates held, and an alert sent to the watchtower topic (AUTO_ROLLBACK=false turns this off). If it was never well after the update, its data from just before goes back with the image (nothing new can have been written); if it was well for a while, today's data stays and the alert says homelab rollback <app> --data puts the copy back What is new homelab updates notes <app> lists the releases newer than the version it runs, with the start of each one's notes; homelab update prints one line per app, and the app's Update shows the notes before it goes ahead. They come from the GitHub project the image names (its org.opencontainers.image.source label, a ghcr.io name, or releases: in the app's x-homelab), kept 6 hours in data/releases.json Held homelab updates hold <app> and release <app> (UPDATES_HELD), or an app's page › Nightly updates; a stopped app can be held too Its own days homelab updates days <app> sun, or an app's page › Only on Sundays: the nightly run on another day leaves it out; every puts it back to each night. Kept in data/update-days.json ({"immich": ["sun"]}), not in .env Alerts ntfy topic watchtower (the name it had under Watchtower, so phones already subscribed keep getting them): what each night updated, and each rollback

docs.title: Who updates what
docs.text: Every container falls into one of three groups, generated from the compose files: rebuilt (a locally built image), by hand (an x-homelab pin saying why, or a database or cache), or nightly (every other app). Each service note's table says the same for its app.

docs.title: Nightly (69)
docs.text:
The background agent runs ./homelab update --all at 4 AM (WATCHTOWER_SCHEDULE): for each app with a newer image it dumps its databases, copies its data, then pulls the image and recreates the container. Vaultwarden, Pocket ID, and CrowdSec (hold: 3) take a new image only once it has been out 3 days, counted from when the homelab first saw it, or once they have waited 14 days; ./homelab update <app> takes it at once.

docs.title: Duplicati (off-site backups)
docs.text:
Duplicati runs the jobs below. Create the backup jobs on the Setup screen (or ./homelab duplicati setup) makes them through Duplicati's API:

  • AES-256 encryption with the passphrases in .env. They are generated if missing: DUPLICATI_SECRETS_PASSPHRASE for Homelab Secrets, and DUPLICATI_PASSPHRASE for the rest.
  • Zip compression and smart retention (a version a day for a week, a week for a month, a month for a year).
  • Each job writes into its own folder in BACKUP_DESTINATION.

It leaves a job that already exists (by name) as it is. When a new job's folder already holds a backup (a rebuilt machine), it rebuilds the job's database from it (a repair) instead of a first run. It creates the photo, Jellyfin, books, and synced Files jobs only once their folder on this machine has something in it, and runs the small jobs once straight away. It first checks that Duplicati sees BACKUP_DESTINATION at /destination, and recreates Duplicati when it still has an older folder (after the setting changed). The sources are container paths. See Backups for the full mapping.
