Then check Status, and run Setup › Create the backup jobs so Duplicati finds the backup folder here. In Tailscale's admin console, remove the old machine if the new one shows up as a new device. With a domain, also move the router's reservation to the new machine and run Set up the domain. Once all is well, ./homelab uninstall on the old one.

docs.title: Scenario: another machine takes over
docs.text:
When the Mac is gone for a while, the Steam Machine or a Windows PC can run the homelab from the same repository and backups. The steps follow the full rebuild above; this is what differs. Host has each platform's runtime and jobs, and ISSUE-0012 and ISSUE-0013 in Known Issues what has not been tried there yet.

  1. One homelab at a time. If the Mac still runs, stop it first: ./homelab schedule remove, then quit OrbStack and turn off its Start at login. Two tunnels with the same token split public visitors between the machines, and two Duplicatis writing to the same backup folders damage each other's databases.
  2. The runtime and the app: Docker Engine with the compose plugin on Linux (loginctl enable-linger $USER so the jobs run without a login), Docker Desktop with WSL 2 on Windows. Then the app for that machine from the release run: the AppImage on the Steam Machine (Setup › Add to the app menu), the installer on Windows. Each carries the CLI.
  3. The files: make the homelab folder (Setup › Set it up for me, or git clone the repository; on Windows, outside OneDrive), then ./homelab rebuild <this machine's copy of the backup folder> (homelab.cmd rebuild on Windows), or restore .env and the data by hand as in steps 3 and 4 above. The rebuild stops at the first folder in .env this machine does not have: change the folder settings in Settings to this machine's folders: MEDIA_ROOT, DOWNLOADS_ROOT, and IMMICH_UPLOAD_LOCATION to where the media drive mounts (on the Steam Machine under /run/media/, on Windows a drive letter), and JELLYFIN_DATA_DIR to the new Jellyfin's data folder. Settings › This machine › Storage then lists the drive with its free space. Then run the rebuild again to carry on (by hand: change them before up).
  4. Backups: BACKUP_DESTINATION to this machine's synced copy of the same cloud drive folder (Setup › Backups leave this machine offers the ones it finds). On Linux, Setup finds ~/Dropbox, ~/OneDrive, and mounted external drives; for a cloud drive with no Linux app, use an rclone mount, and until then a local folder (the backups then stay on the machine).
  5. The address (with a domain): move the router's reservation for 192.168.1.10 to the new machine, so every device's DNS setting and the AdGuard rewrite keep working. (./homelab domain setup finds the address itself, but each phone and computer has 192.168.1.10 typed in.)
  6. Start it: ./homelab up, restore the databases (below), install Jellyfin the way ./homelab install jellyfin says for this platform and restore Homelab Jellyfin into it, then ./homelab tailnet setup (Home mode) or ./homelab domain setup (with a domain), ./homelab notify setup, ./homelab schedule install, and ./homelab duplicati setup (it repairs each job from its existing backup).
  7. Check: ./homelab doctor, ./homelab watchdog, the app's Status and Setup screens, and a few apps from a phone on mobile data.

To go back, do the same in reverse: stop the standby (./homelab schedule remove, then stop Docker and its start at login), restore its newest backups onto the Mac (or let the Mac's jobs repair from them), and move the reservation back.

Keeping a standby ready takes a few minutes a month: git pull on it, its runtime installed but the homelab stopped, and the newest app build. Once a year, a timed takeover on a quiet weekend, with the restore test's timing (Backups) as the first number on record, shows how long the household would wait.

docs.title: Scenario: Nginx Proxy Manager
docs.text:
Only when the proxy is installed (always with a domain). Never pull jc21/nginx-proxy-manager; it lacks the bouncer.

  1. ./homelab update nginx-proxy-manager (rebuilds the image and recreates the container). Its data and certificates come back from data/appdata/nginx-proxy-manager.
  2. Check the bouncer: ./homelab compose crowdsec exec crowdsec cscli bouncers list shows nginx_proxy_manager with a recent pull.
  3. Test a ban (see Runbooks).

docs.title: Scenario: a database (Paperless example)
docs.text:
1. Stop the app, keep the database running: ./homelab stop paperless.
  2. Restore the latest dump:
gunzip -c recovery-staging/databases/paperless-db/paperless-db-<stamp>.sql.gz \
  | ./homelab compose paperless exec -T paperless-db psql -U paperless -d postgres
  1. ./homelab start paperless, then open https://docs.example.com and search for a known document.

MoneyMatter is the same with moneymatter-db and user budget_tracker; restore the attachments archive into its volume:

./homelab stop moneymatter-backend
docker run --rm -i -v homelab_budget_tracker_moneymatter-attachments:/data alpine:3 \
  tar xzf - -C /data < recovery-staging/volumes/moneymatter-attachments/moneymatter-attachments-<stamp>.tar.gz
./homelab start moneymatter-backend

docs.title: Scenario: Immich
docs.text:
Immich's database must use ghcr.io/immich-app/postgres with the same vectorchord/pgvecto.rs tag that is pinned in stacks/immich/compose.yaml. A stock Postgres image cannot restore it.

  1. ./homelab compose immich stop immich-server immich-machine-learning
  2. Make sure immich-database is running and empty (a fresh volume), then restore, fixing the search path the way Immich's own instructions do:
gunzip -c recovery-staging/databases/immich-database/immich-database-<stamp>.sql.gz \
  | sed "s/SELECT pg_catalog.set_config('search_path', '', false);/SELECT pg_catalog.set_config('search_path', 'public, pg_catalog', true);/g" \
  | ./homelab compose immich exec -T immich-database psql -U postgres -d postgres
  1. Photos come back from the Homelab Photos job into IMMICH_UPLOAD_LOCATION if the drive was lost.
  2. ./homelab compose immich up -d, then open https://photos.example.com.

Immich also keeps its own nightly database backups in IMMICH_UPLOAD_LOCATION/backups.

docs.title: Scenario: Vaultwarden
docs.text:
1. ./homelab stop vaultwarden
  2. Restore data/appdata/vaultwarden from Homelab AppData (into /staging/restore, then copy).
  3. ./homelab start vaultwarden; sign in on the web vault before trusting the phone apps.

docs.title: Scenario: Cloudflare Tunnel
docs.text:
With a domain only.

  1. ./homelab status and ./homelab logs cloudflared.
  2. Check TUNNEL_TOKEN in .env, then ./homelab restart cloudflared.
  3. If the token is lost: in Cloudflare Zero Trust › Networks › Tunnels, open the tunnel and copy its token again (or create a new tunnel), update .env, ./homelab up, and run ./homelab domain setup to rewrite the public hostnames.

docs.title: Post-recovery checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] ./homelab status shows every baseline app running and healthy
  • [ ] Setup shows every step done (or ./homelab setup)
  • [ ] Home mode: the apps open at their tailnet addresses on a phone with Tailscale on
  • [ ] With a domain: *.example.com resolves to 192.168.1.10 on the Mac and on a phone; Status › Protection says bans are enforced (otherwise Fix) and a test ban returns 403
  • [ ] ./homelab watchdog passes; an app loads from a phone on mobile data
  • [ ] ./homelab schedule status shows the agent installed
  • [ ] Duplicati jobs complete without errors
  • [ ] ntfy test messages arrive (./homelab notify test)
  • [ ] Settings › People and Phones list the household and its phones, and Finances shows the household's plan

docs.title: Environment
docs.text: Property Value Runtime OrbStack (Linux VM on the Mac), Start at login on; Docker Engine on Linux, Docker Desktop on Windows (Host) Engine and Compose The runtime's Docker Engine and Compose (2.20 or newer required) Compose files compose/<category>.yaml (one project each) and stacks/*/compose.yaml; compose.yaml holds the catalog How the homelab talks to it Reads (the containers, their events, what they use, the engine's info) and commands run in containers go to the engine's own API over its socket (Docker Desktop's named pipe on Windows), found as the docker CLI finds it; the CLI answers whenever the API fails, and DOCKER_API=off keeps the CLI. Starting, stopping, and updating apps is docker compose. ./homelab doctor says which is in use Shared network homelab (external; created by ./homelab up) Settings ~/Homelab/.env for every project Architecture Apple Silicon (arm64); MoneyMatter's Intel-only images run under Rosetta unless MONEYMATTER_*_IMAGE names native builds

docs.title: Networking facts
docs.text:
• Containers on homelab reach each other by service name: nginx-proxy-manager, immich-server, paperless, ntfy, crowdsec.
  • host.docker.internal is the host itself. Only native apps (Jellyfin, the phone companion) are reached that way.
  • 127.0.0.1 inside a container is the container, never the host.
  • App ports are published on the host's 127.0.0.1 for local use; only the proxy (80/443) and DNS (53) listen on the LAN. In Home mode the tailscale container serves the apps on the tailnet (data/appdata/tailscale/serve.json).
  • Database services are not on homelab at all; only their own stack can reach them.

docs.title: Compose projects
docs.text:
Project Notes homelab_<category> One per category (compose/<category>.yaml): the single-container apps, baseline and optional (profiles: [optional]) homelab_cloudflare cloudflared; waits for TUNNEL_TOKEN homelab_immich Four containers; pinned database and Redis images homelab_paperless Three containers homelab_budget_tracker MoneyMatter, five containers (folder budget-tracker, not money) homelab_beszel, homelab_dawarich, homelab_docmost, homelab_firefly_iii, homelab_frigate, homelab_ghostfolio, homelab_karakeep, homelab_linkwarden, homelab_nextcloud, homelab_romm, homelab_tandoor Optional apps with their own database or helpers (one folder each under stacks/) homelab_custom Your own apps (stacks/custom/compose.yaml, written by homelab custom add; not in git)

Run Compose through the CLI so the right folder, project name, and .env are used:

./homelab compose paperless ps
./homelab compose security logs --tail 50 crowdsec

docs.title: Operational rules
docs.text:
• Always go through ./homelab (or ./homelab compose), not a bare docker compose in a stack folder.
  • Never update Nginx Proxy Manager by pulling an image; ./homelab update nginx-proxy-manager rebuilds it.
  • Never run docker volume prune or docker system prune --volumes: databases live in named volumes.
  • Never mount /var/run/docker.sock into a new service; read-only consumers use docker-socket-proxy. The one exception is the optional Beszel agent, which runs on the host's network and cannot reach the proxy by name, mounts it read-only.
  • Never bind a port to a specific LAN address.
  • Use --remove-orphans only on purpose.

docs.title: Container standards
docs.text:
Every service starts from the shared settings in its file:

x-service: &service
  restart: unless-stopped
  security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
  logging:
    driver: json-file
    options: { max-size: 10m, max-file: "3" }

and, when its image must not update nightly, an x-homelab pin saying why. If an image refuses to start with no-new-privileges, remove it for that one service and say why in the note.

Background work yields the CPU to the apps people are using: Duplicati, Immich's machine learning, qBittorrent, Dawarich's Sidekiq worker, Karakeep's crawler browser, and Speedtest Tracker run with cpu_shares: 256 (a quarter of Docker's default 1024), and so do the throwaway containers the nightly backup starts for dumps and archives. Shares only count while the CPU is busy, and only between containers: on an idle machine, background work still gets all of it, and while someone uses an app, its container comes first. Native apps (Jellyfin) are outside this. Give a new background service the same line.

docs.title: Custom image
docs.text: Property Value Image homelab/nginx-proxy-manager-crowdsec:<NPM_VERSION> Base jc21/nginx-proxy-manager (NPM_VERSION in .env) Adds lua-cs-bouncer v1.0.19, lua-resty-http v0.17.2, ban/captcha templates, crowdsec_openresty.conf in /etc/nginx/conf.d, an entrypoint that writes the bouncer config Source dockerfiles/npm-crowdsec/ Update Bump NPM_VERSION, then ./homelab update nginx-proxy-manager Nightly updates Left out (built locally)

docs.title: Maintenance
docs.text:
./homelab status
./homelab logs <app> --tail 100
./homelab fix                    # restart what is down or unwell, recreate apps whose settings changed; with a low disk, remove unused images and build cache
docker system df                 # disk used by images, containers, volumes
docker image prune               # unused images only (safe)

./homelab uninstall removes every app's containers and images, the images the homelab made itself (homelab-rollback/*, kept to undo an update, and homelab/sqlite), any container of a homelab_ project no compose file lists any more, and the homelab network; volumes stay unless --data. Containers that are not the homelab's stay, and it names them; an image one of them uses stays too (Resource is still in use). --everything-else removes those too: every container, volume, image, and network left (Docker's own bridge, host, and none stay), and the build cache.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text: Every setting lives in ~/Homelab/.env, read by every Compose project. .env.example in the repository is the template.

docs.title: How .env is managed
docs.text:
• ./homelab up (or install) creates .env from .env.example with mode 0600. It sets PUID, PGID, and TZ from this machine, and replaces every __REPLACE_ME__ with a generated secret.
  • Later runs add keys that are new in .env.example and never change values you already have.
  • Copy each generated secret into Vaultwarden as homelab - <service> <credential>.
  • .env is never committed (.gitignore), never printed by the CLI, and never pasted into notes or chats. ./homelab backup copies it into recovery-staging/secrets for the encrypted Homelab Secrets job.
  • Never add COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME or COMPOSE_PROFILES: they would override each stack's own project name and the optional profile.

docs.title: This machine
docs.text: Variable Default Purpose TZ this machine's timezone Timezone for every container PUID, PGID your user and group (501, 20 on a Mac) File ownership for linuxserver.io images and Paperless BIND_IP 127.0.0.1 Where app ports listen. Keep it: other devices go through the proxy LAN_BIND_IP 0.0.0.0 Where the proxy (80/443) and DNS (53) listen; follows the machine's address ADGUARD_DNS_BIND_IP empty Where AdGuard Home's DNS (53) listens when not LAN_BIND_IP. On Linux, where systemd-resolved holds 127.0.0.53:53 (Ubuntu, Fedora), a new .env sets it to this machine's address, since a 0.0.0.0 bind would collide; homelab doctor warns when the address has changed DOCKER_SOCKET empty Docker's socket for the apps that talk to Docker (the socket proxy, Beszel's agent); empty is /var/run/docker.sock. With Docker run as you (SteamOS, homelab runtime install), a new .env sets your own, /run/user/<id>/docker.sock, and PUID/PGID to 0: a container's root is your account then, so what the apps write is yours DOCKER_API auto How the homelab reads the containers, their events, what they use, and the engine's info, and runs commands in them (the database copies, CrowdSec's): auto talks to the engine's API over its socket, or Docker Desktop's named pipe on Windows (found as the docker CLI finds it: DOCKER_HOST, the current context, OrbStack, Docker Desktop, a rootless engine, /var/run/docker.sock, \\.\pipe\docker_engine), and uses the docker command whenever that fails, resting the API 10 minutes; off uses the docker command only. Starting, stopping, and updating apps is docker compose either way. homelab doctor says which is in use, and the last fallback HOST_GATEWAY empty How containers reach this machine's own apps (Jellyfin, the phone companion, Ollama) as host.docker.internal; empty is Docker's host-gateway. With Docker run as you, a new .env sets this machine's address, since host-gateway is then Docker's own namespace, not this machine; homelab doctor warns when the address has changed KEEP_AWAKE true The awake job keeps this machine from sleeping while plugged in (the screen still sleeps). false: it sleeps as set. The menu bar item's (tray icon's) Keep this Mac/PC/computer awake while plugged in sets it, ticked while it is on; the awake job follows a change within a minute, and Setup says which it is BATTERY_SAVER true On a laptop running on battery, the watchdog pauses the heavy background apps (internal/battery lists them), and the awake job starts them again within a minute of being plugged in (the watchdog too, every 15 minutes). One that will not start stays paused for the next try without holding back the rest. Tdarr in the middle of a video finishes it first, taking no new one, and pauses within a minute of being done; its workers come back on power. false keeps them running PHONE_COMPANION true The serve job runs the phone companion on port 8099 (home network and tailnet only; phones pair with homelab phone pair). false: off HOMELAB_BASELINE empty small: up starts only updates, backups, and alerts, and you pick the rest (folders the desktop app makes). Empty or full: every app without a profile

docs.title: Storage
docs.text: Variable Default Purpose MEDIA_ROOT /Volumes/Media The media drive: music, tv, movies, Books, comics, audiobooks, podcasts DOWNLOADS_ROOT /Volumes/Media/downloads Download folder shared by qBittorrent and the *arr apps IMMICH_UPLOAD_LOCATION /Volumes/Media/photos Immich's photo library BACKUP_DESTINATION ./backups Duplicati's destination: a Homelab Backups folder in a cloud drive's synced folder or on an external drive, which Setup › Backups leave this machine offers (Backups) JELLYFIN_DATA_DIR ~/.local/share/jellyfin Native Jellyfin's data folder, backed up by Duplicati SYNC_ROOT ./data/sync Syncthing's shared folders (backed up only if you add them to a Duplicati job) KOPIA_REPOSITORY ./backups-kopia Where Kopia (optional, the second backup beside Duplicati) keeps its repository: best another drive, never Duplicati's folder. Setup's A second copy with Kopia step, or homelab kopia repository <folder>, sets it (Kopia) NAVIDROME_MUSIC_PATH empty Where Navidrome sees the music folder in its container. Empty: the same path as on this machine, so playlists with full paths keep working; Windows sets /music KIWIX_ZIM_ROOT, NEXTCLOUD_DATA, FRIGATE_RECORDINGS not in the template Optional folders for Kiwix's libraries, Nextcloud's files, and Frigate's recordings, when they should not be in their default places (MEDIA_ROOT/kiwix, appdata/nextcloud/data, MEDIA_ROOT/frigate). Add the line to .env yourself

docs.title: Domain, Tailscale, and Cloudflare
docs.text:
Every new homelab starts in Home mode: HOMELAB_DOMAIN is empty, and a domain is optional.

Variable Default Purpose HOMELAB_DOMAIN empty Empty: Home mode, every app at https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:<port> (Tailscale). A domain such as example.com gives every app https://<subdomain>.<domain> through the proxy instead. An existing .env keeps its domain AUTO_DOMAIN true With a domain, each new app gets its proxy host (and tunnel hostname, if public) as soon as it is installed, once Set up the domain has run. false: only when you run Set up the domain TAILSCALE_AUTHKEY empty Optional secret. A reusable auth key signs Tailscale in without the browser; without one, homelab tailnet login opens Tailscale's sign-in page TAILSCALE_ROUTES this machine's network (192.168.1.0/24 in the template) The home network Tailscale makes reachable (approve the route in Tailscale's admin) TAILSCALE_EXTRA_ARGS empty Extra flags for tailscale up: --login-server=https://headscale.example.com signs in to a tailnet on your own Headscale server instead of Tailscale's. The nightly test uses it for a fake tailnet TAILSCALE_HOST empty Home mode only: this machine's tailnet name, written by homelab tailnet setup TAILNET_ADMIN_APPS true Home mode: false keeps the admin apps (the proxy, AdGuard Home, Duplicati, Dozzle) off the tailnet, so only this machine opens them; the household's apps stay on it POCKET_ID_API_KEY generated Pocket ID's static API key (STATIC_API_KEY), which homelab sso setup uses to make the apps' sign-in clients. A secret JELLYFIN_API_KEY empty A Jellyfin API key (Dashboard › API Keys). With it, homelab person makes each person's Jellyfin account, gives them a new password, and turns the account off when they are removed. A secret; Settings › Test checks it NAVIDROME_ADMIN_USER, NAVIDROME_ADMIN_PASSWORD empty A Navidrome administrator's login, best one of its own (homelab), for the same in Navidrome. Navidrome has no API keys. The homelab never changes this login's own password SSO_HOST empty Pocket ID's name (id.<domain>), written by homelab sso setup; the apps that sign in with it map it to this machine, so they reach it through the proxy VAULTWARDEN_URL, PAPERLESS_URL, KARAKEEP_URL, MONEYMATTER_URL, POCKET_ID_URL, NTFY_URL, NAVIDROME_URL, and the other *_URL settings empty The address an app is opened at, for the apps that need to know it (sign-in, links). Empty: https://<subdomain>.<domain>. Home mode writes the tailnet address, and Set up the domain clears it again (x-homelab url) CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN empty Secret. For the wildcard certificate and the tunnel's public hostnames. Permissions: Zone:Read, DNS:Edit, Cloudflare Tunnel:Edit TUNNEL_TOKEN empty Secret. The tunnel's token; cloudflared stays off until it is set COMPANION_PROXY_KEY empty Made by Set up the domain: the phone companion's proxy host sends it, so the companion knows a phone reached it over https and not over the Wi-Fi (Security, N25). A secret COMPANION_ACCESS_TEAM, COMPANION_ACCESS_AUD, COMPANION_ACCESS_CLIENT_ID, COMPANION_ACCESS_CLIENT_SECRET, COMPANION_AWAY_HOST empty The iPhone app away from home through the tunnel (ADR-0023), made by Setup's Reach Finances away from home (homelab phone away): the Cloudflare Access team and application, the household's service token (its secret given to a phone only when it pairs at home), and the companion's name through the tunnel. Empty: the companion answers only at home and on the tailnet

docs.title: Nginx Proxy Manager and CrowdSec
docs.text: Variable Default Purpose NPM_VERSION 2.16.0 Upstream version the custom image is built from NPM_HTTP_PORT, NPM_HTTPS_PORT 80, 443 Proxy ports on the LAN NPM_ADMIN_PORT 8181 Proxy admin UI on this machine NPM_API_EMAIL homelab@<domain> The automation account, created on first start; also the Let's Encrypt account email NPM_API_PASSWORD generated Secret. Keep 2FA off for this account; use a separate personal admin with 2FA CROWDSEC_BOUNCER_KEY generated Secret. Shared by CrowdSec (registers the bouncer) and the proxy (uses it) CROWDSEC_ENROLL_KEY empty Optional. Enrolls the engine in the CrowdSec console

docs.title: AdGuard Home
docs.text: Variable Default Purpose ADGUARD_PORT 3003 Admin UI after setup ADGUARD_SETUP_PORT 3002 First-run wizard ADGUARD_USER, ADGUARD_PASSWORD admin, empty AdGuard's login: homelab adguard setup makes it in the first-run wizard, or put in the one you made there. The CLI uses it to add the *.domain rewrite. The password is a secret

docs.title: Notifications and updates
docs.text: Variable Default Purpose NTFY_PORT 9293 ntfy on this machine NTFY_PUBLISH_TOKEN, NTFY_PUBLISH_AUTH empty Secrets, filled in by homelab notify setup: the publishers' access token, and the same as an ?auth= parameter for publishers that only take a URL NTFY_READ_TOKEN empty Secret, made by notify setup: read-only access for the app's list of recent alerts DESKTOP_ALERTS true Alerts also show on this machine's screen (Notification Center on a Mac). false: the phone only QUIET_HOURS 22-7 The night: alerts between these hours (22:00 to 07:00) reach the phone at ntfy's low priority, without a sound, unless serious (the vault unreachable, backups failing for two days). 13-15 for other hours; off sounds every alert HELPER_EMAIL empty Who helps you with the homelab: Email it to my helper writes to them with the diagnostics report HEARTBEAT_URL empty An external heartbeat (such as a healthchecks.io ping URL, period and grace 15 minutes). The watchdog pings it every run and pings /fail when something is down WATCHTOWER_SCHEDULE 0 0 4 * * * When the background agent runs the nightly updates (a cron with seconds): 4:00 AM daily, after the 03:30 backup. Named for Watchtower, which ran them before SOCKET_PROXY_VERSION v0.5.0 docker-socket-proxy's version, chosen by hand: it controls Docker for Homarr and Dozzle, so it never updates itself nightly (Security, M6) BESZEL_AGENT_VERSION 0.21.1 The Beszel agent's version, chosen by hand: it holds Docker's socket, so it never updates itself nightly (Security, N18) FRIGATE_VERSION, KOPIA_VERSION, NEXTCLOUD_VERSION 0.18.2, 0.23.1, 35 Kept until you choose a newer one: read the release notes, change the setting, then ./homelab update <app>. For Nextcloud this is the major version (the nightly updates bring its fixes); move it one major at a time UPDATE_CHANNEL testing What homelab upgrade and the app's update get: testing (every build of main, numbered v0.9.4-beta and on) or stable (only a new minor or major version, vX.Y.0). Before the first such version, stable has nothing to move to. Either way a git checkout moves only to a release whose build provenance checks out UPDATES_PAUSED not in the template Written by homelab updates pause (removed by resume): the agent runs no nightly update until it is resumed UPDATE_COPY_LIMIT 2GB The largest folder or volume homelab update copies before an app's update, for its rollback (500MB, 10GB; 0 copies any size). A larger one is left out and named in the update's output; databases are dumped whatever their size AUTO_ROLLBACK true The watchdog rolls back an app that stays unhealthy, keeps restarting, or does not answer 20 minutes to 6 hours after its update, and holds its updates; with its data from before the update only if it was never well after it. false: it only alerts AUTO_HEAL true The watchdog restarts an app that is unhealthy or not answering on two checks in a row, and makes one whose container is gone again (once in 6 hours at most); it stops an app Docker restarted 3 times in an hour, with its last log lines in the alert. false: it only alerts OLLAMA_MODEL empty The Ollama model that explains logs (Explain this under an app's log, homelab logs <app> --explain), such as llama3.2. Empty: the first of Llama, Qwen, Gemma, Mistral, or Phi that Ollama has. Ollama's own OLLAMA_HOST says where it runs (this machine by default) <APP>_DIGEST (PAPERLESS_DIGEST, VAULTWARDEN_DIGEST, …) not in the template The version each app the nightly update moves forward runs: its image and that image's digest (ghcr.io/paperless-ngx/paperless-ngx:latest@sha256:…). Written by homelab update, a rollback, and the watchdog when what runs changes; homelab up, install, a move, and a rebuild start that version again, so a restore or a new machine opens the data with the version that wrote it. A version you choose by hand (IMMICH_VERSION) wins: a kept line for another image is left alone until the app runs the new one. Delete a line to let that app start on its newest version UPDATES_HELD empty Apps left out of nightly updates (after a rollback, or homelab updates hold). Written by the CLI; homelab updates release <app> takes one off

docs.title: Tidy Up
docs.text:
Tidy Up sorts, tags, and shrinks the libraries on the media drive (MEDIA_ROOT). Settings (its Tidy Up section) changes them.

Variable Default Purpose TIDY_UP true false turns its background work off (the inbox, Tdarr's finished work, and the nightly sweep); the screen still works TIDY_INBOX, TIDY_INBOX_FOLDERS true, empty File what finishes downloading in Downloads and DOWNLOADS_ROOT into the libraries; other folders to watch instead, separated by ; TIDY_INBOX_WHEN arrive When the inbox files: arrive (checked every minute), daily (once a day, after 03:00), or manual (only on Tidy up now) TIDY_SCRUB true Every night at 03:00, leftovers whose film, song, or book is gone (posters, .nfo and subtitle files, empty folders) go to the Trash TIDY_TDARR_REST, TIDY_ARR_REST true Tdarr, and the download apps (Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Prowlarr, Bazarr, FlareSolverr, qBittorrent, Gluetun), rest stopped while they have nothing to do, freeing their memory; false keeps them running TIDY_KEEP_LANGUAGES eng The audio and subtitle languages films and episodes keep (ISO 639-2: eng, jpn); Tdarr removes the rest when it shrinks them TIDY_VIDEO_CODEC hevc What Tdarr shrinks video to: hevc (plays everywhere) or av1 (smaller, newer players) TIDY_SHRINK_LOSSLESS true New lossless music (FLAC, WAV) is stored as 256k AAC, about a fifth of the size; false keeps it lossless TIDY_LYRICS embed Lyrics inside each song file (embed) or in a .lrc file beside it (lrc) TIDY_MUSIC_ENGINE empty Where beets runs: local (this computer, fastest) or container; empty picks local when Python can make its own environment here PLEX_URL, PLEX_TOKEN, PLEX_PATH_MAP empty A Plex server to tell about each new or changed file, its token, and how its folders map to this computer's (/Volumes/Media=/data) AUDIOBOOKSHELF_API_KEY empty Audiobookshelf's API token (Settings › Users › your user), so Tidy Up tells it about new files TDARR_API_KEY generated Tidy Up's key to Tdarr, which Tdarr takes as its own when it starts. A secret TDARR_USER, TDARR_PASSWORD empty An older Tdarr's sign-in: made by Tidy Up (user homelab) when Tdarr had none; one you made first goes here

docs.title: App ports
docs.text: Each app's port on this machine is a variable named <APP>_PORT (for example VAULTWARDEN_PORT=8087). The installer moves a port if something else already holds it and writes the new value back. Inventory shows the current addresses.

docs.title: Adding a variable
docs.text:
1. Add it to .env.example (secrets as __REPLACE_ME__, with a comment saying what it is for).
  2. Add it to this page.
  3. ./homelab up adds it to .env. ./homelab validate fails if a requires entry, or a port variable without a default, is missing from .env.example.

docs.title: Everyday tasks
docs.text: What you do with the homelab once it runs: each in the app, then the same from a terminal in the homelab folder (homelab.cmd on Windows). New here? The tour shows each screen first.

docs.title: The common ones
docs.text: To… In the app In a terminal More Add an app Choose apps › tick it › Install ./homelab install <app> Services Open an app on a phone Status › the app's page › Open on a phone (a QR code) ./homelab status lists the addresses Inventory Put right what is down Status › Fix it (the plan first) ./homelab fix Troubleshooting Read an app's log, in plain words Status › the app's page › its log › Explain this ./homelab logs <app> --explain Monitoring Update an app now, or undo an update The app's page › Check for an update, or Roll back ./homelab update <app>, ./homelab rollback <app> Automation Pause the nightly updates Status › Nightly updates › Pause ./homelab updates pause (and resume) Automation See what's left after each paycheck Finances in the sidebar (on a phone too, once allowed in Settings › Phones) — Phone companion File a download into the right library, or free space Tidy Up › Inbox › Tidy up now, or a library's tab ./homelab media inbox --apply, ./homelab media <library> scan Tidy Up Back up now, or prove a restore works Backups › Back up now, Test a restore ./homelab backup --apply, ./homelab restore-test --auto Backups Update Homelab Wizard and the homelab Update now on the line at the top of the window ./homelab upgrade Upgrading Add someone in the household Settings › People › Add a person ./homelab person add "Anna Smith" --email anna@example.com docs.title: Add your own app, or one to the catalog
docs.text:
The quick way, for any container image: Add your own app at the bottom of the app's Choose apps screen, or

./homelab custom add wiki --image ghcr.io/requarks/wiki:2 --port 3000 --volume /wiki/data --install

It goes into stacks/custom/compose.yaml with the same metadata as the catalog, a free port, an address on your tailnet (or https://wiki.example.com with a domain), and its folders under data/appdata/wiki, which the nightly backup already covers. Like .env, the custom stack is yours alone: git ignores it, so git pull keeps working. ./homelab custom lists your apps; ./homelab custom remove wiki takes one out (its data stays).

Adding an app to the catalog itself (with its note, bundles, and wiring):

  myapp:
    <<: *service
    image: example/myapp:latest
    profiles: [optional]
    ports:
      - ${BIND_IP:-127.0.0.1}:${MYAPP_PORT:-8123}:8080
    volumes:
      - ./data/appdata/myapp:/config
    x-homelab:
      name: My App
      category: documents
      description: What it is for
      subdomain: myapp
      web: 8080

./homelab docs && make check          # creates its note, checks everything
./homelab install myapp               # starts it
./homelab domain setup                # with a domain: https://myapp.example.com

Multi-container apps get their own stacks/<name>/ folder. The full guide and checklist are in Contributing.

docs.title: Commands at a glance
docs.text:
./homelab                       # interactive menu
./homelab help                  # every command
./homelab status                # what runs, health, addresses
./homelab doctor                # anything wrong with this machine, the runtime, disk space, or .env
./homelab install '*-arr'       # slot in apps by name, alias, bundle, or category
./homelab update <app>          # what is new first, then dump its database, pull (or rebuild), and recreate
./homelab updates notes <app>   # the release notes newer than the version it runs
./homelab rollback <app>        # back to the image before its last update
./homelab fix                   # restart what is down or unwell, apply changed settings, reconnect the proxy to CrowdSec
./homelab logs <app> --explain  # what its log says, in plain words, from the Ollama on this machine
./homelab upgrade               # the newest homelab files, then up (the app's Update now)
./homelab tailnet setup         # Home mode: every app's address on the tailnet (signs in if needed)
./homelab domain setup          # with a domain: proxy hosts, LAN DNS, certificate, tunnel hostnames
./homelab domain resolver       # with a domain: this machine finds every app by name
./homelab backup                # database dumps, volume archives, .env copy
./homelab watchdog              # every app and address checked, a hung app restarted, ntfy alerts
./homelab digest                # this week's summary, as on Status
./homelab media                 # Tidy Up: each library, and the engines (music, books, movies, tv, audiobooks)
./homelab schedule install      # the background agent (launchd, systemd, or the Windows Run key)
./homelab person add "Anna Smith" --email anna@example.com   # an account, a welcome page, a start-page tab
./homelab sso setup             # the apps sign in with Pocket ID
./homelab phone pair            # the phone companion
./homelab export                # everyone's data in open formats, in one folder
./homelab move out              # to a new machine (then move in there)
./homelab rebuild <folder>      # the machine is lost: everything back from Duplicati's backups
./homelab report                # a diagnostics file to share, every secret removed
./homelab compose immich ps     # docker compose for any project

Commands that change something show a plan first and ask (or need --apply when not in a terminal). --json gives one object per line, each with "schema": 1, for scripts and apps. Full list, with how to pick apps (@arr, cat:media, --exclude): Commands.

docs.title: Take the homelab off this machine
docs.text:
In the app: Settings › This Mac (This PC, This machine) › Take the homelab off this machine. Tick what else goes, Review what goes… shows the plan, and nothing happens until you type uninstall (delete everything with the last box ticked). The same from a terminal:

./homelab uninstall                    # the plan first; --apply removes the containers, images (the update undo copies too), scheduled jobs, and the tray icon at login
./homelab uninstall --data             # ...and the apps' data, and signs this machine's homelab out of the tailnet
./homelab uninstall --folder           # ...and the whole homelab folder, .env included (print the recovery kit first)
./homelab uninstall --backups          # ...and the backups on this machine; a backup folder in a cloud drive always stays
./homelab uninstall --app              # ...and Homelab Wizard itself, with its settings and downloads
./homelab uninstall --everything-else  # ...and every other container, image, and volume in the runtime, the homelab's or not

Combine them as you like (--folder --backups --app takes everything of the homelab off). In a terminal, --folder, --backups, and --everything-else are typed out before anything goes. The media drive is never touched, --folder alone keeps the backups inside the folder (./backups by default), --backups deletes only the backups' own files and folders (anything else on a backup drive stays), and a backup folder in a cloud drive (Proton Drive, iCloud Drive, Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox) is never deleted: another machine's homelab may use it, and the deletion would sync. --app moves the app to the Trash on a Mac, runs its uninstaller on Windows (Windows asks for approval), deletes the AppImage, or names the package command on Linux (it needs your password). With a domain, ./homelab domain resolver --undo takes back this machine's name lookups first. The container runtime itself stays; the last lines say how to remove it.

docs.title: Feature Roadmap
docs.text:
The features that would make Homelab Wizard a pleasure to use, grouped by area: the small touches (a right-click menu, an undo, a hover that answers a question) as much as the big screens. The Roadmap says what each version must prove; this page is the list of what to build, to pick from.

Each item has a size and a status:

  • Size: S is a day or less, M a few days, L a week or more, or a piece of the backend that does not exist yet.
  • Status: Idea (only written here), Mocked up (drawn, not built), Next (the next batch), or Built (in the app, with the pull request).

The Finances screen's history and rules are in the Finances loop's file; its unfinished items are under Finances below.
