docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
A script for testing a new build on the Mac, in order. Each step says what to do and what you should see. When something does not match, check Troubleshooting, then stop there and make a report:

./homelab report

It writes scripts/logs/report-<date>.txt with doctor, status, the setup checklist, the jobs, Duplicati's jobs, the weekly summary, the updates waiting, which settings are set, and the logs of anything unwell. Passwords, tokens, and anything shaped like one are replaced with [redacted …]. Read it through, then share the file or paste it. Never paste .env itself, a token, or a password. The app has the same thing as Settings › This Mac › Make a diagnostics report.

Type each command as shown, one line at a time. In zsh a # on the line is not a comment, so there are none here.

docs.title: 1. Bring the Mac up to date
docs.text:
If you tested an earlier build, read Upgrading first: it lists what changed and the few steps it asks of you.

cd ~/Homelab
./homelab upgrade
./homelab version
./homelab doctor
  • upgrade lists what changed and what is new, asks, moves the folder forward, and runs up afterwards. Update now in the app does the same, and updates the app too. (A clone from before upgrade existed: git checkout main and git pull once instead.)
  • version prints the repository's version; the first run after an update builds the CLI ("Building the homelab CLI...").
  • doctor ends without ✗ lines. Expected ! warnings: a VPN if one is on, and settings you have not filled in yet.
  • If OrbStack still lists a homelab_core project, upgrade moves the containers into their category projects (homelab migrate, a backup first). OrbStack then lists them grouped as homelab_network, homelab_security, homelab_system, homelab_media, and so on, every app keeps its data and settings, and doctor no longer mentions homelab_core.
  • With brew install smartmontools done, doctor lists each drive under Drive health as passed (the Mac's own SSD at least; a USB drive may say it gives no report).

docs.title: 2. The desktop app
docs.text:
1. The first time only, in Terminal (Linux too; on Windows, irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Snooper42/homelab-wizard/main/install.ps1 | iex in PowerShell):
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Snooper42/homelab-wizard/main/install.sh | sh

It installs the newest build from GitHub › Releases › Latest after checking its checksum, and opens it. Once the app is installed, it updates itself (Update now on the line at the top), so skip to step 3. 2. From a browser instead: download Homelab-Wizard-macOS.dmg, drag Homelab Wizard to Applications, then clear the download flag once (the build is not signed):

xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/Homelab Wizard.app"
  1. Open it from Applications.
Check You should see First screen Setup, with the number of steps left beside it in the sidebar, unless every step is done Scroll down Choose apps with Add more open, pick Status, then Choose apps again; quit and open the app again Status opens at its own top (or where you left it), not partway down; Choose apps is back where it was with Add more open, and so is each screen after opening the app again Settings › This Mac macOS, OrbStack with its engine version, the homelab folder ~/Homelab, the version, and Storage: a green line for the Mac's disk (homelab folder, backups) and one for the media drive (photos, media, downloads), each with its free space. ./homelab doctor lists the same under Disk space Settings › This Mac › Version "✓ up to date" after the pull, and "build" with the commit this app was made from An update found by itself Within 15 minutes of a newer build (or on bringing the window forward after 10), with no click: one line at the top of every screen, Homelab Wizard … is ready, with What's new, Later, and Update now; Settings › This Mac › Updates says when it last looked Update now, with changes waiting and a newer build on GitHub The line says Updating… with a bar while the homelab files move forward and the new app goes in place (no log, no Setup); the app closes, and the new one opens by itself within a minute on the same screen, saying Updated to …, its build commit changed Later The line goes; the sidebar says ● Update ready, and clicking it (or Enter on it) brings the line back Window and menus The window buttons sit at the top of the sidebar, which shows the desktop through it (as in Finder). The menu bar has View (Choose Apps to Setup on ⌘1 to ⌘4, Finances on ⌘6, Settings… on ⌘,, Hide Amounts on ⌘⇧H, Reload on ⌘R) and Help; ⌘5 opens Settings too, and Homelab Wizard › About shows the version. Buttons show the arrow, not a hand; dragging the sidebar or the strip above a screen moves the window Menu bar One house icon. Its menu lists the apps' health and the yearly savings, and Update to … once the app (or, with the window closed, the menu bar item itself, every 15 minutes) found an update; clicking it opens the window, which puts it in place. Opening the app again from it brings the same window forward Text size ⌘+ makes the whole app bigger, ⌘− smaller (80% to 200%), ⌘0 back to the usual size; after quitting and opening again, the size is kept. With the window made as small as it goes, a few ⌘+ turn the sidebar into its icons (the counts on them, the names on hover), and no screen scrolls sideways Keyboard Tab reaches every link that acts (Open Setup, Show, go back to …, Settings on an app row) and Enter or Space presses it VoiceOver (⌘F5) Picking a screen reads its heading and the sidebar button says current page; a finished backup or an error is read out without moving there; the search fields are read by name VoiceOver (⌘F5) on Status, then Restart an app from its menu; then docker pause two apps (and docker unpause them) while Status stays open; Narrator (Ctrl+Win+Enter) on Windows the same Vikunja: Restarting…, then Vikunja: Running, read without the focus moving; after Status checks again, Navidrome and Vikunja: Not answering: … as one line when their reason is the same, then their return. Nothing is read for Status's changes while another screen is shown Choose apps › tick Speedtest Tracker The plan says in one line that it installs 1 app and lists Speedtest Tracker only; helpers, port moves, and settings are under Details Then Install Each step ticks off; Details shows Compose pulling and starting. Then it is listed under Started with a link Choose apps › preset Media automation The plan lists Prowlarr, Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Bazarr, FlareSolverr, qBittorrent, and Seerr (Gluetun under Details as qBittorrent's VPN), says the VPN key is needed by its setting's name, and shows the field to fill in with where to find it. Do not install unless you mean to Choose apps › type "spotify" in the search box Add more opens by itself; Navidrome and Feishin only Choose apps › click Music under Start here The card is marked ✓, Navidrome, Feishin, and beets are ticked under Add more, and the plan lists them; clicking it again unticks them Choose apps › Presets under Add more Only the bundles (Media automation, Household, Ad blocking, and the starters), no stack folders or categories; app rows have no baseline/optional badges Settings › HELPER_EMAIL (your own address), then Settings › This Mac › Make a diagnostics report › Email it to my helper Mail opens a message to you, and Finder shows the report to attach Settings › This Mac › Make a diagnostics report › Show in Finder Finder opens with the new report selected Quit OrbStack, then look at Setup A card Start OrbStack with Open OrbStack; clicking it starts OrbStack and the card goes away by itself within a few seconds of it answering Quit (⌘Q) It asks Quit Homelab Wizard and stop the homelab?; Quit and Stop stops every app, the agent, and the menu bar icon, and opening the app again starts them all On the Mac: Status, then Backups, then Finances; ⌘[ twice, ⌘] once; then open an app's page, go to Settings, and swipe right with two fingers on the trackpad; then swipe left Back goes to Backups, then Status; Forward to Backups; the swipe right brings back that app's page (an arrow shows at the left edge for a moment), the swipe left Settings; over Finances' wide Net worth table a sideways swipe scrolls the table instead From Status, open Finances, then Spending, then Plan › Recurring; press ⌘[ four times, then ⌘] four times Back goes to Plan's Calendar (where Plan opened), Spending's Transactions, the Dashboard, then Status; Forward comes back the same way to Recurring. Tidy Up's tabs step the same way Finances › Net worth: click an account (checking, then a card, then the home) Its own page: today's balance (a card says owed) with a chart, this month's in and out, its latest transactions, Update balance and Edit; All of them in Transactions opens Transactions with that account picked; ‹ Net worth and ⌘[ go back; a home charts what was typed in over time Finances' Dashboard: Arrange the Dashboard; drag a card by its handle, then ▲ on another; set one to ⅓; Hide one; Done; quit and open the app again; then Reset to the usual Each moves as asked, the width applies, the hidden waits below with +; after reopening it's as left; Reset puts the usual board back. The phone's page has no Arrange Finances › Net worth › a loan (the mortgage): link a payment that pays it (Link a payment…), then another from the same payee The loan says each month's payment (and the whole one, when only a share is in the plan), months left and when it's paid off; the payment shows Counted; the next one from the same payee is offered with Link and Not this one; one that paid more than the plan's asks count all of it? (Count it keeps it, Not this one takes it off) Finances › Net worth › Investments: Follow a ticker, look one up, Follow; then Read now; then Unfollow The Watchlist lists it with its price and its change since today; the figures above don't change; a read prices it again; Unfollow takes it off. A ticker Ghostfolio can't price says so and isn't added Status Four tiles at the top (running, needs a look, savings, nightly updates). Categories where every app runs are folded into one line with the apps' names; clicking one opens it, Show every app opens them all, and after quitting and opening again the choice is kept Choose apps › Add more (with Navidrome running and Sonarr not installed) First, Suggested for what you run: Beets says Goes with Navidrome, which you run: Tags and sorts the music…; Bazarr is not there. Install Sonarr: Bazarr and Prowlarr join it. Ticking one there picks it below too Choose apps › Add more, search kavita (with Komga running) Kavita's row says You already run Komga: Both read comics and manga from the same folders…; Komga's own row says nothing of the kind. tandoor with Mealie installed says the same of Mealie Status › hover (or Tab to) the figure under Instead of subscriptions A card: Saved so far: $… since …, from what the apps replace each day, then each month (up to 12), newest first, the month so far at the top. With fewer than one nightly record, just the figure Status › a category's count ("7 running ✓ · 2.1 GB") A menu: what the group holds in memory now, each running app's memory biggest first, and Start the stopped, Restart, and Stop them all; Stop needs a second click; Stop for a while › offers For an hour, Until 9 PM tonight, and Until 8 AM tomorrow, with ‹ Back; Escape or a click elsewhere closes it. What's using power says how much memory the apps hold in all An app that stops by itself: run a container labelled as one (docker run -d --name homelab_household-mealie-1 --label com.docker.compose.project=homelab_household --label com.docker.compose.service=mealie --memory 16m --memory-swap 16m --entrypoint sh <any image with sh> -c 'x=$(head -c 200000000 /dev/zero \| tr "\0" a)'), or one with exit 3, or one whose -p port another program holds homelab status says it ran out of memory, it quit with an error, or another program is using its port … in HEALTH; Status's row and its page say Stopped at …: … with a red dot, and Needs a look counts it. After docker stop the row says only Stopped at …. Tried on Linux with Docker Engine 29.9.2, Nov 6, 2026 (the CLI; the screens against the fake backend) Stop an app from its group's menu or its page, then wait 15 minutes, plug a laptop in, or Start the N stopped Its row says Stopped by you with Start, its group stays folded, and nothing starts it: not Start them, the watchdog, the battery saver, a drive appearing, Fix it, or logging in again (homelab up, which also leaves out an app that needs it, such as Feishin for Navidrome). Stop for a while on its page or the group's menu says Stopped until 9:00 PM (or until tomorrow, 8:00 AM), and within a minute of that time it runs again. data/stopped.json holds the record; Start clears it Status › type navi with nothing focused A box beside the list holds navi and has the focus, the list shows only Navidrome under its open group (the heading's count still the whole group's), and the box says 1 of 22 apps. A name nothing has says No app's name has "…" across the table with Show every app. Escape brings every app back and the focus to where it was; Return opens the first app's page. ⌘A, Space, or a letter in an open menu does not start it Any screen › ⌘K (Ctrl+K), then navi A box near the top with the focus in it; navi lists Open Navidrome first, then its page, Restart, Stop, its logs, and Copy its address. Down and Up pick (round from the first to the last), Return runs the one picked, a name nothing has says Nothing has "…". Escape or a press outside closes it, the focus back where it was. stop media picks Stop the N Media apps, which asks Press Return again (or Click again) before it stops them, with the Undo note after; back up now starts the backup on Backups; update all shows Update all's list on Status with nothing done yet. While a sheet is open ⌘K does nothing. On a Mac, View › Command Palette… opens it too Status › ? (Shift+/ on most keyboards; another layout's own key for ? works the same), then Escape; then Choose apps › type ? in the search box; then ⌘K (Ctrl+K) › keyboard › Return on Finances A sheet: On Status (typing to filter, the menu arrows), Everywhere (⌘K, ⌘R, ⌘+ ⌘− ⌘0, ⌘⇧H, ⌘Z, Shift+F10, Escape; on Windows Ctrl, with F5, the menu key and F1) and The screens; no filter box opens, and Escape closes it. In the search box ? is typed. From the palette, Finances' sheet starts with the calendar's keys, and Close puts the focus back. A screen reader reads it as a dialog named Keyboard shortcuts, each key beside what it does Status › Start on a stopped app's row (one whose image isn't here yet), then Restart and Stop from its menu No panel opens: the row says Downloading the app… while the image comes down, then Starting…, then Running; Restart and Stop the same, Stop with the Stopped … · Undo note. One that fails says Could not start: … under the row with Details, which opens Docker's output. Update still opens its panel with what's new Status › right-click an app's row (or Shift+F10 on its button) A menu where the pointer is (under its name from the keyboard), inside the window: Open, Open on a phone, Copy address, Restart, Stop, Stop for a while ›, Logs, Back up now, and Tell me if it stops (ticked when its alerts are on); Start in place of Restart and Stop when it is stopped. Copy address says Address copied under the row; Stop asks Click again; Escape or a click elsewhere closes it. A right-click on a group's heading opens the group's menu Status: ⌥-click (Alt-click) an app's address, then ⇧-click (Shift-click) its Open The address is copied and Address copied shows under the row, with nothing opened; ⇧-click opens its address on this machine (http://localhost:…) in the browser, where a plain click opens the domain. The tooltips say so, with ⌥ and ⇧ on a Mac and Alt- and Shift- elsewhere Status › right-click an app › Pin to the top, then another A Pinned group under Needs a look (open, even when everything in it is fine) holds both, in the order pinned, and neither shows in its own group; the menu bar's Open an app lists them first, under Pinned. Pin to the top is ticked on a pinned app; picking it again puts the app back in its group Right-click Status, Backups, or Finances in the sidebar (or Shift+F10 on it) A menu where the pointer is (under it from the keyboard), and the screen showing stays as it was: Status has Check again and Update all apps… (and Fix it when there's something to fix); Backups has Back up now and Test a restore; Finances has Add a transaction, Update balances, and Hide amounts. Each opens its screen and does what its button there does: Update all shows its list first. Escape closes it back on the sidebar Status › a group's menu › Stop the N running, twice A note at the bottom: Stopped 6 Media apps · Undo (an app's name for one; until 9:00 PM after Stop for a while). Undo or ⌘Z starts the same apps again; with the pointer on it, it stays; otherwise it goes after 10 seconds. Restart all shows none Status › an app's row One button, Open (or Start when stopped), and the chevron; a click on the row opens the app's page; each row shows one address, with the address on this machine in the tooltip Status › Vaultwarden's page › Open on a phone A QR code of its address; the phone's camera opens it (with Tailscale on in Home mode); the panel says what the phone needs and names Bitwarden Status › Nginx Proxy Manager's page › Sign-in details The user name the homelab made, and Copy puts the password on the clipboard (cleared after 90 seconds); the password is never shown Status › This week The same lines as ./homelab digest (apps, backups, restore test, attacks caught, disk space), with ✓ All well or what needs a look marked Status › What the apps keep (after a nightly backup) Up to six app folders with their sizes, largest first, under Photos per person when Immich runs, each on one line (name, bar, size); with Protection, in one column beside Recent alerts. A long alert (eleven apps down) shows 3 lines and Show 8 more Status, after an app was down for a while this week Its row has a badge such as 96.2% up this week; apps up over 99% have none. Hovering it (or Tab, or a tap) shows the week as a strip with each time it was down, how long, and why; Escape or moving away closes it Status, opened between 5 AM and noon Under the heading, Overnight: …: the apps updated since 8 PM, any rolled back, the size of the night's database copies, and nothing needed you, or which app was down for a while. Hide until tomorrow puts it away until the next morning; after noon there is none Status: rest the pointer on an app's up 9 minutes (or Tab to it) after restarting it, after Fix it, after the watchdog restarted it, or after the power came back on battery A card says why it last started (You started it, Fix it restarted it, The watchdog restarted it…, It started again when the power came back…) and when; an app with no reason kept has plain words, with no card Status, after leaving it for another screen while an app restarts, updates, stops, or starts (or after quitting and opening the app again) Each of those rows has a small dot after its name; hovering it (or VoiceOver) says Restarted since you looked, Updated…, Stopped…, or Started…. An app's page counts as Status. Leaving Status and coming back clears them Status: hover updates held on an app rolled back (or Tab to it) A card says it is left out of the nightly updates after a rollback, that Nightly updates on its page puts it back, and its newest release (tag, date, what it runs now) with the first lines of its notes; read once, when the card first opens. With GitHub unreachable it says Could not read its releases: … Choose apps › tick Memos › Install (with a domain, after Set up the domain has run) The install log ends with domain setup --auto and https://notes.example.com, which opens with a padlock without running anything else Paperless's page › Reach it away from home off (with the domain and its Cloudflare tunnel); then on a phone on mobile data, and at home The switch moves at once and says Home only: it opens on your home Wi-Fi…; ./homelab domain status lists Paperless as home only; https://<paperless>.<domain> does not open on mobile data and does at home. If the app says it cannot find the homelab folder, use Choose… beside Homelab folder in Settings › This Mac and pick ~/Homelab. To try the new-machine path without touching ~/Homelab, open the app on another Mac user account (or rename the folder for a moment): Setup offers Set it up for me, which makes ~/Homelab with .homelab-kit.json in it, and ./homelab kit names the build.

The window remembers itself: make it smaller and move it, quit (⌘Q), open the app again: it opens the same size in the same place. Zoom it to fill the screen (double-click the title area), quit, open: it fills the screen; zoom back: the earlier size returns.

The Dock: with an app stopped by hand (./homelab stop memos), the app's Dock icon shows a red 1 within seconds, like Mail's unread count; ./homelab start memos clears it.

The accent colour: System Settings › Appearance › Accent colour › Purple, then the app's Setup › Check again (or reopen the app): links, buttons, the progress bar, and the selected sidebar item turn purple, on light and dark; Yellow gives buttons dark text; Multicolor brings back the blue.

Increase contrast: System Settings › Accessibility › Display › Increase contrast on: the app's dividers and card edges get darker and grey text gets darker too, on light and dark; off, as before.

docs.title: 3. Setup, in order
docs.text:
Work down the Setup screen (or ./homelab setup in Terminal). After each step, Check again should turn it ✓. Each step's first line says what it gives you, then what to do.

On a homelab whose Setup was first opened less than a week ago (data/setup.json › since), Backups leave this machine, Backup jobs in Duplicati, and Alerts when this machine is down show last, under Can wait; the group says Can wait · 3 and the Setup tab's number leaves them out. Done early, they count as done.

First, with a few steps ready: Do the N I can do for you. It runs each ready step in turn (its button shows Doing: …), and stops with What is left needs you or at the first step that fails, with the log saying why.

Home mode is the default (HOMELAB_DOMAIN empty in .env):

Step What to do You should see This laptop stays plugged in and open (a MacBook only; a Mac mini has no such step) Unplug the charger, Check again; plug it back in, Check again Unplugged: It is on battery now: plug it in; plugged in: ✓. With the lid closed and no display, a phone loses the apps within a few minutes (expected: that is what the step warns about) Addresses on your tailnet (Tailscale) With TAILSCALE_AUTHKEY empty: Set up the addresses. Tailscale's sign-in page opens in the browser; sign in (no auth key needed). In the Tailscale admin console › DNS, turn on HTTPS Certificates ✓; ./homelab tailnet setup lists https://homelab.<tailnet>.ts.net:<port> addresses, Status shows them, and Vaultwarden's opens on the phone with Tailscale on Password manager account Open sign-ups for 10 minutes, create the accounts at the passwords address, then close sign-ups (or wait) The countdown, then "sign-ups closed"; a new sign-up is refused afterwards Two-step sign-in Each Vaultwarden account: Settings › Security › Two-step login (authenticator app). Nginx Proxy Manager: add a personal administrator under Users, then its avatar menu › Two-Factor Auth. Tick Done Signing in again asks for the code; with a domain, Set up the domain still works (it uses NPM_API_EMAIL, which stays without it) Backups leave this machine One button per place found: Use Proton Drive (it makes Homelab Backups in the Proton Drive folder), and Use iCloud Drive or Use the … drive where those exist; the media drive is not offered. For another folder, use Settings › BACKUP_DESTINATION › Choose… and Save instead. Then Test beside the setting ✓, and the test wrote and removed a file there A second copy with Kopia (once Kopia is installed) Plug in a second drive, Check again, then Use the … drive No button for the drive with BACKUP_DESTINATION or the media; Kopia starts again and its page lists the repository at Homelab Kopia on that drive; the step turns ✓ with "Kopia's copies go to …". With KOPIA_REPOSITORY inside Duplicati's folder, the step says it is no second copy Backup jobs in Duplicati Create the backup jobs, then Settings › DUPLICATI_SECRETS_PASSPHRASE › Copy into Vaultwarden, and onto the recovery kit The plan, then (recreating Duplicati first if it still had an older folder) each job created and the first runs queued; Duplicati shows the jobs; their files appear in the Proton Drive web app (ISSUE-0003); Backups › Off-site jobs shows each ran, and the step turns ✓ Alerts on the phone Set up the alert token (it also makes the app's read token and the phone's login), in the phone's ntfy app add the server with user phone and Settings › NTFY_PHONE_PASSWORD › Copy, subscribe to the topics, add the alert address to Uptime Kuma (Monitoring; Duplicati gets it from this step) Settings › Test passes beside NTFY_PUBLISH_TOKEN, NTFY_READ_TOKEN, and NTFY_PHONE_PASSWORD; ./homelab notify test reaches the phone, also on mobile data (ISSUE-0011), and shows under Recent alerts on Status and in the menu bar Scheduled jobs Install the jobs ./homelab schedule status lists the agent, loaded (always), and System Settings › Login Items & Extensions shows one homelab entry; pmset -g assertions lists caffeinate preventing sleep, and doctor says the awake job keeps the Mac up Alerts when this machine is down A healthchecks.io check (15 minutes, 15 minutes grace); its ping URL in Settings › HEARTBEAT_URL After the next watchdog run (up to 15 minutes) the check turns green Tailscale on phones and computers Install Tailscale on the phone, sign in with the same account, tick Done ✓; on mobile data, the apps' tailnet addresses open Admin apps on the tailnet Settings › Admin apps on the tailnet off (TAILNET_ADMIN_APPS=false), Save, then ./homelab tailnet setup On the phone, Nginx Proxy Manager's, AdGuard's, Duplicati's, and Dozzle's tailnet addresses no longer open, while Immich's and Vaultwarden's still do; on the Mac they open at their local address. Turn it back on afterwards if you prefer

With a domain (in a copy, or once you are ready: Settings › HOMELAB_DOMAIN = your domain, Save), the tailnet step gives way to these:

Step What to do You should see Home DNS answers (AdGuard Home) Set up AdGuard (or, if you already made a login in AdGuard's wizard, put it in Settings › ADGUARD_USER, ADGUARD_PASSWORD › Save) ✓, and ADGUARD_PASSWORD is filled in Cloudflare API token Create it with the three permissions the step lists; paste it in Settings › CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, Save, then Test beside it ✓, and the test says the token can read example.com Addresses and certificate Set up the domain; the first time takes a few minutes (the certificate) https://npm.example.com opens with a padlock, on the Mac and on your phone over Wi-Fi This Mac finds its apps by name With Proton VPN connected (Allow LAN connections on): Find the apps on this Mac, enter the Mac password once cat /etc/resolver/<domain> shows nameserver and the Mac's address, https://photos.example.com opens in the browser, and an app installed afterwards opens too, with nothing run again Access away from home Create the tunnel in Cloudflare Zero Trust, paste its token in Settings › TUNNEL_TOKEN, Start the tunnel On your phone with Wi-Fi off, https://passwords.example.com opens Alerts on the phone, again Set up the domain again so ntfy is published The ntfy app on the phone reaches https://ntfy.example.com on mobile data Phones and computers use the home DNS Set the Wi-Fi DNS server on each device to the Mac's address, tick Done The app names open at home

docs.text: Check You should see ./homelab plan immich-server vaultwarden navidrome feishin filebrowser syncthing No Memory: warning (about 2.2 GB of the room an 8 GB Mac has) ./homelab --json plan paperless open-webui karakeep dawarich stirling-pdf immich-machine-learning on an 8 GB Mac A Memory: warning naming the heaviest; on 16 GB, none. memory.room is this Mac's memory less 4 GB After a week of use: ./homelab doctor's memory line against the plan's memory.use Within about a third of each other; if not, the estimates in the compose files need adjusting

docs.title: 4. The jobs
docs.text:
./homelab watchdog
./homelab backup --apply
./homelab schedule status
  • Stop one baseline app (./homelab stop navidrome), run ./homelab watchdog twice: the second run shows Homelab: something is down in Notification Center as well as on the phone. ./homelab start navidrome and the next run shows recovered.
  • A restart that keeps failing: ./homelab custom add crashy --image alpine:3.20 --install --apply (it exits at once, so Docker keeps restarting it). Run ./homelab watchdog, wait 3 minutes (Docker waits longer between each restart, up to a minute), and run it again: the second run says stopped crashy: Docker restarted it … times in an hour, the phone gets Homelab: stopped an app that kept restarting, and Status's crashy row says Stopped: it restarted … times in an hour with a red dot. Another ./homelab watchdog leaves it stopped. ./homelab start crashy makes the row plain again (and the app loops again); ./homelab remove crashy --apply, then ./homelab custom remove crashy --apply, takes it away. (A wrong NAVIDROME_MUSIC_PATH doesn't make a loop: Navidrome mounts the music folder at that path itself.) Tried on Linux with Docker Engine 29.9, Nov 5, 2026.
  • watchdog lists every check as ✓. A check that fails once only says so; it alerts when it fails twice in a row. The app's Status screen then shows Watchdog with all checks passed and when it ran.
  • backup writes the database dumps and the .env copy into recovery-staging (Duplicati takes them off-site from 05:00) and ends with a summary.
  • schedule status shows each job loaded, with a last exit code of 0 once it has run.
  • The app's Backups screen lists each app's newest copy under Up to date, the settings file copied a moment ago, and the Off-site tile naming the place (Proton Drive, the Backup drive); Back up now streams the same backup and ends with "Backup done".
  • The menu bar's Back up now ends with "done" and the time.
  • ./homelab digest prints the same lines as Status › This week; ./homelab digest --send reaches the phone as Homelab this week, listing what needs a look (expect the restore test until step 6). From then on it arrives each Sunday morning.
  • After logging out and back in, schedule status still lists the jobs; the next morning there is a new dump in recovery-staging/databases (ISSUE-0005).
  • With HEARTBEAT_URL set: quit OrbStack, and within 30 minutes healthchecks.io alerts (ISSUE-0006). Start OrbStack again afterwards.

docs.title: 5. The proxy and CrowdSec
docs.text:
./homelab update nginx-proxy-manager
./homelab logs nginx-proxy-manager
./homelab compose crowdsec exec crowdsec cscli bouncers list
  • update rebuilds the proxy image with CrowdSec AppSec; logs shows no Lua errors (ISSUE-0001).
  • bouncers list shows nginx_proxy_manager with a recent last pull, and ./homelab doctor says the proxy's bouncer pulled decisions … seconds ago.
  • With a domain, the ban test in Runbooks returns 403 on the phone, then loads again once lifted. Within a minute the app's Status › Protection lists it as a manual ban.
  • Status › Nginx Proxy Manager (or CrowdSec) › What CrowdSec stopped today: after the ban test, its row says manual 'ban' from 'localhost' with the address, Banned, and the time; the heading counts today's and those banned now. With nothing since midnight it says Nothing yet today and the week's count; with CrowdSec stopped it says it can't be read. Other apps' pages have no such card.
  • With a domain, open any app from a phone on Wi-Fi, then check which address the proxy logged (ISSUE-0002):
./homelab compose nginx-proxy-manager exec nginx-proxy-manager sh -c 'tail -n 1 /data/logs/proxy-host-*_access.log'

docs.title: 6. The first restore test
docs.text:
Once the Homelab AppData job has run in Duplicati, the Backups screen shows Test a restore. Click it (or run the command):

./homelab restore-test --auto
  • The panel shows Duplicati restoring a dozen files, then ends with "12 files checked, all the same as now" (fewer when few files have settled for a day) and "Restore test passed". The Restore test tile says a moment ago and "in N minutes" (how long it took), hovering it lists the test on record, and recovery-staging/restore-test is gone again. ./homelab report has it under "restore tests".
  • Then the manual way once, as in Backups: restore Homelab AppData in Duplicati to /staging/restore-test, run ./homelab restore-test recovery-staging/restore-test data/appdata, and delete the folder afterwards.
  • With Kopia installed and its first snapshot made (3:45, or Snapshot now in its page): ./homelab restore-test --auto --engine kopia ends the same way, with "Kopia restores N files". A restore you make in its page (into /staging/restore-test, Restore File Ownership unticked) lands as yours, not root's.

docs.title: 8. After a few days
docs.text: Once everything has run without trouble: Status › More… › Clean up old containers (or ./homelab cleanup, then ./homelab cleanup --volumes). Delete the older setup's folders only when you are sure.

docs.title: A newcomer's first run
docs.text:
For handing it to someone who is not technical (the 1.0 test), on an M1 MacBook Air with 8 GB. Watch without helping, and note every place they stop, hesitate, or ask; each becomes its own fix.

What they meet, in Home mode (counted in October 2026 against the code, before a real run):

# Step Who does it Friction 1 Install OrbStack: the website's download, drag it to Applications, open it, approve its helper with the Mac's password Them Four actions and a password prompt; the app's Open the install guide only opens the page (an Install OrbStack button is next, once it can be tried on a Mac) 2 Install Homelab Wizard: a Terminal line, or the download and Open Anyway in System Settings Them The unsigned-app warning, until the Developer ID 3 Set it up for me App None 4 OrbStack is running App checks None once OrbStack is open 5 Start the homelab App A long first download 6 This laptop stays plugged in and open App checks A sentence to read (new) 7 Set up the addresses: sign in to Tailscale in the browser, then turn on HTTPS Certificates in its admin console Them An account, and a toggle on a website the app cannot reach without an API key 8 Alerts on the phone: the ntfy app, a server, a user, and a password copied from Settings Them The most typing of any step 9 Install the jobs App macOS shows Background items added (expected) 10 Tailscale on phones and computers Them An app per device, the same account 11, 12 Password manager account and two-step sign-in, once Passwords is picked Them Accounts and an authenticator app later Backups (where they go, the jobs) and the outside check (healthchecks.io) Them Can wait a week now: not counted until then

Removed in this pass: the router's DHCP reservation (Home mode does not need it), and backups and healthchecks.io on day one. Added: the laptop step, and the install plan's memory warning (the small baseline with every Start here pick uses about 2.2 GB of the 4 GB an 8 GB Mac has room for).

docs.title: Proven every night
docs.text:
Before a step reaches this page, CI tries it against a real Docker Engine on a Linux runner every night (.github/workflows/nightly.yml, the tests in test/realdocker), and on each pull request that changes the catalog: ntfy, Vaultwarden, Paperless with its PostgreSQL, and Nginx Proxy Manager installed; doctor; the alert token made and a test alert read back; data put into each app through its own API; Duplicati given a backup folder and its jobs (duplicati destination, duplicati setup), each job read back through Duplicati's API (sources, destination, AES, retention, schedule, the alert URL), then, once the AppData job has run, restore-test --auto restoring a sample of settled files and comparing them; Status timed, failing at more than twice the last good run; the nightly backup; the app's page served by homelab serve and paired as a phone, with Status, Backups, and Back up now clicked through against the real containers; the watchdog bringing back an app that hung and one whose container was removed, with its alert in ntfy; an update and its rollback, across a change of ntfy's database schema (the run starts on ntfy v2.25.0, which refuses the newer ntfy's migrated databases), with ntfy answering on its tokens from before; the same update again with ntfy made to hang before the watchdog saw it well, which the watchdog puts back with its data from before, its tokens checked the same way; then the homelab moved out, wiped, moved in, and the data read back, with ntfy back on the older version it ran, not the newest (the restore drill: timed from the move in to every app answering with its data, written on the run's summary page beside Status's time, and failing at more than twice the last good run and a minute more), and Duplicati's jobs made again on that "new machine" from their existing backups (repaired, then backing up into the same folders). A failed night opens an issue with the run's diagnostics report. Beside it, each night starts a seventh of the rest of the catalog (TestTheCatalogStarts, by the day of the week): each app installed alone on a homelab of its own, then its page answering (or, with no page, its container still running a minute on), so every app starts against real Docker at least once a week. An app that needs a setting only the person's own account gives (a tunnel token, a VPN key) is listed as skipped with that reason. Run by hand, the workflow starts all seven shares at once. Beside it, the rebuild job (on pull requests that change the real-Docker tests too) is the full rebuild of Disaster Recovery: Vaultwarden, Paperless with its PostgreSQL, Actual Budget, and Firefly III given data, the nightly backup and every Duplicati job run into a backup folder beside the homelab, the homelab wiped, and homelab rebuild <that folder> with the Secrets passphrase bringing it back from the backups alone, each app answering with its data again; its time is on the run's summary page, and a rebuild taking more than twice the last good run's, and a minute more, fails. Beside it, the domain job takes domain setup through the real proxy and AdGuard Home (Cloudflare left out, as it needs a real account): each proxy host and the rewrite read back, the name resolved through AdGuard, and ntfy answering through the proxy by its name. Beside it, the wire job runs homelab wire against the real Prowlarr, Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, and FlareSolverr, and reads each link back from Prowlarr. Beside it, the proxy job builds the homelab's proxy image and runs it with CrowdSec: the bouncer pulling, and a banned address getting 403 until the ban is lifted. Beside it, the home job is a new household's first run in Home mode, with a fake tailnet (a Headscale server of the run's own) in place of Tailscale's: Setup's checklist walked as Do the N I can do for you walks it (the homelab started, Tailscale installed and signed in, the addresses set up, the alert token, the scheduled jobs installed for real), each step left checked to name the person's part, then that part played (the boxes ticked, a backup folder chosen, the outside check's address filled in) and every step ending done. What it cannot reach (a real Mac, Windows, the Steam Machine, the phone, Proton Drive) stays in the lists below.

Upgrades are proven on every pull request: testdata/upgrades keeps the files a homelab folder of each release keeps (.env as homelab.env, the paired phones, the update history with ntfy's updates held, Setup's steps, the restore tests, the watchdog's state, the savings, the household), made by that release's own code (testdata/upgrades/make.sh). TestEachReleasesFolderUpgrades opens each with this build, runs install, Setup, and Status, and fails on a question asked, a setting changed or lost, or a file that no longer reads back.

docs.title: Waiting for real hardware
docs.text: What only the Mac, the Windows PC, or the Steam Machine can prove: each row of the parity table in Host that CI shows only against fakes, and each change made since without the machine to run it on. Work down a machine's list in one session; each step says what to do and what you should see. When a step does not match, make a report (homelab report), note the step's number, and go on to the next. When a step passes, write Passed and the day in its Result column; Host's Proven by names the steps, and this column is where they are marked.

docs.title: After testing
docs.text: Tick what worked in Known Issues (the "To verify" items) and in the To-do, and make a report for anything that did not.

docs.title: Tidy Up
docs.text: Tidy Up keeps the libraries on the media drive (MEDIA_ROOT) sorted, tagged, and lean: music, books, films, TV, and audiobooks. It has its own screen in the app, and homelab media does the same from a terminal. Everything it throws away goes to the Trash (the Recycle Bin on Windows), never straight away. On Windows, a USB drive, SD card or network share has no Recycle Bin, so what Tidy Up throws away there goes to a hidden .tidy-trash folder at the top of that drive, a folder a day. The nightly sweep empties a day's folder once it is over 30 days old (as long as Undo reaches), unless Undo still offers something in it; empty it yourself sooner to free the space, or before the drive goes to someone else.

docs.title: The first time
docs.text: The first time (no library anywhere, and no drive Tidy Up is waiting for), Inbox opens on Where should your libraries live?: this computer's own disk (a Media folder in your home folder) and every drive plugged in, each with its space and the libraries already on it; the drive Duplicati backs up to can't be picked; Another folder… for a NAS or one folder for everything. The one picked lists where each library goes on it and what's there (found 1,204 artists, a Calibre library, new). Use it keeps MEDIA_ROOT and runs homelab fix, which lists the apps that read the libraries (Jellyfin, Navidrome, Calibre-Web…) and recreates them once, after asking; nothing is moved or copied. A library kept elsewhere with TIDY_<KIND>_LIBRARY stays there. After that, Change where your libraries live… under Tidy up now opens it again, as does Choose another… beside a media drive that isn't plugged in.

docs.title: The Inbox
docs.text: Otherwise Inbox opens on Drop anything here: the folders Tidy Up watches (Downloads and DOWNLOADS_ROOT until others are picked; Add… opens the folder picker, Remove is there while another is left, and one on a drive that's unplugged says Not there now), when it files what lands in them (As things arrive, every minute the folders change; Once a day, 3 AM; or Only when I press it, kept as TIDY_INBOX_FOLDERS and TIDY_INBOX_WHEN), and Tidy up now across the card, which files what's waiting at once.

docs.title: Needs a look
docs.text: Under it, when there is one, Needs a look: each download no engine could place (a video whose name says nothing, another cut of a film you have, a library copy that can't be read) and each one Undo put back, with why, from the inbox's list in data/media-needs.json (HOMELAB_MEDIA_NEEDS). A video has It's a film… (its title, and year if known) and It's an episode… (the show and season, and the episode for a single file; in either, Look it up asks Radarr for a film or Sonarr for a show (with the key in its config.xml, while it runs), else Jellyfin's search (with JELLYFIN_API_KEY), and lists what it finds with its year, so a person picks The Big Lebowski (1998) rather than typing the year; picking is a help, not a must, and with nothing here to ask the sheet says so and files what's typed; a folder of episodes keeps each one's own number): Tidy Up renames it to that and files it (homelab media inbox name <path> movie "<title>" [<year>], or episode "<show>" <season> [<episode>]), and the line in What I did today says named by you, then filed; one it still can't place stays, saying so. Songs that don't say which artist or album they are wait here too, rather than being filed into a folder with no name; with AcoustID set up (fpcalc and beets' chroma), beets first tries them by their sound, files the ones it matches, and leaves the rest where they are (quiet_fallback: skip, on top of the inbox's beets settings), so only those wait here, and a download that may stay isn't shrunk first. Name these songs… asks the album (and the artist, if known), Look it up asks MusicBrainz for the albums by that name (each with its artist, year, number of songs, format and country, so editions can be told apart), and File them writes the picked album's names onto the songs (title, artist, album, year, track and disc, and its MusicBrainz ids) and files them as that album (homelab media inbox name <path> album <MusicBrainz release id>). The songs are matched to the album by the track numbers in their names (01 …, 1-03 …, a CD2 folder), or in order when the counts agree; a different count with no numbers to go by, or a song far longer or shorter than its place on the album (another edition, most likely), stops it, and it stays, saying why. Only the two names typed are sent to MusicBrainz. A download that is or holds only a .rar or .7z (or their parts, .r00, .7z.001), which Tidy Up doesn't open, is listed once with It's packed in a .rar file…: open it (double-click it), and what's inside is filed on the next sweep; a .zip is unpacked by the sweep itself, and a .rar beside a download's film (its subtitles, say) is no reason to hold the film. Every one has Show in Finder (Explorer on Windows) and Leave it (homelab media inbox leave <path>), after which the inbox never files it. Only a download Needs a look lists can be named or left from the app.

docs.title: What I did today
docs.text: Then What I did today: a line for each download the inbox filed that day, newest first, saying what it is, where it went, and what was done (tags cleaned, lyrics added, too big so Tdarr shrinks it first, the better copy kept), from the inbox's record in data/media-filed.jsonl (HOMELAB_MEDIA_FILED_LOG). Undo (homelab media inbox undo <id>) moves just the files that download became back where it came from, a folder as a folder, and the inbox leaves them there until they change; a book added to Calibre has no Undo here.

docs.title: Needs your OK, your libraries, and what was done
docs.text: Below that, the rest answers three things in order. First, Needs your OK, beside the drive (a ring of what each library takes, and what is free): the next thing to do leads it, larger, under Next up, after only a drive to plug in or a tool to install. Then Your libraries, a tile for each in its own colour: what it holds, how far along it is where the record can say (songs with lyrics, films and episodes already lean), and what it waits on; a tile opens the library's tab, which starts with that library (its folder and figures, and for music its clean-up step by step: scanned, built, swapped in, checked, freed). Then the genres and Recently done. Needs your OK is the next thing each library waits on (a scan, a swap, films to shrink, books to look over), what it wins back (films and shows to shrink, extra copies, audiobooks to merge, from the last scan), and its one button. The first thing to do has the screen's one main button; a step that throws things away (freeing the old music library, removing extra copies) never does, however early it comes. Beside it, a ring of genres, with a dropdown for whose: your music's in your 14 genres (homelab media music genre-counts), your films' and shows' from Jellyfin or the .nfo files beside them (movies genre-counts, tv genre-counts), and your books' from each book's first tag in Calibre (books genre-counts, which only reads Calibre's database); the media drive with what each library takes and what is free (measured in the background, at most every six hours, into ~/.homelab-media/sizes.json), and Recently done, with Undo on the music swap until the space is freed, on the books' last apply, and on whatever a run put in the Trash: each thing Tidy Up throws away is noted under its run in data/media-trash.jsonl, and Undo (homelab media restore <run>) puts back what is still in the Trash, never over something now in its place. Two runs don't offer it: Tdarr's collect (the smaller copy has the original's name) and freeing the old music library. On Windows, what went to the Recycle Bin is named instead, to restore from there; a USB or network drive's .tidy-trash is put back like a Mac's or Linux's Trash.

docs.title: Each library's tab
docs.text: Each library has its own tab: what could be tidier, its space, and its history. A music check that finds songs missing says how many and whose, with Put the old library back… and Check again; the space can't be freed until every song is found.

docs.title: Sizes
docs.text: Sizes are counted as the Finder and Explorer count a drive (1000 to a KB), the way the engines write them, so 412 GB won back at the top and the 412 GB a run freed, on the right of its line in Recently done (where Finances puts an amount; lines from before this say it in their words), are one figure; the first line counts the same things as Needs your OK, a tool to install included.

docs.title: The engines
docs.text:
The work is done by Python scripts in tools/media, run by the homelab with Python 3.8 or newer (3.10 to 3.14 for music run on this computer: its one-time setup installs beets and its helpers at the versions pinned in tools/media/requirements, each checked against its hashes):

Script What it does music_organizer.py The owner's music organizer, vendored with their two Windows fixes: scan, build a cleaned copy with beets (MusicBrainz, your 14 genres, artwork), swap it in with Navidrome paused and backed up, verify, undo books_organizer.py The owner's books organizer, vendored with their Windows fix: review (titles, series, publishers, genres, covers, misfiled books), apply with Calibre-Web paused, undo books_run.py How the books jobs start books_organizer.py: unchanged, but with a time limit on each tool it runs (a minute for sips on a cover, an hour for anything else), so a file built to hang one can't hold Tidy Up books_tidy.py Beside it: genre counts from Calibre's database, and Make a Calibre library (build) for a books folder with no metadata.db: each folder holding a book's files moves aside to <folder> (before Calibre) on the same drive, calibredb add --recurse --one-book-per-directory adds each as one book (its formats together, its metadata.opf and cover read) with Calibre-Web paused, and every book is counted in; the copy aside is kept music_tidy.py What Tidy Up adds around the organizer: free the space once verify says every song is there, Navidrome's full scan and missing entries, a smart playlist (.nsp) a genre, LRCLIB lyrics, and new music from Downloads movies_organizer.py, tv_organizer.py, video_engine.py Find the videos that waste space, hand them to Tdarr, and swap each checked result in; file new films as Title (Year)/Title (Year).mkv and episodes as Show/Season 01/Show - S01E01.mkv (S01E01-E02 for two in one file, Show - 112 for anime numbered from its first episode) audiobook_organizer.py Merge a book in many files into one .m4b with a chapter a file and one cover (m4b-tool, else ffmpeg); its scan also counts the books that are one file already, so a library with nothing to merge says so inbox.py Watch Downloads and hand each finished download to its engine scrubber.py The nightly sweep of leftovers tdarr_setup.py Tidy Up's two libraries in Tdarr, with the space-saving plugins

media_common.py holds what they share: the Trash on each system, ffprobe, Tdarr's API, and the media servers' refreshes. The vendored scripts are otherwise never edited: tools/media/tests fails if either changes. The owner agreed to two fixes on Nov 3, 2026: on Windows, Docker Desktop's names for a mounted folder (/run/desktop/mnt/host/m/music for M:\music) are read as drive letters, so Navidrome and Calibre-Web are paused while files move; and beets runs on this machine there, since its container can't open Windows folders.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
homelab media writes data/homelab_media.json from .env before every run (the Tidy Up section of Settings): the libraries under MEDIA_ROOT, the folders to watch, the languages to keep, Tdarr's codec, where lyrics go, and the address of each media server that is installed. Keys and passwords (JELLYFIN_API_KEY, NAVIDROME_ADMIN_PASSWORD, PLEX_TOKEN, AUDIOBOOKSHELF_API_KEY, TDARR_API_KEY, TDARR_USER, TDARR_PASSWORD) reach the engines in their environment, never on a command line or in that file.

Tdarr asks for a sign-in (its accounts are on since 2.4x). Before a job that talks to it (Set up Tdarr, a films' or TV's Shrink or Collect), a Tdarr with no account yet gets one made for Tidy Up through its own sign-up: user homelab, a generated password, both kept in .env (TDARR_USER, TDARR_PASSWORD; Settings › Tidy Up), which also sign you in to Tdarr's own page. If you made an account in Tdarr first, put its user name and password there; the engines sign in with them and send its token (TDARR_API_KEY still works where Tdarr gives one). Without either, the job says so, plainly.

A new Tdarr's node has no transcode worker, and a node without one takes nothing from its queue: Set up Tdarr, a films' or TV's Shrink, and Collect give each node with none one worker (/api/v2/alter-worker-limit; on the graphics card when there is one, else the processor). More can be given on Tdarr's own page; a node that has any is left as it is. Reports go to reports/media in the homelab folder, not Downloads, which the inbox watches.

Tdarr's Tidy Up libraries never scan by themselves: Tidy Up hands Tdarr each film or episode that wastes space. Shrink reads the videos that came in since the last scan first (Radarr and Sonarr file straight into the library), then hands every one that wastes space. Only what Tdarr's container mounts can be handed: the media drive's movies and tv folders (MEDIA_ROOT), as /media/movies and /media/tv; a library elsewhere (TIDY_MOVIES_LIBRARY, TIDY_TV_LIBRARY) is named, with the folder Tdarr can open, and nothing is handed. A video Tdarr still has no record of 20 minutes after it was handed is handed again; after three tries it waits for the next Shrink, said on the card, and a new download waiting for Tdarr is filed as it is. Shrink stops, saying to run Set up Tdarr again, when Tdarr no longer has the library Tidy Up made (its data was cleared, or it was installed again).

docs.title: How it keeps out of the way
docs.text:
• One job moves files at a time: data/homelab.media.lock holds the job's process, and a job that crashed leaves a lock the next run takes over, carrying on where it stopped. A lock whose process ID another program has since been given (one that started after the lock was written, as after a restart) counts as left behind too. While a job this window didn't start holds the lock (the agent's Collect every few minutes, a run from Terminal), the screen shows it with its step and bar, read from its log every few seconds, and every button waits, saying for what; once it's done the screen is read again by itself. Both say when the job started, by the day (Started yesterday at 3:04 AM). A job that stopped part-way says what it was, with Carry on: a step that asks first (a swap, putting the old library back, freeing the space, a books Undo, removing extra copies) asks again; a books apply opens the review instead, since which books you left alone isn't kept with the job; an Undo from Recently done is pressed there again.
  • Stop stops a job at its next safe point, which can take a while: until then the panel says stopping. A job that ends without finishing says didn't finish and why, with Try again (a step that asks first is tried again from its own button). Transcodes aren't under the lock: Tdarr's own queue and its nodes' worker limits pace them; only putting their results in place is.
  • While a job runs, the nightly update leaves every app that reads a library (Navidrome, beets, Calibre-Web, Komga, Kavita, Audiobookshelf, Jellyfin, the *arr apps, Tdarr) for the next night, homelab update refuses them alone, and Duplicati's scheduled backups are paused, then resumed.
  • Lyrics: each song without time-synced lyrics is looked up on LRCLIB by its exact record (title, artist, album, and length), then, when that has nothing time-synced, by a search on title and artist that takes the same title (without Remastered, Live, or feat.), the same artist, and a length within 3 seconds, time-synced first; the exact record's plain lyrics are kept only when no record has synced ones. Plain lyrics never replace plain ones; instrumentals are skipped. A song's lyrics are read as Navidrome reads them (its LyricsPriority: a .lrc beside the song, then a .txt, then the song's own tags), and written where it will read them: into the song (TIDY_LYRICS=embed), or into the .lrc beside it when that is set (lrc) or when a .lrc or .txt is already there and would hide the song's own. Lyrics with a translation after a caret on most lines (¡NUEVAYoL!^NEW YORK!) keep both languages: each translation goes on a line of its own under its original, with the same time, so a player shows the two together, whether they come from LRCLIB or are already in the song. A song LRCLIB has nothing for is kept in ~/.homelab-media/lyrics-not-found.json and asked about again after 30 days (or on the next run when the lookup has changed since), and Overview's Add lyrics counts only songs not yet asked. Check lyrics counts the songs with two languages on one line too, and once every song has lyrics, Overview offers Tidy lyrics for them (a check from before it counted them is offered again). The card ends with what came of every song.
  • Power: building the music library, merging audiobooks, lyrics, and handing videos to Tdarr wait for power and stop at a safe point when a laptop goes on battery; the battery saver pauses Tdarr too, but lets it finish the video it is on first (it takes no new one meanwhile), so no half-made copy is left in its cache; plugged in, it gets its workers back.
  • The agent's minute: the inbox when a watched folder changed (TIDY_INBOX_WHEN=arrive, the default), once after 03:00 (daily), or never by itself (manual, only on Tidy up now), Tdarr's finished work every few minutes, and the scrubber daily at 03:00. TIDY_UP=false turns all three off; TIDY_INBOX and TIDY_SCRUB each one.
  • Tdarr rests while it has nothing to do: once Set up Tdarr has made Tidy Up's libraries in it, with no film or episode with it, nothing converting, and no job (nor a start) for 15 minutes, the agent stops Tdarr to free its memory, noting it in data/stopped.json as Tidy Up's ("why": "tidy"), so the watchdog and the battery saver leave it stopped. Shrink, Collect, Set up Tdarr, filing a film or episode, and a sweep of the watched folders with a video in it start it first (Starting Tdarr, which was resting); on battery it stays resting, as the battery saver would have it. A Tdarr someone starts meanwhile stays up until a job next uses it; one a person stopped is never started here. TIDY_TDARR_REST=false keeps it running.
  • The *arr apps rest too (the owner, Nov 9): Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Prowlarr, Bazarr and FlareSolverr, and qBittorrent with Gluetun, are stopped while nothing is pending, noted in data/stopped.json as Tidy Up's ("why": "tidy"). Pending is anything in a Sonarr, Radarr or Lidarr queue, a torrent not finished in qBittorrent, or a Seerr request approved and not yet available, and 15 minutes after any of these or after they started; what can't be read counts as pending. A torrent seeding keeps qBittorrent and Gluetun up (qBittorrent is read with QBITTORRENT_PASSWORD; without it, it and Gluetun stay up). They wake every 12 hours and ask for an RSS sync and a search of what's missing, at once when Seerr has a request, and before Hand the libraries to Tidy Up; on battery, qBittorrent and Gluetun wait for power. One someone starts meanwhile keeps them up until the next 12-hour wake; one a person stopped is never started here. Seerr, Jellyfin and Navidrome stay up. TIDY_ARR_REST=false keeps them running.

docs.title: Before a run
docs.text:
homelab media preflight checks Python (on a Mac, Homebrew's, or Apple's only with its developer tools, so no install prompt appears), the media drive, the container runtime, a graphics card for Tdarr, power, ffmpeg and ffprobe, ffsubsync, m4b-tool, and Calibre's tools, each with its fix. Calibre is found on PATH, as the Mac app, in Program Files, in /opt/calibre, in a home folder (where Calibre's installer puts it on SteamOS, whose / is read-only), or as the Flatpak from Discover, whose tools it runs through flatpak run; CALIBRE_BIN_DIR points at another place. ffmpeg from Homebrew or Nix on Linux is found too. Tidy Up's screen shows the same under This machine. beets, when no beets image is in Docker, runs from a venv in ~/.music-cleanup/venv that the first music scan makes; when the Python it was made with is upgraded away (a Homebrew upgrade, say), every run removes the venv whose Python no longer starts, says so, and the engine makes it again, leaving beets' library beside it. The music scripts run straight from Terminal (music_tidy.py) do the same before they start.

Without ffmpeg, Install (homelab media install ffmpeg --yes) gets it with no Terminal and no password. With Homebrew (a Mac, or Linux) or winget (Windows) already there, it runs brew install ffmpeg or winget install Gyan.FFmpeg itself, each line shown on the card, so ffmpeg is updated with everything else. Without either, it fetches ffmpeg for Tidy Up alone: one pinned build per system (Martin Riedl's for macOS and Linux, Gyan Doshi's for Windows, both GPL), downloaded over HTTPS and checked against its SHA-256 in internal/media/ffmpeg-pins.json before anything is unpacked, then run once (ffmpeg -version) before it is kept in ~/.homelab-media/bin. A download that doesn't match is thrown away and never run, and what was there stays. An ffmpeg installed another way (Homebrew, winget, apt) comes first. The pins are written by go run ./internal/tools/ffmpegpins, which follows each publisher's latest link to its versioned file and downloads it once; run it to move to a newer ffmpeg.

docs.title: Shrink & Strip
docs.text:
New downloads are compared with what the library has. A duplicate replaces the library's copy only when it is leaner for the same picture or sound: AV1 over HEVC over H.264 at the same resolution and length, high-quality AAC or Opus over a huge FLAC; otherwise it goes to the Trash. A download that can't be weighed against the library's copy (that copy can't be read, or the two differ in length, as another cut does) is left where it is, and nothing is replaced; a second version kept on purpose (Heat (1995) - Director's Cut.mkv) is never taken for a duplicate. A bloated film or episode waits in a hidden folder in its library until Tdarr's copy is ready, and is filed then. New lossless music is stored as 256k AAC (TIDY_SHRINK_LOSSLESS=false keeps it lossless).

A film or episode already in the library twice (the same title and year, or the same episode of a show, and the same length) is found by the films' and TV's scan. homelab media movies dedupe (and tv dedupe) puts the extra copies in the Trash, after asking: the copy with the best picture stays (the tallest, then the newer codec, then the smaller file), each extra is checked again first (one changed since the scan stays, and so do its copies if the kept one no longer reads), and a version kept on purpose is never one.

TV's scan also says which episodes are missing: a gap in a season's numbering (S02E01, E02, E05: E03 and E04), read from the files alone, specials (season 0) left out. One missing after a season's last episode is past what the files can tell.

With Jellyfin set up here (its address and JELLYFIN_API_KEY), the films' and TV's scan also asks it which films or shows in that library it shows with no poster. Fetch posters (homelab media movies posters, tv posters) asks Jellyfin to look for those alone again; images are only added, never replaced.

docs.title: The download apps
docs.text: homelab media arr --apply (or Hand over on the screen) turns Sonarr's, Radarr's, and Lidarr's renaming off, and their Completed Download Handling, which is what moves finished downloads into the libraries. They keep finding and downloading; the downloads stay in their folder, where the inbox files them. LazyLibrarian is told how by hand: turn its post-processing off.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
homelab media

homelab media preflight

homelab media music scan

homelab media movies run

homelab media inbox --apply

homelab media scrub

homelab media help lists every library's actions. A step that changes a library asks first in a terminal; from a script, --yes answers. --background runs a job detached, its log in scripts/logs/media.

docs.title: To-do
docs.text: After the first install: the steps that only you can do, in order. For each testing session, follow Testing; when something does not work, ./homelab report makes a file to share with every secret removed. What the code will do next is in the Roadmap; problems to check are in Known Issues.

docs.title: First: finish the setup
docs.text:
• [ ] A VPN app on the Mac that carries all traffic (with a kill switch) blocks the homelab's own addresses: turn on Allow LAN connections and turn the kill switch off. ./homelab doctor warns while one does.
  • [ ] Open the app's Setup screen (or run ./homelab setup) and work down the checklist; Do the N I can do for you runs every step that is ready and stops at the first that needs you. The steps that need a person:
  • [ ] Home mode (the default): sign in to Tailscale when Addresses on your tailnet opens its page, then install Tailscale on each phone and computer.
  • [ ] With a domain instead: the AdGuard login and the Cloudflare API token in Settings (Zone › Zone › Read, Zone › DNS › Edit, Account › Cloudflare Tunnel › Edit), Set up the domain, then the Cloudflare tunnel (create it in Zero Trust, put its token in Settings, Start the tunnel), and each phone and computer using the Mac's address as its DNS server.
  • [ ] Open sign-ups for 10 minutes and create the Vaultwarden accounts; save the passwords from .env in the vault (Settings › Copy beside each one).
  • [ ] Two-step sign-in: each Vaultwarden account, and a personal Nginx Proxy Manager administrator (not the NPM_API_EMAIL account).
  • [ ] Backups: pick where they go (a cloud drive folder or an external drive), then Create the backup jobs; keep DUPLICATI_SECRETS_PASSPHRASE in Vaultwarden and on the recovery kit.
  • [ ] Alerts: Set up the alert token, subscribe the ntfy app on the phone (Duplicati gets the token from the step).
  • [ ] Install the jobs (startup, nightly backup, watchdog, keep awake, phone companion).
  • [ ] A healthchecks.io check (15-minute period and grace), its ping URL in HEARTBEAT_URL.
  • [ ] Rebuild the proxy once so it uses CrowdSec AppSec: ./homelab update nginx-proxy-manager.
  • [ ] After a few days of everything working: Status › More… › Clean up old containers (or ./homelab cleanup, then --volumes), and delete the older setup's folders when you are sure.

docs.title: Soon: try the new apps
docs.text:
• [ ] Tailscale with a domain: approve the route, and add 192.168.1.10 as the split-DNS nameserver for example.com (its note).
  • [ ] Home Assistant: install it; its starter configuration already trusts the proxy (its note).
  • [ ] The Household preset: Grocy, Karakeep, Vikunja, and Homepage (the start page). The Stack Data job already covers appdata/karakeep.
  • [ ] Open WebUI: brew install ollama, brew services start ollama, ollama pull llama3.2, then install it.
  • [ ] Speedtest Tracker, Dozzle, and Syncthing if you want them.
  • [ ] The first restore test: Backups › Test a restore in the app (or ./homelab restore-test --auto).

docs.title: This month
docs.text:
• [ ] Install the app with the one line in the README (install.sh; it checks the download and needs no xattr), then check the app and the menu bar item start. Later builds come through Update now on the line at the top of the window.
  • [ ] Decide on signing: the Apple Developer Program for the Mac, and the Windows route (Releasing).
  • [ ] Work through the "To verify" items in Known Issues and close each one that holds.

docs.title: After the Mac testing
docs.text:
• [ ] Print the recovery kit (Backups › Recovery kit) and write the Secrets passphrase on it.
  • [ ] Add the household (Settings › People, or ./homelab person add), then ./homelab sso setup once Pocket ID has its admin (single sign-on needs a domain).
  • [ ] Pair your phone (Settings › Phones), and your partner's, each with the https link; pick Sees Finances or Changes Finances beside the ones that should have them.
  • [ ] Type the household into Finances: checking and the cards, who gets paid and when, and the payments that repeat (a subscription on a card charged to that card). Then Update balances once a week.
  • [ ] Practise a rebuild once the Duplicati jobs have run: ./homelab rebuild <backup folder> into a spare folder (another account, or a second machine), and note how long it took (Disaster Recovery).
  • [ ] Ad blocking on every device: Choose apps › Ad blocking, then the nameserver it shows in Tailscale's DNS settings.
  • [ ] Read the app with VoiceOver on the Mac, and have a second person read the security review.

docs.title: Someday
docs.text:
• [ ] Try the Linux profile on the Steam Machine (ISSUE-0012), with the AppImage from the release run (ISSUE-0014).
  • [ ] Try the Windows profile when a Windows machine is around (ISSUE-0013).
  • [ ] Hand the homelab to someone who is not technical, as the roadmap says, and note where they get stuck.
  • [ ] Home Assistant OS in a VM, if device discovery or Zigbee/Thread radios become important.

docs.title: A tour of Homelab Wizard
docs.text:
Homelab Wizard turns a computer you already own into your household's own private cloud. It installs free apps that do the jobs you would otherwise pay subscriptions for (photos, passwords, documents, films, music, books), connects them, and then looks after them: a copy of everything every night, updates while you sleep with a one-click undo, a restart for anything that hangs, and an alert on your phone when something needs you.

This page walks through the app screen by screen. The pictures are the real app on made-up data, in light or dark to match your GitHub theme. To try it yourself, see Getting Started.

Screen What it answers Status Is everything running? An app's page What is this app doing, and how do I fix it? Choose apps What can I add, and what does it replace? Setup What's left to finish, and can it do it for me? Backups Is everything copied, and does a restore really work? Finances What does each paycheck leave once the bills are paid? Tidy Up Are the music, films, and books sorted, and where did the space go? Settings and phones How do I change a setting, add a person, or pair a phone? On your iPhone Can I check on it, and fix it, from my phone? Updates Is there a newer version, and what changed?

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
The screen the app opens on. Every app the computer runs, live, with a coloured dot, its address, and one button: Open, or Start when it's stopped. A category where everything runs folds into one line, and what needs a look stays open at the top. The tiles above say how many apps run, what needs a look, what the apps would cost as subscriptions, and whether the nightly updates are on.

Further down, the same screen shows the watchdog's checks, what CrowdSec blocked, recent alerts, This week's summary, what each person and app keeps on disk, and a live line of what each busy app uses right now.

When something is wrong, Fix it shows a plan and puts it right. More: Monitoring, Troubleshooting.

docs.title: An app's page
docs.text:
A click on any row on Status. Everything about one app: its state with Restart, Stop, and Open; its address (with a QR code to open it on a phone); what it uses now and its week as the watchdog saw it; its last backup; its log, with Explain this to have the AI on this computer say in plain words what it shows; its updates, with Roll back; who in the household uses it; and its own settings.

The log never leaves the house: Explain this uses Ollama on this computer, never a cloud service.

More: Monitoring, Automation.

docs.title: Choose apps
docs.text:
Where the homelab grows. Start here has the five things most homes want first (Photos, Passwords, Movies and TV, Music, Files); Add more lists every app by category, each saying what it does and which subscription it can replace. Tick what you want, or pick a preset. The plan on the right says in one line what it will install, names any setting an app needs first, and warns if the apps wouldn't fit in this computer's memory. Then Install.

More: Services, every app's own page.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
On a new computer, Setup is where the app opens: it checks for the container engine, then Set it up for me makes the homelab folder, with a strong password for every app.

After that, it's the checklist for finishing up, checked live: private addresses on your tailnet, the password manager's accounts, where backups go, alerts on the phone. Each step says first what it gives you. Do the N I can do for you runs every step that's ready; the rest say in one line what only you can do. Once everything is done, Setup leaves the sidebar, and comes back by itself if a step comes undone.

More: Getting Started.

docs.title: Backups
docs.text:
Each app's newest copy, the encrypted off-site jobs, and the last restore test: once a month the app restores a sample and checks it against the live files, so a backup is proven, not assumed. Back up now, Test a restore, the printable Recovery kit (where the backups and passphrases are), and Move out… / Move in… for a new computer.

More: Backups, Disaster Recovery.

docs.title: Finances
docs.text:
A screen of the app itself, not a separate app: the household's money, typed in by hand and kept on this computer, with no bank connection. The Dashboard takes one paycheck at a time: checking now and after the next paycheck, every account after that paycheck's bills, and what's left.

Net worth draws it month by month, with a home's and a car's equity beside what's still owed on them.

Plan holds the calendar, the payments that repeat, and each person's paycheck: take-home, the deductions, and where it goes.

Spending keeps what actually happened (transactions with receipts, budgets, and reports by category, payee, and month). Phones you allow can see or change Finances too, and the file goes off-site with the nightly backup, encrypted. More: the phone companion.

docs.title: Tidy Up
docs.text:
Also a screen of the app itself. It keeps the music, films, shows, books, and audiobooks on the media drive sorted, tagged, and lean. Drop a download into a folder it watches and it works out what it is, cleans it up, and files it in the right library, as things arrive, once a day, or when you press Tidy up now.

Each library has a tile saying what it holds and how far along it is, beside the genres and what was done recently, each with Undo.

Each library's tab has its own clean-up. Music is rebuilt with beets step by step (scanned, built, swapped in, checked, freed), with lyrics and playlists; films and shows are shrunk with Tdarr; books are tidied in Calibre; an audiobook in many files becomes one. Anything thrown away goes to the Trash first.

More: Tidy Up.

docs.title: Settings and phones
docs.text:
Every setting of the homelab as a form, the everyday ones first, searchable. Passwords and tokens are never shown back: Test checks one, Copy hands it to the password manager. This Mac has the machine and its updates; Appearance the theme, accent, and contrast; People gives each person their own sign-in and a welcome page.

Phones pairs a phone with a QR code. A phone can only look until you let it make changes, and sees Finances only if you choose that for it.

More: Environment (every setting), Pocket ID (sign-in for the household).

docs.title: On your iPhone
docs.text:
The Homelab app for iPhone and iPad is how the household keeps an eye on the homelab: the same homelab in your pocket, at home or away. It opens behind Face ID, and a phone only looks until you let it make changes (Settings › Phones on the computer); then Start, Restart, or a backup asks Face ID first.

Status leads with what needs a look, with Start and Logs right there, then each category folded into one line. A tap on any app opens its page: its state, Open, Restart, Stop, its log, and Roll back. Backups shows the last one, the restore test, and anything stale.

Finances, on the phones you allow, is laid out as the phone's own Settings: checking now and after the next paycheck, net worth over three months, then Transactions, Budgets, Investments, and the rest, each a tap away. Without a connection it shows the last Finances it read, marked As of, to look at.

It locks itself whenever you leave it, and Settings has the homelab's everyday settings, each change asking Face ID.

It's built with Xcode on your own Mac for now, not from the App Store: apple-client has the steps. Any other phone (Android, a visitor's) can open the same Status, Backups, and Finances in its browser once paired. What each device can do: What each device can do.

docs.title: Updates
docs.text:
The app looks for a new version every 15 minutes. When there is one, a line at the top of the window says so: What's new shows the patch notes, Update now puts it in place and opens it again, keeping your settings, data, and own apps. The apps themselves update overnight, each with its data copied first, and one that comes back unwell is rolled back by itself.

More: Upgrading.

docs.title: And from a terminal
docs.text: Everything the app does, homelab does from a terminal too, with a plan shown before anything changes: ./homelab status, ./homelab install <app>, ./homelab fix, ./homelab backup, ./homelab media. Every command: Commands.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptoms and their usual fixes, grouped by where you notice them. When none of these fits, make a diagnostics report (Settings › This Mac › Make a diagnostics report, or ./homelab report): it collects doctor, status, the setup checklist, the jobs, and the logs of anything unwell, with every password and token removed and your home folder, account name, and email addresses replaced, ready to share. Read it through before you send it.

Many problems are fixed by Fix it on Status (./homelab fix): it shows what it will do first.

An app's log usually says why it is unwell. With Ollama and a model on this machine (ollama pull llama3.2), Explain this under the log on the app's page (or ./homelab logs <app> --explain) has the model read the last 200 lines and say what is wrong, the likely cause, and what to try.
