The log stays on this machine, and what looks like a password or token is removed before the model reads it. A small model can be wrong: the line it quotes is in the log below to check.

docs.title: The desktop app
docs.text: Symptom Fix macOS says the app is damaged or from an unidentified developer The app is not signed with an Apple Developer ID, and macOS blocks unsigned apps downloaded in a browser: run xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/Homelab Wizard.app" once, then open it again. Installing with install.sh (README › Get started) avoids this The app opens again on the same version after Update now, or the line says … did not install Something stopped the new build going in place, and the line says what: most often Windows' SmartScreen or Smart App Control blocking a new unsigned build, or the administrator's prompt (Windows) or password (a Linux package) not given. Try again, or Download it and install the new version by hand (on Windows, SmartScreen's More info › Run anyway). Each attempt's steps are in update.log: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Homelab Wizard\update.log on Windows, ~/Library/Caches/Homelab Wizard/update.log on a Mac, ~/.cache/Homelab Wizard/update.log on Linux "Unknown app" in Choose apps, or only some apps listed The app is older than the homelab files: Update now on the line at the top (it downloads the newest build, checks it, replaces the app, and opens it again, on every system). Newer builds say this homelab folder is newer than this copy instead. ./homelab in Terminal keeps working meanwhile Status is slow to load ./homelab status --timing says which part takes the time (the runtime, the containers, the apps' pages, the settings check, or docker stats); Settings › This Mac › Make a diagnostics report includes the same. Each docker command costs more with Docker Desktop on Windows than with OrbStack on a Mac "Choose the homelab folder in Setup first" Settings › This Mac › Homelab folder › Choose… (or Change…) and pick ~/Homelab (the folder with compose.yaml) Status says an app is Restarting, or shows restarted N× It stops on its own and Docker starts it again. Its log (on its page: click its row on Status, or ./homelab logs <app>) says why: often a setting it needs, a full disk, or a database it cannot reach. The badge clears when the container is next recreated, for example by an update Status says the container runtime is not running Open OrbStack (open -a OrbStack) and turn on Settings › General › Start at login. Every app is paused until it runs A button says another install or setup step is running One change runs at a time. Wait for the panel to finish; quitting asks first while something runs No menu bar icon Open the app once; the icon starts with it and stays after the window closes. On Linux it needs a status-notifier tray Recent alerts says the alert token is not set up Setup › Alerts on the phone › Set up the alert token (run it again if you did it before October 2026)

docs.title: At home
docs.text: Symptom Fix Tailscale keeps restarting, or its sign-in link stops working An older homelab folder: Tailscale gave up on the sign-in after a minute and restarted with a new link. Update (Update now on the line at the top), then ./homelab tailnet login (or Setup › Addresses on your tailnet): it now waits up to 30 minutes An app's tailnet address does not open (Home mode) The phone or computer needs the Tailscale app, on and signed in to the same account, the homelab's own machine too: its Tailscale runs inside the homelab, apart from the machine (Setup › This machine opens the tailnet addresses; until then its localhost addresses work there). On this machine, Setup › Addresses on your tailnet must be done: if Tailscale waits for a sign-in, the step (or ./homelab tailnet login) opens its sign-in page; no auth key is needed. HTTPS Certificates must be on in the Tailscale admin console › DNS With a domain: photos.example.com (or any app name) does not open on a phone or laptop The device must use the Mac for DNS: Wi-Fi settings › DNS › 192.168.1.10. On iPhone also turn off iCloud Private Relay and Limit IP address tracking for the home Wi-Fi; on Android set Private DNS to Off. Each sends names past AdGuard With a domain: app names do not open on the Mac with a VPN on (or at all on the Mac) Setup › This Mac finds its apps by name (./homelab domain resolver --apply) writes /etc/resolver/<domain>, so the Mac asks AdGuard Home for every name under the domain whatever DNS the VPN sets. It asks for the Mac's password once. A VPN with a kill switch can still block the home network: turn on Allow LAN connections and turn off the kill switch With a domain: on a phone at home with a VPN on, only the public apps open (photos, passwords, music), and the others say the server cannot be found The VPN's DNS knows only the public names. Run Set up the domain again with a Cloudflare token: it adds the home record (*.your-domain → this machine's address at home), which any DNS server answers. Then turn on Allow LAN connections in the VPN app (on an iPhone, Proton VPN may need its kill switch off first), so the phone reaches the address over Wi-Fi rather than through the VPN A password saved for one app does not work, or the password manager fills in another app's One login can serve two names (Navidrome's at navidrome. is also Feishin's at music.), and a password manager keeps a password per name; find the entry under the other name. A Subsonic music app (Arpeggi, Amperfy, play:Sub) signs in at navidrome., never at music., which is Feishin's web page. Without a domain, every app is localhost or one tailnet name with a different port, and most password managers ignore the port: in Bitwarden set each entry's URI match detection to Host, which includes the port With a domain: Find the apps on this Mac stops with making /etc/resolver with sudo: exit status 1 An older build ran sudo where no password could be typed. Update now: the step now asks for the Mac's password in a window (on Linux too, as do Set up Docker and keeping the computer awake). Or run ./homelab domain resolver --apply in Terminal With a domain: the browser warns about the certificate, or shows no padlock Run Set up the domain (./homelab domain setup --ssl); the first certificate takes a few minutes. If it fails, the Cloudflare token lacks a permission: Settings › CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN › Test names it With a domain: an app works at localhost but not at its name ./homelab domain setup adds the proxy host for apps installed since it last ran Everything stopped after a restart FileVault keeps everything off until someone logs in; log in and the startup job brings the baseline back within a few minutes The Mac's address changed Reserve it again in the router; phones (and, with a domain, the app names) point at 192.168.1.10

docs.title: Away from home
docs.text: Symptom Fix An app does not open away from home (Home mode) Turn Tailscale on in the phone; the apps open at their tailnet addresses anywhere. Nothing is published to the internet With a domain: a public app does not open on mobile data Check the tunnel: Status shows Cloudflare Tunnel running, Settings › TUNNEL_TOKEN › Test passes, and ./homelab domain setup has run since the token was added. Only apps marked public are published With a domain: a private app does not open away from home That is by design. Turn on Tailscale to reach it privately Alerts reach the phone only at home Home mode: turn Tailscale on in the phone. With a domain: run ./homelab domain setup after Set up the alert token: it publishes ntfy once the publishers use the token Status › Protection says bans are not enforced (or doctor or an alert says the proxy's bouncer is not pulling) Click Fix on the Protection card (or Fix it, or ./homelab fix): it removes the old bouncer, restarts CrowdSec, and restarts the proxy. If it comes back, ./homelab logs nginx-proxy-manager shows why (CrowdSec) CrowdSec blocked you ./homelab compose crowdsec exec crowdsec cscli decisions list, then cscli decisions delete --ip <address> (Runbooks)

docs.title: Apps
docs.text: Symptom Fix AdGuard Home does not start on Linux: bind 0.0.0.0:53: address already in use, or on Windows: listen udp4 0.0.0.0:53: bind: Only one usage of each socket address Something already holds port 53. On Linux, systemd-resolved (127.0.0.53:53): installing again fixes it, since the homelab sets ADGUARD_DNS_BIND_IP (Settings › AdGuard Home DNS listens on) to this machine's home-network address, where port 53 is free (by hand: the address homelab doctor names, then homelab install adguard-home). On Windows, Internet Connection Sharing (SharedAccess, the Mobile hotspot service) holds 0.0.0.0:53, and Docker Desktop binds DNS there even with ADGUARD_DNS_BIND_IP set (seen on a Windows 11 PC): in PowerShell as administrator, Set-Service SharedAccess -StartupType Disabled, restart the PC, then homelab install adguard-home. Mobile hotspot stops working until you set it back to Manual On Fedora (or another Linux with SELinux), apps stop with Permission denied on their folders Fedora's Docker (moby-engine) gives containers SELinux labels, which keep them out of folders in your home folder; ./homelab doctor warns about it. Turn Docker's SELinux option off (--selinux-enabled in /etc/sysconfig/docker, or "selinux-enabled" in /etc/docker/daemon.json) and restart Docker, or use Docker CE from docker.com, which runs without it This account may not use Docker Engine yet (Docker Desktop on Windows) Docker runs, but your account is not allowed to use it. On Linux: sudo usermod -aG docker $USER, then log out and back in. On Windows, as an administrator: net localgroup docker-users %USERNAME% /add, then sign out and back in Installing stops with Docker Hub's download limit … was reached (Docker's own words: 429 Too Many Requests or toomanyrequests) Docker Hub limits how many images one internet connection downloads without an account. Wait an hour and press Install again (or ./homelab up again): what already downloaded is kept. To lift the limit, make a free account at hub.docker.com and run docker login once An app is unhealthy or stopped Click its row on Status: its page shows the last 200 log lines, and Restart often clears it. Status lists what needs a look first, and Fix it offers the usual repairs An app broke after the nightly update Roll back on its page puts the previous version back (kept a week). Pause the rest with Pause on Status's Nightly updates tile, read its log, and check the app's release notes; the update table says which images update and which are pinned Vaultwarden says it needs a secure connection Open it at its https address from Status (its tailnet address in Home mode, https://passwords.example.com with a domain), not by IP Vaultwarden's web vault shows a black screen Seen in LibreWolf (ISSUE-0020): use Safari or another browser MoneyMatter signs in, then loops Open it at exactly MONEYMATTER_URL The installer moved an app's port Something else held the port; the plan (or ./homelab plan <app>) says which setting changed and why. On macOS, AirPlay Receiver holds 5000 and 7000; ./homelab doctor warns about it Prowlarr, Sonarr, Radarr, Bazarr, Seerr, or qBittorrent are not connected Status › More… › Connect apps (or ./homelab wire --apply); qBittorrent needs a permanent Web UI password in QBITTORRENT_PASSWORD

docs.title: Finances
docs.text: Symptom Fix Finances were changed on another device after this was read Someone saved on a phone (or the computer) after this screen read the plan. The latest is shown: check your change and save it again. Neither save undoes the other The heading says Balances from …: N days ago The balances in checking and the cards were typed in a week or more ago, and Finances reads forward from that day. Update balances on the dashboard types today's in, each box starting at what is expected A paycheck or bill shows under Taken as done but has not happened yet It is dated between the day the balances were typed in and today, so it is taken as in them. Click Not yet beside it: it then comes today A loan or card owes more or less than its statement Give it its interest rate (the account's form): interest is charged a day at a time and each payment pays it first. A card paid in full each time is charged none Finances do not show on a phone, or show no Edit Settings › Phones: Sees Finances or Changes Finances beside it. A phone paired with the http: link never gets them (Phone companion)

docs.title: Tidy Up
docs.text: Symptom Fix A download stays in Downloads and shows under Needs a look Tidy Up couldn't tell what it is (a video whose name says nothing, songs with no artist or album). It's a film…, It's an episode…, or Name these songs… says what it is, and Tidy Up files it; Leave it keeps it where it is for good (Tidy Up › Needs a look) It's packed in a .rar file… Tidy Up doesn't open .rar or .7z files. Double-click it to unpack it, and what's inside is filed on the next sweep. A .zip is unpacked for you A library or watched folder says Not there now Its drive isn't plugged in. Plug it in, or Choose another… beside it A step waits for a tool (ffmpeg, Python, Calibre) This machine on Tidy Up (or homelab media preflight) lists what is missing with its fix. Without ffmpeg, Install gets it with no Terminal (homelab media install ffmpeg --yes) The music check finds songs missing, and the space can't be freed It says how many and whose. Put the old library back… returns the library as it was; Check again once they are found. Nothing is freed until every song is there Films or shows wait in Tdarr and never shrink Set up Tdarr (or a library's Shrink) gives Tdarr's node the worker it needs, and its sign-in if it asks for one (Tidy Up › Settings) Something went that shouldn't have Undo beside it in What I did today or Recently done puts it back from the Trash (the Recycle Bin on Windows: restore it from there)

docs.title: Backups and jobs
docs.text: Symptom Fix Backups shows a stale copy The row says why from its app's state. Stopped: the nightly copy skips it; start it, and tonight's copy catches up. Running: the nightly job did not run or the dump failed: ./homelab schedule status, then Back up now and read its output Backups shows a copy as Paused Its app is stopped because the drive its folders are on is unplugged (the Hobbies drive): plug the drive in, the app starts, and the next nightly backup copies it again. Its last copies are kept meanwhile An off-site job failed or has not run for a week Backups › Off-site jobs shows Duplicati's error. Most often the backup folder is missing or offline: the cloud drive's app is not running, or the drive is unplugged (ISSUE-0003) Off-site jobs fail after months of working The cloud drive may be full: its quota cannot be read from this machine (ISSUE-0019), so check the space left in the drive's own app Create the backup jobs says Duplicati does not see the folder It recreates Duplicati for a changed BACKUP_DESTINATION by itself, so this means the folder is not reachable from containers: check that the cloud drive's app is running (or the drive plugged in) and the path in Settings is right, then ./homelab up and the step again Off-site jobs says to set DUPLICATI_PASSWORD It is the Duplicati web UI password from .env; Settings › Test checks it schedule status shows a job not loaded ./homelab schedule install again, then log out and back in (ISSUE-0005) An alert says a disk is low on space Settings › This Mac › Storage and ./homelab doctor show each disk and what is on it; doctor also says how much the runtime keeps in images, volumes, and build cache, and the alert how much pruning images would free. On the homelab folder's disk, docker image prune -a removes images no container uses (often many GB after updates) and Status › More… › Clean up old containers removes leftovers; on the media disk, finished downloads and Immich's trash (Administration › Trash) are the usual culprits. The check clears on the next watchdog run once the disk has room healthchecks.io says the Mac is down, but it is up The watchdog is not running: ./homelab schedule status, and check HEARTBEAT_URL with Test An alert says to delete a plain vault export A readable Bitwarden export is in recovery-staging/secrets: delete it and export again as a password-protected .json (Backups) Backups has no Test a restore button It appears once Off-site jobs lists the Homelab AppData job with a run (named exactly that, as in Automation) Test a restore fails The log names the step. "no job named" means the job has another name: rename it, or run ./homelab restore-test --auto --job "<name>". On a difference, the restored files stay in recovery-staging/restore-test for a look; run the AppData job again in Duplicati and test again, and read Duplicati's log if it repeats

docs.title: "homelab can run in the background" notices
docs.text: macOS announces each login item when it is added or changes. The homelab has one: its background agent (starting the apps at login, the nightly backup, the watchdog, the phone companion, keeping awake, and the menu bar item). Older versions installed six, which the app replaces with the one agent the first time it opens. It is listed in System Settings › General › Login Items & Extensions; Settings › This Mac › Runs in the background › What are these? says what each one does, and Turn the scheduled jobs off removes them (the apps keep running, but nothing starts them after a restart, backs them up, or watches them; Setup offers to put them back). Until the builds are signed with a Developer ID, an app update can make macOS announce them once more, because each unsigned build looks new to it. On macOS 13 and later the app registers the agent as its own login item (SMAppService), so the list names it Homelab Wizard rather than a bare "homelab"; where macOS refuses that or waits for approval, the app puts the ordinary launchd job back (~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.homelab.agent.plist), and tries again with the next build. What it last did is in ~/Library/Application Support/Homelab Wizard/login-item.json.

docs.title: Apps on an external drive are stopped after a restart
docs.text: Status says Waiting for the Hobbies drive (with your drive's name) for these. Docker starts the apps before macOS has mounted the drive, so the ones whose folders are on it cannot start. The startup job waits up to 15 minutes for every drive the apps use, then starts them, and the watchdog starts any left over within 15 minutes of the drive appearing. If they stay stopped, check the drive is mounted under /Volumes, run ./homelab schedule install, and read scripts/logs/startup.log.

docs.title: The laptop's battery runs down
docs.text: The homelab's apps run all the time inside the container runtime, whether or not anyone is signed in, and some work hard in the background. On battery, the battery saver pauses those (Status says Paused on battery) and starts them again on power; the rest keep running. The keep-awake job (caffeinate -s) only holds sleep off while plugged in. For the longest battery life, quit OrbStack while away from power; everything starts again when it opens. Status › What's using power names the apps working hardest right now; one that stays busy for hours (beyond a photo import or a library scan) is worth stopping if you don't use it. pmset -g assertions shows what holds sleep off.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text: What to do after pulling a newer version, and what each batch of changes asks of you. The newest batch is at the top; once you have done its steps, nothing below it applies again. For what each version changed, read the CHANGELOG; this page is only what you need to do.

docs.title: Every time
docs.text:
In the app there is nothing to look for. Homelab Wizard looks for updates by itself, the homelab files and its own build together: every 15 minutes while it runs, and when you bring its window forward. What it finds it downloads at once. Then one line at the top of every screen says Homelab Wizard 0.15.0 is ready (the version, when it has one), with What's new, Later, and Update now; the menu bar item says Update to 0.15.0.

Update now moves the homelab files forward and starts the homelab again, then puts the new app in place (checked against GitHub's SHA-256 checksum) and opens it again on the same screen: the line says Updating… with a bar, then Updated to 0.15.0. Your apps keep running. Later hides the line until something newer turns up; the sidebar's ● Update ready brings it back. On the testing channel the build is the latest one (Releases › Latest, rebuilt from every change to main); on stable the newest v* release. On Windows and Linux it is the one for how the app was installed (the installer or portable zip, the AppImage, or the .deb, .rpm, or Arch package).

  • On quit: quitting the app also puts a downloaded update in place, so the next open is the new version (Settings › This Mac › Updates › Install updates when I quit the app, on unless you turn it off). An app in Program Files (the Windows installer's) and a Linux package ask for an administrator's approval or password, so there they are installed with Update now only.
  • When it can't finish by itself (the homelab folder has changes of its own, or this copy of the app cannot replace itself), the line says why in one sentence, and offers the download when there is one. Each attempt's steps are kept in update.log (Troubleshooting).
  • To look now: Look now in Settings › This Mac, or Setup's Check again.

In Terminal:

cd ~/Homelab
./homelab upgrade
./homelab doctor
  • A folder the app made with Set it up for me has no git: upgrade compares it with the homelab files inside the app instead, so a new app build brings the update. When the new app opens, it puts those files in place by itself (the line says Finishing the update…), so updating is one step. It keeps .env, data, and your own apps, and a file you edited that the update also changes is saved beside it as .local.
  • upgrade lists the changes waiting on GitHub and what is new in the CHANGELOG, says whether the desktop app or the settings changed, and asks before going ahead. It then moves the folder forward (fast-forward only: your own edits are never merged or overwritten; when the update changes a file you edited, git stops and nothing changes), rebuilds the CLI, and runs up.
  • It moves only to a release: a v* tag on main whose build provenance shows the project's own release workflow built that very commit, as the app's own update is checked. A tag that points elsewhere, or a release with no provenance, is refused and nothing changes. Changes on main newer than the latest release come with the next one, once its build is published; upgrade says how many are waiting.
  • up adds any new settings from .env.example to .env (generating new secrets), and recreates apps whose compose definition changed. It never touches values you already have.
  • doctor ends without ✗ lines.
  • Which changes you get is UPDATE_CHANNEL in Settings: testing (every release of main, one per change to the app or the engine) or stable (only a new minor or major version, vX.Y.0).
  • Something wrong after an upgrade: ./homelab upgrade --back (or go back to … beside the version in Settings › This Mac) returns the homelab files to where they were before it, then runs up. Settings, data, and your own apps stay. Undo one app's nightly image update with ./homelab rollback <app> instead.
  • Before upgrade existed (release run 5 and earlier), the same is git pull, then ./homelab up.

docs.title: After 0.15.0: Finances, and a rebuild in one command
docs.text:
Update now as usual; nothing else is required. What to expect:

  • Finances joins the sidebar, empty until you type in an account, a paycheck, and a payment. Its file (data/finance.json) goes off-site with the nightly backup inside the encrypted Secrets job, as the household and the phones do.
  • Finances show on no phone until you pick Sees Finances or Changes Finances beside it in Settings › Phones (or ./homelab phone finances <id> view). A phone paired with the http: link never gets them: pair it again with the https link first.
  • On Windows, if updating went round in a loop (the app closed, opened again, and was still the old version), the fix is in the new build's own updater, which the old one cannot run: download Homelab-Wizard-Windows-Setup.exe from Releases › Latest and run it once (SmartScreen: More info › Run anyway). Later updates go in by themselves, asking for an administrator's approval only when the app is in Program Files.
  • ./homelab rebuild <backup folder> is new: nothing to do now, but it is the first thing to reach for if the machine is ever lost (Disaster Recovery).

docs.title: After 0.15.0: each app's version is kept in .env
docs.text: Update now as usual; nothing else is required. Within 15 minutes (the watchdog's next run) .env gains, under the heading The version each app runs, one <APP>_DIGEST line for each app the nightly update moves forward: the image it runs and that image's digest. A version you set by hand (IMMICH_VERSION) still wins. homelab update and a rollback keep them current, and homelab up, a move, and homelab rebuild start those versions again, so data restored on a new machine is opened by the version that wrote it, not the newest. Delete an app's line to let it start on its newest version.

docs.title: After 0.14.0: the homelab talks to Docker directly
docs.text:
Update now as usual; nothing else is required. What to expect:

  • up adds DOCKER_API=auto to .env: the homelab reads the containers, their events and what they use, and runs commands in them (the nightly database copies), through Docker's own API rather than the docker command. Starting, stopping and updating apps is still docker compose.
  • ./homelab doctor says which is in use (reads the containers through the engine's API at …), and the last time the API failed and the docker command answered instead. If something reads wrong, set DOCKER_API to off in Settings (or .env) to go back to the docker command, and send the diagnostics report.
  • Status keeps itself current: the background agent sends each change with the Status after it, so a screen no longer asks again when you open it. Nothing to set.

docs.title: After 0.14.0: Watchtower goes
docs.text:
Update now as usual (the line at the top of the window, or ./homelab upgrade); nothing else is required. What to expect:

  • Starting the homelab removes Watchtower's container (homelab_system-watchtower-1) and its image, saying so: the background agent runs the nightly updates now, at the same time (WATCHTOWER_SCHEDULE, 4:00 by default), copying each app's data before its update so a rollback can put it back.
  • Every app updates nightly unless it is pinned (its note says why), a database, or built here, as before; held apps (UPDATES_HELD) and Pause nightly updates work as before. WATCHTOWER_VERSION and UPDATES_HELD_CONTAINERS in .env are no longer used and can go.
  • The phone keeps getting the nightly summary on the watchtower topic.

docs.title: After 0.14.0: updates find themselves, and take one step
docs.text:
Update this one last time as before (Setup, or ./homelab upgrade); from then on the line at the top of the window does it, as Every time says. What changes:

  • No more Check again to see an update: the app looks every 15 minutes and when the window comes forward, and downloads what it finds.
  • Setup's update card and the Restart to update banner are gone: one line at the top of every screen, and Update now does the homelab files and the app together. Setup no longer comes back into the sidebar for an update.
  • Install updates when I quit the app is on unless you turned it off; it moved to Settings › This Mac › Updates, with Look now.
  • The menu bar item's update line says Update to 0.15.0, and opens the window to put it in place.

docs.title: 23 October 2026: Status follows live, and the homelab heals
docs.text:
Update as usual (Setup, or ./homelab upgrade); nothing else is required. What to expect:

  • The update recreates six containers once, so background work yields the CPU to the apps in use: Duplicati, Immich's machine learning, qBittorrent, Dawarich's worker, Karakeep's crawler, and Speedtest Tracker. Each is down for a few seconds. If Status still shows settings changed on one afterwards, Fix it recreates it.
  • Two new settings are added to .env: AUTO_HEAL=true (the watchdog restarts an app that hangs, once in 6 hours at most; false makes it alert only) and OLLAMA_MODEL, empty (which model Explain this log uses).
  • Watchtower and docker-socket-proxy stop updating themselves: they control Docker, so they now stay on a version you choose (WATCHTOWER_VERSION=1.23.2, SOCKET_PROXY_VERSION=v0.5.0, added to .env). These are the versions they run today, so they are recreated once and nothing else changes. To update one later: read its release notes, change the setting, then ./homelab update watchtower (or docker-socket-proxy).
  • On Linux, add your account to the docker group if Setup's first step says so (then log out and back in); on Windows, to docker-users.

What is new:

  • Status changes the moment an app starts, stops, or changes health, on the computer, in the menu bar, and on paired phones. Longer jobs show a progress bar.
  • An app that runs but whose page does not answer shows Not answering (with why); one still running settings you have since changed shows settings changed. Fix it handles both.
  • Update on an app shows its release notes first (./homelab updates notes <app>). An update that leaves an app not answering is rolled back by itself, as one that leaves it unhealthy was.
  • Explain this log in an app's Logs panel, with Ollama and a model on this machine (ollama pull llama3.2); ./homelab logs <app> --explain does the same.
  • Kiosk mode: pair a TV or a wall tablet like a phone, with &kiosk at the end of the pairing link (Settings › Phones shows it).
  • The power card shows each busy app's last five minutes.
  • Typed values in Settings survive a search or a change of page, and live updates keep the keyboard's place.
  • For scripts: --json output includes step lines for longer jobs ({"type":"step","data":{"n":2,"total":5,"text":"…"}}).

docs.title: 16 October 2026: the app updates itself
docs.text:
From this build on, Setup › Update also replaces the app on a Mac, so there is no more downloading from GitHub Actions. An app from before this change cannot do that yet: if Setup says A newer Homelab Wizard is ready with Open the release builds, download it this one last time from GitHub › Releases › Latest (Homelab-Wizard-macOS.dmg), drag it to Applications, and clear the download flag:

xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/Homelab Wizard.app"

Nothing else to run. What is new:

  • Setup › Do the steps I can runs every ready step in turn. Each step now says what it gives you first.
  • Status: categories where everything runs fold into one line; each app row has a phone button (its address as a QR code) and, for the proxy, AdGuard, Duplicati, and PsiTransfer, a key button with the sign-in. This week, What the apps keep, and an x% up this week badge are new. Protection has Fix when the proxy stops enforcing CrowdSec's bans, and the watchdog card has Fix it.
  • Settings shows the everyday settings first (Show all settings for the rest), and People adds and removes household members (it needs Pocket ID).
  • Backups › Moving to a new machine: Move out… and Move in….
  • Choose apps has a shorter plan (the rest under Details), and the Media automation preset now includes qBittorrent with Gluetun, its VPN, and Seerr.
  • Tailscale needs no auth key: Setup's tailnet step (or ./homelab tailnet login) opens Tailscale's sign-in page. A TAILSCALE_AUTHKEY you already set still works.
  • With a domain, on a Mac: Setup › This Mac finds its apps by name (./homelab domain resolver) writes /etc/resolver/<domain>. Once it is ✓, lines you added to /etc/hosts for the apps, or a DNS server set by hand on the Mac, can go.
  • In Home mode, TAILNET_ADMIN_APPS=false (Settings › Admin apps on the tailnet) keeps the proxy, AdGuard, Duplicati, and Dozzle off the tailnet; the next ./homelab tailnet setup or install applies it.
  • Cmd and + or − (Ctrl on Windows and Linux) change the text size; Cmd and 0 goes back.
  • For scripts: every --json line now carries "schema": 1.

docs.title: 16 October 2026: Home mode is the default
docs.text: Nothing to do. A new homelab starts in Home mode (HOMELAB_DOMAIN empty: every app at its address on your tailnet). Your .env keeps its domain; only .env.example's default changed.

docs.title: 16 October 2026: CrowdSec starts again
docs.text: If Status showed CrowdSec restarting (with a growing restarted N× badge), ./homelab upgrade fixes it: it picks up the new AppSec setting the next time CrowdSec restarts, which it was doing every few seconds. Status then shows it running, and ./homelab doctor no longer says the bouncer last pulled decisions days ago.

docs.title: 15 October 2026: the public repository
docs.text:
The project now lives in a public repository, Snooper42/homelab-wizard, with example.com and neutral examples in its docs. A homelab folder cloned from the earlier private repository switches over once, in Terminal:

cd ~/Homelab
git remote set-url origin https://github.com/Snooper42/homelab-wizard.git
git fetch origin
git reset --hard origin/main
./homelab up

.env, data/, appdata/, and your own apps (stacks/custom) are not in git, so they stay as they are, and your real domain and folders keep coming from .env. The reset replaces only the homelab's own files (an edit you made to one of them is lost; git stash first keeps it). From then on, ./homelab upgrade and Setup › Update follow the public repository. A folder made with Set it up for me has no git and needs nothing.

docs.title: 15 October 2026: single sign-on
docs.text: up generates POCKET_ID_API_KEY and restarts Pocket ID with it, and restarts Karakeep, Open WebUI, Paperless-ngx, Mealie, Vikunja, and Immich once (they can now read sign-in settings and reach Pocket ID through the proxy). Nothing changes how people sign in until you run ./homelab sso setup.

docs.title: 15 October 2026: database versions as settings
docs.text: Paperless's, Ghostfolio's, RomM's, Docmost's, and MoneyMatter's databases now take their PostgreSQL major version from .env (up adds the settings with the versions they run now), and all but Paperless's set PGDATA to the folder they already use. The next up restarts those database containers once, which takes a few seconds; nothing else changes. Move to a new major version with ./homelab db upgrade <database> only.

docs.title: 15 October 2026: updates you can undo
docs.text: The nightly backup moves from 04:30 to 03:30, before Watchtower, so every update has a fresh dump behind it: click Install the jobs on Setup again (or ./homelab schedule install). ./homelab upgrade restarts Watchtower with its new settings (it keeps old images now, and the watchdog tidies them). Rollbacks work for updates from then on.

docs.title: 15 October 2026: the phone companion
docs.text: A fifth scheduled job runs the phone companion. Setup's Scheduled jobs step shows 4 of 5 until you click Install the jobs again (or ./homelab schedule install). It listens on port 8099 for the home network and the tailnet only, and shows nothing until a phone is paired (./homelab phone pair). Set PHONE_COMPANION=false in Settings first if you would rather not have it. Then Set up the domain once more (or ./homelab domain setup) gives it https://homelab.<domain>; in Home mode the next install, or ./homelab tailnet setup, gives it the tailnet address.

docs.title: 15 October 2026: Home mode, a starter pick, two new apps
docs.text:
Nothing to do for a homelab with a domain. upgrade adds empty *_URL settings (each app's own address, used in Home mode) and HOMELAB_BASELINE; empty keeps everything as it was. Homepage restarts once on the next up because its list of allowed names grew.

Two optional apps: Docmost (the household wiki) and Dawarich (location history). Install either from Choose apps › Add more.

docs.title: 15 October 2026: ad blocking on the tailnet
docs.text: A new optional app, tailnet-dns, lets every phone and computer signed in to Tailscale use AdGuard Home, at home and away, with no router or Wi-Fi setting. Nothing changes until you install it (Choose apps › Ad blocking, or ./homelab install @adblock); then do what the install shows in the Tailscale admin console › DNS. Setup's AdGuard step now has Set up AdGuard, which answers AdGuard's first-run wizard for you; a login you already made stays as it is.

docs.title: 15 October 2026: one Compose project per category
docs.text:
Each category is now its own Compose project, so OrbStack shows the containers grouped as Network, Security, System, Media, and so on, instead of one long homelab_core list. The containers move once:

cd ~/Homelab
./homelab upgrade

upgrade runs homelab migrate before up: it backs up first (as the nightly job does), then removes each container from homelab_core and starts the app again in its category's project. Settings and data stay where they are: the folders under data/ and the named volumes keep their names. Apps you had stopped are left stopped. Afterwards ./homelab doctor no longer mentions homelab_core, and the app's Status shows every app as before.

To move them without the rest of the update: ./homelab migrate shows the plan, ./homelab migrate --apply does it.

docs.title: 15 October 2026: keep awake
docs.text: A fourth scheduled job keeps the Mac from sleeping while it is plugged in. Setup's Scheduled jobs step shows 3 of 4 until you click Install the jobs again (or ./homelab schedule install). Set KEEP_AWAKE=false in Settings first if you would rather it slept.

docs.title: 15 October 2026: one Compose file per category
docs.text: The core apps moved out of compose.yaml into compose/<category>.yaml. They stay in the same Compose project, so nothing is recreated and no step is needed. If you edited compose.yaml by hand, upgrade stops and says so (fast-forward only); move your edit into the category's file in compose/ after the update, or into your own apps with homelab custom.

docs.title: 15 October 2026: new apps
docs.text:
Ten optional apps: Baikal, PairDrop, PsiTransfer, Pocket ID, Wallos, Changedetection.io, Memos, Homebox, RomM, and Ghostfolio. Install any from Choose apps. RomM looks for games on the media drive under games/roms/<platform>.

  • There is a new alert topic, reminders, for notifications from the apps themselves (Wallos renewals, Changedetection.io). Run Set up the alert token on Setup again (or ./homelab notify setup) so the homelab may publish to it, then subscribe to reminders in the ntfy app on the phone.

docs.title: 15 October 2026: new categories
docs.text:
The apps are regrouped: Network, Security, System, Cloud & Files, Documents, Finance, Media, Media Automation, and Household. Nothing running changes and no step is needed.

  • Each app's note moved to its new folder under services/ (for example services/infrastructure/Duplicati.md is now services/system/Duplicati.md). A bookmark to an old note needs updating.
  • Your own apps (stacks/custom) keep working: infrastructure, productivity, and home count as System, Documents, and Household. New ones made with Add your own app use the new names.
  • ./homelab install cat:<id> takes the new ids (cat:network, cat:household, and so on).

docs.title: 11 October 2026: native look, disk space, restore drills
docs.text:
Setup › Update (or ./homelab upgrade), then the newest app build. Nothing else to run.

  • The app follows each platform: on the Mac the window buttons sit in a translucent sidebar, and the menu bar gains View (Settings… on ⌘,) and Help. Windows 11 and Linux get their own look.
  • The watchdog now checks the free space on each disk the homelab writes to, so the first run after the update can alert if one is already low (Troubleshooting says where space usually hides). Setup › Disk space shows each disk.
  • Each restore test goes on record with how long it took (Backups). Earlier tests are not in the record; the next one starts it.
  • Backups shows when each Duplicati job runs next.

docs.title: October 2026: the app grows up (after release run 4)
docs.text:
This one time, pull by hand (upgrade arrives with it): git checkout main, git pull, then ./homelab up, and get the newest app build. From then on, Setup › Update or ./homelab upgrade does it.

New in the app

  • Status: restart, update, stop, and logs for each app, with what needs a look first. It also shows recent alerts and the savings trend.
  • Backups: each app's newest copy, each Duplicati job's last run, Back up now, and Test a restore.
  • Setup: Use Proton Drive, Create the backup jobs, and the homelab's own updates (Update), including when the app itself has a newer build.
  • Settings: Test checks a login or token with its service; Copy hands a password to Vaultwarden without showing it.
  • Elsewhere: search on Choose apps, and Show in Finder after a diagnostics report.
  • Menu bar: the newest alert, the last backup, and Update ready.

New in the jobs

  • Nightly backup: records the day's savings, reminds about the restore test and the vault export, asks GitHub for updates, and on Sundays sends Homelab this week.
  • Watchdog: also alerts when a Duplicati job fails or stops running.
  • With Homepage installed, its page lists every running app.

New settings (up adds them; all optional or generated): NTFY_READ_TOKEN, NTFY_PHONE_PASSWORD, DUPLICATI_SECRETS_PASSPHRASE, DUPLICATI_PASSPHRASE, VIKUNJA_PORT, VIKUNJA_SECRET, MONEYMATTER_FRONTEND_IMAGE, MONEYMATTER_BACKEND_IMAGE, MONEYMATTER_PLATFORM.

If… Then You already ran Set up the alert token (notify setup) Run it again. It keeps the publishers' token. It adds the read-only homelab-reader (for the app's recent alerts) and the phone login (NTFY_PHONE_PASSWORD; sign the phone's ntfy app in with it). It also gives every Duplicati job its alerts You have not yet Nothing extra: the step does all of that You have not made the Duplicati jobs yet Setup › Create the backup jobs makes them all. Then Settings › DUPLICATI_SECRETS_PASSPHRASE › Copy into Vaultwarden, and write it on the recovery kit You made Duplicati jobs by hand They stay as they are, and the per-job send-http-url can go (the alert token step sets it for every job). Create the backup jobs adds only jobs whose names are missing Vaultwarden has accounts Once a month, keep a password-protected export in recovery-staging/secrets (Backups); the nightly backup reminds you You want a start page for the household Install Homepage (it comes with the Household preset); its list of apps keeps itself current You want a to-do app Install Vikunja from Choose apps, then make each account with the command in its note You want MoneyMatter without Rosetta (optional, untried) Follow its note; leaving the settings empty keeps it as it is

Nothing else changes how the apps run: no image was swapped and no data moves.

docs.title: Before that
docs.text: Release run 4 and earlier: follow Testing from the top.

docs.title: Usability scoreboard
docs.text:
Is the app getting easier? Each row is a task a household does, tried end to end by the tester (Account 3, .claude/prompts/audit-loop.md) as someone who isn't technical: on each system, in light and dark, at 320px and with big text, against the fake backend. A row is run again whenever a lane says it fixed one of its findings.

  • Steps: screens and presses from the start to done. Fewer is better.
  • Dead ends: places where the screen doesn't say what to do next.
  • Words: wrong, misleading, or jargon text met on the way.
  • Keys: whether the keyboard and a screen reader reach everything (yes or no).
  • 320px: whether it all fits on a small phone with big text (yes or no).
  • Open: findings still waiting, by owner (A1 is Account 1, A2 is Account 2).
# Task Owner Last run Steps Dead ends Words Keys 320px Open 1 From a new computer to the first app open, with no docs A2 2 Something is down: find out what, and fix it A2 Nov 13 2 (phone: Status, Start; computer: Status, Start) 0 2 not tried yes A2: 1 3 Install an app that needs a login or a drive A2 Nov 13 4 (Frigate), 5 (qBittorrent, with its key) 1 5 no yes A2: 4 4 Update everything, and know it worked A2 Nov 6 3 0 2 not tried not tried A2: 2 5 Get one file back from last week's backup A2 Nov 13 can't be done in the app 1 3 not tried not tried A2: 3 6 Pair a partner's phone (look only), then remove a lost phone A2 Nov 6 5 to pair, 3 to remove 1 5 not tried not tried A2: 5 7 Give a person their own account, and send the welcome page A2 Nov 13 5 (with Pocket ID installed) 1 6 keyboard yes, screen reader not tried no A2: 4 8 Put the apps on your own domain A2 9 The computer is slow: find out why and free memory A2 10 After a restart or power cut: is everything back? A2 11 An alert on the phone: understand it, and act from the phone A2 12 Move the homelab to a new computer A2 13 Tidy Up: clean a music library and undo a mistake A1 14 Tidy Up: find what takes the space and free some A1 15 Finances: set up the month's bills and see what's left A1 Nov 13 12 (checking 4, a paycheck 5, a bill 3), then read the Dashboard 1 3 no no A1: 5 16 Finances: bring in a bank file and fix a wrong category A1

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Each run, newest first: the date, the task, what changed since the last run, and the findings handed over.

  • Nov 13, task 15 (set up the month's bills and see what's left), first run. Finances against the fake backend from nothing, then the example household; the Mac at 1280px in light, the phone at 390px light and 320px dark with big text. From nothing the Dashboard offers three things to start with, but the card goes once the checking account is in: nothing then points to Plan › Paychecks (one dead end). The bills themselves are quick to type in. "What's left" is the hard part: the first card's big number is checking right after payday, before that paycheck's bills, and what's actually left is the second card's smaller figure. Keyboard: no (344 presses of Tab through the logos to reach a payment's Name). 320px: no (the period bar's arrows split onto two lines). Three words. Five findings for Account 1 (its items 1 to 5).
  • Nov 13, task 5 (get one file back from last week's backup), first run. Backups against the fake backend, on the Mac in light. The screen says a lot about the backups (last night, each app's copies, the off-site jobs, the restore test) but nothing gets one file back. The only door is Open Duplicati, the engine's own admin page behind a password, and the docs say a restored file is copied back by hand: one dead end. Three words (Duplicati, Stale, sampled). Found on the way: the synced Files (Syncthing's SYNC_ROOT) are in no backup, and nothing says so (N76, for Account 2). Three findings for Account 2 (items 22 to 24).
  • Nov 13, task 3 (install an app that needs a login or a drive), first run. Choose apps against the fake backend, on the Mac in light and at 320px dark with big text. Frigate (records to a drive): search, tick, Install, Done (4 steps). Nothing asks or says where the recordings go, or what to do next, so you land in an empty Frigate: one dead end. qBittorrent (needs a ProtonVPN key): search, tick, paste the key, Install, Done (5 steps). The plan says plainly what it waits for, but the key's help calls it "Optional". "Connect the apps for me" names apps that aren't there, and Done leaves out the VPN tunnel. Five words (Optional, WireGuard, Gluetun, Prowlarr, Seerr). Keyboard: no, because Gluetun's Settings link is skipped by Tab. 320px: fits. Four findings for Account 2 (items 18 to 21).
  • Nov 13, task 2 (something is down), re-run. Against the fake backend with Mealie stopped, on the phone (390px light, 320px dark with big text) and the computer. Better in every column. Steps 3 to 2: the phone now has Start on a stopped app's row, and the computer's row has it too. Dead ends 2 to 0: the page says it was stopped outside the homelab and that Start starts it again, and the phone can start it. Words 6 to 2: "Choose apps", the subscription sense and Protection in plain words; left are "AUTO_HEAL=false" in the watchdog's note and "tailnet" on the page. 320px: fits now, but a status dot wraps away from its word. Findings 1 to 5 are done (2 and 5 by the lane, 1, 3 and 4 confirmed here); one new small finding for Account 2 (item 17).
  • Nov 13, task 7 (give a person their own account, send the welcome page), first run. Settings › People, against the fake backend. Without Pocket ID the card offers only Install Pocket ID, which opens Choose apps with it picked. With it running: Settings, People, a name, an email, Add them (5 steps). The person appears, but nothing says the welcome page opened or how to get it to them. There is no Send, and the page holds their sign-in link and a password: one dead end. Six words or phrases unexplained (passkey, Pocket ID, Infuse, "their keys in Settings", which of Welcome page and New sign-in link to use, the inverted app ticks). Tab reaches every button in order; screen reader not tried. At 320px with big text the row breaks (name a letter per line, buttons off the edge), and the stopped-app banner is cut off on every width. Four findings for Account 2 (items 13 to 16).
  • Nov 6, task 4 (update everything), first run. Status › Update apps, Update them, Close (3 steps), on the Mac, light, against the fake backend. No dead end, but you can't tell it worked: the sheet says "✓ updated" in a terminal's words before anything happens, and "Done" lists every app as Running without saying what changed. Two findings for Account 2 (items 11 and 12).
  • Nov 6, task 6 (pair a phone, remove a lost one), first run. Settings › Phones on the Mac, light, against the fake backend. To pair: Settings, Phones, a name, Pair a phone, then scan on the phone and tap Pair (5 steps, then Add to Home Screen). To remove: Settings, Phones, Remove (3). One dead end: a wall screen needs &kiosk typed onto a link. Five words or marks unexplained (two links with no word on which, a red ▲, "tailnet", "key", "kiosk"); the controls differ phone to phone. Keyboard and the phone's own screens not tried this run. Five findings for Account 2 (items 6 to 10).
  • Nov 6, task 2 (Something is down), first run. Against the fake backend with Mealie stopped, on the Mac at full width and on the phone at 390px, light. Three steps to start it on the computer: Status, open Household, Start. On the phone there is no way, and no word. Two dead ends: no reason it stopped, and nothing to do on the phone. Six wrong or unreadable phrases: the two screens disagreeing about checks; "Choose stacks"; "baseline"; "Replaces a year"; scanner names. The phone cuts log lines off at 390px. Keyboard and screen reader not tried this run. Five findings for Account 2, in audit-loop.md; pictures in images/usability/.

docs.title: Tidy Up's look: the owner's references
docs.text:
Screenshots of a finance app whose style Tidy Up should borrow, read by the Tidy Up loop (.claude/prompts/tidy-loop.md, The look) at the start of every look round. They're kept here for reference only: the app never loads them, and Tidy Up takes their layout and feel, never their name, logo, icons, words, or pictures.

To add one: on GitHub, open this folder, Add file › Upload files, and commit to main. Then add a line below.

Picture What I like in it (e.g. dashboard.png) (e.g. the big number on top, and the chart right under it)

docs.title: Baikal
docs.text:
Calendars and contacts for every phone and computer (CalDAV and CardDAV)

Service baikal in compose/cloud.yaml (project homelab_cloud) Image ckulka/baikal:nginx Category Cloud & Files Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install baikal Address https://dav.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:5232 (BAIKAL_PORT) Data data/appdata/baikal/config → /var/www/baikal/configdata/appdata/baikal/specific → /var/www/baikal/Specific Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first Also known as radicale, calendar, contacts, caldav, carddav

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: The household's calendars and contacts, synced to every iPhone, Mac, and Android phone over the open CalDAV and CardDAV standards, instead of iCloud or Google. Shared calendars (the family calendar, bin days) live here too.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. ./homelab install baikal and open it: https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:5232 in Home mode, or https://dav.example.com with a domain.
  2. The first visit runs Baikal's setup: set the admin password (save it in Vaultwarden as homelab - baikal admin), keep SQLite, and finish.
  3. In the admin pages, Users and resources › Add user for each person. Each user gets a default calendar and address book.
  4. On an iPhone: Settings › Apps › Calendar › Calendar Accounts › Add Account › Other › Add CalDAV Account, server dav.example.com (in Home mode <TAILSCALE_HOST>:5232), the person's user name and password. Then the same under Contacts with Add CardDAV Account. On a Mac: System Settings › Internet Accounts › Add Other Account. On Android: DAVx⁵ with https://dav.example.com/dav.php.
  5. To move from iCloud: export each calendar from Calendar on the Mac (File › Export) and import it into the new account; export contacts as a vCard from Contacts and import it the same way.

docs.title: Away from home
docs.text: In Home mode (the default), Baikal is on the tailnet: it opens at home and away on every device signed in to Tailscale. With a domain, it is on the home network only: install Tailscale to reach it from anywhere, or, to publish it through the tunnel, add public: true to its x-homelab block and run ./homelab domain setup again.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• A PHP app built on the sabre/dav library; this image runs it with nginx and PHP-FPM in one container.
  • Phones and computers talk to /dav.php over CalDAV (calendars and reminders) and CardDAV (contacts). The /.well-known/caldav and /.well-known/carddav addresses point clients there, which is why the server name alone works on an iPhone.
  • The admin pages at /admin manage users and their calendars and address books. There is no calendar web page: you read and edit events in your usual apps.
  • All data is in one SQLite database; settings are in one YAML file.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Settings (admin password, sign-in type, time zone) data/appdata/baikal/config/baikal.yaml (/var/www/baikal/config) Database: users, calendars, events, contacts data/appdata/baikal/specific/db/db.sqlite (/var/www/baikal/Specific/db)

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Add or remove people at /admin › Users and resources. The buttons beside each user open their calendars and address books, where you can add more (for example "Bin days").
  • A user's addresses, for apps that ask for a full URL: https://dav.example.com/dav.php/calendars/<user>/ and https://dav.example.com/dav.php/addressbooks/<user>/.
  • Apps: Calendar, Contacts, and Reminders on iPhone, iPad, and Mac; DAVx⁵ on Android; Thunderbird on any computer.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Reached through Nginx Proxy Manager at dav.example.com; from away through Tailscale. In Home mode, Tailscale serves it at https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:5232.
  • The admin password belongs in Vaultwarden.
  • Home Assistant has a CalDAV integration that shows these calendars and can start automations from events.
  • .env: BAIKAL_PORT.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Make a family user whose calendar every device adds as a second account, for things everyone should see.
  • Keep shopping and to-do lists in Reminders on the CalDAV account, so they sync through Baikal too.
  • Use Home Assistant's CalDAV integration to announce bin day the evening before.
  • On Android, pair DAVx⁵ with jtx Board or Tasks.org for tasks.
  • Add the same accounts to Thunderbird for calendars and contacts on a Windows or Linux computer.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
The well-known redirect, a user's calendars listed over CalDAV (replace alice; it asks for her password), the users in the database, the logs, and a restart:

curl -sI http://localhost:5232/.well-known/caldav
curl -s --anyauth -u alice -X PROPFIND -H 'Depth: 1' http://localhost:5232/dav.php/calendars/alice/
sqlite3 data/appdata/baikal/specific/db/db.sqlite 'SELECT username FROM users;'
./homelab logs baikal -f
./homelab compose baikal restart baikal

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• Docs: https://sabre.io/baikal/
  • Source: https://github.com/sabre-io/Baikal
  • Image: https://github.com/ckulka/baikal-docker
  • DAVx⁵ for Android: https://www.davx5.com/

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: The SQLite database and settings are in data/appdata/baikal, covered by the AppData job.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• The phone says the account cannot be verified: use the server name without https:// on iOS, and check the address opens in Safari on the same Wi-Fi.
  • The setup page comes back: data/appdata/baikal/config is empty or not writable; check its owner.

docs.title: Dawarich
docs.text:
Where you have been, from the phone's location history, on a map with trips and stats.

Service dawarich in stacks/dawarich/compose.yaml (project homelab_dawarich) Image docker.io/freikin/dawarich:latest Category Cloud & Files Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install dawarich Address https://location.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:3050 (DAWARICH_PORT) Depends on dawarich-db, dawarich-redis, dawarich-sidekiq Helpers dawarich-db docker.io/postgis/postgis:17-3.5-alpine, dumped daily by ./homelab backupdawarich-redis docker.io/valkey/valkey:9-alpinedawarich-sidekiq docker.io/freikin/dawarich:latest Data dawarich-public (volume) → /var/app/publicappdata/dawarich/watched → /var/app/tmp/imports/watchedappdata/dawarich/storage → /var/app/storage Updates By hand. Dawarich changes quickly and some releases need steps from their notes; update by hand with ./homelab update dawarich dawarich-sidekiq Also known as google-timeline, location-history, owntracks

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Where you have been, kept on this Mac instead of Google's servers: every point the phone records, on a map, with trips, places you visited, countries and cities, distance per month, and a year in review. It replaces Google Maps Timeline (which moved onto the phone and no longer keeps history in the cloud) and works with Owntracks, Overland, or Dawarich's own iOS app.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. ./homelab install dawarich. The first start runs the database migrations and takes a few minutes; ./homelab logs dawarich -f shows when Rails is listening.
  2. Open http://localhost:3050. Sign in with demo@dawarich.app / password, then change the email and password at once (Account settings).
  3. Account settings › API key: copy it.
  4. On the phone, install the Dawarich app (iOS) or Overland or Owntracks, and point it at the address you open Dawarich with, plus the key. Away from home that means Tailscale (Home mode) or the domain through the tunnel; Dawarich is not published to the internet by default.
  5. Bring your history: Imports › New import takes a Google Takeout (Records.json or the phone's Timeline export), GPX, GeoJSON, or Owntracks files.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• A Ruby on Rails app (dawarich) with a Sidekiq worker (dawarich-sidekiq) that does the heavy lifting: imports, reverse geocoding, and working out visits, trips, and stats in the background.
  • Points live in PostgreSQL with PostGIS (dawarich-db), which answers the map's "which points fall in this area" questions. Redis (dawarich-redis, Valkey here) is the job queue.
  • STORE_GEODATA keeps reverse-geocoding results so each place is looked up once. Without a geocoding service of your own, Dawarich uses a public one with a rate limit, so naming thousands of places takes a while.
  • APPLICATION_HOSTS lists the names Rails answers to: localhost, location.<domain>, and the tailnet name. A name not on the list gets "Blocked host".
  • It runs Dawarich's default development mode, as their compose file does.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Location points, users, trips the dawarich-pgdata volume (PostGIS 17) Daily database dump recovery-staging/databases/dawarich-db Uploaded imports and exports appdata/dawarich/storage (/var/app/storage) Watched import folder appdata/dawarich/watched (/var/app/tmp/imports/watched) Built web assets the dawarich-public volume (rebuilt from the image)

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Map: pick a day, week, or range; layers show the route, points, a heatmap, visited cities, and fog of war.
  • Trips: name a date range ("Lisbon 2025") and Dawarich draws it with its distance and photos from Immich once connected.
  • Visits: places you stayed at; confirm or rename the suggestions.
  • Stats: distance, countries, and cities per month and year.
  • Exports: GeoJSON or GPX of any range.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Immich: Account settings › Integrations takes Immich's address (http://immich-server:2283 from inside Docker) and an Immich API key, and shows your photos on the map and in trips.
  • Tailscale: the phone keeps reporting away from home without publishing Dawarich.
  • Duplicati: the Databases job keeps the dump; the Stack Data job keeps appdata/dawarich.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Drop GPX files from a bike computer or watch into appdata/dawarich/watched/<your email>/ and Dawarich imports them by itself.
  • Connect Immich so trips show the photos taken there.
  • Areas: draw home, work, and the gym, and see time spent in each.
  • Turn on the public share of a single trip for family.
  • Point reverse geocoding at your own Photon instance for faster place names (PHOTON_API_HOST).

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
The app and worker logs, a Rails console, and the size of the history:

./homelab logs dawarich -f
./homelab logs dawarich-sidekiq -f
./homelab compose dawarich exec dawarich bin/rails console
./homelab compose dawarich exec dawarich-db psql -U postgres -d dawarich_development -c 'select count(*) from points'
./homelab update dawarich dawarich-sidekiq

docs.title: API
docs.text:
Each user's key is under Account settings. The base URL is http://localhost:3050/api/v1/; pass the key as api_key or a Bearer header. Interactive docs are at http://localhost:3050/api-docs.

curl -s "http://localhost:3050/api/v1/points?api_key=YOUR_KEY&start_at=2025-01-01&end_at=2025-01-02" | head -c 400

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• Dawarich and its documentation
  • Dawarich on GitHub

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: The nightly backup dumps the database (dawarich-db, every location point), and the Stack Data job keeps appdata/dawarich (imports and exports). Redis and the public assets rebuild themselves. Keep your original Google Takeout too: it can always be imported again.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• "Blocked host" in the browser: you opened it at a name not in APPLICATION_HOSTS; use localhost, location.<domain>, or the tailnet name, or add yours in stacks/dawarich/compose.yaml.
  • The first start shows nothing for minutes: migrations run first; watch ./homelab logs dawarich -f.
  • Imports sit at "processing": the worker is down; ./homelab status, then ./homelab logs dawarich-sidekiq.
  • Slow on Apple Silicon: the PostGIS image is Intel-only and runs under Rosetta; it is fine for one household's history.
  • After an update the app will not start: read Dawarich's release notes for manual steps, or go back with the previous image tag.

docs.title: File Browser
docs.text:
A web file manager for the media drive: browse, upload, download, and share files from a browser.

Service filebrowser in compose/cloud.yaml (project homelab_cloud) Image filebrowser/filebrowser:latest Category Cloud & Files Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install filebrowser Address https://files.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:8086 (FILEBROWSER_PORT) Data /Volumes/Media → /srvdata/appdata/filebrowser/database → /databasedata/appdata/filebrowser/config → /config Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Reach files on /Volumes/Media from any device on the LAN without file sharing set up on each one.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. ./homelab install filebrowser; with a domain, then ./homelab domain setup.
  2. The first start prints a random admin password: ./homelab logs filebrowser. Sign in at https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:8086 in Home mode, or https://files.example.com with a domain, and change it.
  3. Create a user per person, limited to the folders they need.

It has read-write access to the whole media drive, so keep it LAN-only and give accounts the narrowest scope.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• A single Go program with a Vue web page, serving the media drive mounted at /srv.
  • Users, their scopes and permissions, share links, and settings are in one BoltDB file, /database/filebrowser.db; start-up options are in /config/settings.json.
  • A share is a /share/... link with an optional expiry and password; anyone with the link can download without an account.
  • It can read and write everything the container can, so a user's scope is the only fence.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Files MEDIA_ROOT (/Volumes/Media) → /srv Users, shares, settings data/appdata/filebrowser/database/filebrowser.db (/database) Start-up options data/appdata/filebrowser/config/settings.json (/config)

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Drag files onto the page to upload; select files to download them (several at once come as one archive).
  • Select a file or folder and use the share button to make a link with an expiry and an optional password; the settings pages list current shares.
  • Settings › User Management: add a user, set their scope (for example /games/roms) and what they may do.
  • F1 lists the keyboard shortcuts; F2 renames and Delete deletes the selection.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Sees the whole media drive: Jellyfin's libraries, qBittorrent's downloads, the Books folder for Calibre-Web, games for RomM, and Immich's photos. Change Immich's files only through Immich.
  • Behind Nginx Proxy Manager at files.example.com, LAN only (with a domain); in Home mode Tailscale serves it on the tailnet.
  • .env: FILEBROWSER_PORT, MEDIA_ROOT.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• A user scoped to /games/roms for dropping ROMs into RomM's library, followed by a scan in RomM.
  • A user scoped to /Books that can only upload, for adding books.
  • Hide clutter with a rule: Settings › Global Settings › Rules, regular expression \.DS_Store.
  • Rename the page and pick the dark theme under Settings › Global Settings › Branding.
  • Script uploads or listings from the Mac with the API below.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
The first-start admin password, the logs, a restart, and the health check:

./homelab logs filebrowser | grep -i password
./homelab logs filebrowser -f
./homelab compose filebrowser restart filebrowser
curl -s http://localhost:8086/health

docs.title: API
docs.text:
• Sign in with POST /api/login and a JSON body with username and password; the reply is a token to send as the X-Auth header.
  • Base URL on this Mac: http://localhost:8086/api.
  • Example, listing the top folder of the drive:
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8086/api/login -d '{"username":"admin","password":"your-password"}')
curl -s -H "X-Auth: $TOKEN" http://localhost:8086/api/resources/

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• Docs: https://filebrowser.org/
  • Source and image: https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: data/appdata/filebrowser (users, shares, settings) is in the Homelab AppData job. The files themselves are on the media drive.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: If uploads fail, check that the drive is mounted (./homelab doctor) and that OrbStack may access /Volumes.

docs.title: Immich
docs.text:
Photo and video backup for the family's phones, with face recognition, maps, and search by what is in the picture.

Service immich-server in stacks/immich/compose.yaml (project homelab_immich) Image ghcr.io/immich-app/immich-server:v3 Category Cloud & Files Starts with ./homelab up Yes (./homelab up) Address https://photos.example.com (LAN and public, through the Cloudflare Tunnel) On this machine http://localhost:8013 (IMMICH_PORT) Depends on immich-redis, immich-database Helpers immich-redis docker.io/valkey/valkey:9@sha256:c123e3715db63d06d4ad6964884037aa0d5d4d703939b9929954112889708e1dimmich-database ghcr.io/immich-app/postgres:14-vectorchord0.4.3-pgvectors0.2.0@sha256:bcf63357191b76a916ae5eb93464d65c07511da41e3bf7a8416db519b40b1c23, dumped daily by ./homelab backup Data /Volumes/Media/photos → /data Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first Also known as immich

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Automatic backup of every phone's camera roll, at home and away.
  • Shared albums and partner sharing within the family.
  • The photo library itself lives on the media drive (IMMICH_UPLOAD_LOCATION).

The stack follows Immich's own release compose file; the database and Redis images are pinned to what that release specifies.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Open https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:8013 in Home mode, or https://photos.example.com with a domain; the first account becomes the administrator.
  2. Administration › Users: create an account per person, with a storage quota if wanted.
  3. In the Immich phone app, server URL: the same address, then turn on backup for the camera roll.
  4. Machine learning runs on the CPU. The first indexing of a large library takes hours (Administration › Jobs shows progress).

Updating: IMMICH_VERSION is the major tag (v3), and the nightly updates apply minor updates. Before a new major version, read Immich's release notes: it may change the database image, which must be updated in stacks/immich/compose.yaml exactly as the release says.

docs.title: Sending an album to family without an account
docs.text:
For grandparents, cousins, or friends: a link that opens the album on their phone or computer, with no account and no app.

Once: the link must carry an address that works away from home.

  • With a domain (HOMELAB_DOMAIN set, and the Cloudflare Tunnel running): Immich is public at https://photos.example.com. In Immich, signed in as its administrator, open Administration › Settings › Server Settings, set External domain to https://photos.example.com, and Save. Setup shows this step, with your own address, once the tunnel is up. Without it, links point at this machine's own address and open only here.
  • In Home mode (Tailscale only): Immich's address works only on devices signed in to your tailnet, so a link sent to someone outside it will not open. Share with them another way: add the album's photos to a shared album in your phone's own photo app, or download them (select, then Download) and send them. Or give a close relative an Immich account and Tailscale on their phone, and share the album with their account.

Each time:

  1. Open the album (or select photos on the timeline) and tap Share › Create link.
  2. Choose how long it lasts under Expire after: a week for a party's photos, longer for a grandchild's album. Turn on Require password if the link might be passed on, and say the password separately (by phone, not in the same message).
  3. Decide what they may do: Allow public user to download (to keep the photos), Allow public user to upload (so they can add theirs, handy after an event), and Show metadata (where and when each photo was taken; leave it off unless they want it).
  4. Create link, then Copy and send it by message or email. It opens in any browser.

Afterwards: Sharing › Shared links lists every link you made, with its expiry. Edit one to change its expiry or password, or delete it to turn it off at once; the photos stay in your library.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• immich-server is a TypeScript (NestJS) app. It serves the web app and the API on port 2283 and also runs the background workers: thumbnails, metadata extraction, and video transcoding.
  • Work waits in job queues in Valkey (immich-redis). Everything about the library (assets, albums, people, users) is in PostgreSQL (immich-database), which stores the face and smart-search vectors with the VectorChord extension.
  • immich-machine-learning is a Python service that runs the CLIP model for smart search and the face detection and recognition models. Here it runs on the CPU; models download on first use into the immich-model-cache volume. The server reaches it at http://immich-machine-learning:3003.
  • Only immich-server joins the shared homelab network (for the proxy and tunnel); the database, Valkey, and machine learning stay on the stack's own network.
  • Originals are never changed. Immich writes thumbnails and transcoded videos beside them under /data.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Library root IMMICH_UPLOAD_LOCATION (/Volumes/Media/photos) → /data Uploads, as sent by phones /data/upload/<user id>/ Files arranged by the storage template (when on) /data/library/ Thumbnails and previews /data/thumbs/ Transcoded videos /data/encoded-video/ Profile pictures /data/profile/ Immich's own database dumps /data/backups/ Database volume homelab_immich_immich-pgdata → /var/lib/postgresql/data in immich-database Machine-learning models volume homelab_immich_immich-model-cache → /cache in immich-machine-learning The homelab's daily dumps recovery-staging/databases/immich-database

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Phone app: the backup screen (cloud icon) chooses albums and turns on background backup. On an iPhone, keep Background App Refresh on for Immich.
  • Search for what is in a picture ("dog on the beach"), a person, or a place; Explore shows People, Places, and Things.
  • Sharing: shared albums with other users, links for people without an account (see Sending an album, above), and partner sharing to see a partner's whole library.
  • Memories ("on this day") above the timeline, the Map, Favorites, Archive, and the Locked Folder for private items.
  • Administration › Jobs runs or re-runs work; Administration › Settings holds everything server-wide; Utilities reviews duplicates.
  • Apps: Immich for iPhone and Android, and any browser.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Its database and queue are covered in PostgreSQL and Redis and Valkey.
  • Public at photos.example.com through Cloudflare Tunnel, and on the LAN through Nginx Proxy Manager.
  • Duplicati's Homelab Photos job backs up the library; the database goes through ./homelab backup and the Homelab Databases job.
  • Sign-in with Pocket ID: ./homelab sso setup makes its client (kept in data/sso/immich-server.env) and says what to paste in Administration › Settings › Authentication Settings › OAuth.
  • Homepage has an Immich widget (needs an API key); Uptime Kuma can watch /api/server/ping.
  • .env: IMMICH_VERSION, IMMICH_DB_PASSWORD, IMMICH_UPLOAD_LOCATION, IMMICH_PORT.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Turn on the storage template (Administration › Settings › Storage Template) to file photos on the drive by year and month.
  • Add an existing photo folder as an external library (Administration › External Libraries); mount it read-only into immich-server in stacks/immich/compose.yaml first.
  • Import an old archive from the Mac with the Immich CLI (@immich/cli from npm: immich login, then immich upload --recursive <folder>).
  • Try another smart-search model (Administration › Settings › Machine Learning Settings), then rerun Smart Search in Jobs; a multilingual model helps if the family searches in more than one language.
  • Review duplicates under Utilities after a big import.
  • Sign in with Pocket ID passkeys instead of passwords.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
Whether the server answers and its version, the containers, the logs, Immich's admin tool inside the server (list users, reset the admin password), and a restart:

curl -s http://localhost:8013/api/server/ping
curl -s http://localhost:8013/api/server/version
./homelab compose immich ps
./homelab logs immich-server -f
./homelab logs immich-machine-learning -f
./homelab compose immich exec immich-server immich-admin list-users
./homelab compose immich exec immich-server immich-admin reset-admin-password
./homelab compose immich restart immich-server

docs.title: API
docs.text:
• Key: your profile picture › Account Settings › API Keys › New API Key. Send it as the x-api-key header.
  • Base URL: https://photos.example.com/api, or http://localhost:8013/api on this Mac.
  • Example, your own account:
curl -s -H "x-api-key: $IMMICH_API_KEY" http://localhost:8013/api/users/me
  • The API reference is linked from the docs.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• Docs: https://docs.immich.app/
  • Source and images: https://github.com/immich-app/immich

docs.title: Backup
docs.text:
Data How Photos and videos (IMMICH_UPLOAD_LOCATION) Homelab Photos job Database Dumped daily by ./homelab backup, then the Homelab Databases job; Immich also keeps its own dumps in IMMICH_UPLOAD_LOCATION/backups Machine-learning models Not backed up (downloaded again)

The restore needs Immich's Postgres image and a search-path fix: see Disaster Recovery.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Fix Server unhealthy after an update The release changed the database image. Check the release notes and ./homelab logs immich-server Uploads fail from outside Cloudflare limits uploads to 100 MB per request through the tunnel. Long videos sync when the phone is home Faces or search missing Administration › Jobs: run Face Detection and Smart Search for missing items "Upload location not found" The media drive was not mounted when Immich started. ./homelab compose immich restart

docs.title: Nextcloud
docs.text:
The family's shared files, synced to every phone and computer.

Service nextcloud in stacks/nextcloud/compose.yaml (project homelab_nextcloud) Image docker.io/library/nextcloud:35-apache Category Cloud & Files Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install nextcloud Address https://cloud.example.com (LAN and public, through the Cloudflare Tunnel) On this machine http://localhost:8089 (NEXTCLOUD_PORT) Depends on nextcloud-db, nextcloud-redis Helpers nextcloud-db docker.io/library/postgres:18, dumped daily by ./homelab backupnextcloud-redis docker.io/valkey/valkey:9-alpine Data appdata/nextcloud/html → /var/www/htmlappdata/nextcloud/data → /var/www/dataconfig/nextcloud/post-installation, read-only → /docker-entrypoint-hooks.d/post-installationconfig/nextcloud/before-starting, read-only → /docker-entrypoint-hooks.d/before-starting Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
The family's shared files in one place, synced to every phone and computer the way Dropbox or OneDrive does it: a folder on each computer that stays in step, phone apps that upload and open files, and links to share a file with someone outside the family. It can also hold calendars, contacts, and notes, and edit documents in the browser with add-ons.

It is heavy and optional, in no starter.
