The homelab already covers its parts with lighter apps: File Browser for sharing from the media drive, Syncthing for keeping folders in step, Immich for photos, and Baikal for calendars and contacts. Choose Nextcloud when the family wants all of it in one app with one account each.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. ./homelab install nextcloud (it brings its PostgreSQL, its cache, and its jobs container). The first start installs it, which takes a minute or two.
  2. Sign in as NEXTCLOUD_ADMIN_USER (admin) with NEXTCLOUD_ADMIN_PASSWORD from Settings (Show), or Sign-in details on its page in Status.
  3. Accounts › New account for each person in the family. Give each a quota if the disk is small.
  4. On each computer, install the Nextcloud desktop app and sign in with https://cloud.example.com (with a domain) or https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:8089 (Home mode); on each phone, the Nextcloud app with the same address.
  5. Administration settings › Overview lists anything left to set up; the homelab has already set the background jobs (cron, every 5 minutes), the night maintenance window, the proxy, and the addresses it answers on.

The addresses it answers on are set at each start from HOMELAB_DOMAIN and TAILSCALE_HOST, so after changing either, ./homelab up is enough.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• nextcloud: the official image with Apache and PHP, on port 80 inside, 8089 on this machine. Before it starts, its www-data account takes your user's ID (PUID, PGID), so the files it writes are yours: they move with homelab move, and the backup can read them on every system.
  • nextcloud-cron: the same image running Nextcloud's background jobs every 5 minutes (previews, clean-up, notifications).
  • nextcloud-db: PostgreSQL with accounts, shares, and the list of files; nextcloud-redis: Valkey for file locking and caching.
  • Two scripts in config/nextcloud run inside the image: after installing (cron and the maintenance window) and at each start (the trusted addresses).
  • The program lives in appdata/nextcloud/html (with its settings in config/config.php); the files themselves in appdata/nextcloud/data, or NEXTCLOUD_DATA.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Everyone's files appdata/nextcloud/data/<account>/files, or NEXTCLOUD_DATA Settings (config.php) and installed apps appdata/nextcloud/html Accounts, shares, file list, calendars, contacts PostgreSQL in the Docker volume homelab_nextcloud_nextcloud-pgdata Secrets NEXTCLOUD_ADMIN_PASSWORD and NEXTCLOUD_DB_PASSWORD in .env

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Sync a folder: the desktop app keeps the Nextcloud folder on each computer in step; files can stay online-only until opened.
  • Phone photos: the phone app can upload the camera roll (Immich does this better if photos are the main need).
  • Share: a file's share menu makes a link, with a password and an expiry date if you like, for someone without an account.
  • Family folders: make a folder and share it with the other accounts, or install Team folders from Apps for folders that belong to everyone.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Duplicati: the Homelab Stack Data job covers appdata/nextcloud (files and settings), and ./homelab backup dumps the database.
  • Pocket ID: sign-in with passkeys through Nextcloud's OpenID Connect app (Tinkering ideas).
  • .env: NEXTCLOUD_PORT (default 8089), NEXTCLOUD_URL, NEXTCLOUD_VERSION, NEXTCLOUD_DATA, and the secrets above.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Files on the media drive: set NEXTCLOUD_DATA to a folder there before the first install (moving it later needs occ); add that folder to a Duplicati job, since it is then outside the Stack Data job.
  • Office documents in the browser: install Nextcloud Office from Apps with its built-in server (CODE), or run Collabora as a container of its own.
  • Calendars and contacts: the Calendar and Contacts apps, synced to phones with DAVx⁵ (Android) or the system's own accounts (iPhone).
  • Sign-in with Pocket ID: install OpenID Connect user backend from Apps and add Pocket ID as a provider.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
./homelab logs nextcloud -f
./homelab compose nextcloud exec -u www-data nextcloud php occ status
./homelab compose nextcloud exec -u www-data nextcloud php occ files:scan --all     # after copying files in by hand
./homelab compose nextcloud exec -u www-data nextcloud php occ maintenance:mode --off

docs.title: API
docs.text:
• WebDAV (what the apps use): https://cloud.example.com/remote.php/dav/files/<account>/, signed in with the account's password or an app password (Personal settings › Security).
  • Upload a file: curl -u admin:PASSWORD -T notes.txt http://localhost:8089/remote.php/dav/files/admin/notes.txt
  • The OCS API (shares, accounts) is described in Nextcloud's developer manual.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• nextcloud.com and the administration manual
  • The official image, whose PostgreSQL example this stack follows

docs.title: Updates
docs.text: The nightly updates bring fixes for the major version in NEXTCLOUD_VERSION (35) every night. A new major version is a deliberate step: take a backup (./homelab backup --apply), raise NEXTCLOUD_VERSION by one (never skip one), then ./homelab update nextcloud; the image upgrades itself on start. Check Administration settings › Overview afterwards.

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: ./homelab backup dumps the database nightly into recovery-staging/databases/nextcloud-db. The files and settings are in appdata/nextcloud, which the Homelab Stack Data job in Duplicati takes off-site with the rest. With NEXTCLOUD_DATA elsewhere, add that folder to a job of its own.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• It keeps restarting, and the log says Nextcloud did not install: its first install failed (the lines above in ./homelab logs nextcloud say why, often a files folder it cannot write). Fix that, delete appdata/nextcloud/html, and ./homelab up; it installs again.
  • Access through untrusted domain: the address you opened is not localhost, cloud.<HOMELAB_DOMAIN>, or TAILSCALE_HOST; set the one you use in Settings, then ./homelab up.
  • Slow, or file is locked: check that nextcloud-redis is running (./homelab compose nextcloud ps).
  • Stuck in maintenance mode after an update: read ./homelab logs nextcloud, then occ maintenance:mode --off (Useful commands).
  • Files copied into the data folder by hand do not show: occ files:scan --all.

docs.title: PairDrop
docs.text:
AirDrop between any devices on the home network, from the browser.

Service pairdrop in compose/cloud.yaml (project homelab_cloud) Image lscr.io/linuxserver/pairdrop:latest Category Cloud & Files Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install pairdrop Address https://drop.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:3020 (PAIRDROP_PORT) Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first Also known as airdrop

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: AirDrop for every device, including Windows, Android, and the Steam Machine: open the page on two devices on the home network and they see each other. Files go directly between the devices (peer to peer); the server only introduces them.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. ./homelab install pairdrop.
  2. Open https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:3020 in Home mode, or https://drop.example.com with a domain on both devices; tap the other device and pick files, or paste text.
  3. On a phone, add it to the home screen. To pair devices that are not on the same network, use Pair device with the code it shows.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• A small Node.js server and a web app. The server only introduces devices to each other over a WebSocket; files and text go straight between the browsers over WebRTC.
  • Devices that reach the server from the same network see each other on their own. Paired devices find each other wherever they are; the pairing is kept in each browser.
  • Nothing is stored on this Mac. WS_FALLBACK is off, so when two devices cannot connect directly the transfer fails instead of going through the server. RATE_LIMIT is off.

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Click a device to send files; right-click it (long-press on a phone) to send a text message.
  • Paste on the page (⌘V) to send what is on the clipboard.
  • Your device's name is shown at the bottom of the page.
  • Pair a device once from the pairing option, or join a temporary public room with a code to swap files with a guest.
  • On Android, install it from the browser menu as an app, and PairDrop appears in the share sheet.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Behind Nginx Proxy Manager at drop.example.com, with WebSockets on; on Tailscale, devices see each other when both are on the tailnet.
  • To send to people outside the home, use PsiTransfer; for folders that stay the same everywhere, Syncthing.
  • .env: PAIRDROP_PORT.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Pair your phone and this Mac once, so they find each other even on different networks.
  • On the Mac, add it to the Dock from Safari (File › Add to Dock) so it opens like an app.
  • Use a public room to swap files with a visitor's phone without pairing.
  • If transfers fail on some networks, try WS_FALLBACK: "true" in its environment; transfers then go through this Mac when a direct link fails.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
The logs (each device joining shows up), a restart, and whether the page answers:

./homelab logs pairdrop -f
./homelab compose pairdrop restart pairdrop
curl -sI http://localhost:3020

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• Source and docs: https://github.com/schlagmichdoch/PairDrop
  • Image: https://docs.linuxserver.io/images/docker-pairdrop/

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: Nothing to back up: PairDrop keeps no files.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• The other device does not appear: both must be on the home Wi-Fi (or both on Tailscale), and the page must be open on both.
  • Transfers stall: a VPN with a kill switch on one device blocks peer-to-peer connections; turn it off or allow LAN connections.

docs.title: PsiTransfer
docs.text:
Send large files to anyone with a link that expires.

Service psitransfer in compose/cloud.yaml (project homelab_cloud) Image psitrax/psitransfer:latest Category Cloud & Files Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install psitransfer Address https://send.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:3030 (PSITRANSFER_PORT) Data data/appdata/psitransfer → /data Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first Also known as wetransfer

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Send large files (videos, scans, photo sets) to anyone with a link, like WeTransfer: upload, set how long the link lasts and an optional password, and share it. Only the household can upload (the upload password); anyone with a link can download.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. ./homelab install psitransfer and open https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:3030 in Home mode, or https://send.example.com with a domain.
  2. Enter the upload password (Settings › PSITRANSFER_UPLOAD_PASSWORD › Copy), add files, choose the expiry, and upload.
  3. To send to people outside the home (with a domain), publish it: add public: true to its x-homelab block and run ./homelab domain setup. The upload password still keeps strangers from uploading.
  4. The admin page (/admin, PSITRANSFER_ADMIN_PASSWORD) lists the current uploads. Sign-in details on its page in Status copies that password.

docs.title: Away from home
docs.text: In Home mode it is on the tailnet, so every device signed in to Tailscale reaches it at home and away. With a domain it is on the home network only: install Tailscale to reach it from anywhere, or, to publish it through the tunnel, add public: true to its x-homelab block and run ./homelab domain setup again.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• A Node.js server with a Vue page. Uploads use the tus protocol, so a large upload resumes after a dropped connection.
  • Each upload is a bucket with its own link, files, retention, and optional password, stored under /data, one folder per bucket.
  • Expired buckets are deleted on their own; a one-time bucket is deleted after its first download.
  • Its settings come from the defaults in its config.js, overridden by PSITRANSFER_* environment variables; here only the admin and upload passwords are set.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Uploads, one folder per bucket data/appdata/psitransfer → /data

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Upload: enter the upload password, drop the files, choose how long the link lasts (from one download to several weeks), optionally set a password, then copy the link.
  • The recipient sees each file with a download button, and can download everything at once as an archive.
  • /admin lists the current buckets, their size, and when they expire.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Behind Nginx Proxy Manager at send.example.com; Cloudflare Tunnel when you make it public.
  • Its folder is in Duplicati's AppData job unless you exclude it.
  • Keep both passwords in Vaultwarden. For devices in the same home, PairDrop is quicker.
  • .env: PSITRANSFER_PORT, PSITRANSFER_ADMIN_PASSWORD, PSITRANSFER_UPLOAD_PASSWORD.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Change the retention choices or the default, or cap file and bucket size, with the matching PSITRANSFER_* variables listed in its README.
  • Exclude /source/appdata/psitransfer/ from the AppData job (Duplicati › job › Edit › Source data › Filters).
  • Publish it for sending to family elsewhere; the upload password still guards uploads.
  • Put a password on sensitive buckets and send the password by a different route than the link.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
The logs, a restart, how much space uploads take, and whether the page answers:

./homelab logs psitransfer -f
./homelab compose psitransfer restart psitransfer
du -sh data/appdata/psitransfer
curl -sI http://localhost:3030

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text: • Source, configuration, and the psitrax/psitransfer image: https://github.com/psi-4ward/psitransfer

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: Uploads in data/appdata/psitransfer expire on their own and are not worth keeping; the AppData job covers them anyway. Exclude the folder in Duplicati if they grow large.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: • Upload fails for big files: the proxy's upload limit; in Nginx Proxy Manager, edit send.example.com › Advanced and add client_max_body_size 0;.

docs.title: Syncthing
docs.text:
Keeps folders in sync between your devices, with no cloud in between.

Service syncthing in compose/cloud.yaml (project homelab_cloud) Image lscr.io/linuxserver/syncthing:latest Category Cloud & Files Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install syncthing Address https://sync.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:8384 (SYNCTHING_PORT) Data data/appdata/syncthing → /configdata/sync → /data Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Keeps folders in sync between your devices directly over the home network, with no cloud in between. Complements File Browser (sharing from the media drive) and Immich (photos).

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. ./homelab install syncthing. Shared folders live under SYNC_ROOT (data/sync by default).
  2. Open the web UI, set a GUI user and password under Actions › Settings › GUI.
  3. Install Syncthing (or Möbius Sync on iPhone) on each device, add this Mac by its device ID, and share folders.
  4. On each device, edit this Mac's entry: Advanced › Addresses tcp://192.168.1.10:22000, dynamic. In a container Syncthing cannot announce the Mac's own address, so without this devices go through slow relays.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• A Go program. Each device has an ID derived from its TLS certificate; devices only talk to IDs you have accepted, and all traffic is encrypted.
  • Devices sync on port 22000 (TCP, and QUIC over UDP) and find each other on the LAN with broadcasts on 21027/UDP. When no direct path works they fall back to global discovery and public relays run by the Syncthing project.
  • Each folder has a folder ID; devices sharing that ID keep it in step block by block, both ways unless the folder is send-only or receive-only.
  • The container's host name is homelab, the name other devices see by default.
  • The web UI and its REST API listen on 8384.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Settings: devices, folders, GUI user, API key data/appdata/syncthing/config.xml (/config) This device's identity data/appdata/syncthing/cert.pem and key.pem Index database data/appdata/syncthing/ Shared folders SYNC_ROOT (data/sync) → /data/<folder> Old versions, when versioning is on .stversions inside each folder Ignore patterns .stignore inside each folder

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Add Folder: a path under /data/..., then the Sharing tab to pick devices.
  • Add Remote Device: paste the other device's ID. Actions › Show ID shows this Mac's ID as text and a QR code.
  • Devices or folders offered by others appear as a banner at the top to accept.
  • Pause a folder or device from its panel; Actions › Recent Changes shows what moved.
  • Apps: Syncthing for macOS, Windows, and Linux; Syncthing-Fork on Android (the original Android app is no longer maintained); Möbius Sync on iPhone.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Complements File Browser (the media drive), Immich (photos), and PairDrop (one-off transfers).
  • SYNC_ROOT is not mounted in Duplicati: add a read-only volume to Duplicati's service and a job to back it up.
  • Only the web UI goes through Nginx Proxy Manager (sync.example.com); sync traffic uses ports 22000 and 21027 on the Mac directly (LAN_BIND_IP).
  • .env: SYNCTHING_PORT, SYNC_ROOT, LAN_BIND_IP, and PUID/PGID (who owns the synced files).

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Turn on versioning (folder › Edit › File Versioning, Staggered) so a file deleted on a phone can still be recovered here.
  • Make a receive-only folder for a phone's camera or scans, so the copy on the Mac cannot be changed by mistake.
  • Add .DS_Store and other junk to a folder's Ignore Patterns.
  • Keep it on the LAN: Actions › Settings › Connections, untick Global Discovery and Enable Relaying (devices then need this Mac's address, step 4 of Setup).
  • Share a folder with an untrusted device (a friend's computer) encrypted, for an off-site copy it cannot read.
  • Sync a notes folder, such as an Obsidian vault, between the Mac and a phone.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
The health check, this device's status (including its ID), its connections, the logs, and a restart. Put the API key from Actions › Settings › General in SYNCTHING_API_KEY first:

curl -s http://localhost:8384/rest/noauth/health
curl -s -H "X-API-Key: $SYNCTHING_API_KEY" http://localhost:8384/rest/system/status
curl -s -H "X-API-Key: $SYNCTHING_API_KEY" http://localhost:8384/rest/system/connections
./homelab logs syncthing -f
./homelab compose syncthing restart syncthing

docs.title: API
docs.text:
• Key: Actions › Settings › General › API Key; send it as the X-API-Key header.
  • Base URL on this Mac: http://localhost:8384/rest.
  • Example, rescan a folder now (its folder ID is in the folder's Edit dialog):
curl -s -X POST -H "X-API-Key: $SYNCTHING_API_KEY" "http://localhost:8384/rest/db/scan?folder=abcd-1234"
  • Reference: https://docs.syncthing.net/dev/rest.html

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• Docs: https://docs.syncthing.net/
  • Source: https://github.com/syncthing/syncthing
  • Image: https://docs.linuxserver.io/images/docker-syncthing/

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: The configuration in data/appdata/syncthing is covered by the AppData job. The synced folders in SYNC_ROOT are not: add them to a Duplicati job if this Mac is their only extra copy.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Devices do not connect: ports 22000 (TCP and UDP) and 21027 (UDP) must be free on the Mac; a VPN on the Mac can block the LAN.
  • Slow syncing ("relay" in the device list): the device does not have this Mac's address; see step 4.

docs.title: Changedetection.io
docs.text:
Watches web pages for price drops, restocks, and changes, and tells you through ntfy.

Service changedetection in compose/documents.yaml (project homelab_documents) Image ghcr.io/dgtlmoon/changedetection.io:latest Category Documents Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install changedetection Address https://watch.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:5010 (CHANGEDETECTION_PORT) Data data/appdata/changedetection → /datastore Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first Also known as price-tracker

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Watches web pages and tells you when they change: a price drops, an item is back in stock, a page you care about is updated. Notifications go to the phone through ntfy.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. ./homelab install changedetection and open https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:5010 in Home mode, or https://watch.example.com with a domain.
  2. Settings › General: set a password (it has none by default).
  3. Settings › Notifications: add ntfys://:TOKEN@ntfy.example.com/reminders, with the publish token from Settings › NTFY_PUBLISH_TOKEN › Copy in place of TOKEN.
  4. Paste a page's address and Watch. For a price, use Edit › Filters & Triggers and pick the price with the visual selector, or restock detection on shop pages.

docs.title: Away from home
docs.text: In Home mode (the default), Changedetection.io is on the tailnet: it opens at home and away on every device signed in to Tailscale. With a domain, it is on the home network only: install Tailscale to reach it from anywhere, or, to publish it through the tunnel, add public: true to its x-homelab block and run ./homelab domain setup again.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• A Python (Flask) app. For each watch it fetches the page on a timer with a plain HTTP request, keeps a text snapshot, and compares it with the previous one.
  • There is no database: settings, watches, and every snapshot are plain files in /datastore, one folder per watch.
  • Filters (CSS, XPath, JSONPath, and text to ignore) decide which part of a page counts as a change. The restock and price processor reads the stock text and price data that shop pages publish.
  • Notifications go out as Apprise URLs; ntfys:// sends them to ntfy over HTTPS.
  • BASE_URL (https://watch.example.com) makes the links inside notifications open the right page.
  • Pages that build themselves with JavaScript need a real browser through PLAYWRIGHT_DRIVER_URL. None is configured here, so those pages come back empty.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where App settings and tags data/appdata/changedetection/changedetection.json → /datastore/changedetection.json (older versions: url-watches.json) One watch: its settings and snapshots data/appdata/changedetection/<watch-uuid>/ (watch.json plus the saved history) Session secret data/appdata/changedetection/secret.txt Password reset switch /datastore/removepassword.lock: create it and restart, and the password is removed on start Logs Container output only: ./homelab logs changedetection

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Add a watch: paste the address on the main page, give it a tag, and Watch. Tags group related watches in the list.
  • Less noise: Edit › Filters & Triggers: limit the watch to one element, and list lines to ignore (dates, view counters, ads).
  • How often: Edit › General sets the recheck interval for one watch; Settings › General sets the default for all.
  • What changed: History on a watch shows the difference between any two snapshots; Preview shows the latest text.
  • Check now: Recheck on a watch, or select several in the list and recheck them together.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• ntfy: alerts go to the reminders topic, with NTFY_PUBLISH_TOKEN from .env inside the notification URL.
  • FreshRSS: Changedetection.io also publishes an RSS feed of changes (its address carries an access token); follow it in FreshRSS to read changes alongside your feeds.
  • Nginx Proxy Manager serves https://watch.example.com; the app's own port (CHANGEDETECTION_PORT, default 5010) only listens on this Mac.
  • Wallos pairs well: watch a subscription's pricing page to hear about a price rise before the renewal.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Price drops: choose the restock and price processor when you add a shop page, then set its price limits so only a real drop notifies you.
  • Trigger text: Edit › Filters & Triggers › trigger on text such as In stock, so only that wording sends an alert.
  • Separate alerts per tag: a tag has its own notification settings, so price alerts and page changes can go to different ntfy topics.
  • Watch an API instead of a page: point a watch at a JSON URL and filter with json:$.price.
  • JavaScript-heavy shops: add a dgtlmoon/sockpuppetbrowser container and set PLAYWRIGHT_DRIVER_URL=ws://<its name>:3000 on changedetection, as the upstream compose file shows. That also enables Browser Steps (sign in, click, then check).
  • Restock watches for several shops under one tag, so you hear from whichever restocks first.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
Follow the log, restart, list the data folder, reset a forgotten password (create the switch file, then restart), and use the API with the key from Settings › API:

./homelab logs changedetection -f
./homelab compose changedetection restart changedetection
./homelab compose changedetection exec changedetection ls /datastore
./homelab compose changedetection exec changedetection touch /datastore/removepassword.lock
curl -s -H "x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY" http://localhost:5010/api/v1/watch
curl -s -H "x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY" http://localhost:5010/api/v1/systeminfo

docs.title: API
docs.text:
• Key: Settings › API.
  • Base URL: http://localhost:5010/api/v1 on this Mac, or https://watch.example.com/api/v1 on the LAN. Send the key in the x-api-key header.
  • Add a watch: curl -s -X POST -H "x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"url":"https://example.com"}' http://localhost:5010/api/v1/watch
  • Other endpoints list a watch's history (/watch/<uuid>/history), tags (/tags), and import a list of URLs (/import).

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• changedetection.io
  • GitHub: dgtlmoon/changedetection.io (source of the ghcr.io/dgtlmoon/changedetection.io image, and its wiki)

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: Watches and their history are in data/appdata/changedetection, covered by the AppData job.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: • A shop page shows nothing: it needs a browser to render; those pages need the optional Playwright browser container, not set up here yet.

docs.title: Docmost
docs.text:
The household wiki, with pages, spaces, comments, and diagrams.

Service docmost in stacks/docmost/compose.yaml (project homelab_docmost) Image docker.io/docmost/docmost:latest Category Documents Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install docmost Address https://wiki.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:3040 (DOCMOST_PORT) Depends on docmost-db, docmost-redis Helpers docmost-db docker.io/library/postgres:17, dumped daily by ./homelab backupdocmost-redis docker.io/valkey/valkey:9-alpine Data appdata/docmost → /app/data/storage Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first Also known as notion, confluence

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: The household's own wiki: how-tos, the house manual (Wi-Fi, appliances, who to call), recipes that are not in Mealie, trip plans, and anything else worth writing down once. Pages live in spaces (one per topic or per person), with comments, page history, and diagrams. It replaces Notion or Confluence for a family.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. ./homelab install docmost, then open http://localhost:3040 (or https://wiki.example.com once the domain is set up).
  2. The first visit creates the workspace and its owner account. Use a password from Vaultwarden.
  3. Settings › Members: invite the household. Without an email server Docmost shows the invite link; copy it to the person.
  4. Make a space per topic (Home, Recipes, Travel) and set who can edit it under the space's settings.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• A Node.js (NestJS) server with a React editor built on Tiptap and Yjs, so two people can edit the same page at once and see each other's cursors.
  • Pages, spaces, members, and history live in PostgreSQL (docmost-db). Redis (docmost-redis, Valkey here) carries the background jobs and the live-editing traffic; it holds nothing worth keeping.
  • Uploaded files and images are stored on disk in /app/data/storage, which is appdata/docmost on this Mac.
  • APP_URL is the address it builds links with (invites, shares). It is DOCMOST_URL in .env: empty means https://wiki.\<domain>, and in Home mode homelab tailnet setup writes the tailnet address.
  • APP_SECRET signs sign-in sessions. Changing it signs everyone out.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Attachments and images appdata/docmost (/app/data/storage) Pages, spaces, users, history the docmost-pgdata volume (PostgreSQL 17) Daily database dump recovery-staging/databases/docmost-db Settings DOCMOST_PORT, DOCMOST_URL, DOCMOST_APP_SECRET, DOCMOST_DB_PASSWORD in .env

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Type / in a page for headings, tables, callouts, code blocks, and diagrams (Draw.io, Excalidraw, Mermaid).
  • Drag pages in the sidebar to nest them; each space has its own tree.
  • The search box looks through every page you can see.
  • Page menu › History shows earlier versions and restores one.
  • Share a page publicly from its Share menu; on this homelab "publicly" means anyone who can reach the address.
  • Import Markdown, HTML, or a Notion or Confluence export from the space's settings.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Vaultwarden for the accounts' passwords.
  • Pocket ID can be the sign-in only in Docmost's paid edition; the free one signs in with email and password.
  • Duplicati backs up appdata/docmost with the Stack Data job and the database dump with the Databases job.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• A House manual space: Wi-Fi, the boiler, appliance manuals as attachments, and the recovery-kit location (never the secrets themselves).
  • Templates: write a page once (a trip plan, a meeting note) and duplicate it.
  • Diagrams of the home network with the Draw.io block.
  • Export a space as Markdown now and then, so it opens without Docmost too.
  • Email for invites and password resets: Docmost's MAIL_DRIVER and SMTP_* settings (add them to the compose file's environment).

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
The log, a restart, and a look inside the database:

./homelab logs docmost -f
./homelab compose docmost restart docmost
./homelab compose docmost exec docmost-db psql -U docmost -d docmost -c '\dt'
du -sh appdata/docmost

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• Docmost and its documentation
  • Docmost on GitHub

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: The nightly backup dumps the database (docmost-db), and the Stack Data job keeps appdata/docmost (attachments). Redis holds nothing to keep. To restore, follow the PostgreSQL note for the dump and put the attachments folder back before starting Docmost.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Links in invites point to the wrong address: set DOCMOST_URL to the address you open it at (or leave it empty with a domain), then ./homelab compose docmost up -d docmost.
  • Everyone is signed out: DOCMOST_APP_SECRET changed; restore .env from the Secrets backup.
  • Pages load but live editing stalls: Redis is down; ./homelab status and start docmost-redis.
  • "Cannot connect to the database" on start: docmost-db is still starting after an update; wait a minute, then check ./homelab logs docmost-db.

docs.title: FreshRSS
docs.text:
A self-hosted RSS reader: follow sites and newsletters in one place, synced to any reader app.

Service freshrss in compose/documents.yaml (project homelab_documents) Image lscr.io/linuxserver/freshrss:latest Category Documents Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install freshrss Address https://freshrss.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:8085 (FRESHRSS_PORT) Data data/appdata/freshrss → /config Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Read news and blogs without algorithms or accounts elsewhere.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. ./homelab install freshrss; with a domain, then ./homelab domain setup.
  2. Open https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:8085 in Home mode, or https://freshrss.example.com with a domain, and finish the installer (SQLite is fine for one household).
  3. For mobile apps: Settings › Authentication › allow API access, then set an API password in your profile. Use the Google Reader API URL it shows.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• A PHP app. The LinuxServer.io image runs it with nginx and PHP-FPM; the app itself is in /app/www, and its data and extensions folders are links into /config.
  • Each user has their own SQLite database (the installer's choice here); FreshRSS can also use PostgreSQL or MySQL, not set up here.
  • A built-in cron job fetches every feed every 15 minutes. Feeds that support WebSub can push new items sooner, but only when FreshRSS is reachable from the internet, which it is not.
  • Mobile and desktop readers sync through its Google Reader API (/api/greader.php) or Fever API (/api/fever.php), with a separate API password.
  • The image turns off FreshRSS's built-in updater; the nightly updates update the image instead.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Main configuration data/appdata/freshrss/www/freshrss/data/config.php → /config/www/freshrss/data/config.php Each user's database and settings data/appdata/freshrss/www/freshrss/data/users/<user>/ (db.sqlite, config.php) Extensions data/appdata/freshrss/www/freshrss/extensions/ → /config/www/freshrss/extensions Web server and PHP settings data/appdata/freshrss/nginx/, data/appdata/freshrss/php/ Command-line tools /app/www/cli/ in the container

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Add a feed: the + next to Subscriptions, or Subscription management › Add a feed. Paste a site's address and FreshRSS finds its feed.
  • Read: j and k move between articles, r toggles read, f stars, space opens the original page, and q refreshes feeds; Settings › Shortcuts lists and changes them.
  • Organise: put feeds in categories, and add labels to articles you want to keep.
  • Saved searches: search, then save it as a user query from the search menu so it appears in the sidebar.
  • Phone and desktop apps: any Google Reader API client, such as NetNewsWire or Reeder on Apple devices and Readrops or FocusReader on Android. Use https://freshrss.example.com/api/greader.php, your user name, and the API password.
  • Import and export: Subscription management › Import / export takes and gives OPML files.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Changedetection.io: its RSS feed of changes can be followed here, and so can sites that have no feed of their own.
  • Karakeep: save an article you want to keep for good with the Karakeep browser extension or the share sheet.
  • Nginx Proxy Manager serves https://freshrss.example.com; .env sets FRESHRSS_PORT (default 8085), PUID, PGID, and TZ.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Sites without a feed: Add a feed › choose the HTML + XPath (Web scraping) type and point it at the parts of the page that list the articles.
  • Extensions: browse the official collection, copy one into the extensions folder, then turn it on under Settings › Extensions.
  • Filters: a feed's settings can mark articles as read automatically when they match a search, to mute topics you never read.
  • Reading view: Settings › Display sets the theme, article width, and whether articles open in the list or one by one.
  • Newsletters: many newsletter sites offer an RSS feed of each issue, which keeps them out of your inbox.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
Follow the log, restart, list users, and fetch one user's feeds now (the tools run as the image's abc user so file ownership stays right):

./homelab logs freshrss -f
./homelab compose freshrss restart freshrss
./homelab compose freshrss exec -u abc freshrss php /app/www/cli/list-users.php
./homelab compose freshrss exec -u abc freshrss php /app/www/cli/actualize-user.php --user <name>

docs.title: API
docs.text:
FreshRSS speaks the Google Reader API for apps. Turn on API access under Settings › Authentication, set an API password in Settings › Profile, then sign in to get a token:

curl -s 'http://localhost:8085/api/greader.php/accounts/ClientLogin?Email=<name>&Passwd=<api-password>'

The Auth= line it returns goes in an Authorization: GoogleLogin auth=<token> header on later calls.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• freshrss.org and the documentation
  • GitHub: FreshRSS/FreshRSS and FreshRSS/Extensions
  • GitHub: linuxserver/docker-freshrss (the image)

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: data/appdata/freshrss (feeds, articles, users, SQLite database) is in the Homelab AppData job. Export your feeds (OPML) occasionally as a portable copy.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: If feeds stop refreshing, check ./homelab logs freshrss; the image refreshes every 15 minutes with its built-in cron.

docs.title: Karakeep
docs.text:
Saved links and read-later, with full-page archives and search.

Service karakeep in stacks/karakeep/compose.yaml (project homelab_karakeep) Image ghcr.io/karakeep-app/karakeep:release Category Documents Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install karakeep Address https://links.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:3010 (KARAKEEP_PORT) Depends on karakeep-chrome, karakeep-meilisearch Helpers karakeep-chrome ghcr.io/karakeep-app/karakeep-chrome:releasekarakeep-meilisearch getmeili/meilisearch:v1.41.0 Data appdata/karakeep → /data Database dump Daily by ./homelab backup into recovery-staging/databases/karakeep Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first Also known as hoarder

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Saves links, articles, notes, and images with a full-page archive (so pages survive going offline), full-text search, and tags, automatically or by hand. Read-later and bookmarks in one place, with browser extensions and phone apps.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. ./homelab install karakeep (it brings its headless Chrome and Meilisearch).
  2. Open it and create the first account, the admin. Then turn off sign-ups for others under Admin › Settings if you do not want more accounts.
  3. Install the Karakeep browser extension and phone app, with the server address you open it at (https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:3010 in Home mode, or https://links.example.com with a domain).

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• A TypeScript app (Next.js web app plus background workers) in one container, with its database in SQLite at /data/db.db.
  • When you save a link, a crawler worker opens it in the headless Chrome of karakeep-chrome (BROWSER_WEB_URL, port 9222), takes a screenshot, and keeps a readable copy of the text. Full-page archives of every link are off by default (CRAWLER_FULL_PAGE_ARCHIVE).
  • A search worker feeds every item into Meilisearch (karakeep-meilisearch, port 7700) with KARAKEEP_MEILI_MASTER_KEY. The index can always be rebuilt from the database, which is why it is not backed up.
  • AI tagging and summaries run only when an OpenAI key or an Ollama address is set; neither is set here, so tags are yours.
  • Sign-in is handled by NextAuth; NEXTAUTH_URL (https://links.example.com) must match the address you open.
  • The stack has its own network for the three containers; only karakeep also joins the shared homelab network that the proxy uses.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Database (bookmarks, tags, lists, users) appdata/karakeep/db.db → /data/db.db Screenshots, archives, images, and uploaded files appdata/karakeep/assets/ → /data/assets Search index Docker volume homelab_karakeep_karakeep-meilisearch → /meili_data in karakeep-meilisearch Secrets KARAKEEP_NEXTAUTH_SECRET and KARAKEEP_MEILI_MASTER_KEY in .env

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Save: the browser extension's button, the phone app's share sheet, or paste a link, a note, or an image on the home page.
  • Find: the search box searches titles, page text, and notes; qualifiers such as #tag and is:fav narrow it.
  • Organise: tags, lists (including smart lists that fill themselves from a search), favourites, and archive for things you are done with.
  • Read later: open a bookmark to read the saved text without the site's clutter, and highlight passages.
  • Bring old bookmarks in: User Settings › Import / Export takes a browser bookmarks HTML file and exports from Pocket and other read-later services.
  • Apps: Karakeep for iOS and Android, and extensions for Chrome and Firefox; all ask for the server address https://links.example.com.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Open WebUI uses Ollama on this Mac; Karakeep can use the same Ollama for automatic tags (see Tinkering ideas).
  • Pocket ID is its sign-in once ./homelab sso setup has run: it writes OAUTH_WELLKNOWN_URL, OAUTH_CLIENT_ID, OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET, and OAUTH_PROVIDER_NAME to data/sso/karakeep.env, and an existing account with the same email is linked.
  • FreshRSS: read feeds there, keep the articles worth keeping here.
  • Duplicati backs up appdata/karakeep in the Homelab Stack Data job, and ./homelab backup takes a daily copy of db.db (see Backups).
  • .env: KARAKEEP_PORT (default 3010), KARAKEEP_NEXTAUTH_SECRET, KARAKEEP_MEILI_MASTER_KEY. Meilisearch is pinned and left out of the nightly updates, because its data format changes between versions.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Local AI tags: add OLLAMA_BASE_URL: http://host.docker.internal:11434 and INFERENCE_TEXT_MODEL / INFERENCE_IMAGE_MODEL (models you have pulled) to the karakeep service in stacks/karakeep/compose.yaml, then ./homelab compose karakeep up -d.
  • Full-page archives for every link: add CRAWLER_FULL_PAGE_ARCHIVE: "true" the same way; it uses more disk in appdata/karakeep/assets.
  • Turn off sign-ups for good with DISABLE_SIGNUPS: "true" once everyone has an account.
  • Rules: User Settings › Rule Engine can tag a bookmark or add it to a list automatically when it is saved.
  • RSS: User Settings › RSS Subscriptions saves new items from a feed into Karakeep on their own.
  • Webhooks: User Settings › Webhooks calls a URL when a bookmark is created or crawled, for example a Home Assistant webhook automation.
  • Smart lists: make a list from a search (for example #recipe) so it stays up to date.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
Follow the app and browser logs, check the three containers, restart, look at the data folder, and use the API with a key from User Settings › API Keys:

./homelab logs karakeep -f
./homelab logs karakeep-chrome -f
./homelab compose karakeep ps
./homelab compose karakeep restart karakeep
./homelab compose karakeep exec karakeep ls -la /data
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" http://localhost:3010/api/v1/bookmarks

docs.title: API
docs.text:
• Key: User Settings › API Keys.
  • Base URL: http://localhost:3010/api/v1 on this Mac, https://links.example.com/api/v1 on the LAN, with Authorization: Bearer <key>.
  • Save a link: curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"type":"link","url":"https://example.com"}' http://localhost:3010/api/v1/bookmarks
  • The API reference is in the documentation.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• karakeep.app and the documentation
  • GitHub: karakeep-app/karakeep (source of both ghcr.io/karakeep-app images)
  • Meilisearch, the search engine

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: Saved items and archives live in appdata/karakeep, which the Homelab Stack Data job takes off-site (like appdata/paperless), and ./homelab backup keeps a consistent copy of db.db each night. The Meilisearch index is rebuilt from it and is not backed up.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Pages are not archived: the karakeep-chrome container is not running (./homelab status --all).
  • Search finds nothing: re-index under Admin › Background jobs.

docs.title: Kiwix
docs.text:
Wikipedia and other reference libraries, readable offline.

Service kiwix in compose/documents.yaml (project homelab_documents) Image ghcr.io/kiwix/kiwix-serve:latest Category Documents Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install kiwix Address https://kiwix.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:8098 (KIWIX_PORT) Data data/appdata/kiwix → /library/Volumes/Media/kiwix → /zim Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first Also known as wikipedia, offline-wikipedia

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Wikipedia, Wiktionary, Project Gutenberg's books, Stack Exchange sites, medical references, and other libraries, kept on the media drive and readable from every device at home, with no internet: for a power cut, a trip, or children who should read without the rest of the web. Each library is one ZIM file.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. ./homelab install kiwix. It waits for the media drive, like the other apps that use it, and serves an empty library until you add a file.
  2. Pick a library at library.kiwix.org and download its .zim file into kiwix on the media drive (MEDIA_ROOT/kiwix, or KIWIX_ZIM_ROOT if you set it). All of English Wikipedia with pictures is over 100 GB; "nopic" and "mini" versions are much smaller.
  3. ./homelab restart kiwix: each start adds every .zim file in the folder to the library.
  4. Open it: https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:8098 in Home mode, https://kiwix.example.com with a domain, or http://localhost:8098 on this computer.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• kiwix-serve in one container. Its library is the file data/appdata/kiwix/library.xml (the homelab puts an empty one there at install), which lists the ZIM files; it follows changes to that file while it runs.
  • At each start, a line of shell before it adds every /zim/*.zim to the library with kiwix-manage, so dropping a file in the folder and restarting is enough.
  • A ZIM file is compressed and indexed: articles open straight from it, and its own search works offline.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where The libraries (ZIM files) MEDIA_ROOT/kiwix on the media drive → /zim (or KIWIX_ZIM_ROOT) The list of libraries data/appdata/kiwix/library.xml → /library/library.xml

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Read: the home page lists each library; open one and use its search box, or the search across all of them at the top.
  • Update a library: download the newer ZIM, delete the old one, and ./homelab restart kiwix.
  • On a phone or laptop away from home: the Kiwix apps for iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, and Linux read the same ZIM files directly from the device.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Homepage and Homarr can link it like any other app.
  • .env: KIWIX_PORT (default 8098), and KIWIX_ZIM_ROOT to keep the files somewhere other than MEDIA_ROOT/kiwix.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• A "kids" library: Wikipedia for Schools (wikipedia_en_for-schools) is small and curated.
  • Keep a medical library (WikiMed) and a survival or repair guide (iFixit) for a power cut.
  • Offline documentation for the tools you use (DevDocs ZIMs).

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
./homelab logs kiwix -f
./homelab restart kiwix
./homelab compose kiwix exec kiwix kiwix-manage /library/library.xml show
curl -s http://localhost:8098/catalog/v2/entries

docs.title: API
docs.text: • GET /catalog/v2/entries lists the libraries (OPDS, an Atom feed); GET /search?pattern=… searches them. The reference is in kiwix-serve's documentation.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• kiwix.org and library.kiwix.org
  • GitHub: kiwix/kiwix-tools

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: The ZIM files are not backed up: each can be downloaded again from library.kiwix.org, and they are large. library.xml is in data/appdata/kiwix and is rebuilt from the files at each start.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• A new library does not show: the file's name must end in .zim, and Kiwix needs a restart (./homelab restart kiwix). A half-downloaded file is skipped; download it again.
  • It is not running: the media drive is not mounted; ./homelab status says it is waiting for it.

docs.title: Linkwarden
docs.text:
Bookmarks for the household, each page kept as a screenshot, a PDF, and text.

Service linkwarden in stacks/linkwarden/compose.yaml (project homelab_linkwarden) Image ghcr.io/linkwarden/linkwarden:latest Category Documents Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install linkwarden Address https://bookmarks.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:3060 (LINKWARDEN_PORT) Depends on linkwarden-db, linkwarden-meilisearch Helpers linkwarden-db docker.io/library/postgres:18, dumped daily by ./homelab backuplinkwarden-meilisearch getmeili/meilisearch:v1.41.0 Data appdata/linkwarden → /data/data Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Bookmarks the household shares: each saved page is kept as a screenshot, a PDF, and its readable text, so it survives the site changing or going away. Links go into collections, which can be shared with other people's accounts, with tags and full-text search. Like Karakeep, it stands in for Raindrop.io; Linkwarden leans to shared collections and keeping every page, Karakeep to a personal read-later list.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. ./homelab install linkwarden (it brings its PostgreSQL and Meilisearch).
  2. Open it and create the first account: it is the administrator.
  3. Make the household's accounts (each person signs up, or the administrator adds them under Administration), then set LINKWARDEN_DISABLE_REGISTRATION=true in Settings and ./homelab up so no one else can sign up.
  4. Install the Linkwarden browser extension or phone app with the address you open it at (https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:3060 in Home mode, or https://bookmarks.example.com with a domain).

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• A Next.js app with a background worker in one container. The worker opens each new link in its own headless browser and saves a screenshot, a PDF, and a readable copy of the text.
  • Links, collections, tags, and accounts live in PostgreSQL (linkwarden-db); the saved pages are files under appdata/linkwarden.
  • Meilisearch (linkwarden-meilisearch, port 7700 inside the stack) indexes the text for search, with LINKWARDEN_MEILI_MASTER_KEY. The index can be rebuilt from the database, so it is not backed up.
  • Sign-in is handled by NextAuth; NEXTAUTH_URL comes from LINKWARDEN_URL (https://bookmarks.example.com by default) and must match the address you open.
  • The stack has its own network for the three containers; only linkwarden also joins the shared homelab network that the proxy uses.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Links, collections, tags, accounts PostgreSQL in the Docker volume homelab_linkwarden_linkwarden-pgdata Saved pages (screenshots, PDFs, text) and uploads appdata/linkwarden → /data/data Search index Docker volume homelab_linkwarden_linkwarden-meilisearch Secrets LINKWARDEN_DB_PASSWORD, LINKWARDEN_NEXTAUTH_SECRET, and LINKWARDEN_MEILI_MASTER_KEY in .env

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Save: the browser extension's button, the phone app's share sheet, or New Link on the dashboard.
  • Share: make a collection and add people's accounts to it, to look or to add links too; a collection can also be made public with its own link.
  • Find: search looks through titles, tags, and the saved text of every page.
  • Read the saved copy: open a link and pick the readable view, the screenshot, or the PDF; it works after the site is gone.
  • Bring old bookmarks in: Settings › Import takes a browser's bookmarks file and exports from other bookmark services.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Karakeep does much the same for one person's read-later; most households keep one of the two.
  • Open WebUI's Ollama on this machine can tag links (see Tinkering ideas).
  • Duplicati backs up appdata/linkwarden, and ./homelab backup dumps its database daily (see Backups).
  • .env: LINKWARDEN_PORT (default 3060), LINKWARDEN_URL, LINKWARDEN_DISABLE_REGISTRATION, and the secrets above. Meilisearch is pinned and left out of the nightly updates, because its data format changes between versions.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Local AI tags: add NEXT_PUBLIC_OLLAMA_ENDPOINT_URL: http://host.docker.internal:11434 and OLLAMA_MODEL (a model you have pulled) to the linkwarden service in stacks/linkwarden/compose.yaml, then ./homelab compose linkwarden up -d.
  • RSS: Settings › RSS Subscriptions saves new items from a feed into a collection.
  • A public collection of the family's recipes or school links, shared with its own address.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
./homelab logs linkwarden -f
./homelab compose linkwarden ps
./homelab compose linkwarden restart linkwarden
./homelab compose linkwarden exec linkwarden-db psql -U linkwarden -c 'select count(*) from "Link"'
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" "http://localhost:3060/api/v1/links?sort=0"

docs.title: API
docs.text:
• Token: Settings › Access Tokens, or POST /api/v1/session with {"username":…,"password":…} (its response.token).
  • Base URL: http://localhost:3060/api/v1 on this machine, https://bookmarks.example.com/api/v1 on the LAN, with Authorization: Bearer <token>.
  • Save a link: curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"url":"https://example.com","name":"Example"}' http://localhost:3060/api/v1/links
  • The API reference is in the documentation.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• linkwarden.app and the documentation
  • GitHub: linkwarden/linkwarden
  • Meilisearch, the search engine

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: ./homelab backup dumps the PostgreSQL database nightly into recovery-staging/databases/linkwarden-db, and Duplicati takes it off-site with the rest. The saved pages are in appdata/linkwarden, which the Homelab Stack Data job takes off-site with the rest of appdata. The Meilisearch index is rebuilt from the database and is not backed up.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Every page fails to save: the worker's browser needs memory; check ./homelab logs linkwarden for out-of-memory errors and give the machine more room, or save fewer pages at once.
  • Search finds nothing: ./homelab compose linkwarden restart linkwarden-meilisearch linkwarden; the index fills again from the database.
  • Signed out right after signing in: the address you opened is not LINKWARDEN_URL; set it in Settings and ./homelab up.

docs.title: Memos
docs.text:
Quick notes from any device, with tags and search.

Service memos in compose/documents.yaml (project homelab_documents) Image neosmemo/memos:stable Category Documents Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install memos Address https://notes.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:5230 (MEMOS_PORT) Data data/appdata/memos → /var/opt/memos Database dump Daily by ./homelab backup into recovery-staging/databases/memos Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Quick notes from any device: a thought, a link, a list, a photo, with tags and search, like a private timeline. Longer documents and scans belong in Paperless-ngx; Memos is for the small things.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. ./homelab install memos and open https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:5230 in Home mode, or https://notes.example.com with a domain.
  2. The first account becomes the admin. Then Settings › System › turn off Allow user signup once everyone has an account.
  3. On a phone, add it to the home screen.

docs.title: Away from home
docs.text: In Home mode (the default), Memos is on the tailnet: it opens at home and away on every device signed in to Tailscale. With a domain, it is on the home network only: install Tailscale to reach it from anywhere, or, to publish it through the tunnel, add public: true to its x-homelab block and run ./homelab domain setup again.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• A single Go program that serves both the API and the React web app on port 5230.
  • Everything lives in one SQLite database, memos_prod.db, in the data folder /var/opt/memos.
  • Memos are Markdown. A #word becomes a tag and - [ ] makes a checklist.
  • Attachments are stored in the database or as files in the data folder, depending on Settings › Storage; local files go under assets.
  • Each memo has a visibility: private (only you), workspace (signed-in users), or public.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Database (memos, users, settings) data/appdata/memos/memos_prod.db → /var/opt/memos/memos_prod.db Attachments kept as files data/appdata/memos/assets/ → /var/opt/memos/assets Daily consistent copy recovery-staging/databases/memos (by ./homelab backup)

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Write: type in the box at the top and press Cmd+Return (or Save). Add #tags as you go.
  • Find: the search box, the tag list, and the activity calendar filter the timeline by word, tag, or day.
  • Keep on top: pin a memo from its ... menu; archive it when it is done.
  • Checklists: tick boxes right in the timeline, without opening the memo.
  • Phone: the web app added to the home screen, or a third-party app such as MoeMemos (iOS and Android).
  • Export: Settings › Export & Import.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Paperless-ngx is the place for scans and long documents; Memos is for small notes.
  • Karakeep is better for links you want archived; Memos for a quick thought about one.
  • Pocket ID can be its sign-in: Settings › SSO, with a client made in Pocket ID.
  • Nginx Proxy Manager serves https://notes.example.com; .env sets only MEMOS_PORT (default 5230).

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Quick capture from the iPhone: a Shortcut with Get Contents of URL that POSTs to the API (see API), on the share sheet or the Action button.
  • Webhooks: Settings › Webhooks calls a URL whenever a memo is created or changed.
  • Attachments as files: Settings › Storage › local storage keeps new images in assets instead of the database, so the database stays small.
  • Share a single note: set one memo to public and send its link (public memos are only reachable on the LAN or the tailnet here).
  • A daily review: filter the calendar to a day a year ago and see what you were thinking.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
Follow the log, restart, look at the data folder, and use the API with an access token from Settings › My Account › Access Tokens:

./homelab logs memos -f
./homelab compose memos restart memos
./homelab compose memos exec memos ls -la /var/opt/memos
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" http://localhost:5230/api/v1/memos

docs.title: API
docs.text:
• Token: Settings › My Account › Access Tokens.
  • Base URL: http://localhost:5230/api/v1 on this Mac, or https://notes.example.com/api/v1, with Authorization: Bearer <token>.
  • New memo: curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"content":"Buy batteries #shopping"}' http://localhost:5230/api/v1/memos

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• usememos.com (documentation and API reference)
  • GitHub: usememos/memos (source of the neosmemo/memos image)

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: The nightly backup takes a consistent copy of the database (memos_prod.db); attachments in data/appdata/memos are covered by the AppData job.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: • Images do not load after a move: attachments are stored in data/appdata/memos/assets; keep that folder with the database.

docs.title: Open WebUI
docs.text:
Private AI chat with models that run on this Mac (Ollama)

Service open-webui in compose/documents.yaml (project homelab_documents) Image ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:main Category Documents Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install open-webui Address https://ai.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:3080 (OPEN_WEBUI_PORT) Data data/appdata/open-webui → /app/backend/data Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: A private ChatGPT-style chat whose models run on this Mac through Ollama. Prompts and answers never leave the house. Local models are smaller than the big cloud ones, so treat it as a private assistant rather than a full ChatGPT Plus replacement.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Install Ollama on the machine itself, outside a container, so it can use the GPU, then pull a model, for example ollama pull llama3.2:
Install and start macOS brew install ollama, then brew services start ollama Linux curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh \| sh. It listens only on 127.0.0.1, which containers cannot reach. Have it listen on Docker's own address instead (ip -4 -br addr show docker0 shows it, 172.17.0.1 unless Docker was told otherwise), which the containers reach and the home network does not: sudo systemctl edit ollama, add Environment=OLLAMA_HOST=172.17.0.1 under [Service] and After=docker.service under [Unit] (that address exists once Docker runs), then sudo systemctl restart ollama. The homelab's own Explain and checks find it there. Not 0.0.0.0: Ollama has no password, and that opens it to every device on the home network SteamOS The standalone build in the home folder, started with OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0 ollama serve. Docker run as you reaches this machine only through its home-network address, so Ollama answers the home network too: keep that network to people you trust Windows winget install Ollama.Ollama (it starts at sign-in)

./homelab doctor warns while Open WebUI runs and Ollama does not answer, with this machine's line from the table. 2. ./homelab install open-webui. 3. Open it and create the first account, which becomes the admin. Later accounts wait for the admin's approval.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• A Python (FastAPI) backend with a Svelte web app, both in one container on port 8080.
  • It holds no models itself. Each chat is sent to Ollama, which runs natively on this Mac so it can use the GPU, at OLLAMA_BASE_URL (http://host.docker.internal:11434).
  • Users, chats, and settings are in a SQLite database, webui.db, in /app/backend/data. Most admin settings are saved there too, so they survive restarts.
  • Files you attach or put in a knowledge base are split up and embedded by a small local model, then stored in a Chroma vector index in vector_db, so the chat can quote them (RAG).
  • WEBUI_SECRET_KEY (OPEN_WEBUI_SECRET_KEY in .env) signs sign-in sessions; changing it signs everyone out. Telemetry is off (ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY).

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Database (users, chats, settings) data/appdata/open-webui/webui.db → /app/backend/data/webui.db Uploaded files data/appdata/open-webui/uploads/ Document index (RAG) data/appdata/open-webui/vector_db/ Downloaded helper models (embeddings, speech) data/appdata/open-webui/cache/ Chat models Ollama's own folder on this Mac, ~/.ollama/models

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Chat: New Chat, pick a model at the top, and type. Set a favourite as the default from the model menu.
  • Ask about a file: attach it with +, or type # to pull in a knowledge base.
  • Saved prompts: Workspace › Prompts; type / in a chat to use one.
  • Your own assistants: Workspace › Models: a base model plus a system prompt, knowledge, and settings, shown in the model list.
  • Accounts: Admin Panel › Users approves new sign-ups and sets roles.
  • Phone: open https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:3080 in Home mode, or https://ai.example.com with a domain, and add it to the home screen; it works as an app.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Ollama on this Mac, outside the homelab: brew services start ollama, models with ollama pull. ./homelab doctor warns when it does not answer.
  • Karakeep can use the same Ollama for automatic tags.
  • Pocket ID is its sign-in once ./homelab sso setup has run (OPENID_PROVIDER_URL, OAUTH_CLIENT_ID, OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET, ENABLE_OAUTH_SIGNUP, and the rest in data/sso/open-webui.env); accounts with the same email are merged.
  • Home Assistant has its own Ollama integration if you want a local model behind its voice assistant.
  • .env: OPEN_WEBUI_PORT (default 3080), OPEN_WEBUI_SECRET_KEY, and HOMELAB_DOMAIN for WEBUI_URL.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Household manuals: Workspace › Knowledge › new collection, upload the PDFs, then ask "how do I descale the coffee machine" with # and the collection.
  • Try other models: ollama pull qwen2.5, ollama pull gemma3, or a vision model such as llama3.2-vision to ask about photos.
  • Voice: the microphone button transcribes with a local Whisper model (Admin Panel › Settings › Audio).
  • Web search: Admin Panel › Settings › Web Search can add results to answers; it sends your queries to the search provider you choose.
  • Cloud models side by side: Admin Panel › Settings › Connections takes any OpenAI-compatible API key, if you want a bigger model now and then.
  • Tools and functions from the community (Workspace › Tools) run as code inside the container: read them before installing.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
Follow the log, restart, check which models Ollama has and which are loaded, and check that the container can reach Ollama:

./homelab logs open-webui -f
./homelab compose open-webui restart open-webui
ollama list
ollama ps
curl -s http://localhost:11434/api/tags
./homelab compose open-webui exec open-webui curl -s http://host.docker.internal:11434/api/version

docs.title: API
docs.text:
• Key: API keys are off by default. Turn them on in Admin Panel › Settings › General, then make one under Settings › Account › API Keys.
  • Base URL: http://localhost:3080/api, with Authorization: Bearer <key>. It is OpenAI-compatible, so OpenAI clients work against it.
  • List models: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY" http://localhost:3080/api/models
  • Chat: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"llama3.2","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}]}' http://localhost:3080/api/chat/completions

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• Open WebUI documentation
  • GitHub: open-webui/open-webui (source of the ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui image)
  • ollama.com (model library) and GitHub: ollama/ollama

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: data/appdata/open-webui (accounts, chats, settings) is covered by the AppData job. Models live in Ollama's own folder (~/.ollama) and can be pulled again.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• "Ollama not reachable": Ollama is not running natively (brew services start ollama), or it only listens on localhost, which host.docker.internal reaches on OrbStack.
  • Slow answers: pick a smaller model; 16 GB of memory suits 3-8B models.

docs.title: Paperless-AI
docs.text:
Titles, tags, and correspondents for Paperless-ngx's documents, from an AI model.

Service paperless-ai in stacks/paperless/compose.yaml (project homelab_paperless) Image docker.io/clusterzx/paperless-ai:latest Category Documents Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install paperless-ai Address https://docs-ai.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:8011 (PAPERLESS_AI_PORT) Depends on paperless Helpers paperless-db docker.io/library/postgres:18, dumped daily by ./homelab backuppaperless-broker docker.io/valkey/valkey:9-alpine Data appdata/paperless-ai → /app/data Database dump Daily by ./homelab backup into recovery-staging/databases/paperless-ai Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first Needs in .env PAPERLESS_AI_PAPERLESS_TOKEN

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Reads each new document in Paperless-ngx and asks an AI model for a title, tags, a correspondent, and the document's date, then writes them back to Paperless, so a scanned bill comes out as City Water, January invoice with the right tags instead of scan_0042. It also answers questions about your documents in a chat. The model can run on this machine with Ollama, so the documents never leave it, or be an OpenAI-compatible service you choose.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Have Paperless-ngx running and sign in to it as an administrator.
  2. Have a model it can use: Ollama on this machine (Setup shows how on each system, once Paperless-AI is installed, and Open WebUI's Setup has the details), then ollama pull llama3.2 or a larger model if the machine has the memory; or the address and key of an OpenAI-compatible service.
  3. In Paperless, open your account (top right) › My Profile and create an API Auth Token. Paperless-AI acts as that account and needs to see its tags, correspondents, document types, custom fields, and users, so an administrator's token is simplest.
  4. Put the token in Settings › PAPERLESS_AI_PAPERLESS_TOKEN, then ./homelab install paperless-ai: it installs only once the token is set. Its image is about a 135 MB download (version 4).
  5. Open Paperless-AI. Its setup page has Paperless's address (http://paperless:8000) and the token filled in; add your Paperless username, then:
  6. AI provider: Ollama, at http://host.docker.internal:11434 with the model you pulled; or Custom, with the service's address, key, and model.
  7. Your own username and password for Paperless-AI.
  8. Save. The settings take effect at once (no restart), and it works through the documents it has not seen yet on its schedule. Scan Now on its dashboard starts at once.

Until its first account exists, its setup page answers anyone who can reach it (versions before 4 answered without a sign-in even once set up), so the homelab keeps Paperless-AI off the internet (LAN and Tailscale only): finish step 5 right after installing.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• One Node.js app (version 4; 3.x had a Python search service beside it). It lists Paperless's documents through its API, sends each one's text to the model with a prompt, and writes the answer back: title, tags, correspondent, document type, date, and custom fields, each switched on or off in its settings.
  • It indexes the documents' text for the chat (Chat and RAG Chat), on this machine.
  • Its settings live in its own data/config.json (3.x's data/.env is read once on the first start of version 4), written by its setup page and Settings; settings the homelab sets show there as locked. The homelab gives it Paperless's address and token (PAPERLESS_AI_PAPERLESS_TOKEN), which win over the ones on its own pages, so a new token goes in the homelab's Settings, followed by ./homelab up. It also gives it API_KEY (PAPERLESS_AI_API_KEY, for its API) and JWT_SECRET (PAPERLESS_AI_JWT_SECRET, for its sign-in).
  • Which documents it has done, its history, its accounts, and the token counts are kept in a SQLite database, paperless-ai.db (3.x's documents.db is imported once, then left as it was).

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Settings (model, prompt, what it changes) appdata/paperless-ai/config.json Documents done, history, accounts appdata/paperless-ai/paperless-ai.db The chat's search index appdata/paperless-ai Secrets PAPERLESS_AI_PAPERLESS_TOKEN, PAPERLESS_AI_API_KEY, and PAPERLESS_AI_JWT_SECRET in .env

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• New scans: drop them in Paperless as usual; within half an hour they have a title and tags. History lists what it changed; Reset Selected there has it look at those documents again on the next scan.
  • Only some documents: in Settings, have it process only documents with a tag you choose, or switch off automatic processing and use Manual on the documents you pick.
  • Your own tags: in Settings, limit it to the tags and correspondents you already have, so it does not invent new ones.
  • Ask your documents: Chat answers from one document; RAG Chat searches all of them (when does the car insurance renew?).

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Paperless-ngx: the documents it reads and writes, through Paperless's API with your token (PAPERLESS_AI_PAPERLESS_TOKEN).
  • Ollama on this machine (see Open WebUI) or an OpenAI-compatible service: the model.
  • On battery the homelab pauses it with the other background work (see Host).
  • .env: PAPERLESS_AI_PORT (default 8011), PAPERLESS_AI_URL, and the secrets above.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Your own prompt, in Settings: ask for titles in your language, or for the amount and due date in a custom field.
  • Webhook: a Paperless workflow that calls POST /api/webhook/document when a document is added, so it is done at once instead of on the next scan.
  • A bigger model for the chat only, on a machine with the memory for it.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
./homelab logs paperless-ai -f
./homelab compose paperless restart paperless-ai
curl -s -X POST -H "x-api-key: $PAPERLESS_AI_API_KEY" http://localhost:8011/api/scan/now
curl -s -H "x-api-key: $PAPERLESS_AI_API_KEY" "http://localhost:8011/api/history?pageSize=5"

docs.title: API
docs.text:
• Key: PAPERLESS_AI_API_KEY from .env, sent as the x-api-key header.
  • Base URL: http://localhost:8011 on this machine, https://docs-ai.example.com on the LAN.
  • Scan now: POST /api/scan/now. History: GET /api/history. A document as soon as it is added: POST /api/webhook/document.
  • The full reference is its own Swagger page at /api-docs.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• GitHub: clusterzx/paperless-ai and its wiki
  • Ollama, the models that run on this machine

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: ./homelab backup copies paperless-ai.db nightly into recovery-staging/databases/paperless-ai, and Duplicati takes it off-site with the rest. Its settings in appdata/paperless-ai/config.json go off-site with the Homelab Stack Data job, which covers all of appdata. The chat's search index is rebuilt from Paperless. The documents themselves are Paperless's, backed up with it.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• The setup page says the Paperless connection failed: the token in Settings › PAPERLESS_AI_PAPERLESS_TOKEN is wrong or from an account that cannot see tags, correspondents, document types, custom fields, and users; make a new one in Paperless, put it there, and ./homelab up. The address is http://paperless:8000, not localhost (inside its container, localhost is Paperless-AI itself).
  • Ollama connection failed: Ollama is not answering on this machine, or (Linux) listens only on 127.0.0.1; Open WebUI's Setup shows how to let containers reach it. The model name must be one ollama list shows.
  • Documents are not changed: in Settings, check that titles and tags are switched on and that no tag filter leaves them out; ./homelab logs paperless-ai shows each document's answer from the model.
  • Slow or out of memory: a smaller model, or fewer documents at once. The first start indexes every document for the chat, which takes a while on a large archive.

docs.title: Paperless-ngx
docs.text:
The household's document archive. Scan or drop a file in, and Paperless reads it (OCR), tags it, and makes it searchable.

Service paperless in stacks/paperless/compose.yaml (project homelab_paperless) Image ghcr.io/paperless-ngx/paperless-ngx:latest Category Documents Starts with ./homelab up Yes (./homelab up) Address https://docs.example.com (LAN and public, through the Cloudflare Tunnel) On this machine http://localhost:8010 (PAPERLESS_PORT) Depends on paperless-db, paperless-broker Helpers paperless-db docker.io/library/postgres:18, dumped daily by ./homelab backuppaperless-broker docker.io/valkey/valkey:9-alpine Data appdata/paperless/data → /usr/src/paperless/dataappdata/paperless/media → /usr/src/paperless/mediaappdata/paperless/export → /usr/src/paperless/exportappdata/paperless/consume → /usr/src/paperless/consume Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first Also known as paperless-ngx

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Every letter, bill, contract, and receipt in one searchable place, reachable from anywhere.
  • Original files are kept untouched; Paperless adds an archived PDF with a text layer.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Create the admin account:
./homelab compose paperless exec paperless python3 manage.py createsuperuser

Until an account exists, Paperless's own sign-up page makes whoever opens it first a superuser. So the homelab keeps it off the internet until then, and Set up the domain puts it on once the account is made.

  1. Sign in at https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:8010 in Home mode, or https://docs.example.com with a domain, turn on two-factor authentication (Profile), and create accounts for the family.
  2. Add correspondents, document types, and tags as documents arrive; let matching learn from them.
  3. Drop files into appdata/paperless/consume (or upload in the web UI or the mobile apps) to import.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• A Python (Django) web app on port 8000, with Celery workers in the same container that do the slow work: importing, OCR, and training the matching model.
  • Three containers: paperless (web app and workers), paperless-db (PostgreSQL 18, the database), and paperless-broker (Valkey, the task queue between the web app and the workers). The database and broker are only on the stack's own network; paperless also joins the shared homelab network for the proxy.
  • The consumer watches consume. Each new file is OCRed with OCRmyPDF and Tesseract in PAPERLESS_OCR_LANGUAGE, gets a searchable PDF/A copy and a thumbnail, and is filed in media. The original is kept unchanged next to it.
  • A full-text index (Whoosh) in data/index powers search. A classifier learns from your past choices to suggest the correspondent, document type, tags, and storage path for new documents.
  • PAPERLESS_URL must match the address you open, or sign-in fails with a CSRF error. Files are written as USERMAP_UID/USERMAP_GID (PUID/PGID), so you own them on this Mac.
  • It is the one app in this group that is also public, through the Cloudflare Tunnel.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Originals, as you gave them appdata/paperless/media/documents/originals/ → /usr/src/paperless/media/documents/originals Searchable PDF copies appdata/paperless/media/documents/archive/ Thumbnails appdata/paperless/media/documents/thumbnails/ Search index appdata/paperless/data/index/ → /usr/src/paperless/data/index Matching model appdata/paperless/data/classification_model.pickle Logs (paperless.log, mail.log) appdata/paperless/data/log/ Inbox folder appdata/paperless/consume/ → /usr/src/paperless/consume Exports appdata/paperless/export/ → /usr/src/paperless/export Database Docker volume homelab_paperless_paperless-pgdata → /var/lib/postgresql in paperless-db Task queue Docker volume homelab_paperless_paperless-redisdata (not backed up)

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Add documents: drag files onto the web page, drop them in consume, or upload from a phone app (Swift Paperless on iOS, Paperless Mobile on Android).
