  • Inbox: give a tag the inbox setting (Tags › edit › Inbox tag) and every new document gets it; review, correct, and remove the tag.
  • Find: the search box searches the text of every page. Filter the document list by tag, correspondent, type, or date, then save the filter as a view and show it on the dashboard.
  • Teach it: correct the suggestions on a few documents of each kind; matching set to Auto learns from them.
  • Share: a document's Share button makes a link that expires, for sending one bill to someone without an account.
  • Notes and history: each document has notes and a history of changes.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Stirling PDF for clean-up before import: merge, split, rotate, or remove blank pages.
  • Pocket ID is its sign-in once ./homelab sso setup has run (PAPERLESS_APPS and PAPERLESS_SOCIALACCOUNT_PROVIDERS in data/sso/paperless.env). An existing user links it under My Profile › Connect new social account.
  • PostgreSQL and Redis and Valkey describe its two helpers; Duplicati backs up the folders and the daily dump (see Backups).
  • Memos is for quick notes; Homebox can hold a copy of a receipt next to the thing you bought.
  • .env: PAPERLESS_PORT (default 8010), PAPERLESS_DB_PASSWORD, PAPERLESS_SECRET_KEY, PAPERLESS_OCR_LANGUAGE (default eng), TZ, PUID, PGID. PAPERLESS_URL comes from HOMELAB_DOMAIN.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Email import: Mail › add the account, then a mail rule that takes PDF attachments from bills and assigns a correspondent.
  • Workflows: Workflows › add one that sets tags, a type, or an owner when a document arrives from a given source or matches a file name.
  • Folders as tags: PAPERLESS_CONSUMER_RECURSIVE=true and PAPERLESS_CONSUMER_SUBDIRS_AS_TAGS=true make subfolders of consume into tags.
  • Tidy file names on disk: Storage paths › add one (for example by year and correspondent) and assign it, so media/documents/originals reads like a filing cabinet.
  • Custom fields: Custom Fields › add an amount or a due date, then filter or sort by it.
  • Split stacks of scans: PAPERLESS_CONSUMER_ENABLE_BARCODES=true splits a batch at pages with a separator barcode.
  • Office files: Paperless can read Word and email files when two helper containers (Tika and Gotenberg) are added and PAPERLESS_TIKA_ENABLED=true is set; see its docs.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
Follow the log, check the three containers, restart, and run its management commands (export, rebuild the search index, retrain the matching model, check files against the database, reset a password):

./homelab logs paperless -f
./homelab compose paperless ps
./homelab compose paperless restart paperless
./homelab compose paperless exec paperless document_exporter ../export
./homelab compose paperless exec paperless document_index reindex
./homelab compose paperless exec paperless document_create_classifier
./homelab compose paperless exec paperless document_sanity_checker
./homelab compose paperless exec paperless python3 manage.py changepassword <user>
curl -s -H "Authorization: Token YOUR_TOKEN" 'http://localhost:8010/api/documents/?query=invoice'

docs.title: API
docs.text:
• Token: user menu › My Profile › API Auth Token (generate it there).
  • Base URL: http://localhost:8010/api/ on this Mac, or https://docs.example.com/api/, with Authorization: Token <token>. The API is browsable in a signed-in browser.
  • Upload: curl -s -H "Authorization: Token YOUR_TOKEN" -F document=@scan.pdf http://localhost:8010/api/documents/post_document/
  • Reference: REST API.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• Paperless-ngx documentation
  • GitHub: paperless-ngx/paperless-ngx (source of the ghcr.io/paperless-ngx/paperless-ngx image)

docs.title: Backup
docs.text:
Data How Documents and thumbnails (appdata/paperless/media) Homelab Stack Data job Search index and settings (appdata/paperless/data) Homelab Stack Data job Database Dumped daily by ./homelab backup, then the Homelab Databases job

For a portable copy independent of the database, run the exporter now and then:

./homelab compose paperless exec paperless document_exporter ../export

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Fix CSRF error on sign-in It must be opened at exactly the address in PAPERLESS_URL (https://docs.example.com, or the tailnet address in Home mode) Files sit in consume ./homelab logs paperless; the consumer reports why (permissions, unsupported type) OCR in the wrong language Set PAPERLESS_OCR_LANGUAGE (for example eng+deu) and ./homelab compose paperless up -d Slow imports OCR is CPU-heavy; give OrbStack more CPU or memory

docs.title: Stirling PDF
docs.text:
A toolbox for PDFs that never leaves the house: merge, split, rotate, compress, convert, OCR, and sign.

Service stirling-pdf in compose/documents.yaml (project homelab_documents) Image ghcr.io/stirling-tools/stirling-pdf:latest Category Documents Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install stirling-pdf Address https://pdf.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:8095 (STIRLING_PDF_PORT) Data data/appdata/stirling-pdf → /configs Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Do quick PDF jobs without uploading documents to an online converter.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text: ./homelab install stirling-pdf and open https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:8095 (Home mode), or, with a domain, run ./homelab domain setup and open https://pdf.example.com. No login is needed on the LAN.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• A Java (Spring Boot) web app on port 8080. The heavy lifting is done by tools bundled in the image: PDFBox and qpdf for page work, OCRmyPDF and Tesseract for OCR, and LibreOffice for Office conversions.
  • Each tool is a form that posts your file to the server, which returns the result. Every tool is also an HTTP API endpoint, so the same jobs can be scripted.
  • Its settings are in settings.yml in /configs; values you change belong in custom_settings.yml, which overrides it and survives upgrades.
  • Whether it asks for a sign-in is security.enableLogin in settings.yml. If a new version starts asking, set it to false and restart for the no-login setup this note describes.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Main settings data/appdata/stirling-pdf/settings.yml → /configs/settings.yml Your overrides data/appdata/stirling-pdf/custom_settings.yml → /configs/custom_settings.yml Accounts, when login is on also in data/appdata/stirling-pdf

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Find a tool: type in the search box on the home page (merge, split, compress, OCR, sign, redact) rather than browsing the list.
  • Many pages at once: the page editor (multi tool) reorders, rotates, deletes, and splits pages by dragging.
  • Scans: OCR adds a text layer so a scanned PDF becomes searchable and copyable.
  • Office and images: convert Word, Excel, PowerPoint, or images to PDF and back.
  • Private papers: Redact (automatic by search, or by hand) and Add Password before sending a document.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Paperless-ngx: tidy a batch here (merge, split, remove blank pages), then drop the result into appdata/paperless/consume.
  • Nginx Proxy Manager serves https://pdf.example.com; .env sets only STIRLING_PDF_PORT (default 8095).
  • Pocket ID can be its sign-in through OAuth2 (security.oauth2 in settings.yml) if you turn the login on.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Pipelines: chain steps (for example OCR, then compress, then add a watermark) and run them in one go from the pipeline tool.
  • Compare: the compare tool shows the text differences between two versions of a contract.
  • Script it: every tool has an API endpoint; the Swagger page lists them with their fields.
  • Sign: draw or upload a signature once and place it on any PDF.
  • Accounts for the family: turn the login on in settings.yml if you want to restrict who can use it.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
Follow the log, restart, read the settings, and rotate a PDF through the API (the result lands in the current folder):

./homelab logs stirling-pdf -f
./homelab compose stirling-pdf restart stirling-pdf
./homelab compose stirling-pdf exec stirling-pdf cat /configs/settings.yml
curl -s -o rotated.pdf -F fileInput=@scan.pdf -F angle=90 http://localhost:8095/api/v1/general/rotate-pdf

docs.title: API
docs.text:
• Key: none while login is off. With login on, each account has an API key in its account settings, sent as the X-API-KEY header.
  • Base URL: http://localhost:8095/api/v1/ on this Mac, or https://pdf.example.com/api/v1/.
  • Reference: the Swagger page at http://localhost:8095/swagger-ui/index.html lists every endpoint and lets you try it.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• Stirling PDF documentation
  • GitHub: Stirling-Tools/Stirling-PDF (source of the ghcr.io/stirling-tools/stirling-pdf image)

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: data/appdata/stirling-pdf holds only settings; it is in the Homelab AppData job. Files are processed and discarded.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Large OCR jobs are slow on CPU; give OrbStack more memory if a job fails.

docs.title: Actual Budget
docs.text:
An envelope budget, lighter than MoneyMatter, with the same budget on every device.

Service actual-budget in compose/finance.yaml (project homelab_finance) Image actualbudget/actual-server:latest Category Finance Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install actual-budget Address https://actual.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:5006 (ACTUAL_PORT) Data data/appdata/actual-budget → /data Database dump Daily by ./homelab backup into recovery-staging/databases/actual-budget Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first Also known as actual

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: An envelope budget: every dollar that comes in gets a job (rent, groceries, the holiday), and spending comes out of its envelope. It is the lighter choice beside MoneyMatter: one small container instead of a stack, no bank connection needed, and the same budget on a phone, a laptop, and this computer, each keeping a copy that syncs through the homelab. Pick one of the two for the household's budget; both can run.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. ./homelab install actual-budget, then open it: https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:5006 in Home mode, https://actual.example.com with a domain, or http://localhost:5006 on this computer.
  2. Set the server password on the first page. Everyone in the household signs in with this one password; keep it in Vaultwarden.
  3. Create a new file (or Import my budget from YNAB, nYNAB, or another Actual file), then add your accounts and their balances.
  4. On each phone: open the same address in the browser and add it to the home screen. The budget works offline there and syncs when the homelab is reachable.

The app needs a secure address (https, or localhost on this computer): the tailnet and domain addresses are, a plain http://192.168.1.10:5006 from another device is not, and it then shows Actual requires access to SharedArrayBuffer.

docs.title: Away from home
docs.text: In Home mode (the default), Actual Budget is on the tailnet: it opens at home and away on every device signed in to Tailscale. With a domain, it is on the home network only; install Tailscale to reach it from anywhere. Since every device keeps its own copy, a phone away from both still shows the budget and catches up later.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• One Node.js server (actual-server) on port 5006 serves the web app and keeps the sync data. The budget itself runs in the browser, in a local database the browser keeps, and changes travel to the server and on to the other devices.
  • The server's own database (account.sqlite) holds the password and the list of budget files; each budget's file and its change history live beside it in user-files.
  • End-to-end encryption is optional (a budget's Settings › Encryption): the server then keeps only data it cannot read, and each device asks for the key once.
  • Bank sync (GoCardless in Europe, SimpleFIN in North America) is optional and set up in the app; without it, transactions are typed in or imported from your bank's CSV, OFX, or QIF files.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Server database (password, list of budgets) data/appdata/actual-budget/server-files/account.sqlite Each budget's file and history data/appdata/actual-budget/user-files/ Daily consistent copy of the server database recovery-staging/databases/actual-budget (by ./homelab backup)

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Budget: on the budget page, put this month's money into envelopes until To budget is zero; move money between envelopes when one runs short.
  • Spend: add a transaction on the phone as you pay, or import the bank's file once a week (an account's Import).
  • Look back: Reports for spending by envelope, net worth, and cash flow.
  • Plan ahead: schedules for bills that repeat; envelope templates fill next month's budget the same way (Apply budget template).

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Homelab Wizard's own Finances screen (in the sidebar, not an app) reads the household's pay and bills forward, paycheck by paycheck, with no envelopes; Actual Budget gives each dollar a job. Either works alone.
  • MoneyMatter, the fuller budget with bank imports and investments; Actual Budget is the simpler of the two.
  • Wallos keeps the subscriptions; their amounts make a good Subscriptions envelope.
  • .env: ACTUAL_PORT (default 5006).

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• End-to-end encryption on a budget (Settings › Encryption), so even the homelab's copy is unreadable.
  • Rules (Payees › Rules) that file transactions from the same shop in the same envelope.
  • A second budget file for a side project or a club, each with its own envelopes, on the same server.
  • @actual-app/api (its Node.js library) for your own imports and reports.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
./homelab logs actual-budget -f
./homelab compose actual-budget restart actual-budget
curl -s http://localhost:5006/health

docs.title: API
docs.text: Actual has no web API for budgets: its Node.js library, @actual-app/api, opens a budget through the server with the server password and works on it locally. The server answers GET /health ({"status":"UP"}) for checks. The nightly real-Docker run uses it (test/realdocker/actual/budget.js): runImport makes a budget and uploads it, and getBudgets, downloadBudget, and getTransactions read it back from the server.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• actualbudget.org and its documentation
  • GitHub: actualbudget/actual

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: The nightly backup takes a consistent copy of the server database (account.sqlite); the budget files in user-files are covered by the AppData job. Every device also keeps a full copy of each budget it opened, and Export data (a budget's Settings) saves one as a file.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• "Actual requires access to SharedArrayBuffer": the page was opened at a plain http address from another device. Use the tailnet or domain address (https), or http://localhost:5006 on this computer.
  • A phone shows old numbers: it could not reach the homelab; open the budget with the homelab reachable and it syncs. Reset sync (Settings › Advanced) makes that device fetch the server's copy again.
  • Forgot the server password: ./homelab compose actual-budget exec actual-budget node /app/scripts/reset-password.js sets a new one.

docs.title: Firefly III importer
docs.text:
Brings bank files (CSV, CAMT) into Firefly III.

Service firefly-iii-importer in stacks/firefly-iii/compose.yaml (project homelab_firefly_iii) Image docker.io/fireflyiii/data-importer:latest Category Finance Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install firefly-iii-importer Address https://firefly-import.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:8097 (FIREFLY_IMPORTER_PORT) Depends on firefly-iii Helpers firefly-iii-db docker.io/library/postgres:18, dumped daily by ./homelab backupfirefly-iii-cron docker.io/library/alpine:3 Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Brings bank files into Firefly III: a CSV or CAMT export from the bank's website, or a bank connection you set up in it, turned into transactions with Firefly III's rules applied.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Make a personal access token in Firefly III (its note's Setup, steps 3 and 4) and put it in Settings as FIREFLY_IMPORTER_TOKEN, then ./homelab up.
  2. Open the importer (http://localhost:8097, or https://firefly-import.example.com with a domain). It finds Firefly III inside the stack and signs in with the token.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• A PHP app of its own, made by Firefly III's author, in its own container. It talks to Firefly III at http://firefly-iii:8080 inside the stack (FIREFLY_III_URL) and sends people to Firefly III's own address (VANITY_URL, from FIREFLY_URL).
  • It keeps nothing of its own: each import's settings can be downloaded as a file and loaded again next time.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where The token it signs in with FIREFLY_IMPORTER_TOKEN in .env Import settings you save A JSON file you download from it; nothing stays in the container

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• A month's statement: upload the bank's CSV, map its columns once (date, amount, description), save that configuration, and next month load it with the new file.
  • CAMT: European banks' XML statements need no mapping.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text: • Firefly III, whose API it writes to; its rules and categories apply to what comes in.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text: • Keep each bank's saved configuration file next to its statements in Paperless-ngx.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
./homelab logs firefly-iii-importer -f
./homelab compose firefly-iii restart firefly-iii-importer

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• The data importer's documentation
  • GitHub: firefly-iii/data-importer

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: Nothing to back up of its own: what it imports is in Firefly III's database, which ./homelab backup dumps nightly. Keep the configuration files you download.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• "No access token" or 401 errors: FIREFLY_IMPORTER_TOKEN is empty, expired, or was revoked; make a new one in Firefly III and ./homelab up.
  • Dates or amounts come in wrong: the column mapping or the date format in its configuration does not match the bank's file; adjust it and save the configuration again.

docs.title: Firefly III
docs.text:
A full household ledger, with budgets, bills, rules, and reports.

Service firefly-iii in stacks/firefly-iii/compose.yaml (project homelab_firefly_iii) Image docker.io/fireflyiii/core:latest Category Finance Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install firefly-iii Address https://firefly.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:8094 (FIREFLY_PORT) Depends on firefly-iii-db, firefly-iii-cron Helpers firefly-iii-db docker.io/library/postgres:18, dumped daily by ./homelab backupfirefly-iii-cron docker.io/library/alpine:3 Data firefly-iii-upload (volume) → /var/www/html/storage/upload Volume archive firefly-iii-upload daily by ./homelab backup into recovery-staging/volumes/firefly-iii-upload Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first Also known as firefly

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: A full ledger for the household's money: every account, what came in and went out, budgets, bills, and rules that sort transactions as they arrive, with reports over months and years. It is the detailed one of the homelab's money apps: Actual Budget and MoneyMatter are for an envelope budget, Firefly III for keeping the books. Bank files come in through its data importer.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. ./homelab install firefly-iii (it brings its PostgreSQL and its daily jobs); ./homelab install firefly-iii-importer too for bank files.
  2. Open it and register the first account: it is the administrator. Registration closes itself after that unless you allow more under Administration.
  3. A fresh install has no client for personal access tokens, so Profile › OAuth cannot make one yet. Make it once: ./homelab compose firefly-iii exec firefly-iii php artisan passport:client --personal --name="Firefly III Personal Access Client" --provider=users --no-interaction
  4. For the importer: Profile › OAuth › Personal access tokens › Create new token, then put it in Settings as FIREFLY_IMPORTER_TOKEN and ./homelab up. Open the importer (http://localhost:8097) and bring in a bank's CSV or CAMT file.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• A PHP (Laravel) app with its own web server in one container, on port 8080 inside the stack; its data is in PostgreSQL (firefly-iii-db), and attachments in the volume firefly-iii-upload.
  • APP_KEY (FIREFLY_APP_KEY, 32 characters) encrypts what it keeps; it must stay the same, or the data cannot be read.
  • Recurring transactions, bill reminders, and auto-budgets run when its cron address is called: firefly-iii-cron, a small Alpine container, calls it daily at 03:00 with FIREFLY_CRON_TOKEN.
  • The data importer (firefly-iii-importer) is a separate app that reads files (or a bank connection you set up in it) and sends the transactions to Firefly III's API with the personal access token.
  • The stack has its own network; only Firefly III and the importer also join the shared homelab network that the proxy uses.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Accounts, transactions, budgets, rules, users PostgreSQL in the Docker volume homelab_firefly_iii_firefly-iii-pgdata Attachments (receipts, statements) Docker volume homelab_firefly_iii_firefly-iii-upload → /var/www/html/storage/upload Secrets FIREFLY_APP_KEY, FIREFLY_DB_PASSWORD, FIREFLY_CRON_TOKEN, and FIREFLY_IMPORTER_TOKEN in .env

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Add a transaction: the + button, or the importer for a month's bank file at once.
  • Sort them: Automation › Rules files transactions into categories and budgets as they arrive (for example, everything from the supermarket under Groceries).
  • Budgets: Budgets sets an amount a month per budget, and shows what is left.
  • Bills: Bills says which regular payments are due and which were paid.
  • Reports: Reports compares months and years by category, budget, and account.
  • Apps: there is no official phone app; the web pages work on a phone, and third-party apps use its API.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Homelab Wizard's own Finances screen (in the sidebar, not an app) is the light view forward (paychecks, bills, net worth, typed in by hand); Firefly III is the full ledger of what happened, from bank files.
  • Paperless-ngx keeps the statements and receipts as documents; Firefly III can hold a copy as an attachment.
  • Duplicati takes what ./homelab backup makes off-site: its database dump and its attachments' archive (see Backups).
  • .env: FIREFLY_PORT (default 8094), FIREFLY_IMPORTER_PORT (default 8097), FIREFLY_URL, FIREFLY_IMPORTER_URL, and the secrets above.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Webhooks (Automation › Webhooks) call an address when a transaction is stored, for example a Home Assistant automation or an ntfy topic.
  • Piggy banks track saving towards something (a holiday, a new laptop).
  • The importer's configuration can be saved and reused, so each month's file goes in the same way.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
./homelab logs firefly-iii -f
./homelab compose firefly-iii ps
./homelab compose firefly-iii exec firefly-iii php artisan firefly-iii:verify
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" -H "Accept: application/vnd.api+json" http://localhost:8094/api/v1/accounts?type=asset

docs.title: API
docs.text:
• Token: Profile › OAuth › Personal access tokens (after the one-time step in Setup).
  • Base URL: http://localhost:8094/api/v1 on this machine, https://firefly.example.com/api/v1 on the LAN, with Authorization: Bearer <token> and Accept: application/vnd.api+json.
  • The API reference is at api-docs.firefly-iii.org.
  • Finances › Update balances has From Firefly III while Firefly III runs: it reads the asset accounts' balances with FIREFLY_IMPORTER_TOKEN, on a click, from this machine only; it changes nothing in Firefly III.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• firefly-iii.org and the documentation
  • GitHub: firefly-iii/firefly-iii and the data importer

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: ./homelab backup dumps the PostgreSQL database nightly into recovery-staging/databases/firefly-iii-db, and Duplicati takes it off-site with the rest. Its attachments' volume is archived the same night (recovery-staging/volumes). FIREFLY_APP_KEY must come back with it: it is in .env, which the nightly backup copies into the encrypted Homelab Secrets job (see the recovery kit). Without it the restored data cannot be read.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• "Personal access client not found" when making a token: the one-time step in Setup has not run yet.
  • The importer says it cannot reach Firefly III: FIREFLY_IMPORTER_TOKEN is empty or was revoked; make a new one and ./homelab up.
  • Signed out right after signing in, or links point elsewhere: the address you opened is not FIREFLY_URL; set it in Settings and ./homelab up.
  • It does not start where IPv6 is turned off in the kernel: its web server also listens on [::]:8080 and stops when that fails (as Tandoor's does). Turn IPv6 back on, which every desktop system has by default.

docs.title: Ghostfolio
docs.text:
Investments and net worth across every account, with performance and dividends.

Service ghostfolio in stacks/ghostfolio/compose.yaml (project homelab_ghostfolio) Image docker.io/ghostfolio/ghostfolio:latest Category Finance Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install ghostfolio Address https://invest.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:3333 (GHOSTFOLIO_PORT) Depends on ghostfolio-db, ghostfolio-redis Helpers ghostfolio-db docker.io/library/postgres:17, dumped daily by ./homelab backupghostfolio-redis docker.io/valkey/valkey:9-alpine Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first Also known as investments, portfolio, net-worth

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Investments and net worth across every brokerage, retirement, and savings account: holdings, performance over time, allocation, and dividends, without handing your account logins to a third party. Prices come from public market data.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. ./homelab install ghostfolio and open https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:3333 in Home mode, or https://invest.example.com with a domain.
  2. Get started creates the first account, which becomes the admin. Save the security token it shows in Vaultwarden (homelab - ghostfolio token): it is how you sign in.
  3. Add accounts, then import activities from each brokerage's CSV export (Portfolio › Activities › Import) or add them by hand.

GHOSTFOLIO_ACCESS_TOKEN_SALT and GHOSTFOLIO_JWT_SECRET_KEY in .env must never change: a new salt makes every security token stop working.

docs.title: Away from home
docs.text: In Home mode (the default), Ghostfolio is on the tailnet: it opens at home and away on every device signed in to Tailscale. With a domain, it is on the home network only: install Tailscale to reach it from anywhere.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• A TypeScript app: a NestJS API and an Angular web app, served together on port 3333.
  • Three containers: ghostfolio, ghostfolio-db (PostgreSQL 17, through the Prisma ORM), and ghostfolio-redis (Valkey, its cache). The helpers are only on the stack's own network; ghostfolio also joins the shared homelab network for the proxy.
  • You record activities (buys, sells, dividends, fees) per account. Ghostfolio fetches prices for each symbol from public data sources (Yahoo Finance by default, CoinGecko for crypto) on a schedule and works out values, performance, and allocation from them.
  • There is no user name or password: each user signs in with a security token. GHOSTFOLIO_ACCESS_TOKEN_SALT hashes those tokens and GHOSTFOLIO_JWT_SECRET_KEY signs sessions, which is why neither may change.
  • Nothing is kept in files; everything is in the database.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Database (accounts, activities, market data, users) Docker volume homelab_ghostfolio_ghostfolio-pgdata → /var/lib/postgresql/data in ghostfolio-db Cache ghostfolio-redis, in memory only (rebuilt on its own) Secrets GHOSTFOLIO_DB_PASSWORD, GHOSTFOLIO_ACCESS_TOKEN_SALT, GHOSTFOLIO_JWT_SECRET_KEY in .env

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Record: Portfolio › Activities › add one by hand, or import a CSV or JSON file; the same page exports everything.
  • See where you stand: Overview for the total and the chart, Holdings for each position, Summary for the figures.
  • Dig in: Portfolio › Analysis (performance and dividends by period), Allocations (by account, asset class, currency, region), and X-ray (rule checks for risks such as too much in one fund).
  • Plan: Portfolio › FIRE projects when your savings could cover your spending.
  • Hide the numbers: the eye icon switches to a view without amounts, useful when showing someone the screen.
  • Phone: it is a Progressive Web App: open https://invest.example.com and add it to the home screen.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Homelab Wizard's own Finances screen (in the sidebar, not an app) draws net worth month by month from balances typed in, a home's and a car's equity included; Ghostfolio follows each holding with market prices.
  • Vaultwarden holds each user's security token (homelab - ghostfolio token).
  • MoneyMatter tracks day-to-day spending and budgets; Ghostfolio tracks what you invest. Wallos covers subscriptions.
  • PostgreSQL and Redis and Valkey describe its helpers; ./homelab backup dumps the database daily (see Backups).
  • .env: GHOSTFOLIO_PORT (default 3333) and the three secrets above.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Benchmarks: as admin, add an index fund under Admin Control › Market Data and mark it as a benchmark, then compare against it in Analysis.
  • Cash and savings accounts: give each account its cash balance so net worth includes it, not only investments.
  • A read-only share: My Ghostfolio › Access › grant a public access, and the public portfolio page shows allocation without amounts.
  • Tags on activities to group them your own way (for example by goal).
  • Crypto prices with a CoinGecko demo key: add API_KEY_COINGECKO_DEMO to the ghostfolio service, then ./homelab compose ghostfolio up -d.
  • An AI assistant over your portfolio: Ghostfolio has an experimental MCP server (ENABLE_FEATURE_MCP=true, then an MCP access under My Ghostfolio › Access).

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
Follow the log, check the three containers, restart, open the database, check health, and get an API token from your security token:

./homelab logs ghostfolio -f
./homelab compose ghostfolio ps
./homelab compose ghostfolio restart ghostfolio
./homelab compose ghostfolio exec ghostfolio-db psql -U ghostfolio ghostfolio
curl -s http://localhost:3333/api/v1/health
curl -s -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"accessToken":"YOUR_SECURITY_TOKEN"}' http://localhost:3333/api/v1/auth/anonymous

docs.title: API
docs.text:
• Token: POST your security token to /api/v1/auth/anonymous (above); the authToken it returns goes in Authorization: Bearer <token>.
  • Base URL: http://localhost:3333/api/v1 on this Mac, or https://invest.example.com/api/v1.
  • Export everything: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN" http://localhost:3333/api/v1/export
  • Import: POST /api/v1/import with the same JSON format the export produces. The endpoints are listed in the README on GitHub.
  • Finances: put your security token in Settings › GHOSTFOLIO_SECURITY_TOKEN, and Finances › Update balances has From Ghostfolio while Ghostfolio runs. It signs in on this machine, reads what each account is worth (/api/v1/account), only reading, and fills the boxes of the accounts with the same name and currency.
  • Finances › Net worth › Investments: Read now signs in the same way and reads what each account holds (/api/v1/portfolio/holdings for each account, or /api/v1/portfolio/details on an older Ghostfolio): each fund and share, how many, what went in, and what it is worth. Each account is matched to the investment or retirement account in Finances with its name (one that does not match is picked by hand once), and what was read is kept with the plan, so the card shows with Ghostfolio stopped and on a phone. After the first read, Finances reads again once a day as it opens, unless that box is unticked. Ghostfolio looks prices up by ticker symbol itself; amounts and accounts never leave the homelab.
  • Adding from Finances: Add a holding on the Investments card looks a ticker or a name up (/api/v1/symbol/lookup), makes the Ghostfolio account of the Finances account's name when there is none (POST /api/v1/account, no platform, in the account's currency), and records the buy or sale (POST /api/v1/activities, or /api/v1/order before 2.249) at what was paid a share, with no fee; then it reads again. A new account is made in Finances and Ghostfolio by one name, so they always match. Only the ticker typed leaves the homelab, when Ghostfolio looks it up.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• ghostfol.io
  • GitHub: ghostfolio/ghostfolio (source of the ghostfolio/ghostfolio image, with the API in its README)

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: The nightly backup dumps Ghostfolio's database. The cache rebuilds on its own.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Prices are missing for a fund: set its data source to Yahoo Finance in the admin's Market Data, or add prices by hand.
  • Everyone is signed out and tokens fail: GHOSTFOLIO_ACCESS_TOKEN_SALT changed; restore .env from the Secrets backup.

docs.title: MoneyMatter
docs.text:
The household budget tracker: accounts, transactions, budgets, and reports, with exchange rates for foreign currencies.

Service moneymatter-frontend in stacks/budget-tracker/compose.yaml (project homelab_budget_tracker) Image letehaha/budget-tracker-fe:sha-f862f3d Category Finance Starts with ./homelab up Yes (./homelab up) Address https://money.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:13480 (MONEYMATTER_PORT) Depends on moneymatter-backend Helpers moneymatter-backend letehaha/budget-tracker-be:sha-f862f3d, volume moneymatter-attachments archived daily by ./homelab backupmoneymatter-db postgres:16, dumped daily by ./homelab backupmoneymatter-redis redis:7moneymatter-rates letehaha/currency-rates-api:latest Updates By hand. Pinned to the tested v0.30.2 build; read the release notes, then bump the frontend and backend tags together (its note) Also known as moneymatter, budget-tracker, money

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Track spending and budgets on our own hardware instead of a third-party service.

The stack mirrors MoneyMatter's own self-hosting compose file. Its images are Intel-only, so they run through Rosetta (or natively, built from source: see below), and they are pinned to one tested build.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Open the address in MONEYMATTER_URL: https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:13480 in Home mode, or https://money.example.com with a domain (sign-in does not work at localhost).
  2. Create your account. Demo mode is off.
  3. The first start is slow under Rosetta; the health checks allow 5 minutes.

Updating: read the release notes, change the two letehaha/budget-tracker-*:sha-... tags in stacks/budget-tracker/compose.yaml, run ./homelab backup --apply, then ./homelab compose money pull and ./homelab compose money up -d.

docs.title: Running natively on Apple Silicon (optional)
docs.text:
MoneyMatter only publishes Intel images, but its Dockerfiles build for any CPU (Node on Alpine for the backend, static files served by nginx for the frontend), and its own release workflow notes that adding linux/arm64 is all multi-arch images need. Built natively, the frontend and backend start in seconds instead of minutes and skip Rosetta. The exchange-rate service stays on Intel: its source is not public.

  1. Back up first: ./homelab backup --apply.
  2. Build both images from the same v0.30.2 commit the pinned images come from (a few minutes each; OrbStack includes docker buildx):
docker buildx build --platform linux/arm64 --load -t homelab/moneymatter-frontend:v0.30.2 -f self-hosting/frontend/Dockerfile "https://github.com/letehaha/budget-tracker.git#f862f3d3c5c008ce10bcf7e5af31429b35b486a7"
docker buildx build --platform linux/arm64 --load -t homelab/moneymatter-backend:v0.30.2 -f self-hosting/backend/Dockerfile "https://github.com/letehaha/budget-tracker.git#f862f3d3c5c008ce10bcf7e5af31429b35b486a7"
  1. In Settings (or .env): MONEYMATTER_FRONTEND_IMAGE=homelab/moneymatter-frontend:v0.30.2, MONEYMATTER_BACKEND_IMAGE=homelab/moneymatter-backend:v0.30.2, MONEYMATTER_PLATFORM=linux/arm64.
  2. ./homelab up: the frontend and backend are recreated from the new images. The database, attachments, and accounts are untouched, since it is the same version.

Check: docker image inspect homelab/moneymatter-backend:v0.30.2 --format '{{.Architecture}}' says arm64, and the app opens and signs in at MONEYMATTER_URL.

Updating a native build: build the new commit with a new tag (for example v0.31.0), change the two settings, and run ./homelab up. homelab update moneymatter cannot pull images built here. Going back: empty the three settings and run ./homelab up; the pinned Intel images return.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
This is what the stack file (stacks/budget-tracker/compose.yaml) sets up, mirroring MoneyMatter's own self-hosting/docker-compose.yml:

  • moneymatter-frontend: the web app, static files served by nginx on port 80. It skips the landing page (SKIP_LANDING) and passes API calls (/api/v1) to the backend at http://moneymatter-backend:8081. It waits until the backend reports healthy.
  • moneymatter-backend: the API, a Node app on port 8081 with a /health check. It runs in self-host mode with demo mode off (SYSTEM_DEMO_DISABLED), signs people in only at MONEYMATTER_URL (BETTER_AUTH_URL, AUTH_ORIGIN), and stores attachments in /app/packages/backend/data/attachments.
  • moneymatter-db: PostgreSQL 16 with the budget_tracker database and user.
  • moneymatter-redis: Redis 7 for cache and sessions.
  • moneymatter-rates: the exchange-rate service on port 8080. It keeps its rates in SQLite (currency_rates.db), with USD as the base, fills them on first start, and syncs four times a day (SYNC_CRON).
  • Only the frontend joins the shared homelab network for the proxy; the other four are on the stack's own network. All five are left out of the nightly updates.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Database Docker volume homelab_budget_tracker_moneymatter-db → /var/lib/postgresql/data in moneymatter-db Attachments Docker volume homelab_budget_tracker_moneymatter-attachments → /app/packages/backend/data/attachments in moneymatter-backend Exchange rates Docker volume homelab_budget_tracker_moneymatter-rates → /app/data/currency_rates.db in moneymatter-rates Cache and sessions Docker volume homelab_budget_tracker_moneymatter-redis → /data in moneymatter-redis Image tags and platform MONEYMATTER_FRONTEND_IMAGE, MONEYMATTER_BACKEND_IMAGE, MONEYMATTER_PLATFORM in .env (empty: the pinned Intel images)

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Open it at https://money.example.com (exactly MONEYMATTER_URL) and keep accounts, transactions, budgets, and reports there.
  • Accounts in other currencies are converted with the rates from moneymatter-rates, refreshed four times a day.
  • On a phone, open the same address and add it to the home screen.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Homelab Wizard's own Finances screen (in the sidebar, not an app) looks forward instead: each paycheck, the bills it covers, and what checking holds after, typed in by hand. MoneyMatter keeps what was spent; the two sit side by side.
  • Ghostfolio tracks investments and net worth; Wallos tracks subscriptions. MoneyMatter is the day-to-day budget. Savings counts it against YNAB.
  • PostgreSQL and Redis and Valkey list its database and cache; the nightly updates leave its pinned images alone.
  • Known Issues ISSUE-0009 covers the Rosetta images and the native build.
  • .env: MONEYMATTER_PORT (default 13480), MONEYMATTER_URL, MONEYMATTER_DB_PASSWORD, MONEYMATTER_JWT_SECRET, MONEYMATTER_SESSION_SECRET, MONEYMATTER_AUTH_SECRET, and the three image settings above.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Run the frontend and backend natively on Apple Silicon with the steps above, and compare start times.
  • Read the release notes on GitHub before each bump, and keep the frontend and backend on the same commit.
  • Watch it in Uptime Kuma with an HTTP monitor on https://money.example.com, so you hear when a slow Rosetta start does not finish.
  • Browse your own data with psql (below), using only SELECT, to see how accounts and transactions are stored.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
Check the five containers, follow the backend and exchange-rate logs, restart the backend, check both health endpoints from inside their containers, and open the database:

./homelab compose money ps
./homelab logs moneymatter-backend -f
./homelab logs moneymatter-rates -f
./homelab compose money restart moneymatter-backend
./homelab compose money exec moneymatter-backend wget -qO- http://localhost:8081/health
./homelab compose money exec moneymatter-rates wget -qO- http://localhost:8080/health
./homelab compose money exec moneymatter-db psql -U budget_tracker budget_tracker

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text: • GitHub: letehaha/budget-tracker (source, release notes, and the Dockerfiles the native build uses)

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: Data How Database Dumped daily by ./homelab backup, then the Homelab Databases job Attachments (moneymatter-attachments volume) Archived daily by ./homelab backup, then the Homelab Databases job Exchange rates, cache Not backed up (rebuilt automatically)

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Fix Sign-in loops or fails Open it at exactly MONEYMATTER_URL Frontend waits forever The backend is still starting (Rosetta). ./homelab compose money ps until it is healthy Exchange rates missing ./homelab logs moneymatter-rates; it syncs four times a day

docs.title: Wallos
docs.text:
Every subscription you still pay for, with renewal dates and the yearly total.

Service wallos in compose/finance.yaml (project homelab_finance) Image bellamy/wallos:latest Category Finance Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install wallos Address https://subscriptions.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:8282 (WALLOS_PORT) Data data/appdata/wallos/db → /var/www/html/dbdata/appdata/wallos/logos → /var/www/html/images/uploads/logos Database dump Daily by ./homelab backup into recovery-staging/databases/wallos Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first Also known as subscriptions

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Every subscription the household still pays for in one list: price, billing cycle, renewal date, payment method, and the monthly and yearly total, with a reminder before each renewal. It is the other half of Savings: what you cancelled, and what is left.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. ./homelab install wallos and open https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:8282 in Home mode, or https://subscriptions.example.com with a domain.
  2. Register the first account (it becomes the admin), then turn registrations off in Settings › Admin.
  3. Add subscriptions; Settings › Notifications › ntfy with https://ntfy.example.com, topic reminders, and the publish token (Settings › NTFY_PUBLISH_TOKEN › Copy) sends renewal reminders to the phone.

docs.title: Away from home
docs.text: In Home mode (the default), Wallos is on the tailnet: it opens at home and away on every device signed in to Tailscale. With a domain, it is on the home network only: install Tailscale to reach it from anywhere, or, to publish it through the tunnel, add public: true to its x-homelab block and run ./homelab domain setup again.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• A PHP app served by nginx and PHP-FPM in one container on port 80, with its data in one SQLite database, wallos.db.
  • Cron jobs inside the container do the background work each day: move renewal dates forward (1:00), refresh exchange rates (2:00), and send renewal reminders (9:00), in the container's time zone (TZ).
  • Logos you upload or pick from a web search are saved as files in the logos folder.
  • Prices in other currencies are converted with a free exchange-rate provider (Settings, Fixer API key or a provider that needs no key), so totals and statistics stay right.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Database data/appdata/wallos/db/wallos.db → /var/www/html/db/wallos.db Logos data/appdata/wallos/logos/ → /var/www/html/images/uploads/logos Cron logs /var/log/cron/ in the container (not kept across updates) Daily consistent copy recovery-staging/databases/wallos (by ./homelab backup)

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Add: + on the main page: name, price, currency, cycle, next payment, payment method, and who pays.
  • Cancelled something: edit it and Disable Subscription instead of deleting it; Statistics then show what the cancelled ones save each month and year.
  • See the year: Statistics for totals by category, member, and payment method; Calendar for what renews when, with Export iCalendar for your calendar app.
  • Set up once: Settings › Household (who pays), Categories, Payment methods, and the main currency.
  • Phone: add https://subscriptions.example.com to the home screen.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• ntfy: renewal reminders go to the reminders topic with NTFY_PUBLISH_TOKEN (Setup step 3).
  • Savings lists the services the homelab replaced; Wallos holds what you still pay.
  • MoneyMatter is the full budget; Changedetection.io can watch a service's pricing page for increases.
  • .env: WALLOS_PORT (default 8282) and TZ, which sets when reminders go out.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Monthly budget: Settings › Monthly Budget compares what you set against the monthly total.
  • Cancellation reminders: give a subscription a cancellation date to be reminded before a free trial turns paid.
  • Two-factor sign-in: Profile › Enable Two Factor Authentication.
  • AI recommendations: Settings › AI Recommendations suggests where to save. Pick Local Ollama with http://host.docker.internal:11434 (the Ollama that Open WebUI uses) so your list stays on this Mac.
  • Household split: set who pays each subscription, and Statistics shows each person's share.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
Follow the log, restart, look at the cron logs, and list subscriptions through the API with the key from your profile page:

./homelab logs wallos -f
./homelab compose wallos restart wallos
./homelab compose wallos exec wallos ls /var/log/cron
curl -s 'http://localhost:8282/api/subscriptions/get_subscriptions.php?api_key=YOUR_API_KEY&convert_currency=true'

docs.title: API
docs.text:
• Key: Profile › API Key (Regenerate makes a new one).
  • Base URL: http://localhost:8282/api/ on this Mac, or https://subscriptions.example.com/api/; the key goes in the api_key parameter.
  • Example: get_subscriptions.php (above) returns every subscription as JSON, with filters for member, category, payment method, and state.
  • Finances: put the key in Settings › WALLOS_API_KEY, and Finances › Recurring has From Wallos while Wallos runs. It reads the subscriptions on this machine (prices in Wallos's main currency), only reading, and lists those not in the plan yet to add.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• wallosapp.com
  • GitHub: ellite/Wallos (source of the bellamy/wallos image)

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: The nightly backup takes a consistent copy of the database (wallos.db); logos are covered by the AppData job.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: • Logos do not upload: data/appdata/wallos/logos must be writable by the container.

docs.title: Grocy
docs.text:
Groceries and household stock, chores, and shared to-dos.

Service grocy in compose/household.yaml (project homelab_household) Image lscr.io/linuxserver/grocy:latest Category Household Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install grocy Address https://grocy.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:9283 (GROCY_PORT) Data data/appdata/grocy → /config Database dump Daily by ./homelab backup into recovery-staging/databases/grocy Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: What is in the pantry and fridge, what to buy, who does which chore, and shared to-dos: the household's running list, with barcode scanning from the phone.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. ./homelab install grocy and open it.
  2. Sign in with admin / admin, then change the password under the user menu and create an account for each person.
  3. Optionally turn off the parts you do not use with the FEATURE_FLAG_* settings in data/appdata/grocy/data/config.php (see Tinkering ideas).

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• A PHP app. The LinuxServer.io image runs it with nginx and PHP-FPM; the app is in /app/www, and its data folder is a link to /config/data.
  • Everything is in one SQLite database, grocy.db. Settings that apply to the whole install (currency, language, which parts are on) are in config.php; per-user settings are in the web app.
  • Scanning an unknown barcode looks the product up on Open Food Facts (the default lookup plugin).
  • Product pictures and other uploads are files in the data folder.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Database data/appdata/grocy/data/grocy.db → /config/data/grocy.db Settings (currency, locale, feature flags) data/appdata/grocy/data/config.php → /config/data/config.php Pictures and uploads data/appdata/grocy/data/storage/ Barcode lookup plugins data/appdata/grocy/data/plugins/ Web server and PHP settings data/appdata/grocy/nginx/, data/appdata/grocy/php/

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Bought something: Purchase, scan or pick the product, and set the due date. Used it: Consume.
  • What is low or expiring: Stock overview, with colours for due soon, overdue, and below the minimum.
  • Shopping: Shopping list; products under their minimum stock can be added in one click.
  • Chores and tasks: Chores overview (who is next, when it is due) and Tasks for one-off jobs.
  • Phone: the browser's barcode camera works on https://grocy.example.com. There is also a community Android app (Grocy Android) that talks to the API.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Mealie is the better place for recipes and meal plans; use one of the two for the shopping list, not both.
  • Homebox tracks things you keep (tools, electronics); Grocy tracks things you use up.
  • Home Assistant can show stock and chores through a community integration (installed with HACS), using a Grocy API key.
  • Nginx Proxy Manager serves https://grocy.example.com; .env sets GROCY_PORT (default 9283), PUID, PGID, and TZ.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Turn off what you do not use: set FEATURE_FLAG_BATTERIES, FEATURE_FLAG_EQUIPMENT, or others to false in config.php and reload the page.
  • Your currency and language: CURRENCY and DEFAULT_LOCALE in config.php.
  • Batteries: track when smoke-alarm batteries were last changed and get them on the overview when due.
  • Locations: give each product a location (fridge, freezer, cellar) and freeze or thaw stock to change its due date.
  • Meal plan: plan recipes on the calendar and put the missing ingredients on the shopping list.
  • Calendar feed: the calendar page offers an iCal link with chores and due dates for your calendar app.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
Follow the log, restart, read the settings, and call the API with a key from the user menu › Manage API keys:

./homelab logs grocy -f
./homelab compose grocy restart grocy
./homelab compose grocy exec grocy grep FEATURE_FLAG /config/data/config.php
curl -s -H "GROCY-API-KEY: YOUR_KEY" http://localhost:9283/api/stock
curl -s -H "GROCY-API-KEY: YOUR_KEY" http://localhost:9283/api/system/info

docs.title: API
docs.text:
• Key: user menu (top right) › Manage API keys › Add.
  • Base URL: http://localhost:9283/api on this Mac, or https://grocy.example.com/api, with the key in the GROCY-API-KEY header.
  • Reference: opening https://grocy.example.com/api in the browser shows the interactive API documentation.

docs.title: Home Assistant
docs.text:
Smart-home hub for lights, locks, sensors, and automations.

Service home-assistant in compose/household.yaml (project homelab_household) Image ghcr.io/home-assistant/home-assistant:stable Category Household Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install home-assistant Address https://home.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:8123 (HOME_ASSISTANT_PORT) Data data/appdata/home-assistant → /config Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: The smart-home hub: lights, locks, thermostats, sensors, and the automations that tie them together, all running locally instead of in each vendor's cloud.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. ./homelab install home-assistant, open it, and create the owner account.
  2. The install writes a starter configuration.yaml (from config/home-assistant) that already trusts the proxy, so https://home.example.com works from the first start. On a configuration of your own it writes nothing new, but before each start it adds the two addresses below to a trusted_proxies list it finds there. If you have no such list, add this block yourself and restart it (./homelab restart home-assistant): 
    http:
  use_x_forwarded_for: true
  trusted_proxies:
    - 198.18.89.18
    - 198.18.89.19
    Those are the proxy's and Tailscale Serve's fixed addresses on the homelab-front network, the only one Home Assistant is on. Trust nothing wider: a device on the Wi-Fi reaching Home Assistant's own port could then say it was anyone, and get a fresh address for each password guess.
  3. Add integrations. In a container on macOS, Home Assistant cannot discover devices on its own (no mDNS, Bluetooth, or USB radios such as Zigbee sticks), so add network devices by their address. For discovery and radios, run Home Assistant OS in a VM instead and point the proxy at it.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• A Python app (Home Assistant Core) on port 8123. This is the Container install: there is no Supervisor, so no add-on store and no OS updates from inside the app. Extra services such as an MQTT broker or Zigbee2MQTT run as containers of their own.
  • Integrations connect devices and services. Each one adds entities (a light, a sensor, a switch) whose state changes are written to the recorder database, a SQLite file in /config.
  • Automations, scripts, and scenes react to those states. Ones you build in the web editor are saved to automations.yaml, scripts.yaml, and scenes.yaml; integrations and dashboards set up in the web app live in .storage.
  • configuration.yaml is the starting point. The starter one the homelab wrote (config/home-assistant) loads default_config and trusts only the proxy and Tailscale Serve to name a visitor.
  • It runs on the homelab's front network (homelab-front), not the host network, so it sees devices only by address. That is why discovery, Bluetooth, and USB radios do not work here.
  • Inside Docker it finds Frigate and its broker by name (they are on the front network too), but not the other apps. For another app, such as Mealie or Baikal, use its https address.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Main configuration data/appdata/home-assistant/configuration.yaml → /config/configuration.yaml Automations, scripts, scenes automations.yaml, scripts.yaml, scenes.yaml in the same folder Passwords referenced as !secret secrets.yaml Settings made in the web app .storage/ (do not edit while it runs) History database home-assistant_v2.db Log home-assistant.log Built-in backups backups/ Community integrations, blueprints custom_components/, blueprints/

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Add a device or service: Settings › Devices & services › Add integration, then search by brand. Here most need an IP address.
  • Automate: Settings › Automations & scenes › Create automation: a trigger (motion, time, sunset, someone arriving), optional conditions, and actions.
  • Dashboards: Overview › pencil to edit; Settings › Dashboards to make more.
  • Phone: the Home Assistant companion app (iOS and Android) with https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:8123 in Home mode, or https://home.example.com with a domain. It adds notifications, location for presence, and phone sensors (battery, Wi-Fi) as entities.
  • Check and reload YAML: Developer tools › YAML checks the configuration and reloads automations without a restart.
  • Keyboard: e searches entities, c opens the command palette, a opens Assist.
  • Backups: Settings › System › Backups makes a backup into backups/.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Nginx Proxy Manager serves https://home.example.com; that is why the trusted_proxies block must be there.
  • ntfy: send alerts to the phone through ntfy with a rest_command (or use the companion app's own notifications).
  • Mealie has a built-in integration (meal plan and shopping lists); Grocy has a community one.
  • Open WebUI uses Ollama on this Mac; Home Assistant's Ollama integration can use the same server for its voice assistant.
  • Jellyfin, AdGuard Home, and Uptime Kuma have integrations too, to show what is playing, DNS stats, or monitor states.
  • .env sets only HOME_ASSISTANT_PORT (default 8123) and TZ.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Presence: with the companion app on each phone, turn things off when the last person leaves (Settings › People sets who is tracked).
  • Blueprints: Settings › Automations & scenes › Blueprints › import a ready-made automation from the community forum.
  • Zigbee without USB: a network (Ethernet or Wi-Fi) Zigbee coordinator works with ZHA or Zigbee2MQTT by its address, sidestepping the USB limit on macOS.
  • Energy: Settings › Dashboards › Energy, with a smart plug or meter reading, tracks use over time.
  • HACS: the community store, copied into custom_components, adds integrations and cards that are not built in. Read what you install; it runs inside Home Assistant.
  • Keep the history smaller: a recorder: block with purge_keep_days: 10 in configuration.yaml.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
Follow the log, restart, check the configuration before a restart, and call the API with a long-lived token:

./homelab logs home-assistant -f
./homelab restart home-assistant
./homelab compose home-assistant exec home-assistant python -m homeassistant --script check_config --config /config
./homelab compose home-assistant exec home-assistant ls -la /config
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" http://localhost:8123/api/
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" http://localhost:8123/api/states

docs.title: API
docs.text:
• Token: your profile › Security › Long-lived access tokens › Create token.
  • Base URL: http://localhost:8123/api/ on this Mac, or https://home.example.com/api/, with Authorization: Bearer <token>. /api/ answers API running. when the token works.
  • Turn on a light: curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"entity_id":"light.kitchen"}' http://localhost:8123/api/services/light/turn_on
  • Reference: REST API; there is also a WebSocket API that the web app itself uses.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• Home Assistant documentation
  • Companion apps
  • GitHub: home-assistant/core (source of the ghcr.io/home-assistant/home-assistant image)

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: data/appdata/home-assistant (configuration, history database, and its own backups) is covered by the AppData job. Home Assistant's built-in backups land there too.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• 400 Bad Request through the proxy: the trusted_proxies block is missing (an existing configuration is never overwritten).
  • A device is not found: add it by IP address; automatic discovery does not work in this setup.

docs.title: Homebox
docs.text:
What you own, where it is, and its receipts, serial numbers, and warranties.

Service homebox in compose/household.yaml (project homelab_household) Image ghcr.io/sysadminsmedia/homebox:latest Category Household Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install homebox Address https://inventory.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:7745 (HOMEBOX_PORT) Data data/appdata/homebox → /data Database dump Daily by ./homelab backup into recovery-staging/databases/homebox Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first Also known as inventory

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: A home inventory: what you own, where it is, what it cost, its serial number, the receipt, the manual, and when the warranty ends. Useful for insurance, moving, and finding the spare charger. Labels with QR codes can be printed for boxes.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. ./homelab install homebox and open https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:7745 in Home mode, or https://inventory.example.com with a domain.
  2. Register an account, create a group for the household, and invite the others from Profile.
  3. Once everyone has an account, set HOMEBOX_ALLOW_REGISTRATION=false in Settings and run ./homelab install homebox again.

docs.title: Away from home
docs.text: In Home mode (the default), Homebox is on the tailnet: it opens at home and away on every device signed in to Tailscale. With a domain, it is on the home network only: install Tailscale to reach it from anywhere, or, to publish it through the tunnel, add public: true to its x-homelab block and run ./homelab domain setup again.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• A single Go program that serves the API and the web app on port 7745.
  • Everything is in a SQLite database, homebox.db, in /data, with photos, receipts, and manuals stored as files next to it.
  • Data belongs to a group (the household): everyone invited to the group sees the same items and locations.
  • Each item can get an asset ID, and the label generator prints QR codes that open the item's page when scanned.
  • HBOX_OPTIONS_ALLOW_REGISTRATION (fed by HOMEBOX_ALLOW_REGISTRATION in .env) decides whether the sign-up form is open.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Database data/appdata/homebox/homebox.db → /data/homebox.db Photos, receipts, manuals under data/appdata/homebox/ → /data Daily consistent copy recovery-staging/databases/homebox (by ./homelab backup)

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Add: the Create menu › Item / Asset: name, location, tags, then photos and attachments. Fill in purchase price, date, serial number, and warranty under the item's details.
  • Find: Search, or browse Locations (rooms, shelves, boxes can nest).
  • Scan: the Scanner reads a printed QR label or a product barcode with the phone's camera.
  • Maintenance: log what was done and when (filter changes, servicing), and schedule the next one.
  • Templates: save an item as a template for things you add often.
  • Phone: add https://inventory.example.com to the home screen.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Paperless-ngx keeps the official copy of receipts and warranties; attach a copy here too, or note the Paperless document number on the item.
  • Grocy is for things you use up; Homebox is for things you keep.
  • Pocket ID: Homebox supports OpenID Connect sign-in; see its documentation for the settings.
  • ntfy: Homebox notifiers take Shoutrrr URLs, which include ntfy, for its reminders.
  • .env: HOMEBOX_PORT (default 7745) and HOMEBOX_ALLOW_REGISTRATION.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Print labels ahead: Tools › Asset ID Labels › Label Generator makes a PDF of QR labels to stick on boxes before you fill them in.
  • Insurance list: Tools › Bill of Materials exports a CSV of items with prices.
  • Move in from a spreadsheet: Tools › Import / Export takes and gives CSV files.
  • A full export: Tools › Backups writes everything, attachments included, to a zip you can restore on another server.
  • Warranty dates on every new appliance, so you know what is still covered when something breaks.
  • API keys: Profile › API Keys makes a token for scripts (it expires after 30 days unless you set a date).

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
Follow the log, restart, look at the data folder, and check the version:

./homelab logs homebox -f
./homelab compose homebox restart homebox
./homelab compose homebox exec homebox ls -la /data
curl -s http://localhost:7745/api/v1/status

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• homebox.software (documentation)
  • GitHub: sysadminsmedia/homebox (source of the ghcr.io/sysadminsmedia/homebox image)

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: The nightly backup takes a consistent copy of the database (homebox.db); photos and receipts in data/appdata/homebox are covered by the AppData job.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: • Cannot sign up: registration is off (HOMEBOX_ALLOW_REGISTRATION); invite people from an existing account instead.

docs.title: Mealie
docs.text:
Recipes and meal planning. Import a recipe from any website by its URL, plan the week, and build the shopping list.

Service mealie in compose/household.yaml (project homelab_household) Image ghcr.io/mealie-recipes/mealie:latest Category Household Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install mealie Address https://mealie.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:9000 (MEALIE_PORT) Data data/appdata/mealie → /app/data Database dump Daily by ./homelab backup into recovery-staging/databases/mealie Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: One family cookbook, with meal plans and shopping lists everyone can open.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. ./homelab install mealie; with a domain, then ./homelab domain setup.
  2. Open https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:9000 in Home mode, or https://mealie.example.com with a domain, and sign in with the default admin, changeme@example.com / MyPassword. Change the email and password immediately.
  3. Invite the family from the admin settings; open sign-up is off (ALLOW_SIGNUP=false).

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• A Python (FastAPI) backend with a Vue (Nuxt) web app, both on port 9000 in one container.
  • Data is in a SQLite database, mealie.db, in /app/data; recipe images and assets are files in recipes/, one folder per recipe.
  • Importing from a URL reads the recipe data most recipe sites publish in the page (schema.org), so ingredients, steps, times, and the photo come across cleanly.
  • Users belong to a household within a group. Recipes are shared across the group; meal plans and shopping lists belong to the household.
  • BASE_URL (https://mealie.example.com) is used for links in invitations and shared recipes; ALLOW_SIGNUP=false keeps the sign-up form closed.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Database data/appdata/mealie/mealie.db → /app/data/mealie.db Recipe images and assets data/appdata/mealie/recipes/ → /app/data/recipes Mealie's own backups data/appdata/mealie/backups/ → /app/data/backups User avatars data/appdata/mealie/users/ Daily consistent copy recovery-staging/databases/mealie (by ./homelab backup)

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Add a recipe: + › Import from a URL, or create one by hand; bulk URL import takes a list of addresses.
  • Cook: open a recipe, scale the servings, and use cook mode, which keeps the screen on with large steps.
  • Plan: Meal Planner: put recipes on days, or let a random pick fill the week.
  • Shop: Shopping Lists: add a recipe's ingredients in one go, then tick items off in the shop.
  • Organise: tags, categories, and cookbooks (saved collections, for example "Weeknight dinners").
  • Phone: add https://mealie.example.com to the home screen; it is a Progressive Web App.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Home Assistant has a Mealie integration that shows today's meal plan and the shopping lists as to-do lists.
  • Grocy also keeps a shopping list and recipes; pick one place for each so they do not drift apart.
  • Pocket ID is its sign-in once ./homelab sso setup has run (OIDC_AUTH_ENABLED, OIDC_CONFIGURATION_URL, OIDC_CLIENT_ID, and related settings in data/sso/mealie.env).
  • Duplicati backs up data/appdata/mealie in the AppData job.
  • .env: MEALIE_PORT (default 9000), PUID, PGID, TZ; BASE_URL comes from HOMELAB_DOMAIN.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Ingredient parser: on a recipe, parse the ingredients into amount, unit, and food, so scaling and shopping lists combine them properly.
  • Recipe timeline: mark a recipe as made and add a photo and a note, so you remember what worked.
  • Import from other apps: the data migrations page takes exports from apps such as Paprika, Plan to Eat, Tandoor, and Nextcloud Cookbook.
  • Notifiers: Mealie can send events (a new recipe, tomorrow's meal plan) to an Apprise URL such as ntfys:// for ntfy, from the group or household settings.
  • Share one recipe with someone outside the household through a share link.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
Follow the log, restart, look at the data folder, check the version, and call the API with a token from your profile's API tokens page:

./homelab logs mealie -f
./homelab compose mealie restart mealie
./homelab compose mealie exec mealie ls -la /app/data
curl -s http://localhost:9000/api/app/about
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" http://localhost:9000/api/recipes

docs.title: API
docs.text:
• Token: your profile › API tokens › generate one.
  • Base URL: http://localhost:9000/api on this Mac, or https://mealie.example.com/api, with Authorization: Bearer <token>.
  • Import a recipe by URL: curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"url":"https://example.com/recipe"}' http://localhost:9000/api/recipes/create/url
  • Reference: the interactive API documentation at http://localhost:9000/docs.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• Mealie documentation
  • GitHub: mealie-recipes/mealie (source of the ghcr.io/mealie-recipes/mealie image)

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: data/appdata/mealie (database, images) is in the Homelab AppData job. Mealie can also make its own backups (Admin › Backups).

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: If recipe import fails, the site blocks scrapers; paste the recipe text instead.

docs.title: Tandoor
docs.text:
Recipes with meal planning, shopping lists, and nutrition.

Service tandoor in stacks/tandoor/compose.yaml (project homelab_tandoor) Image docker.io/vabene1111/recipes:latest Category Household Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install tandoor Address https://recipes.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:8093 (TANDOOR_PORT) Depends on tandoor-db Helpers tandoor-db docker.io/library/postgres:18, dumped daily by ./homelab backup Data tandoor-static (volume) → /opt/recipes/staticfilesappdata/tandoor/media → /opt/recipes/mediafiles Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first Also known as tandoor-recipes

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: The household's recipes in one place, with what Mealie leaves out: a meal plan by the week, a shopping list built from it and sorted by the shop's aisles, nutrition per serving from the ingredients, and recipes imported from almost any cooking site by its address. Pick one of Mealie and Tandoor for the household; Mealie is simpler, Tandoor does more.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. ./homelab install tandoor, then open it: https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:8093 in Home mode, https://recipes.example.com with a domain, or http://localhost:8093 on this computer.
  2. The first page makes the first account, which is the administrator; keep its password in Vaultwarden.
  3. Create the household's space (its shared cookbook) when asked, then invite the others from the space's settings (Members › Invite), each with their own account.
  4. Import a few recipes by their web address, or bring a whole collection over from Mealie, Paprika, Chowdown, or another app (Import › the app's export file).

docs.title: Away from home
docs.text: In Home mode (the default), Tandoor is on the tailnet: it opens at home and away on every device signed in to Tailscale. With a domain, it is on the home network only; install Tailscale to reach it from anywhere, or set public: true in its x-homelab block and run ./homelab domain setup again to publish it.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• One container runs Tandoor (Django) behind its own nginx on port 80; PostgreSQL keeps the recipes, plans, lists, and accounts.
  • Photos and files you upload are kept in appdata/tandoor/media; the web page's own files (tandoor-static) are rebuilt by every start.
  • Each space is a separate cookbook with its own members, so a second household or a club can share the same Tandoor without seeing each other's recipes.
  • Nutrition comes from the ingredients' foods (Tandoor's food database, or values you add), scaled to the recipe's servings.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Recipes, plans, lists, accounts PostgreSQL in the tandoor-pgdata volume Uploaded photos and files appdata/tandoor/media → /opt/recipes/mediafiles Daily database dump recovery-staging/databases/tandoor-db (by ./homelab backup)

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Plan: Meal Plan › drag recipes onto the week; Add to shopping list puts their ingredients on the list, merged and in aisle order.
  • Shop: the shopping list on a phone, ticked off as you go; it updates for everyone at once.
  • Cook: a recipe's page scales to the servings you need and keeps the screen on while you cook.
  • Collect: Import with a recipe's web address, or the browser bookmarklet from Settings.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Mealie, the simpler recipe app (pick one), and Grocy, for what is already in the cupboards.
  • Tandoor's AI features (importing a recipe from a photo, for one) can use the Ollama on this computer, so recipes stay here: in its AI settings, an Ollama provider at http://host.docker.internal:11434 (the model Open WebUI uses works).
  • .env: TANDOOR_PORT (default 8093), TANDOOR_URL, TANDOOR_SECRET_KEY and TANDOOR_DB_PASSWORD (generated), TANDOOR_DB_VERSION.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Supermarket categories (Settings › Shopping) in the order of your shop's aisles.
  • Recipe books for each person's favourites, shared with the space.
  • The API (below) to put the week's meals on Homepage or a wall screen.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
./homelab logs tandoor -f
./homelab compose tandoor restart tandoor
./homelab compose tandoor exec tandoor sh -c 'cd /opt/recipes && . venv/bin/activate && python manage.py changepassword <user>'

docs.title: API
docs.text: The whole app is an API under /api/ (its schema at /api/schema/, browsable at /docs/api/). Make a token under Settings › API and send it as Authorization: Bearer <token>; for example curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" http://localhost:8093/api/recipe/?query=soup.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• docs.tandoor.dev
  • GitHub: TandoorRecipes/recipes

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: The nightly backup dumps the database (tandoor-db); the uploaded photos and files in appdata/tandoor/media are covered by the Stack Data job. Tandoor's own Export saves recipes as files for another app.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• 400 Bad Request on every page: an old ALLOWED_HOSTS setting; the homelab sets *, so ./homelab update tandoor brings it back.
  • The page does not load at all, and its log says socket() [::]:80 failed (97: Address family not supported by protocol): IPv6 is turned off in this machine's kernel, and Tandoor's built-in nginx always listens on IPv6 too. Turn IPv6 back on (remove ipv6.disable=1 from the kernel's settings), as Linux does by default.
  • Forms fail with "CSRF verification failed": the address it is opened at differs from TANDOOR_URL; set it in Settings to that address and ./homelab update tandoor.
  • Forgot the password: the changepassword command above.

docs.title: Vikunja
docs.text:
To-do lists and projects, shared with the household.

Service vikunja in compose/household.yaml (project homelab_household) Image vikunja/vikunja:latest Category Household Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install vikunja Address https://todo.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:3456 (VIKUNJA_PORT) Data data/appdata/vikunja/db → /dbdata/appdata/vikunja/files → /app/vikunja/files Database dump Daily by ./homelab backup into recovery-staging/databases/vikunja Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Everyday to-dos and longer projects in one place: lists, due dates, reminders, labels, and list, kanban, table, and Gantt views. Lists can be shared with other people in the household. It replaces Todoist.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. ./homelab install vikunja and open it.
  2. Sign-ups are off, so create each person's account from Terminal (it asks for the password):
./homelab compose vikunja exec vikunja /app/vikunja/vikunja user create -u <name> -e <email>
  1. Sign in, then share a project with the others under its ... menu › Share.

On a phone, open https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:3456 in Home mode, or https://todo.example.com with a domain, and add it to the home screen. Apps that sync tasks over CalDAV (Tasks.org on Android, for example) can use https://todo.example.com/dav/ with a CalDAV token from Settings › CalDAV.

docs.title: Away from home
docs.text: In Home mode (the default), Vikunja is on the tailnet: it opens at home and away on every device signed in to Tailscale. With a domain, it is on the home network only: install Tailscale to reach it from anywhere, or, to publish it through the tunnel, add public: true to its x-homelab block and run ./homelab domain setup again.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• A single Go program (/app/vikunja/vikunja) that serves the API, the Vue web app, and CalDAV on port 3456.
  • Here it uses SQLite (VIKUNJA_DATABASE_TYPE, VIKUNJA_DATABASE_PATH=/db/vikunja.db); task attachments and project backgrounds are files in /app/vikunja/files.
  • All settings come from VIKUNJA_* variables in the compose file instead of a config.yml. VIKUNJA_SERVICE_SECRET signs sign-in tokens, VIKUNJA_SERVICE_PUBLICURL is the address used in links and CalDAV, and registration is off.
  • It runs as your user (user: PUID:PGID) rather than the image's uid 1000, so the data folders stay yours on this Mac. The same binary is the command-line tool and the health check.
  • Email (reminders by mail, password resets) needs a mail server in VIKUNJA_MAILER_*, which is not set up here; reminders show in the app.

docs.title: Where things live
