docs.text: What Where Database data/appdata/vikunja/db/vikunja.db → /db/vikunja.db Attachments and backgrounds data/appdata/vikunja/files/ → /app/vikunja/files Program and CLI /app/vikunja/vikunja in the container Daily consistent copy recovery-staging/databases/vikunja (by ./homelab backup)

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Add a task fast: type into the add box with Quick Add Magic: *label, +project, !3 for priority, @user, and dates such as tomorrow or next monday.
  • Views: each project has List, Gantt, Table, and Kanban; switch at the top of the project.
  • Today: the home page and the Upcoming view show what is due across all projects.
  • Keyboard: Cmd+K opens search and quick actions; on a task, t marks it done. The user menu › Keyboard Shortcuts lists the rest.
  • Share: a project's ... menu › Share, with a person, a team, or a link.
  • Phone and other apps: the web app on the home screen, or CalDAV (Settings › CalDAV) for apps such as Tasks.org.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Grocy also has chores and tasks; keep household chores there and projects here, or pick one.
  • Pocket ID: ./homelab sso setup makes it Vikunja's sign-in. It writes the provider as VIKUNJA_AUTH_OPENID_PROVIDERS_POCKETID_* settings in data/sso/vikunja.env; Pocket ID sends people back to /auth/openid/pocketid. Sign-ups stay off for passwords, while a passkey makes the account on first sign-in, and an account with the same email is linked.
  • Baikal is the calendar and contacts server; Vikunja serves its own CalDAV for tasks at https://todo.example.com/dav/.
  • .env: VIKUNJA_PORT (default 3456), VIKUNJA_SECRET, TZ, PUID, PGID.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Two-factor sign-in: Settings › Two Factor Authentication.
  • Webhooks: Settings › Webhooks (or a project's webhooks) calls a URL when tasks are created or done, for example a Home Assistant automation.
  • Saved filters: make a filter such as done = false && priority >= 3; it shows up as a project of its own.
  • Repeating tasks: set a task to repeat every week or month for bills and chores.
  • Import from Todoist, Trello, or Microsoft To Do: Settings › Import, after adding that service's VIKUNJA_MIGRATION_* settings to the service.
  • Project backgrounds from your own photos, to tell projects apart at a glance.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
Follow the log, restart, list accounts, check the setup, and reset a password (use the id from the list; it asks for the new password):

./homelab logs vikunja -f
./homelab compose vikunja restart vikunja
./homelab compose vikunja exec vikunja /app/vikunja/vikunja user list
./homelab compose vikunja exec vikunja /app/vikunja/vikunja doctor
./homelab compose vikunja exec vikunja /app/vikunja/vikunja user reset-password <id> --direct
curl -s http://localhost:3456/api/v1/info
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" http://localhost:3456/api/v1/projects

docs.title: API
docs.text:
• Token: Settings › API Tokens: choose what it may do and when it expires.
  • Base URL: http://localhost:3456/api/v1 on this Mac, or https://todo.example.com/api/v1, with Authorization: Bearer <token>. /api/v1/info needs no token.
  • Add a task to project 1: curl -s -X PUT -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"title":"Call the plumber"}' http://localhost:3456/api/v1/projects/1/tasks
  • Reference: https://todo.example.com/api/v1/docs on your own server.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• Vikunja documentation
  • GitHub: go-vikunja/vikunja (source of the vikunja/vikunja image)

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: The nightly backup takes a consistent copy of the database (data/appdata/vikunja/db/vikunja.db); attachments in data/appdata/vikunja/files are covered by the AppData job.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Signed out after every restart: VIKUNJA_SECRET is empty in .env. Run ./homelab install vikunja again to generate it.
  • "Permission denied" on start: the folders under data/appdata/vikunja must belong to your user (PUID/PGID in .env).

docs.title: Audiobookshelf
docs.text:
Audiobooks and podcasts, with progress synced between devices.

Service audiobookshelf in compose/media.yaml (project homelab_media) Image ghcr.io/advplyr/audiobookshelf:latest Category Media Starts with ./homelab up Yes (./homelab up) Address https://audiobooks.example.com (LAN and public, through the Cloudflare Tunnel) On this machine http://localhost:13378 (AUDIOBOOKSHELF_PORT) Data data/appdata/audiobookshelf/config → /configdata/appdata/audiobookshelf/metadata → /metadata/Volumes/Media/audiobooks → /audiobooks/Volumes/Media/podcasts → /podcasts Database dump Daily by ./homelab backup into recovery-staging/databases/audiobookshelf Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• The audiobook library from /Volumes/Media/audiobooks.
  • Podcast subscriptions, downloaded to /Volumes/Media/podcasts.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Open https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:13378 in Home mode, or https://audiobooks.example.com with a domain, and create the root user.
  2. Add libraries: Audiobooks → /audiobooks, Podcasts → /podcasts.
  3. Create a user per person.
  4. Phone app (Audiobookshelf for iOS/Android): server: the same address.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• A Node.js server with a Vue web app. The official iOS and Android apps use the same REST API, plus a live socket connection that keeps progress in sync.
  • Everything it knows (libraries, books, users, progress, bookmarks, podcast subscriptions) is in one SQLite database, /config/absdatabase.sqlite.
  • Covers, author photos, its own backups, logs, and caches go in /metadata.
  • Scans read folder names, audio tags, and sidecar files such as .opf; Match fills in the rest from online sources such as Audible, Google Books, or iTunes.
  • ffmpeg in the image streams formats a browser cannot play directly and powers the tools that merge files into one .m4b.
  • Podcasts: a scheduler checks each feed on its own schedule and downloads new episodes into /podcasts.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Audiobooks /Volumes/Media/audiobooks → /audiobooks Podcasts /Volumes/Media/podcasts → /podcasts Database data/appdata/audiobookshelf/config/absdatabase.sqlite → /config/absdatabase.sqlite Covers and author photos data/appdata/audiobookshelf/metadata/items and .../metadata/authors → /metadata/... Built-in backups /metadata/backups Logs /metadata/logs (one file per day, plus crash logs) Cache /metadata/cache

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Listen in the browser or the phone app; progress, bookmarks, and finished books sync between them. The phone app downloads books for offline listening.
  • Fix a book's details: open it › Edit (pencil) › Match, and pick the right result.
  • Podcasts: in the podcast library, search for a show or add its RSS feed, then turn on automatic downloads under the podcast's Edit › Schedule.
  • Settings › Users: which libraries each person sees, and whether they may download, edit, or delete.
  • Settings › Backups: when the built-in backups run and how many to keep; download one from there.
  • Your stats page shows listening time per day and per book.
  • Other apps that work with it: ShelfPlayer and Plappa on iOS.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Cloudflare Tunnel publishes it, so the phone app syncs from anywhere.
  • Pocket ID can be its sign-in through OpenID Connect (Settings › Authentication). Pocket ID is on the home network only, so keep password sign-in on for use away from home.
  • Duplicati copies data/appdata/audiobookshelf (AppData job); ./homelab backup dumps the database daily.
  • .env: AUDIOBOOKSHELF_PORT (default 13378), MEDIA_ROOT for the two media folders, TZ.
  • It gives out API keys (Settings › API Keys) for scripts and dashboards.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Merge a book that is many MP3 files into one chaptered .m4b: open the book › Edit › Tools › Make M4B (writes into the library folder).
  • Check chapters: the chapter editor (book › Edit › Chapters) can look up chapter times by ASIN.
  • Open an RSS feed for a book or podcast from its menu, to listen in any podcast app.
  • Collections and playlists: group a series or a reading list for the whole household.
  • Settings › Authentication: try OpenID Connect with Pocket ID for one-tap sign-in at home.
  • Settings › Notifications: send "new episode" alerts through an Apprise server.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
The last command needs an API key from Settings › API Keys in ABS_TOKEN first.

./homelab logs audiobookshelf -f
./homelab compose audiobookshelf restart audiobookshelf
./homelab compose audiobookshelf exec audiobookshelf ls -la /config /metadata/backups /metadata/logs
curl -s http://localhost:13378/ping
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ABS_TOKEN" http://localhost:13378/api/libraries

docs.title: API
docs.text:
• Key: Settings › API Keys › Add API Key (choose the user it acts as).
  • Base URL: http://localhost:13378/api, or https://audiobooks.example.com/api; send the key as Authorization: Bearer <key>.
  • Example: /api/libraries lists libraries; /api/libraries/<id>/items lists a library's books.
  • Docs: https://api.audiobookshelf.org

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• Documentation: https://www.audiobookshelf.org/docs
  • Source and image: https://github.com/advplyr/audiobookshelf

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: data/appdata/audiobookshelf (config: users, progress, settings; metadata: covers and cache) is in the Homelab AppData job. Audiobookshelf also makes its own daily backups (Settings › Backups) into its metadata folder.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: If new books do not appear, scan the library (Library › Scan) and check the folder layout: one folder per book, or Author/Book.

docs.title: Calibre-Web
docs.text:
A web front end for the Calibre e-book library: browse, read in the browser, and send books to e-readers.

Service calibre-web in compose/media.yaml (project homelab_media) Image lscr.io/linuxserver/calibre-web:latest Category Media Starts with ./homelab up Yes (./homelab up) Address https://books.example.com (LAN and public, through the Cloudflare Tunnel) On this machine http://localhost:8083 (CALIBRE_WEB_PORT) Data data/appdata/calibre-web → /config/Volumes/Media/Books → /books Database dump Daily by ./homelab backup into recovery-staging/databases/calibre-web Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: The household's e-books from the Calibre library in /Volumes/Media/Books, reachable from anywhere.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Open https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:8083 in Home mode, or https://books.example.com with a domain, and sign in with the default admin / admin123. Change the password immediately: this app is public.
  2. Database location: /books (the folder that contains metadata.db).
  3. Create a user per person. Turn on uploads only if needed.

Calibre (the desktop app) remains the tool that adds and edits books; Calibre-Web reads the same library.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• A Python (Flask) web app. It reads the Calibre library directly: book records from metadata.db and the files in /books/<Author>/<Title>/.
  • Its own users, settings, shelves, and read status live in a separate SQLite database, /config/app.db.
  • Edits and uploads made in Calibre-Web are written straight into metadata.db, which is why Calibre and Calibre-Web should not edit at the same time.
  • Converting between formats needs Calibre's ebook-convert, which this image does not include (the linuxserver add-on that provides it is x86-64 only, and this Mac is Apple Silicon).
  • The linuxserver image runs as PUID/PGID (your Mac user), so files it writes belong to you.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Calibre library /Volumes/Media/Books → /books Calibre's database /books/metadata.db Users, shelves, settings data/appdata/calibre-web/app.db → /config/app.db Log /config/calibre-web.log (also Admin › Logfile viewer)

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Browse and search by author, series, tag, or language, and read EPUB, PDF, and comic files in the built-in reader.
  • Shelves: make your own lists (private or shared) from a book's page.
  • Send to eReader: once mail is set up, the book page sends a file to the address in your profile.
  • OPDS catalog at https://books.example.com/opds, with your Calibre-Web login, for e-reader apps such as KOReader, Moon+ Reader, and Librera.
  • Admin › Add New User, and per-user rights such as download, upload, and edit.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Calibre, the desktop app on this Mac, edits the same library.
  • LazyLibrarian adds books to /Volumes/Media/Books; with its calibredb import on, they land in metadata.db and show up here.
  • Kavita and Komga can read the same Books folder, read-only.
  • Duplicati: the Calibre job copies the library, the AppData job copies app.db.
  • Cloudflare Tunnel publishes it.
  • .env: CALIBRE_WEB_PORT (default 8083), MEDIA_ROOT, PUID, PGID, TZ.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Kobo sync: Admin › Edit Basic Configuration › Feature Configuration › Enable Kobo sync; each user then finds a Kobo sync URL in their profile to put on the Kobo.
  • Send to Kindle: add an SMTP account under Admin › Edit Email Server Settings, put the Kindle address in your profile, and add the sender to Amazon's approved list.
  • Magic-link sign-in for e-reader browsers: Feature Configuration › Enable Remote Login.
  • Admin › Edit UI Configuration: the dark caliBlur theme, books per page, and which sidebar sections show.
  • Limit what a person sees by tag or custom column in their user settings, for example a children's account.
  • Allow uploads: Feature Configuration › Enable Uploads, then give the person the upload right.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
./homelab logs calibre-web -f
./homelab compose calibre-web restart calibre-web
./homelab compose calibre-web exec calibre-web ls -la /books/metadata.db /config/app.db
./homelab compose calibre-web exec calibre-web tail -n 50 /config/calibre-web.log
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://localhost:8083/login
curl -s -u USER:PASSWORD http://localhost:8083/opds | head -20

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• Source and wiki: https://github.com/janeczku/calibre-web
  • Image: https://github.com/linuxserver/docker-calibre-web
  • Calibre: https://calibre-ebook.com

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: data/appdata/calibre-web (users and settings) is in the Homelab AppData job. The library itself (Books, including metadata.db) is in the Homelab Calibre job.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Fix "DB location is not valid" The drive is not mounted, or metadata.db is not directly in Books Changes in Calibre not shown Restart Calibre-Web, or avoid editing in both at once

docs.title: Feishin
docs.text:
A modern web player for Navidrome. It runs entirely in the browser and talks to Navidrome directly.

Service feishin in compose/media.yaml (project homelab_media) Image ghcr.io/jeffvli/feishin:latest Category Media Starts with ./homelab up Yes (./homelab up) Address https://music.example.com (LAN and public, through the Cloudflare Tunnel) On this machine http://localhost:9180 (FEISHIN_PORT) Depends on navidrome Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: A desktop-class music player in any browser, at https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:9180 in Home mode, or https://music.example.com with a domain.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text: Open it and sign in with your Navidrome account. The server is preset to Navidrome's address, NAVIDROME_URL: its tailnet address in Home mode, or https://navidrome.<domain> with a domain.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Feishin is a React music player. This container only serves its web build on port 9180; it keeps no data on the server.
  • Your browser talks to Navidrome directly at its address (SERVER_URL, from NAVIDROME_URL), so Navidrome has to be reachable from wherever you play.
  • Settings, the play queue, and the sign-in are stored in the browser's local storage, separately in each browser.
  • SERVER_LOCK: "false" lets you add other servers in the app; Feishin also works with Jellyfin and other OpenSubsonic servers.

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Sign in once per browser, then browse by album, artist, genre, or playlist, and add songs or whole albums to the queue.
  • Settings holds playback, theme, and hotkey options; the hotkeys are listed and can be changed there.
  • The desktop app for macOS, Windows, and Linux (from the GitHub releases page) adds media keys and the MPV audio engine.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Navidrome holds the library, the accounts, playlists, and play counts; Feishin is only the front end.
  • .env: FEISHIN_PORT (default 9180) is its port on this Mac; HOMELAB_DOMAIN builds the preset server address.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Install the desktop app and point it at https://navidrome.example.com; for gapless playback, switch its audio player to MPV in Settings (install MPV with brew install mpv).
  • Build a smart playlist in Feishin's playlist editor; it is saved in Navidrome and works in every app.
  • Add .lrc lyric files beside your tracks in the music folder; Feishin shows them in the full-screen player.
  • Try the full-screen "now playing" view on a spare tablet as a living-room display.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
./homelab logs feishin -f
./homelab compose feishin restart feishin
curl -sI http://localhost:9180
curl -s https://navidrome.example.com/ping

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text: • Source, releases, and image: https://github.com/jeffvli/feishin

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: Nothing: settings live in the browser.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: If sign-in fails, open https://navidrome.example.com directly to check Navidrome is up and the password is right.

docs.title: Jellyfin in a container
docs.text:
Movies and TV for the household, the same Jellyfin in a container. It is the Jellyfin for SteamOS: SteamOS's system is read-only and takes no packages, so the native app has no install there, and on SteamOS homelab install jellyfin and the Movies and TV pick install this one. On a Mac, Windows, or another Linux it is an alternative to the native app, which can use the graphics for transcoding.

Service jellyfin-container in compose/media.yaml (project homelab_media) Image jellyfin/jellyfin:latest Category Media Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install jellyfin-container Address https://jellyfin.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:8096 (JELLYFIN_PORT) Data ~/.local/share/jellyfin → /config~/.local/share/jellyfin/cache → /cache/Volumes/Media/movies, read-only → /media/movies/Volumes/Media/tv, read-only → /media/tv Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• The family's video library from the media drive's movies and tv folders.
  • On SteamOS, Jellyfin without installing anything on the system.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. ./homelab install jellyfin on SteamOS (./homelab install jellyfin-container elsewhere), or the Movies and TV pick.
  2. Finish the wizard at http://localhost:8096; create the admin, then a user per person.
  3. Libraries: Movies → /media/movies, Shows → /media/tv (the media drive's folders, read-only inside the container).
  4. In Home mode it is at https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:8096 on the tailnet with nothing more to do. With a domain, ./homelab domain setup creates https://jellyfin.example.com.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• The official image, run as you (PUID/PGID; with Docker run as you on SteamOS, root inside the container is you outside it).
  • Its library (users, watch history, metadata, plugins, settings, logs) is in JELLYFIN_DATA_DIR, the same folder and the same layout as the native app's, so a library moves between the two by keeping that folder. The cache is cache/ inside it.
  • Transcoding is on the processor. Direct play costs almost nothing.
  • Updates come with the nightly updates, like the other containers.

docs.title: Graphics for transcoding (by hand)
docs.text: The Steam Machine's and the Steam Deck's AMD graphics can transcode through VA-API. The container does not get them by default, because a machine without /dev/dri would not start it. To add them, add devices: ["/dev/dri:/dev/dri"] to jellyfin-container in compose/media.yaml, then ./homelab install jellyfin-container again, and in Dashboard › Playback › Transcoding choose Video Acceleration API (VA-API) with /dev/dri/renderD128. If the device is refused, your account must be able to open /dev/dri/renderD128 (ls -l /dev/dri).

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Radarr and Sonarr put films and episodes in movies and tv.
  • Seerr signs in with a Jellyfin admin at jellyfin-container:8096.
  • Nginx Proxy Manager serves https://jellyfin.example.com on the home network; Tailscale reaches it from elsewhere.
  • Duplicati reads JELLYFIN_DATA_DIR as /source/jellyfin (Homelab Jellyfin job).

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
./homelab status
./homelab logs jellyfin-container
curl -s http://localhost:8096/health
./homelab compose jellyfin-container restart jellyfin-container

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: The data folder (JELLYFIN_DATA_DIR) is in the Homelab Jellyfin job, each week; the cache, transcodes, and logs are left out. Stop the container before restoring it. The media itself is not backed up.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Fix Library empty The media drive mounted after the container started. ./homelab compose jellyfin-container restart jellyfin-container, then scan the libraries "cannot run alongside jellyfin" The native Jellyfin is installed and running; keep one of the two Playback stutters A stream is transcoding on the processor (Dashboard › Activity); add the graphics as above, or play on a device that plays the file as it is

docs.title: Jellyfin
docs.text:
Movies and TV for the household, streamed to TVs, phones, and browsers. It runs as the native macOS app, not a container, so it can use Apple Silicon's hardware video encoder.

Runs as A native app, not a container Install brew install --cask jellyfin Category Media Starts with ./homelab up No: a native app (brew install --cask jellyfin) Address https://jellyfin.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:8096

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• The family's video library from /Volumes/Media/movies and /Volumes/Media/tv.
  • Hardware transcoding (VideoToolbox), which containers on macOS cannot do.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. brew install --cask jellyfin, open it, and add it to Login Items.
  2. Finish the wizard at http://localhost:8096; create the admin, then a user per person.
  3. Libraries: Movies → /Volumes/Media/movies, Shows → /Volumes/Media/tv.
  4. Dashboard › Playback › Transcoding: hardware acceleration Apple VideoToolbox.
  5. In Home mode it is at https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:8096 on the tailnet with nothing more to do. With a domain, ./homelab domain setup creates https://jellyfin.example.com (the proxy reaches it at host.docker.internal:8096).
  6. Set JELLYFIN_DATA_DIR in .env to the data folder shown under Dashboard › Paths, so Duplicati backs it up.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• A .NET (C#) server with its own web app, installed by Homebrew as Jellyfin.app and started at login. It runs outside Docker, so the homelab CLI does not start, stop, or update it, and ./homelab logs and ./homelab compose do not apply.
  • When a device cannot play a file as it is, Jellyfin's bundled ffmpeg converts it on the fly using Apple VideoToolbox. Direct play costs almost nothing.
  • Users, libraries, and watch history are in SQLite (data/jellyfin.db in its data folder); posters and other artwork go in metadata/.
  • Film and show details come from online providers such as TMDb; more providers come as plugins.
  • Scheduled tasks (Dashboard › Scheduled Tasks) scan the libraries, extract chapter and trickplay images, and clean the transcode cache.
  • Containers reach it at host.docker.internal:8096: Nginx Proxy Manager, Seerr, Uptime Kuma, and Tailscale. The address and port come from the x-homelab-native block in compose.yaml.
  • Updates come from Homebrew, not the nightly updates.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text:
These paths are inside the data folder (JELLYFIN_DATA_DIR in .env, default ~/.local/share/jellyfin); Dashboard › Paths shows the real ones.

What Where Movies /Volumes/Media/movies Shows /Volumes/Media/tv Data folder JELLYFIN_DATA_DIR (listed in Dashboard › Paths) Database data/jellyfin.db Artwork and metadata metadata/ Plugins plugins/ Logs log/, one log_<yyyymmdd>.log per day (also Dashboard › Logs) Server settings config/ (system.xml, network.xml, encoding.xml) Cache and transcodes cache/ (Cache and Transcodes in Dashboard › Paths) The app /Applications/Jellyfin.app

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Watch in the browser at https://jellyfin.example.com, or in an app: Jellyfin for iOS and Swiftfin (iPhone, iPad, Apple TV), Jellyfin for Android and Android TV, Jellyfin Media Player (Mac and PC), or Infuse (Apple TV).
  • Quick Connect: sign in on a TV by typing its code on your phone, from your user menu › Quick Connect (turn it on in the Dashboard's general settings).
  • Dashboard › Users: library access, parental ratings, and whether a person may transcode. With an API key in JELLYFIN_API_KEY (Dashboard › API Keys), Settings › People makes each person's account here too, resets its password, and turns it off when they are removed.
  • Infuse: Add Files › Add Share › Jellyfin, with the Jellyfin address's host, port 443 and HTTPS on with a domain (the tailnet name, port 8096 and HTTPS on in Home mode, or localhost, 8096, HTTPS off on this Mac), and the person's Jellyfin username and password.
  • Dashboard › Libraries: scan a library or change its options; Dashboard › Activity shows who is watching and whether a stream is transcoding.
  • In the web player: Space pauses, F toggles full screen, M mutes, and the arrow keys seek and change the volume.
  • SyncPlay (the group icon at the top of the page) keeps playback in step for people watching together in different places.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Radarr and Sonarr put films and episodes in movies and tv; Bazarr adds subtitles beside them.
  • Seerr signs in with a Jellyfin admin at host.docker.internal:8096 and imports the household's users.
  • Nginx Proxy Manager serves https://jellyfin.example.com on the home network; Tailscale reaches it from elsewhere.
  • Uptime Kuma watches http://host.docker.internal:8096/health.
  • Duplicati reads JELLYFIN_DATA_DIR as /source/jellyfin (Homelab Jellyfin job).
  • It gives out API keys (Dashboard › API Keys) for apps such as Sonarr and Radarr.
  • .env: only JELLYFIN_DATA_DIR; port 8096 is fixed in compose.yaml.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Refresh Jellyfin when a download lands: in Sonarr and Radarr, Settings › Connect › Emby / Jellyfin, host host.docker.internal, port 8096, with a Jellyfin API key.
  • Trickplay previews on the seek bar: turn on trickplay image extraction in a library's settings; the work runs as a scheduled task.
  • Dashboard › Playback › Transcoding: try tone mapping for HDR films on SDR screens, and allow HEVC encoding.
  • Dashboard › Plugins: Playback Reporting for viewing statistics, OpenSubtitles for subtitles; more plugins come from third-party repositories, such as Intro Skipper.
  • Single sign-on with Pocket ID through the third-party SSO plugin (home network only, like Pocket ID).
  • Add a Home Videos and Photos library for family clips from the media drive.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
Jellyfin is a Mac app, so these run on this Mac directly, without ./homelab logs or compose exec. They use the default data folder; change ~/.local/share/jellyfin if JELLYFIN_DATA_DIR differs. The last command checks that the proxy container can reach it.

./homelab status
open -a Jellyfin
osascript -e 'quit app "Jellyfin"'
lsof -nP -iTCP:8096 -sTCP:LISTEN
curl -s http://localhost:8096/health
curl -s http://localhost:8096/System/Info/Public
ls ~/.local/share/jellyfin/log
tail -f ~/.local/share/jellyfin/log/log_$(date +%Y%m%d).log
brew upgrade --cask jellyfin
./homelab compose nginx-proxy-manager exec nginx-proxy-manager curl -s http://host.docker.internal:8096/health

docs.title: API
docs.text:
• Key: Dashboard › API Keys › add one, named after the app or script that uses it.
  • Base URL: http://localhost:8096; send the key as Authorization: MediaBrowser Token="<key>".
  • Example: curl -s -H 'Authorization: MediaBrowser Token="KEY"' http://localhost:8096/Library/VirtualFolders lists the libraries; curl -X POST with the same header to http://localhost:8096/Library/Refresh scans them all.
  • Docs: https://api.jellyfin.org

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• Documentation: https://jellyfin.org/docs/
  • Source: https://github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin
  • Homebrew cask: https://formulae.brew.sh/cask/jellyfin

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: The data folder (JELLYFIN_DATA_DIR: users, watch history, metadata) is in the Homelab Jellyfin job. Quit Jellyfin before restoring it. The media itself is not backed up.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Fix Proxy gives 502 Jellyfin is not running on the Mac. Open it Library empty after a restart The drive mounted after Jellyfin started. Scan the libraries again Lost the administrator's password On this Mac, open http://localhost:8096 › Forgot Password, give the username: Jellyfin writes a PIN to passwordreset*.json in its data folder (cat ~/.local/share/jellyfin/passwordreset*.json). Enter the PIN, sign in with an empty password (some versions take the PIN as the password), and set a new one under Profile › Password. Someone else's: Settings › People › New music and films password Playback stutters Check that VideoToolbox is selected; Dashboard › Activity shows whether a stream is transcoding

docs.title: Kavita
docs.text:
A reader for books, comics, and manga in one place. An optional alternative to Komga and Calibre-Web.

Service kavita in compose/media.yaml (project homelab_media) Image jvmilazz0/kavita:latest Category Media Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install kavita Address https://kavita.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:5500 (KAVITA_PORT) Data data/appdata/kavita → /kavita/config/Volumes/Media/Books, read-only → /books/Volumes/Media/comics, read-only → /comics Database dump Daily by ./homelab backup into recovery-staging/databases/kavita Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: One reading app for both Books and comics, read-only.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. ./homelab install kavita; with a domain, then ./homelab domain setup.
  2. Open https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:5500 in Home mode, or https://kavita.example.com with a domain, and create the administrator.
  3. Add libraries for /books and /comics.

It listens on 5500 on the Mac because macOS's AirPlay Receiver holds port 5000.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• A .NET (C#) server with an Angular web app, and readers for images (comics and manga), EPUB, and PDF.
  • Libraries, users, progress, and reading lists are in SQLite, /kavita/config/kavita.db; appsettings.json beside it holds the port and the key that signs logins.
  • Scans expect Library/Series/files, read ComicInfo.xml and EPUB metadata, and store cover images in /kavita/config/covers.
  • Background tasks (scans, its own database backups, cleanup) run on schedules set in the server settings.
  • Inside the container it listens on 5000; this Mac maps it to 5500 (KAVITA_PORT).

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Books (read-only) /Volumes/Media/Books → /books Comics (read-only) /Volumes/Media/comics → /comics Database data/appdata/kavita/kavita.db → /kavita/config/kavita.db Server settings file /kavita/config/appsettings.json Covers /kavita/config/covers Built-in backups /kavita/config/backups Logs /kavita/config/logs/kavita.log

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• The home page shows On Deck, recently added series, and your Want to Read list.
  • Collections and reading lists group series and put issues in order; smart filters save a search for reuse.
  • Admins open the server settings from the user menu: libraries, users, tasks (scan now, backups, schedules), and email.
  • Your account settings show your personal API key and OPDS URL, for apps such as Panels, Paperback, KOReader, and Chunky.
  • On Android, Mihon has a Kavita extension that uses the same API key.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Komga and Calibre-Web use the same Books and comics folders; Kavita only reads them.
  • Nginx Proxy Manager serves https://kavita.example.com on the home network; Tailscale reaches it from elsewhere.
  • .env: KAVITA_PORT (default 5500), MEDIA_ROOT, TZ.
  • It gives out a per-user API key, used by OPDS and the Mihon extension.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Send to e-reader: set up email in the server settings, then add your Kindle or Kobo address as a device in your account settings.
  • Import a ComicRack .cbl reading list from the reading lists page.
  • Turn on folder watching in a library's settings so new files appear without a manual scan.
  • Pin your favourite smart filters to the home page and sidebar in your account settings.
  • Try the EPUB reader's layout and font options, and a different theme in your account settings.
  • Kavita+ (a paid subscription) adds online metadata and scrobbling to AniList; everything else works without it.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
./homelab logs kavita -f
./homelab compose kavita restart kavita
./homelab compose kavita exec kavita tail -n 50 /kavita/config/logs/kavita.log
./homelab compose kavita exec kavita ls -la /kavita/config/backups
curl -s http://localhost:5500/api/health

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• Documentation: https://wiki.kavitareader.com
  • Source: https://github.com/Kareadita/Kavita
  • Image: https://hub.docker.com/r/jvmilazz0/kavita

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: data/appdata/kavita (database, users, progress) is in the Homelab AppData job.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: If a library scan finds nothing, check the folder layout Kavita expects (one folder per series).

docs.title: Komga
docs.text:
A reader for comics and manga, in the browser or through compatible apps.

Service komga in compose/media.yaml (project homelab_media) Image gotson/komga:latest Category Media Starts with ./homelab up Yes (./homelab up) Address https://comics.example.com (LAN and public, through the Cloudflare Tunnel) On this machine http://localhost:25600 (KOMGA_PORT) Data data/appdata/komga → /config/Volumes/Media/Books, read-only → /books/Volumes/Media/comics, read-only → /comics Database dump Daily by ./homelab backup into recovery-staging/databases/komga Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: The comics library from /Volumes/Media/comics (CBZ, CBR, PDF, EPUB), read-only.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Open https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:25600 in Home mode, or https://comics.example.com with a domain, and create the administrator.
  2. Add a library pointing at /comics (and one at /books for books from the media drive's Books folder).
  3. Create a user per person, with access to the libraries they should see.
  4. Apps such as Panels or Paperback connect with the same address and login (OPDS is at /opds/v1.2/catalog).

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• A Kotlin and Spring Boot server on the Java runtime, with a Vue web app and a built-in reader.
  • Its library, users, and read progress are in SQLite, /config/database.sqlite; background jobs are queued in /config/tasks.sqlite, and search uses a Lucene index in /config/lucene.
  • Scans walk each library folder (one folder per series), read ComicInfo.xml inside CBZ files and the metadata of EPUBs, and make thumbnails.
  • Both media folders are mounted read-only, so Komga never changes or deletes your files.
  • Apps connect through its REST API (/api/v1) or the OPDS feeds; extra settings, such as OAuth2 sign-in, go in an optional /config/application.yml.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Comics (read-only) /Volumes/Media/comics → /comics Books (read-only) /Volumes/Media/Books → /books Database data/appdata/komga/database.sqlite → /config/database.sqlite Task queue /config/tasks.sqlite Search index /config/lucene (rebuilt if deleted) Log /config/logs/komga.log Optional settings file /config/application.yml

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• The home page shows Keep Reading, On Deck (the next issue of series you follow), and recent additions.
  • Read in the browser: paged, double-page, or continuous vertical (webtoon) mode, chosen in the reader's settings.
  • Collections group series; read lists put issues from several series in reading order.
  • A library's menu (the three dots beside its name) scans it or edits its options.
  • Server settings › Users: which libraries each person can see, and content restrictions by age rating or label.
  • Apps: Panels and Paperback (iOS), Mihon with the Komga extension (Android), or any OPDS reader such as KOReader.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Kavita reads the same comics and Books folders; you can run either or both.
  • Calibre-Web manages Books; Komga only reads it.
  • Cloudflare Tunnel publishes it, so reading apps work away from home.
  • .env: KOMGA_PORT (default 25600), MEDIA_ROOT, TZ.
  • It gives out per-user API keys (sent as the X-API-Key header) for apps and scripts.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Import a ComicRack .cbl reading list from the Import page to get a crossover event in reading order.
  • In a library's options, choose which metadata sources it trusts (ComicInfo, EPUB, local artwork) and whether it scans on startup and on a schedule.
  • Try Komf, a separate tool that fetches series metadata from online databases into Komga: https://github.com/Snd-R/komf
  • Use the webtoon mode for vertical-scroll comics on a phone.
  • Sign in with Pocket ID through OAuth2 settings in /config/application.yml (see Komga's docs on OAuth2).
  • Add the OPDS feed https://comics.example.com/opds/v1.2/catalog to KOReader on an e-ink reader.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
Replace EMAIL and PASSWORD with your Komga login; the health check needs none.

./homelab logs komga -f
./homelab compose komga restart komga
./homelab compose komga exec komga tail -n 50 /config/logs/komga.log
curl -s http://localhost:25600/actuator/health
curl -s -u EMAIL:PASSWORD http://localhost:25600/api/v1/libraries
curl -s -u EMAIL:PASSWORD "http://localhost:25600/api/v1/series?size=5"

docs.title: API
docs.text:
• Auth: your email and password (HTTP basic), or an API key sent as X-API-Key: <key>; create keys in your account settings.
  • Base URL: http://localhost:25600/api/v1/, or https://comics.example.com/api/v1/.
  • Example: curl -X POST -u EMAIL:PASSWORD http://localhost:25600/api/v1/libraries/<id>/scan scans one library.
  • Docs: the interactive API reference at http://localhost:25600/swagger-ui.html.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• Documentation: https://komga.org
  • Source: https://github.com/gotson/komga
  • Image: https://hub.docker.com/r/gotson/komga

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: data/appdata/komga (database, users, read progress) is in the Homelab AppData job. The comics themselves are not backed up.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: If a series is missing, scan the library and check that each series has its own folder.

docs.title: Navidrome
docs.text:
The music server. It indexes the music folder and streams it to Feishin and to any Subsonic-compatible app.

Service navidrome in compose/media.yaml (project homelab_media) Image deluan/navidrome:latest Category Media Starts with ./homelab up Yes (./homelab up) Address https://navidrome.example.com (LAN and public, through the Cloudflare Tunnel) On this machine http://localhost:4533 (NAVIDROME_PORT) Data data/appdata/navidrome → /data/Volumes/Media/music, read-only → ${NAVIDROME_MUSIC_PATH:-${MEDIA_ROOT:-/Volumes/Media}/music} Database dump Daily by ./homelab backup into recovery-staging/databases/navidrome Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• The household's music library, streamed anywhere.
  • Playlists from .m3u files in the library are imported automatically. The library is mounted at the same path as on the Mac, so absolute paths in playlists work.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Open https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:4533 in Home mode, or https://navidrome.example.com with a domain; the first account becomes the administrator.
  2. Create a user per person.
  3. Phone apps (for example Amperfy, play:Sub, Substreamer): server: the same address, with the user's login.

The library is rescanned every hour; Settings › Scan library forces one now.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Navidrome is a single Go program that serves its own web player and the Subsonic API (/rest/..., with the OpenSubsonic extensions), which almost every third-party music app speaks.
  • It reads the tags of your files and keeps what it learns in one SQLite database, navidrome.db, along with users, play counts, ratings, and playlists. The music folder is mounted read-only, so it never changes your files.
  • A scan runs every hour (ND_SCANSCHEDULE: 1h). .m3u playlists in the library are imported during scans (ND_AUTOIMPORTPLAYLISTS).
  • When a player asks for a lower bitrate or another format, ffmpeg in the image transcodes on the fly. Transcoded files and artwork are cached under /data/cache.
  • Its settings are ND_* environment variables in compose/media.yaml. Feishin and phone apps reach it over HTTPS at its public address.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Music (read-only) /Volumes/Media/music, at the same path inside the container (ND_MUSICFOLDER) App data data/appdata/navidrome → /data Database /data/navidrome.db Transcoding and artwork cache /data/cache (safe to delete; it is rebuilt) Settings ND_* variables under navidrome: in compose/media.yaml Logs Container output only (./homelab logs navidrome), at level warn (ND_LOGLEVEL)

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Play in the browser at https://navidrome.example.com, or use Feishin at https://music.example.com for a fuller player.
  • Star and rate songs, albums, and artists; ratings and play counts follow you to every app.
  • The user menu (top right) › Personal: theme, language, and the ListenBrainz link for scrobbling.
  • Share an album or playlist with someone without an account: its Share action makes a public link.
  • Admins add people under Users and set a maximum bitrate per device under Players. With NAVIDROME_ADMIN_USER and NAVIDROME_ADMIN_PASSWORD set (an administrator of its own, such as homelab), Settings › People adds each person here too and resets their password.
  • Music apps (Arpeggi, Amperfy, play:Sub, Symfonium) sign in at Navidrome's own address, https://navidrome.example.com. music.example.com is Feishin, a player in the browser, which signs in with the same login.
  • Phone apps: Amperfy and play:Sub (iOS), Symfonium and Tempo (Android), Substreamer (both). On a computer: the Feishin desktop app.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Feishin is its web player; you sign in to it with your Navidrome account.
  • Lidarr files new albums into /Volumes/Media/music; they appear after the next hourly scan.
  • beets tags and files music you add by hand into the same folder.
  • Cloudflare Tunnel publishes it, so phone apps work away from home.
  • .env: MEDIA_ROOT sets the music path, NAVIDROME_PORT the port on this Mac (default 4533), TZ the time zone.
  • It gives out no API key: Subsonic apps sign in with each person's own name and password.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Smart playlists: save a .nsp file (JSON rules, such as rating 4 or more and played in the last month) in the music folder; the next scan turns it into a self-updating playlist.
  • Scrobble to ListenBrainz: paste your ListenBrainz token under the user menu › Personal.
  • Lyrics: Navidrome shows lyrics embedded in the tags or from .lrc files beside the tracks, in Feishin and in apps that support them.
  • Save mobile data: in Players, pick the phone app's player and set a transcoding format (Opus) and a maximum bitrate.
  • Download playlists in Amperfy or Symfonium for offline listening before a trip.
  • Tidy tags before albums go in, with beets or MusicBrainz Picard; Navidrome groups albums by album artist and MusicBrainz IDs.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
The Subsonic API takes a username and password in the query string (u and p); replace USER and PASSWORD. Starting a scan needs an admin account.

./homelab logs navidrome -f
./homelab compose navidrome restart navidrome
./homelab compose navidrome exec navidrome ls -la /data
curl -s http://localhost:4533/ping
curl -s "http://localhost:4533/rest/ping.view?u=USER&p=PASSWORD&v=1.16.1&c=curl&f=json"
curl -s "http://localhost:4533/rest/startScan.view?u=USER&p=PASSWORD&v=1.16.1&c=curl&f=json"
curl -s "http://localhost:4533/rest/getScanStatus.view?u=USER&p=PASSWORD&v=1.16.1&c=curl&f=json"

docs.title: API
docs.text:
• Base URL: http://localhost:4533/rest/ on this Mac, or https://navidrome.example.com/rest/.
  • Authentication: each request carries u (user) and either p (password) or the safer token pair t (MD5 of password plus salt) and s (the salt), plus v (API version), c (client name), and f=json.
  • Example: getAlbumList2.view?type=newest&size=10 lists the latest additions (same parameters as the calls above).
  • Reference: the Subsonic API at https://www.subsonic.org/pages/api.jsp; Navidrome's docs list which endpoints it supports.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• Documentation: https://www.navidrome.org/docs/
  • Source: https://github.com/navidrome/navidrome
  • Image: https://hub.docker.com/r/deluan/navidrome

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: data/appdata/navidrome (database of users, play counts, ratings, playlists) is in the Homelab AppData job. The music itself is not backed up.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Fix Lost the administrator's password docker exec -it homelab_media-navidrome-1 /app/navidrome user edit -u <username> --set-password -n asks for a new one (nothing shows as you type). Someone else's: Settings › People › New music and films password After a password change, covers stay blurred and scans do nothing Navidrome's web page keeps a key made from the password it signed in with. Sign out (user menu › Logout) and in again; in Feishin too. Music apps need the new password as well Library empty The drive was not mounted. ./homelab doctor, then rescan Playlist missing tracks Paths in the .m3u must match /Volumes/Media/music/...

docs.title: RomM
docs.text:
The game library, with artwork, saves, and play in the browser.

Service romm in stacks/romm/compose.yaml (project homelab_romm) Image rommapp/romm:latest Category Media Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install romm Address https://games.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:7676 (ROMM_PORT) Depends on romm-db Helpers romm-db docker.io/library/postgres:17, dumped daily by ./homelab backup Data /Volumes/Media/games → /romm/libraryappdata/romm/resources → /romm/resourcesappdata/romm/assets → /romm/assetsappdata/romm/config → /romm/configromm-redis (volume) → /redis-data Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first Also known as roms, retro, games

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: The household's game library in one place: ROMs and their saves for every console, with box art, descriptions, and play in the browser for the older systems (through EmulatorJS). It pairs with the Steam Machine: browse the library on the TV, or point an emulator at it.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Put games on the media drive under games/roms/<platform>, using RomM's platform folder names (snes, n64, gba, psx, and so on); BIOS files go in games/bios/<platform>.
  2. ./homelab install romm and open https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:7676 in Home mode, or https://games.example.com with a domain; create the admin account.
  3. Scan the library. For artwork and details, add a metadata source first: IGDB (a free Twitch developer app: its client ID and secret in Settings › ROMM_IGDB_CLIENT_ID and ROMM_IGDB_CLIENT_SECRET) or ScreenScraper (ROMM_SCREENSCRAPER_USER and _PASSWORD), then ./homelab install romm again.
  4. Add each person as a user under Administration.

Only play games you own; the homelab does not fetch ROMs.

docs.title: Away from home
docs.text: In Home mode (the default), RomM is on the tailnet: it opens at home and away on every device signed in to Tailscale. With a domain, it is on the home network only: install Tailscale to reach it from anywhere.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• A Python (FastAPI) back end with a Vue web app, served by nginx inside the romm container on port 8080 (7676 on this Mac).
  • PostgreSQL in romm-db holds platforms, games, users, collections, and fetched details. It sits in the romm-pgdata volume, on the stack's private network only.
  • A Redis-compatible store runs inside the romm container (data in the romm-redis volume) and queues the background workers that scan and run scheduled tasks.
  • A scan walks roms/<platform> in the library, identifies each game by file name and hash, and fetches details and artwork from the metadata sources you have set (IGDB, ScreenScraper).
  • In-browser play uses EmulatorJS (and Ruffle for Flash); saves and save states made in the browser are kept as assets.
  • ROMM_AUTH_SECRET_KEY signs sign-in sessions; ROMM_DB_PASSWORD is shared by both containers.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Games /Volumes/Media/games → /romm/library (roms/<platform>, bios/<platform>) Fetched artwork and details appdata/romm/resources → /romm/resources Saves, states, screenshots appdata/romm/assets → /romm/assets Optional config file appdata/romm/config/config.yml → /romm/config/config.yml Database romm-pgdata volume (romm-db, /var/lib/postgresql/data) Task queue romm-redis volume → /redis-data

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Browse by platform or collection, search and filter, and open a game for its details, files, and the Play button (for systems EmulatorJS supports).
  • Add games by uploading them in the browser, or copy them into roms/<platform> and scan.
  • The scan page offers a quick scan of new files or a complete rescan, for all platforms or only the ones you pick.
  • Favourites and your own collections, per user.
  • Download a game to copy it to a handheld or to the Steam Machine's emulator folders.
  • Administration › Users: each person gets a role (viewer, editor, or admin).

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Nginx Proxy Manager serves https://games.example.com on the home network; Tailscale reaches it from elsewhere.
  • Duplicati copies appdata/romm (Stack Data job); ./homelab backup dumps romm-db daily.
  • .env: ROMM_PORT (default 7676), ROMM_DB_PASSWORD, ROMM_AUTH_SECRET_KEY, ROMM_IGDB_CLIENT_ID, ROMM_IGDB_CLIENT_SECRET, ROMM_SCREENSCRAPER_USER, ROMM_SCREENSCRAPER_PASSWORD, MEDIA_ROOT, TZ.
  • It needs API keys from IGDB (through Twitch) or ScreenScraper for artwork, and gives out none of its own to other apps here.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Map your own folder names to RomM's platforms in config.yml (system: platforms:, for example ps1: psx), or exclude folders and file types under exclude:.
  • Put BIOS files in bios/<platform> so EmulatorJS can run systems that need them, such as the PlayStation.
  • Set both IGDB and ScreenScraper: RomM tries IGDB first and fills gaps from ScreenScraper; change the order under scan: priority: in config.yml.
  • Plug a gamepad into the computer; the in-browser player picks it up through the browser.
  • Make a collection per person or per theme (party games, couch co-op) for quick browsing on the TV.
  • Script imports or reports with the API (see below).

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
Replace USER and PASSWORD with a RomM login; the heartbeat needs none.

./homelab logs romm -f
./homelab compose romm ps
./homelab compose romm restart romm
./homelab compose romm exec romm ls -la /romm/config /romm/library
./homelab compose romm exec romm-db psql -U romm -d romm
curl -s http://localhost:7676/api/heartbeat
curl -s -u USER:PASSWORD http://localhost:7676/api/platforms

docs.title: API
docs.text:
• Base URL: http://localhost:7676/api, or https://games.example.com/api.
  • Auth: HTTP basic with a RomM login (the API also issues OAuth tokens).
  • Example: /api/platforms lists platforms with game counts; /api/heartbeat shows the version and which metadata sources are set.
  • Docs: the interactive reference at http://localhost:7676/api/docs.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• Documentation: https://docs.romm.app
  • Source: https://github.com/rommapp/romm
  • Image: https://hub.docker.com/r/rommapp/romm

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: The nightly backup dumps RomM's database; its artwork and settings in appdata/romm are covered by the Stack Data job. The games themselves are on the media drive, which the backups do not copy: keep your own copy of anything you cannot get again.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• The scan finds nothing: check the folders are games/roms/<platform> on the media drive, with RomM's platform names.
  • No artwork: no metadata source is set; see Setup, step 3.

docs.title: beets
docs.text:
Tags, renames, and organizes music into the library Navidrome plays. It comes with the Music pick in Choose apps, beside Navidrome and Feishin.

Service beets in compose/media.yaml (project homelab_media) Image lscr.io/linuxserver/beets:latest Category Media Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install beets Address this computer only: it has no sign-in of its own, so it gets no tailnet or domain address On this machine http://localhost:8337 (BEETS_PORT) Data data/appdata/beets → /config/Volumes/Media/music → /music/Volumes/Media/downloads → /downloads Database dump Daily by ./homelab backup into recovery-staging/databases/beets Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Keeps the music library tidy: it matches each album you add against MusicBrainz, fixes its tags, adds the cover and a genre, and files it as Album Artist/Album (Year)/01 Title in /Volumes/Media/music.
  • For music that arrives by hand (CD rips, purchases, a friend's drive). Navidrome and every music app then group albums, artists, and covers properly.
  • Its web page at http://localhost:8337 browses and searches the library on this computer. It is read-only, and it has no sign-in, so it gets no tailnet or domain address.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. ./homelab install beets. Its settings, data/appdata/beets/config.yaml, are copied from config/beets the first time and are yours to change after.
  2. Put new music in a folder under the downloads folder, for example /Volumes/Media/downloads/music/Some Album.
  3. Import it. beets shows each match and asks when it is unsure (A applies, S skips, U imports as is, E enters a MusicBrainz ID):
./homelab compose beets exec -u abc beets beet import /downloads/music
  1. The files move into the library. Navidrome picks them up at its next hourly scan, or now with Settings › Scan library.

To bring music already in the library under beets without moving anything, import it in place once: beet import -C -W /music lists it in beets' database (-C no copy or move, -W no tag writes). Drop -W to let it fix the tags too.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• beets is a command-line music organizer. The container keeps one running program, beet web, which serves the library page; imports and every other command run with exec inside it.
  • library.db is beets' SQLite database of every track it has imported: its tags, its path, and the MusicBrainz IDs it matched. The files are the truth: tags are written into them (write: yes), so Navidrome reads the same.
  • move: yes moves files out of /downloads instead of copying them, so nothing is left twice. fetchart and embedart save a cover.jpg beside each album and in each file; lastgenre fills in a genre from Last.fm; scrub strips old, conflicting tags before the new ones are written.
  • File names avoid characters exFAT and NTFS refuse (replace: in the settings), so the library can sit on any drive.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Settings data/appdata/beets/config.yaml (the starter copy is config/beets/config.yaml) Database data/appdata/beets/library.db Import log (what was skipped, and why) data/appdata/beets/import.log Library /Volumes/Media/music → /music New music /Volumes/Media/downloads → /downloads

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Search the library: beet ls artist:Radiohead, beet ls -a year:1990..1999 for albums, beet stats for a count.
  • Fix one album that matched wrongly: beet import -L album:"Album name" re-matches it from the library.
  • Change a tag by hand: beet modify album:"Album name" genre=Jazz, then it writes the files.
  • Import without questions (an overnight batch): beet import -q /downloads/music skips anything it is unsure of, and import.log lists those to do by hand later.

Prefix each with ./homelab compose beets exec -u abc beets (-u abc runs it as the user the files belong to, not as root).

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Navidrome plays what beets files: the same /Volumes/Media/music, read-only there.
  • Lidarr, if you run it, already renames and files what it downloads. Leave its albums out of beets' imports, so the two do not move the same files.
  • .env: MEDIA_ROOT sets the music path, DOWNLOADS_ROOT the downloads folder, BEETS_PORT the page's port on this computer (default 8337), PUID and PGID the owner of the files it writes.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Acoustic fingerprints for files with no tags at all: add chroma to plugins: (the image has fpcalc).
  • ReplayGain so every album plays at the same loudness: add replaygain with backend: ffmpeg.
  • Lyrics into the tags, which Navidrome and Feishin show: add lyrics with auto: yes.
  • A playlist of everything added this month: the smartplaylist plugin writes .m3u files into the library, which Navidrome imports.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
./homelab logs beets -f
./homelab compose beets exec -u abc beets beet import /downloads/music
./homelab compose beets exec -u abc beets beet stats
./homelab compose beets exec -u abc beets beet config
curl -s http://localhost:8337/stats

docs.title: API
docs.text:
• beet web answers JSON at http://localhost:8337: /stats, /item/, /album/, /item/query/<query>, /album/<id>/art.
  • Read-only in this setup (readonly: yes), and only on this computer.
  • Reference: https://beets.readthedocs.io/en/stable/plugins/web.html

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• Documentation: https://beets.readthedocs.io/
  • Source: https://github.com/beetbox/beets
  • Image: https://docs.linuxserver.io/images/docker-beets/

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: data/appdata/beets (the settings and library.db) is in the Homelab AppData job, and ./homelab backup takes a consistent copy of library.db daily. The music itself is not backed up; the tags beets wrote are in the files, so a lost database is rebuilt with beet import -C -W /music.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Fix The page does not open It starts after beets has read its settings; a mistake in config.yaml stops it. ./homelab logs beets names the line. beet config shows what it read "Permission denied" moving or writing files The music and downloads folders belong to someone other than PUID/PGID in .env. Set them to the owner (id -u, id -g) and ./homelab compose beets up -d An album was skipped import.log has why. Import that folder again without -q and answer, or enter its MusicBrainz release ID with E An .m3u playlist lost its tracks beets moved and renamed them. Point the playlist at the new paths, or let smartplaylist write playlists for you An album shows twice in Navidrome Two copies were kept (K at a duplicate). beet ls -a album:"Album name" -p shows both paths; beet rm -d removes one with its files

docs.title: Bazarr
docs.text:
Subtitles for everything Sonarr and Radarr manage: finds, downloads, and keeps them in sync.

Service bazarr in compose/media-automation.yaml (project homelab_media_automation) Image lscr.io/linuxserver/bazarr:latest Category Media Automation Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install bazarr Address https://bazarr.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:6767 (BAZARR_PORT) Data data/appdata/bazarr → /config/Volumes/Media/tv → /tv/Volumes/Media/movies → /movies Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Subtitles in the household's languages next to every episode and film.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Open https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:6767 in Home mode, or https://bazarr.example.com with a domain, and set up authentication (Settings › General).
  2. Settings › Sonarr: address sonarr, port 8989, API key. Settings › Radarr: address radarr, port 7878, API key. The paths are the same in all three apps, so no path mapping is needed.
  3. Settings › Languages: create a language profile and make it the default.
  4. Settings › Providers: add subtitle providers.

./homelab wire --apply (or Status › More… › Connect apps) does step 2 for you once Bazarr, Sonarr, and Radarr run, and corrects a key that changed. Steps 3 and 4 are choices of yours: which languages, and which providers.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Bazarr is a Python web app with a React UI. It keeps its list of series, films, and subtitles in a SQLite database and its settings in config.yaml.
  • It does not scan folders on its own: it reads the series and films from Sonarr's and Radarr's APIs, keeps in step with them on a schedule and through their live update feeds, and then looks at the files on disk.
  • For each file missing a subtitle in the language profile, it asks the enabled providers, scores each result against the release (name, group, resolution, hash), and downloads the best one above the minimum score.
  • Subtitles are saved next to the video, for example Episode.en.srt, where Jellyfin picks them up as external subtitles.
  • It sees the libraries at the same /tv and /movies paths as Sonarr and Radarr, which is why no path mapping is needed. It has no /downloads mount: it only works on files already in the library.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Settings and API key data/appdata/bazarr/config/config.yaml (/config/config/config.yaml) Database data/appdata/bazarr/db/bazarr.db (/config/db/bazarr.db) Logs data/appdata/bazarr/log/ (/config/log/bazarr.log) App backups data/appdata/bazarr/backup/ (/config/backup) TV library ${MEDIA_ROOT}/tv, default /Volumes/Media/tv → /tv Film library ${MEDIA_ROOT}/movies, default /Volumes/Media/movies → /movies

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Series and Movies: subtitle status per episode or film; open one to search, upload, or delete a subtitle by hand.
  • Wanted › Series and Wanted › Movies: everything still missing a subtitle, with a button to search them all.
  • History: what was downloaded, from which provider, and with what score.
  • System › Providers: which providers are throttled or failing right now.
  • System › Tasks: run a sync with Sonarr or Radarr, or a disk scan, immediately.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Sonarr at sonarr, port 8989, and Radarr at radarr, port 7878, each with its API key (Settings › General › Security in that app).
  • Jellyfin shows the .srt files Bazarr writes next to the media.
  • ./homelab wire does not connect Bazarr; it prints these steps as a reminder.
  • .env: BAZARR_PORT, MEDIA_ROOT, PUID, PGID, TZ.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Settings › Subtitles: turn on automatic synchronisation, which shifts downloaded subtitles to match the audio.
  • Settings › Providers: add the Embedded Subtitles provider, so subtitles already inside the video file count and are not downloaded again.
  • Settings › Languages: allow hearing-impaired or forced subtitles per language, and set a cutoff so Bazarr stops after the first good match.
  • Settings › Providers: add a free OpenSubtitles.com account for better limits than anonymous use.
  • Settings › Sonarr and Settings › Radarr: raise the minimum score if wrong subtitles get through, or lower it if nothing is found.
  • Settings › Notifications: send download notices to ntfy (Bazarr's notifications go through Apprise, which supports ntfy).

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
Follow the log, restart, check that Bazarr can reach Sonarr and Radarr, and look at the libraries as Bazarr sees them.

./homelab logs bazarr -f
./homelab compose bazarr restart bazarr
./homelab compose bazarr exec bazarr curl -s http://sonarr:8989/ping
./homelab compose bazarr exec bazarr curl -s http://radarr:7878/ping
./homelab compose bazarr exec bazarr ls /tv /movies

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• Bazarr
  • Bazarr wiki
  • Bazarr on GitHub
  • LinuxServer image

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: data/appdata/bazarr (database, settings) is in the Homelab AppData job.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: If nothing is found, check the providers' status (System › Providers); free providers throttle heavily.

docs.title: FlareSolverr
docs.text:
A helper for Prowlarr: it opens indexer sites in a headless browser to get past Cloudflare challenges.

Service flaresolverr in compose/media-automation.yaml (project homelab_media_automation) Image ghcr.io/flaresolverr/flaresolverr:latest Category Media Automation Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install flaresolverr Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Some indexers sit behind Cloudflare's browser check. Prowlarr hands those requests to FlareSolverr at http://flaresolverr:8191.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Installed with the *arr bundle (./homelab install @arr), or alone with ./homelab install flaresolverr.
  2. In Prowlarr: Settings › Indexers › add FlareSolverr, host http://flaresolverr:8191, tag flaresolverr.
  3. Add the flaresolverr tag to each indexer that needs it.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• FlareSolverr is a small Python web server that drives a headless Chromium browser. It has no web UI and no settings file.
  • Prowlarr sends it a URL; FlareSolverr opens the page, waits for the Cloudflare check to pass, and returns the page together with its cookies and user agent to Prowlarr.
  • It handles only the automatic browser check. It cannot solve CAPTCHAs, so an indexer that asks for one still fails.
  • Each request starts a browser, so it uses a fair amount of memory and CPU while it works, and nothing while idle.
  • It listens on port 8191 on the homelab Docker network only; the compose file publishes no port, so it is not reachable from this Mac's browser.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Prowlarr is its only client, through an indexer proxy at http://flaresolverr:8191 and the flaresolverr tag.
  • ./homelab wire sets this up when Prowlarr and FlareSolverr both run: it creates the flaresolverr tag and the proxy. Tagging the indexers is still up to you.
  • .env: only TZ.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Prowlarr › Settings › Indexers › FlareSolverr: raise the request timeout if challenges time out on a slow site.
  • Tag only the indexers that need it: every tagged request is far slower than a plain one.
  • For more detail in its log while debugging, set LOG_LEVEL: debug in its environment in compose/media-automation.yaml, then ./homelab update flaresolverr.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
FlareSolverr has no published port, so the checks run from inside the Prowlarr container. The first shows the version and that it is ready; the second solves a test page.

./homelab logs flaresolverr -f
./homelab compose flaresolverr restart flaresolverr
./homelab compose prowlarr exec prowlarr curl -s http://flaresolverr:8191/
./homelab compose prowlarr exec prowlarr curl -s -X POST http://flaresolverr:8191/v1 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"cmd":"request.get","url":"https://example.com","maxTimeout":60000}'

docs.title: API
docs.text: There is no key. Send POST /v1 with a JSON body naming a command (request.get, request.post, or the sessions.* commands) and a URL; the reply has the status, the page, and the cookies. The commands and options are listed in the project's README.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text: • FlareSolverr on GitHub (code, image, and documentation)

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: Nothing: it keeps no state.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Challenges change often and FlareSolverr breaks when they do. Check ./homelab logs flaresolverr, then ./homelab update flaresolverr. If it still fails, upstream usually has an open issue.

docs.title: Gluetun
docs.text:
A ProtonVPN WireGuard tunnel. qBittorrent shares Gluetun's network, so its traffic can only leave through the VPN; if the tunnel drops, qBittorrent has no network at all.

Service gluetun in compose/media-automation.yaml (project homelab_media_automation) Image qmcgaw/gluetun:latest Category Media Automation Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install gluetun Data data/appdata/gluetun → /gluetun Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first Needs in .env PROTONVPN_WIREGUARD_PRIVATE_KEY

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
• Kill switch for downloads: qBittorrent has no route except the VPN.
  • ProtonVPN port forwarding (P2P servers only) for better connectivity.
  • Publishes qBittorrent's web UI, because qBittorrent has no network of its own.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. ProtonVPN account › Downloads › WireGuard configuration: create a configuration with NAT-PMP (port forwarding) on.
  2. Copy only the PrivateKey value into PROTONVPN_WIREGUARD_PRIVATE_KEY in .env. Optionally set PROTONVPN_SERVER_COUNTRIES.
  3. ./homelab install qbittorrent (starts Gluetun first and waits until it is healthy).
  4. Check the exit address is ProtonVPN's, not your home's:
./homelab compose gluetun exec gluetun wget -qO- https://ipinfo.io/ip
  1. Find the forwarded port in ./homelab logs gluetun ("port forwarded is ...") and set it as qBittorrent's listening port.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Gluetun is a single Go program that sets up the VPN, a firewall, and a DNS resolver inside its container.
  • On start it picks a ProtonVPN server from its server list: only servers with port forwarding (PORT_FORWARD_ONLY: "on"), limited to PROTONVPN_SERVER_COUNTRIES if set. It then brings up WireGuard with your private key.
  • Its firewall drops everything that does not go through the tunnel. This is the kill switch: when the tunnel is down, nothing leaves.
  • DNS queries are answered by its own resolver, which forwards them over an encrypted connection, so they do not leak to your home router.
  • With VPN_PORT_FORWARDING: "on" it asks ProtonVPN for a forwarded port (NAT-PMP) and keeps renewing it, so peers can connect in to qBittorrent.
  • It checks the tunnel all the time and reconnects when it fails. Docker's health check reads that state; qBittorrent waits for it (depends_on: service_healthy).
  • qBittorrent runs with network_mode: service:gluetun: it has no network of its own and uses Gluetun's. That is why qBittorrent's Web UI port (QBITTORRENT_PORT, default 8082) is published on Gluetun, and why other containers reach qBittorrent at gluetun:8082.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where ProtonVPN server list data/appdata/gluetun/servers.json (/gluetun/servers.json) WireGuard private key .env → PROTONVPN_WIREGUARD_PRIVATE_KEY (passed in as WIREGUARD_PRIVATE_KEY) Server countries .env → PROTONVPN_SERVER_COUNTRIES (passed in as SERVER_COUNTRIES) Logs ./homelab logs gluetun (no log file)

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
There is nothing to click: Gluetun has no web UI. The things you do with it:

  • Check the exit address after a change (Setup step 4).
  • Read the forwarded port after each reconnect, and update qBittorrent's listening port when it changes.
  • Change the country: set PROTONVPN_SERVER_COUNTRIES (comma-separated, for example Netherlands,Switzerland), then ./homelab update gluetun qbittorrent to recreate both.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• qBittorrent lives in its network; restart qBittorrent whenever Gluetun is recreated.
  • Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, and LazyLibrarian reach qBittorrent through it at gluetun:8082. ./homelab wire derives that address from qBittorrent's network_mode.
  • Nginx Proxy Manager sends https://qbittorrent.example.com to gluetun:8082 (the proxy_host in qBittorrent's x-homelab).
  • ./homelab install qbittorrent skips both apps until PROTONVPN_WIREGUARD_PRIVATE_KEY is set.
  • .env: PROTONVPN_WIREGUARD_PRIVATE_KEY, PROTONVPN_SERVER_COUNTRIES, QBITTORRENT_PORT, TZ.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Pin a city or a server instead of a country with Gluetun's SERVER_CITIES or SERVER_HOSTNAMES settings (a change to its environment in compose/media-automation.yaml).
  • Set qBittorrent's listening port automatically: Gluetun's VPN_PORT_FORWARDING_UP_COMMAND runs a command with the new port each time it changes, which can call qBittorrent's Web API (see the Gluetun wiki's port forwarding page).
  • Gluetun can also offer an HTTP proxy (HTTPPROXY: "on", port 8888) so another container, such as Prowlarr, can send its traffic through the VPN (also a compose change).
  • Uptime Kuma: an HTTP monitor on http://gluetun:8082 warns you when the tunnel, and with it qBittorrent, goes away.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
Follow the log, find the forwarded port, check the exit address, and restart both containers.

./homelab logs gluetun -f
./homelab logs gluetun | grep -i "port forwarded"
./homelab compose gluetun exec gluetun wget -qO- https://ipinfo.io/ip
./homelab compose gluetun ps
./homelab compose gluetun restart gluetun qbittorrent

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• Gluetun on GitHub (code and image)
  • Gluetun wiki, including the ProtonVPN provider page and port forwarding

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: data/appdata/gluetun holds only a server list; it is in the AppData job but nothing is lost without it.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Fix Won't start: key missing Set PROTONVPN_WIREGUARD_PRIVATE_KEY Unhealthy, no handshake The key was revoked or the configuration lacks port forwarding. Create a new one qBittorrent unreachable after Gluetun restarted qBittorrent lost its network. ./homelab restart qbittorrent Forwarded port changed ProtonVPN assigns a new port on reconnect. Update qBittorrent's listening port

docs.title: LazyLibrarian
docs.text:
E-book and audiobook automation: follows authors and fetches their books into the library.

Service lazylibrarian in compose/media-automation.yaml (project homelab_media_automation) Image lscr.io/linuxserver/lazylibrarian:latest Category Media Automation Starts with ./homelab up No: optional, ./homelab install lazylibrarian Address https://lazylibrarian.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:5299 (LAZYLIBRARIAN_PORT) Data data/appdata/lazylibrarian → /config/Volumes/Media/Books → /books/Volumes/Media/downloads → /downloads Updates Nightly at 4 AM, with a copy of its data first

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: New books by followed authors arrive in /Volumes/Media/Books.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. ./homelab install lazylibrarian; with a domain, then ./homelab domain setup.
  2. Open https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:5299 in Home mode, or https://lazylibrarian.example.com with a domain. Config › Interface: set a username and password.
  3. Config › Downloaders: qBittorrent, host gluetun, port 8082; download directory /downloads.
  4. Config › Processing: eBook library folder /books. If Calibre-Web manages the library, turn on Calibredb import so metadata.db stays correct.
  5. Add it in Prowlarr (Settings › Apps) to receive indexers.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• LazyLibrarian is a Python web app. It keeps authors, books, and history in a SQLite database (lazylibrarian.db) and its settings in config.ini.
  • It looks authors and books up in online book databases, then follows the authors you add and marks new books as wanted.
  • Searches go to the providers under Config › Providers; with Prowlarr, those are Torznab entries that point back at http://prowlarr:9696.
  • Torrents go to qBittorrent at gluetun:8082. When a download finishes, post-processing finds it in /downloads, renames it, and files it under /books/<Author>/<Title>/.
  • With Calibredb import turned on, it adds books through Calibre's calibredb tool instead, so a Calibre library's metadata.db stays correct. That needs the calibredb program inside the container, which this image does not include by default.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text:
What Where Settings data/appdata/lazylibrarian/config.ini (/config/config.ini) Database data/appdata/lazylibrarian/lazylibrarian.db (/config/lazylibrarian.db) Book library ${MEDIA_ROOT}/Books, default /Volumes/Media/Books → /books Downloads DOWNLOADS_ROOT, default /Volumes/Media/downloads → /downloads

There is no audiobook mount: Audiobookshelf reads ${MEDIA_ROOT}/audiobooks, which LazyLibrarian cannot see. /books and /downloads are separate mounts, so imports are copies; Sonarr has the whole download layout.

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Authors: add an author by name, then choose which of their books you want.
  • Books: search for a single title and mark it wanted.
  • Manage: everything wanted, snatched, or failed, with a button to search again.
  • Logs: why a search, download, or import did not work.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Prowlarr sends it indexers: add LazyLibrarian under Prowlarr's Settings › Apps at http://lazylibrarian:5299 with LazyLibrarian's API key (Config › Interface). ./homelab wire does not do this one.
  • qBittorrent is the download client: host gluetun, port 8082.
  • Calibre-Web serves the same /Volumes/Media/Books folder; Kavita and Komga read it read-only.
  • .env: LAZYLIBRARIAN_PORT, MEDIA_ROOT, DOWNLOADS_ROOT, PUID, PGID, TZ.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Config › Notifications: tell you when a book arrives.
  • Magazines: follow a magazine and have new issues fetched like books.
  • Calibre: the LinuxServer image documents a Calibre mod (DOCKER_MODS, a compose change) that adds calibredb and e-book conversion.
  • Audiobooks: add a volume for ${MEDIA_ROOT}/audiobooks in compose/media-automation.yaml and point LazyLibrarian's audiobook folder at it, so Audiobookshelf picks them up.
  • Config › Processing: adjust the folder and file name patterns to match how Calibre-Web or Kavita expect them.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
Follow the log, restart, and check both mounts from inside the container.

./homelab logs lazylibrarian -f
./homelab compose lazylibrarian restart lazylibrarian
./homelab compose lazylibrarian exec lazylibrarian ls /books /downloads
