  • It reads the same folders Duplicati does, read-only: the apps' data, the homelab's own app data, the stacks, Immich's photos, Jellyfin's data, the books, and the nightly database dumps and secrets copy in recovery-staging. Each folder is its own snapshot, so one app's folder can be brought back alone.
  • A snapshot stores only what changed since the last one (content-addressed, deduplicated), so each night after the first is small. A missed night runs at the next start.
  • It runs at a lower CPU share than the apps, like Duplicati.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where The repository (every snapshot, encrypted) KOPIA_REPOSITORY → /repository Its connection and settings data/appdata/kopia/config Cache and logs (not backed up, rebuilt as needed) data/kopia/cache, data/kopia/logs Restores recovery-staging/restore-test, or a folder you choose in recovery-staging Settings KOPIA_REPOSITORY, KOPIA_PASSWORD, KOPIA_SERVER_PASSWORD, KOPIA_PORT, KOPIA_VERSION in .env

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Snapshots: each folder with its last snapshot, its size, and when the next runs. Snapshot now makes one at once.
  • Restore: open a snapshot, pick a folder or file, and restore it into /staging/... (that is recovery-staging in the homelab folder), then copy it back where it belongs. It never writes into the folders it backs up. Running as you, it cannot give files their original owners, so untick Restore File Ownership; they come back as yours. A folder restored by itself comes back read-only: chmod -R u+w it before deleting it (the restore test does this for its own folder).
  • The restore test: ./homelab restore-test --auto --engine kopia picks a dozen files in data/appdata that haven't changed for a day, restores each from Kopia's newest snapshot into recovery-staging/restore-test, and compares them with the live files, as Duplicati's test does. It is on record beside Duplicati's in scripts/logs/restore-test.json, and the nightly backup reminds you once a month until one passes.
  • Policies: how many snapshots to keep. By default: the latest 10, one a day for 7 days, one a week for 4 weeks, one a month for 24 months, and one a year for 3 years.

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Duplicati, the main backup: the same folders, a different engine and destination.
  • ntfy: a failed snapshot can alert through Kopia's notifications (Settings › Notifications in its page).

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Point KOPIA_REPOSITORY at a USB drive you keep in another room, for a copy that survives this machine's drive failing.
  • Keep more monthly snapshots for the photos folder than for the rest.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
./homelab logs kopia -f
./homelab kopia repository <folder>   # where its copies go, then Kopia starts again there
# Run as you (-u), as Kopia does; as root, its files are no longer yours until it restarts
./homelab compose kopia exec -u "$(id -u):$(id -g)" kopia kopia snapshot list --all
./homelab compose kopia exec -u "$(id -u):$(id -g)" kopia kopia snapshot create /source/appdata
./homelab compose kopia exec -u "$(id -u):$(id -g)" kopia kopia repository status

docs.title: API
docs.text: The server's REST API, with HTTP basic sign-in (admin and KOPIA_SERVER_PASSWORD): GET /api/v1/sources, POST /api/v1/sources/upload?userName=homelab&host=homelab&path=/source/appdata for a snapshot now, GET /api/v1/snapshots?userName=homelab&host=homelab&path=..., and POST /api/v1/restore with the snapshot's rootID, a target under /staging, and skipOwners. See Kopia's documentation.

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• kopia.io
  • GitHub: kopia/kopia

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: Kopia is the backup here, so what matters is its repository and password. The repository is wherever KOPIA_REPOSITORY points, never in the folders it backs up. KOPIA_PASSWORD is in .env, which Duplicati's Secrets job keeps (opened with DUPLICATI_SECRETS_PASSPHRASE). Its settings in data/appdata/kopia are not needed to restore: on a new machine, ./homelab install kopia with the same KOPIA_REPOSITORY and KOPIA_PASSWORD connects to the repository and lists every snapshot again.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• It keeps restarting, and its log says the password is wrong: KOPIA_PASSWORD is not the one the repository was made with. Put the old one back; a repository cannot be opened without it.
  • No snapshots of a folder: the folder was not there when Kopia started (the media drive was not mounted). Restart it once the drive is there: ./homelab restart kopia.
  • It keeps restarting, and its log says it cannot write to its repository folder: Kopia runs as you, and the folder is not yours. A drive formatted exFAT or FAT has no owners of its own: it takes one from how it was mounted. Plugged in on the desktop it is yours; mounted another way (by /etc/fstab, as root), add uid= and gid= with your numbers (id -u, id -g), or choose a folder on another drive.
  • The drive with the repository is gone: Kopia stops answering. Plug the drive back in, then ./homelab restart kopia.

docs.title: Phone companion
docs.text:
Status, alerts, backups, and Finances on your phones, each paired with a code; home network and tailnet only.

Runs as A native app, not a container Install ./homelab schedule install Category System Starts with ./homelab up No: a native app (./homelab schedule install) Address https://homelab.example.com (LAN, through Nginx Proxy Manager) On this machine http://localhost:8099

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
The homelab on your phone, served by homelab serve on the computer. Most phones reach it through the Homelab app for iPhone and iPad (apple-client, above); any other phone gets the same screens in its browser. Either way: the same Status and Backups screens as Homelab Wizard on the Mac, with each app's dot and address, alerts, the watchdog, savings, and the backups and restore test. It is for checking on the homelab from the sofa or from away, and for a quick restart without walking to the Mac.

On the phones you allow, it is also the household's Finances: the same screen as on the Mac (Dashboard, Calendar, Recurring, Pay, Net worth; the calendar is a list of the days something happens, week by week), on your phone and your partner's, to look at or to change.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Nothing to install: the serve job runs it (./homelab schedule install, or Setup › Install the jobs). PHONE_COMPANION=false turns it off.
  2. On the Mac: Homelab Wizard › Settings › Phones, give the phone a name, and Pair a phone. It shows a QR code, the code, and links with the code in them (https://homelab.example.com/#pair=…, the tailnet address in Home mode, and http://<this Mac>:8099/#pair=… at home). The code works once, for 10 minutes. In Terminal, ./homelab phone pair --name "My iPhone" prints the same, QR code included.
  3. Scan the QR code with the phone's camera (or open a link on it), and tap Pair.
  4. In Safari: Share › Add to Home Screen. It then opens full screen, like an app.
  5. To let the phone restart, stop, update, and back up: Allow changes in Settings › Phones, or ./homelab phone allow <id> (./homelab phone list shows the id). Ticking Can make changes before pairing (--can-change) does it at once.
  6. To show Finances on it: pick Sees Finances (look only) or Changes Finances beside the phone in Settings › Phones, or ./homelab phone finances <id> view (or edit; off hides them again). Picking it before pairing (--finances view) does it at once. It is apart from Can make changes: a partner's phone can keep the budget without being able to restart apps, and the reverse.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• homelab serve is a small web server inside the CLI (Go's net/http). It serves the desktop app's frontend (web/dist, built into the binary) with one extra script, companion.js, that turns each of the app's calls into a request to the Mac.
  • Each request carries the phone's own token. The Mac keeps only a hash of each token, with the phone's name, whether it may make changes, and when it was last seen.
  • Pairing: phone pair stores a hash of a one-time code that expires after 10 minutes; the phone trades the code for its token. After 10 wrong codes in 10 minutes, pairing waits.
  • Only requests from this Mac, the home network, containers, and the tailnet get an answer, with one exception: away from home through the Cloudflare tunnel (ADR-0023), the iPhone app may look at Status, its apps, and Finances it may see. That goes to one address only (/api/tunnel), and only with Cloudflare Access's signed pass for the household's service token (set up by Setup's Reach Finances away from home), sealed end to end with a key the phone agreed when it paired at home, and carrying the phone's own token. Nothing else answers through the tunnel: no changes, no Settings, no pairing, not the page itself. Without Access set up, anything with Cloudflare's headers is refused, as before. Setup's Reach Finances away from home (homelab phone away --apply) sets it up with CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN (which needs Access: Apps and Policies and Access: Service Tokens, Edit): a service token for the household's phones, an Access application on homelab-away.<domain> letting in only that token, a proxy host for it, and the hostname through the tunnel. A phone paired at home afterwards gets its key, the tunnel's address and the token; pair each phone again once. Ten wrong attempts lock an address, or a phone, out for 10 minutes.
  • Reading (Status, Backups, alerts, logs) works for every paired phone. Start, stop, restart, update, pausing updates, Back up now, Test a restore, and Fix it need a phone allowed to make changes; the Mac runs the same homelab commands the desktop app does.
  • Finances go only to a phone allowed them, and only over an encrypted connection (Tailscale, or the https address): a phone paired over plain home Wi-Fi never gets them, nor does a wall screen in kiosk mode, whatever was picked. A phone that may only look gets the plan marked read-only, and the server refuses its saves.
  • The plan is the Mac's data/finance.json, read and saved by the Mac's own code. Each read carries the file's version; a save from a phone or the Mac made after another device saved is refused, the latest is shown, and a form left open keeps what was typed, so Save again keeps both changes.
  • Settings, Setup, and Choose apps stay on the Mac.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Paired phones (names, token hashes, permissions, Finances) data/phones.json (only you can read it) Finances data/finance.json, the same file the Mac's Finances keeps A household member's own Finances data/members/<username>/data/; locked in finance.sealed once she keeps them private The screens web/dist, inside the homelab binary The server internal/companion; homelab serve in cmd/homelab/serve.go Its log scripts/logs/ with the other jobs

docs.title: Everyday use
docs.text:
• Open it from the Home Screen. It follows the homelab as it changes, like Status on the computer.
  • Tap an app's address to open the app itself.
  • Tap an app's row for its page: its state, its last 200 log lines, its week, and its last backup.
  • Send to my phone: on the computer, right-click an app on Status and pick Send to my phone › and the phone, or use ⌘K for the page you're on; the phone shows From the computer: … at the bottom with Open. Only the app's own pages are sent (never a link out, nor anything secret), never to a wall screen, Finances only to a phone allowed to see them.
  • Send a report (top of Status) makes the diagnostics report, with every password and token removed, and opens the share sheet to send it to whoever helps you.
  • A lost or sold phone: Remove in Settings › Phones (or ./homelab phone remove <id>); its token stops working at once.

docs.title: On a TV or a wall screen
docs.text: Pair a screen the way you pair a phone, with &kiosk at the end of the pairing link (https://homelab.example.com/#pair=CODE&kiosk; Settings › Phones shows it). It then shows Status only: larger, without the sidebar or any button, with the time in the corner, and it asks the browser to keep the screen on. It follows the computer as it changes, like the phone. The browser keeps it in kiosk mode across restarts; open the address with #kiosk=off to leave. Pair it read-only (the default).

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Nginx Proxy Manager gives it https://homelab.example.com at home, behind CrowdSec like every app.
  • Tailscale gives it the tailnet address in Home mode (https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:8099), which works away from home.
  • ntfy is where the alerts it lists come from; the phone's ntfy app still delivers them.
  • Duplicati is read for the off-site jobs.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• Pair a wall tablet as a read-only status board (kiosk mode, above).
  • Give a family member's phone read-only access so they can see whether the homelab is up before asking.
  • Your partner's phone with Changes Finances and without Can make changes: the budget, but no restart button.
  • curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -X POST http://localhost:8099/api/call/Status -d '[]' returns the same JSON the screens use.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
./homelab phone pair --name "My iPhone"
./homelab phone list
./homelab phone allow <id>
./homelab phone read-only <id>
./homelab phone finances <id> view   # or edit, or off
./homelab phone remove <id>
./homelab schedule status

docs.title: API
docs.text:
• Sign-in: Authorization: Bearer <token>, the token a phone gets when it pairs (POST /api/pair with {"code": "…", "name": "…"}).
  • POST /api/call/<Method> with the method's arguments as a JSON array returns {"result": …, "log": [lines]}. The methods are the desktop app's: Status, LastStatus, Backups, Alerts, Watchdog, Protection, SavingsHistory, DuplicatiJobs, AppIcon, Logs, Report, and, for phones allowed to make changes, AppAction, SetAppSetting, SetUpdatesPaused, and Homelab (backup, restore-test, fix); for phones allowed Finances, over https or the tailnet, Finances and (with Changes Finances) SaveFinances. A household member's own phone, for her private Finances: FinancesSealed (her locked file, or null while they're plain), SaveFinancesSealed ([rev, envelope], "new" to turn privacy on: her plain files go only after it's written), UnsealFinances ([rev, plan, ledger], privacy off), FinancesSealedReceipt and SaveFinancesSealedReceipt (her receipts, locked). The computer checks a locked file's shape and size, never what's in it, and answers these to her own phone only; once hers are private, the plain Finances calls from her phone are refused (FinancesShared still answers).
  • POST /api/call/StatusBoard answers in lines of JSON as they come: Status first, then each card asked for (the watchdog, alerts, storage, usage, the week, protection) as it is read, from the background agent when it runs.
  • GET /api/events follows the homelab's changes as Server-Sent Events, as Status on the computer does.
  • GET /api/me says which phone the token belongs to, whether it may make changes, and its Finances ("view", "edit", or none), and what the computer can do (computer: its version, every call it answers, and features such as tunnel), so a phone newer than the computer can say to update it rather than fail. apple-client/Tests/Resources/CompanionContract.json is this answer as the computer gives it (go test ./cmd/homelab -run TestCompanionContract -update-contract writes it; the test fails when it is out of date).

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• Add to Home Screen on iPhone
  • Web app manifests

docs.title: Backup
docs.text: ./homelab backup copies data/phones.json into recovery-staging/secrets/data each night, and the encrypted Homelab Secrets job takes it off-site; homelab move out carries it too. After a restore or a move, the paired phones keep working.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Fix The link does not open At home: the Mac's address is right and the serve job runs (./homelab schedule status). Away: Tailscale is on, and you used the tailnet address "the phone companion answers only at home and on the tailnet" The request came from a public address or through Cloudflare. Use the home or tailnet address "that code does not work" It was used, mistyped, or is over 10 minutes old: run phone pair again Back on the pairing form The phone was removed on the Mac, or Safari cleared its website data. Pair again Restart or Stop is missing The phone is read-only: ./homelab phone allow <id> No Finances in the tab bar The phone is not allowed them: Settings › Phones, or ./homelab phone finances <id> view. A phone paired with the http: link never gets them: remove it and pair it with the https link Finances show no Edit or Add The phone may only look ("view only" under the heading): pick Changes Finances for it "Finances were changed on another device" Someone saved on another phone or the Mac after this one read the plan. The latest is shown; check your change and Save again

docs.title: PostgreSQL
docs.text:
How the databases are run. Each app that needs PostgreSQL has its own database container in its own stack; none is shared and none is reachable from outside its stack.

Database service Stack Image Used by immich-database homelab_immich ghcr.io/immich-app/postgres (14, vectorchord, pgvecto.rs), pinned by digest Immich paperless-db homelab_paperless postgres:18 Paperless-ngx moneymatter-db homelab_budget_tracker postgres:16 MoneyMatter ghostfolio-db homelab_ghostfolio postgres:17 Ghostfolio (optional) romm-db homelab_romm postgres:17 RomM (optional) docmost-db homelab_docmost postgres:17 Docmost (optional) dawarich-db homelab_dawarich postgis/postgis:17-3.5-alpine (PostgreSQL with PostGIS) Dawarich (optional) firefly-iii-db homelab_firefly_iii postgres:18 Firefly III (optional) linkwarden-db homelab_linkwarden postgres:18 Linkwarden (optional) nextcloud-db homelab_nextcloud postgres:18 Nextcloud (optional) tandoor-db homelab_tandoor postgres:18 Tandoor (optional)

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Data lives in named volumes, never in bind mounts.
  • The nightly updates never update a database. A major version upgrade is ./homelab db upgrade <database>: it dumps, starts the new version, loads the dump, checks it, and goes back by itself if a step fails (Runbooks). Each database's major version is a setting (PAPERLESS_DB_VERSION, MONEYMATTER_DB_VERSION, GHOSTFOLIO_DB_VERSION, ROMM_DB_VERSION, DOCMOST_DB_VERSION, FIREFLY_DB_VERSION, LINKWARDEN_DB_VERSION, NEXTCLOUD_DB_VERSION, TANDOOR_DB_VERSION); change it only through that command. Dawarich's PostGIS image is pinned in its compose file instead.
  • Immich's database only ever uses the image Immich's release specifies. Upgrade it only as Immich's release notes say.
  • ./homelab backup dumps every service marked dump: postgres at 03:30 with pg_dumpall --clean --if-exists.

docs.title: Connect
docs.text:
./homelab compose paperless exec paperless-db psql -U paperless
./homelab compose immich exec immich-database psql -U postgres -d immich
./homelab compose money exec moneymatter-db psql -U budget_tracker
./homelab compose ghostfolio exec ghostfolio-db psql -U ghostfolio
./homelab compose romm exec romm-db psql -U romm
./homelab compose docmost exec docmost-db psql -U docmost
./homelab compose dawarich exec dawarich-db psql -U postgres -d dawarich_development
./homelab compose firefly-iii exec firefly-iii-db psql -U firefly
./homelab compose linkwarden exec linkwarden-db psql -U linkwarden
./homelab compose nextcloud exec nextcloud-db psql -U nextcloud
./homelab compose tandoor exec tandoor-db psql -U tandoor

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Each container runs the official PostgreSQL image; Immich's is a build of it with vector extensions. On its first start it creates the user, password, and database from POSTGRES_USER, POSTGRES_PASSWORD, and POSTGRES_DB. After that those settings are ignored, so changing a *_DB_PASSWORD in .env later does not change the password inside the database.
  • The app reaches its database by service name on port 5432 over its stack's own network (homelab_<stack>_default). No database port is published on this Mac.
  • Immich keeps the vectors for faces and smart search in its database with the VectorChord extension, which is why only Immich's image works for it.
  • ./homelab backup runs pg_dumpall inside each running database container at 03:30, gzips it, and keeps the newest 7 dumps of each. The Homelab Databases job in Duplicati takes them off the Mac at 05:00.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Immich's data volume homelab_immich_immich-pgdata → /var/lib/postgresql/data Paperless's data volume homelab_paperless_paperless-pgdata → /var/lib/postgresql (PostgreSQL 18 keeps its files in 18/docker below it) MoneyMatter's data volume homelab_budget_tracker_moneymatter-db → /var/lib/postgresql/data Ghostfolio's data volume homelab_ghostfolio_ghostfolio-pgdata → /var/lib/postgresql/data RomM's data volume homelab_romm_romm-pgdata → /var/lib/postgresql/data The other optional stacks' data volume <app>-pgdata in each stack's project (homelab_docmost_docmost-pgdata, homelab_firefly_iii_firefly-iii-pgdata, and so on for Dawarich, Linkwarden, Nextcloud, and Tandoor) → /var/lib/postgresql/data Daily dumps recovery-staging/databases/<service>/<service>-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.sql.gz Passwords .env: <APP>_DB_PASSWORD for each (IMMICH_DB_PASSWORD, PAPERLESS_DB_PASSWORD, MONEYMATTER_DB_PASSWORD, GHOSTFOLIO_DB_PASSWORD, ROMM_DB_PASSWORD, DOCMOST_DB_PASSWORD, DAWARICH_DB_PASSWORD, FIREFLY_DB_PASSWORD, LINKWARDEN_DB_PASSWORD, NEXTCLOUD_DB_PASSWORD, TANDOOR_DB_PASSWORD)

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• Each database has one client: Immich, Paperless-ngx, MoneyMatter, Ghostfolio, RomM, Docmost, Dawarich, Firefly III, Linkwarden, Nextcloud, or Tandoor.
  • Their queues and caches are in Redis and Valkey.
  • Duplicati carries the dumps off the Mac; the nightly updates skip every database.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• See how big each database is (\l+ in psql) and which tables are largest (\dt+).
  • Watch what an app is doing with SELECT * FROM pg_stat_activity;.
  • Browse a database in a throwaway Adminer bound to this Mac only: docker run --rm --network homelab_paperless_default -p 127.0.0.1:8079:8080 adminer, server paperless-db, then Ctrl+C to remove it.
  • Read a dump to see what a restore would replay: gunzip -c one from recovery-staging/databases into less.
  • Move MoneyMatter's database from 16 to 17: ./homelab db upgrade moneymatter-db (read the app's release notes first).

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
The version, databases with sizes, open connections, a readiness check, Immich's extensions, the logs, a preview of the nightly dump, the dumps on disk, and the data volumes. Paperless is the example; swap in the stack, service, and user from the table above:

./homelab compose paperless exec paperless-db psql -U paperless -c 'SELECT version();'
./homelab compose paperless exec paperless-db psql -U paperless -c '\l+'
./homelab compose paperless exec paperless-db psql -U paperless -c 'SELECT datname, state, query_start FROM pg_stat_activity;'
./homelab compose paperless exec paperless-db pg_isready
./homelab compose immich exec immich-database psql -U postgres -d immich -c '\dx'
./homelab logs paperless-db -f
./homelab backup
ls -lh recovery-staging/databases/*
docker volume ls --filter name=pgdata

docs.title: Learn more
docs.text:
• Docs: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/
  • Image: https://hub.docker.com/_/postgres and https://github.com/docker-library/postgres

docs.title: Restore
docs.text: See Disaster Recovery. In short: stop the app, pipe the gunzipped dump into psql -d postgres in the database container, and start the app.

docs.title: Redis and Valkey
docs.text:
In-memory stores used as caches and job queues. They hold nothing that cannot be rebuilt, so none is backed up.

Service Stack Image Holds immich-redis homelab_immich valkey/valkey:9, pinned by digest Immich's job queue paperless-broker homelab_paperless valkey/valkey:9-alpine Paperless's task queue moneymatter-redis homelab_budget_tracker redis:7 MoneyMatter's cache and sessions ghostfolio-redis homelab_ghostfolio valkey/valkey:9-alpine Ghostfolio's cache and job queue (optional) docmost-redis homelab_docmost valkey/valkey:9-alpine Docmost's background jobs and live editing (optional) dawarich-redis homelab_dawarich valkey/valkey:9-alpine Dawarich's job queue (optional) nextcloud-redis homelab_nextcloud valkey/valkey:9-alpine Nextcloud's file locking and cache (optional) built into romm homelab_romm inside rommapp/romm, updated with it RomM's task queue and cache (optional)

Valkey is the open-source continuation of Redis and speaks the same protocol.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Each app has its own instance on its stack's private network.
  • Left out of the nightly updates: they move with the app's own release notes.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• Each keeps its data in memory and answers on port 6379, with no password: only containers on the same stack network can reach it.
  • Paperless-ngx uses paperless-broker as Celery's broker: every document to consume or OCR waits there as a task until a worker takes it.
  • Immich keeps its background job queues (thumbnails, metadata, face detection, smart search) in immich-redis.
  • MoneyMatter keeps cached data and sessions in moneymatter-redis; if it is wiped, you may have to sign in again.
  • Ghostfolio caches data and queues its market-data jobs in ghostfolio-redis; it refills on its own.
  • RomM runs its own Redis inside its container for scans and caching.
  • They save a snapshot (dump.rdb) to their data folder from time to time, so a restart keeps most keys where that folder is a named volume.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where paperless-broker volume homelab_paperless_paperless-redisdata → /data moneymatter-redis volume homelab_budget_tracker_moneymatter-redis → /data RomM's built-in Redis volume homelab_romm_romm-redis → /redis-data immich-redis, ghostfolio-redis, docmost-redis, dawarich-redis, nextcloud-redis no named volume; nothing there needs keeping

docs.title: Connects to
docs.text:
• The data that matters for these apps is in PostgreSQL; these only hold work in progress and caches.
  • The nightly updates skip them; Duplicati does not back them up.

docs.title: Tinkering ideas
docs.text:
• See how many Paperless tasks are waiting: LLEN celery in paperless-broker.
  • Check memory use with INFO memory and key counts with INFO keyspace.
  • valkey-cli --stat prints a rolling line of keys, memory, and clients; Ctrl+C stops it.
  • valkey-cli --latency measures how fast it answers.
  • Watch commands arrive with MONITOR for a few seconds while an upload runs; it slows the server, so stop it with Ctrl+C.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
A ping, key counts, the Paperless queue length, memory, MoneyMatter's key count, a live view, the logs, and the volumes:

./homelab compose immich exec immich-redis valkey-cli ping
./homelab compose paperless exec paperless-broker valkey-cli info keyspace
./homelab compose paperless exec paperless-broker valkey-cli llen celery
./homelab compose ghostfolio exec ghostfolio-redis valkey-cli info memory

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: If one is corrupted, stop its stack, remove its volume (for example docker volume rm homelab_paperless_paperless-redisdata), and start the stack again. Queued jobs are lost; the app re-creates what it needs.
